commit_msg:
When the device descriptor is closed, the `substream->runtime` pointer
is freed. But another thread may be in the ioctl handler, case
SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_PCM_INFO. This case calls snd_pcm_info_user() which
calls snd_pcm_info() which accesses the now freed `substream->runtime`.

Note: this fixes CVE-2017-0861

Signed-off-by: Robb Glasser <rglasser@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Nick Desaulniers <ndesaulniers@google.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tmutex_lock(&pcm->open_mutex);', '\t\t\tmutex_unlock(&pcm->open_mutex);']}
description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the snd_pcm_info function in the ALSA subsystem in the Linux kernel allows attackers to gain privileges via unspecified vectors.

code_evidence: The handler takes only register_mutex, resolves pcm via snd_pcm_get, walks pstr->substream to find the matching substream [51-54], and passes that pointer to snd_pcm_info_user [59] before releasing register_mutex [61]. Nothing in this path holds pcm->open_mutex or otherwise pins the substream/runtime; register_mutex does not serialize against the close/release path that frees substream->runtime.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function uses a substream whose runtime may already have been freed by a concurrent thread; the missing synchronization causes a stale pointer dereference, not merely a race or NULL check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_PCM_INFO path dereferences the located substream and its runtime through snd_pcm_info_user without the lock that protects the PCM open/close lifecycle. Trigger: a concurrent close/release of the device frees substream->runtime while this ioctl is between lookup and use. Supported consequence: use-after-free read of freed runtime memory, which can crash or enable privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Fix heap-buffer-overflows when accessing pool

Constants are usually retrieved from the constant pool without verifying
that the pool actually contains them, which may lead to various heap
buffer overflow issues.

In this patch we add a counter keeping track of how many elements the pool
contains, and checks making sure that whenever the pool is accessed, the
constant in present in the pool (constant position < pool counter).

Also, do not return "" when a pointer is excepted (it should be legal to free
this return value).

This patch fixes #112 (CVE-2018-7875), fixes #120 (CVE-2018-7871),
fixes #117 (CVE-2018-7870), fixes #114 (CVE-2018-7872), fixes #122,
fixes #113 (CVE-2018-7868), fixes #123.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn "";'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (act->p.Constant8 > poolcounter)', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: retrieving constants not present in the pool.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '\t\tif (act->p.Constant16 > poolcounter)', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: retrieving constants not present in the pool.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '', '\tt = malloc(sizeof(char));', '\tstrcpyext(t,"");', '', '\treturn t;']}
description: There is a heap-based buffer over-read in the getName function of util/decompile.c in libming 0.4.8 for CONSTANT8 data. A Crafted input will lead to a denial of service attack.

code_evidence: In the PUSH_CONSTANT case, act->p.Constant8 is used directly as an index into pool at lines 47 and 49 without any check that the index is within the pool's bounds before strlenext and strcatext read the entry.
The PUSH_CONSTANT16 case does the same with act->p.Constant16 at lines 53 and 55, indexing pool without validating the offset against the number of constants actually present.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked index causes reads of pool[] beyond its intended boundary, which is exactly an out-of-bounds memory buffer access. CWE-119 covers operations outside a buffer's intended boundary; the missing index constraint is the direct cause of the out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: constant-pool offsets from parsed SWF action data are used as array indices with no bounds validation. Trigger: a crafted SWF file supplies a PUSH_CONSTANT or PUSH_CONSTANT16 action whose constant index exceeds the pool size, so pool[index] points outside the allocated pool. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of heap memory in strlenext/strcatext, leading to heap buffer over-read and denial of service (crash) or disclosure of adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
KVM: x86: Improve thread safety in pit

There's a race condition in the PIT emulation code in KVM.  In
__kvm_migrate_pit_timer the pit_timer object is accessed without
synchronization.  If the race condition occurs at the wrong time this
can crash the host kernel.

This fixes CVE-2014-3611.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Andrew Honig <ahonig@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&pit->pit_state.lock);', '\tmutex_unlock(&pit->pit_state.lock);']}
description: Race condition in the __kvm_migrate_pit_timer function in arch/x86/kvm/i8254.c in the KVM subsystem in the Linux kernel through 3.17.2 allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS crash) by leveraging incorrect PIT emulation.

code_evidence: The function obtains the shared timer pointer from pit->pit_state.timer at line 7, then calls hrtimer_cancel(timer) and conditionally hrtimer_start_expires(timer, HRTIMER_MODE_ABS) at lines 8-9 without holding pit->pit_state.lock, so the timer state is read and mutated without exclusive access.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the code sequence requires temporary exclusive access to the shared pit_state.timer but lacks a lock, allowing an interfering concurrent sequence to modify the resource. The missing mutex_lock/mutex_unlock around the timer operations is the direct cause; the host crash is the availability consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The shared PIT timer state is accessed and modified without synchronization. A concurrent sequence (e.g., another vCPU migration or PIT emulation path) can interleave between hrtimer_cancel and hrtimer_start_expires, corrupting the timer state and crashing the host kernel.

Bug 701844: fixed output buffer size worst case in lp8000_print_page().

description: A heap-based buffer overwrite vulnerability was found in GhostScript's lp8000_print_page() function in the gdevlp8k.c file. This flaw allows an attacker to trick a user into opening a crafted PDF file, triggering the heap buffer overflow that could lead to memory corruption or a denial of service.

code_evidence: buf2 is allocated with only in_size bytes and out is set to buf2, so the output buffer has the same size as the input scan line.

The RLE encoder writes to *outp++ for each literal byte and up to three bytes per run (e.g., *outp++ repeated at 84-86 and 90-92), plus a possible trailing byte at 97, without any check against the buffer end.
The accumulated outp - out length is then passed to gp_fwrite at 113, confirming outp indexes the allocated buf2.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes beyond the end of the allocated buf2 memory buffer, which is an out-of-bounds write within a heap buffer, matching CWE-119. It is not merely an integer issue: the allocation size itself is too small for the encoder's worst case.

evidence_lines.code:
report_size = outp - out;
gp_fwrite(out,1,(outp - out),prn_stream);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buf2 is sized to in_size, but the run-length encoding loop can emit up to roughly 3 bytes per 2 input bytes, so writes via outp exceed the heap allocation. Trigger: a crafted PDF producing scan lines dominated by repeated byte runs. Consequence: heap buffer overflow, memory corruption or denial of service.

data.data = data_signed;

commit_msg:
xen/gnttab: Fix error path in map_grant_ref()

Part of XSA-295 (c/s 863e74eb2cffb) inadvertently re-positioned the brackets,
changing the logic.  If the _set_status() call fails, the grant_map hypercall
would fail with a status of 1 (rc != GNTST_okay) instead of the expected
negative GNTST_* error.

This error path can be taken due to bad guest state, and causes net/blk-back
in Linux to crash.

This is XSA-316.

Signed-off-by: Ross Lagerwall <ross.lagerwall@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                               ld->domain_id) != GNTST_okay) )'], 'added_lines': ['                               ld->domain_id)) != GNTST_okay )']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing guest OS users to cause a denial of service because of a bad error path in GNTTABOP_map_grant. Grant table operations are expected to return 0 for success, and a negative number for errors. Some misplaced brackets cause one error path to return 1 instead of a negative value. The grant table code in Linux treats this condition as success, and proceeds with incorrectly initialised state. A buggy or malicious guest can construct its grant table in such a way that, when a backend domain tries to map a grant, it hits the incorrect error path. This will crash a Linux based dom0 or backend domain.

code_evidence: The _set_status() result is assigned to rc, but the comparison to GNTST_okay is inside the assignment parentheses due to bracket placement, so rc receives the boolean 0/1 rather than the GNTST_* error code. On the error path the comparison is false (0), so the goto is skipped and execution continues treating the failure as success; op->status is later set from rc at line 253.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to properly handle the exceptional condition returned by _set_status(); the error path is silently not taken and a non-error status is propagated, exactly the class of improper exceptional-condition handling. CWE-697 (incorrect comparison) is the underlying low-level cause, but the security-relevant weakness here is the mishandled error condition.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: misparenthesized assignment makes rc a boolean instead of propagating the negative GNTST_* status. Trigger: a guest constructs grant-table state causing _set_status() to fail; the error branch is bypassed and map_grant_ref proceeds with incorrectly initialized state, returning status 1 instead of a negative error, which crashes a Linux backend.

commit_msg:
CVE-2018-10756: Fix heap-use-after-free in tr_variantWalk

In libtransmission/variant.c, function tr_variantWalk, when the variant
stack is reallocated, a pointer to the previously allocated memory
region is kept. This address is later accessed (heap use-after-free)
while walking back down the stack, causing the application to crash.
The application can be any application which uses libtransmission, such
as transmission-daemon, transmission-gtk, transmission-show, etc.

Reported-by: Tom Richards <tom@tomrichards.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        tr_variantInitDict(&node->sorted, n);', '            node->sorted.val.l.vals[i] = *tmp[i].val;', '        node->sorted.val.l.count = n;', '        node->v = &node->sorted;', '        node->v = v;'], 'added_lines': ['        node->sorted = tr_new(tr_variant, 1);', '        tr_variantInitDict(node->sorted, n);', '            node->sorted->val.l.vals[i] = *tmp[i].val;', '        node->sorted->val.l.count = n;', '        v = node->sorted;', '        node->sorted = NULL;', '', '    node->v = v;']}
description: Use-after-free in libtransmission/variant.c in Transmission before 3.00 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted torrent file.

code_evidence: node->sorted is an embedded tr_variant member; node->v is set to &node->sorted, storing a pointer into the SaveNode struct rather than an independent allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because node->v retains a pointer to memory whose lifetime ends on reallocation, and that stale pointer is later used. This is a lifetime/alias issue, not merely an out-of-bounds read, so the use-after-free classification is appropriate.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The node's sorted dictionary is stored inline, and node->v is assigned the address of the embedded member. If the SaveNode (or its containing stack) is reallocated while node->v still references the old embedded location, later traversal through node->v dereferences freed memory. Trigger: variant stack growth/reallocation during walk; consequence: heap use-after-free, crash or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
Added safety check for Compressed RTF Streams

You could potentially overflow the input pointer.

in response to #34
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    while (out < (comp_Prebuf.size + uncompressedSize)) {'], 'added_lines': ['    while ((out < (comp_Prebuf.size + uncompressedSize)) && (in < p->size)) {']}
description: An issue was discovered in ytnef before 1.9.2. There is a potential heap-based buffer over-read on incoming Compressed RTF Streams, related to DecompressRTF() in libytnef.

code_evidence: The decompression loop at line 44 is bounded only by the output size (out < comp_Prebuf.size + uncompressedSize); the input index in is never checked against p->size before src[in++] is read at line 45.

When a flag bit is 1, lines 46-47 read two more bytes src[in++] for offset and length without any bounds check, so a crafted compressed stream can drive in past the end of the src buffer. The literal branch at lines 55-56 does check in >= p->size, but the reference branch does not.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Reading src[in] with in >= p->size is a read past the end of the input buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). The missing in < p->size constraint is the direct cause; the consequence is read memory exposure/DoS, not a write, so a write-based weakness would not apply.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reference branch of the decompression loop increments and dereferences the input pointer without verifying in remains within p->size. Trigger: a compressed RTF stream whose flag bytes select references beyond the available input. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read of src, potentially crashing or leaking adjacent heap memory.

commit_msg:
Fix security vulnerability with FractionalAvgPoolGrad

PiperOrigin-RevId: 462292194
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    int64_t num_elements = 1;', '    for (int i = 0; i < orig_input_tensor_shape.dims(); i++) {', '      OP_REQUIRES(context, orig_input_tensor_shape.dim_size(i) > 0,', '                  errors::InvalidArgument(', '                      "orig_input_tensor_shape must be positive, got: ",', '                      orig_input_tensor_shape.dim_size(i)));', '      num_elements = MultiplyWithoutOverflow(', '          num_elements, orig_input_tensor_shape.dim_size(i));', '      OP_REQUIRES(', '          context, num_elements > 0,', '          errors::InvalidArgument(', '              "The total elements specified by orig_input_tensor_shape",', '              " is too large. Encountered overflow after multiplying ",', '              orig_input_tensor_shape.dim_size(i), ", result: ", num_elements));', '    }', '', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, out_backprop.dims() == 4,', '                errors::InvalidArgument("out_backprop must be 4-dimensional"));', '    for (int i = 0; i < out_backprop.dims(); i++) {', '      OP_REQUIRES(context, out_backprop.dim_size(i) > 0,', '                  errors::InvalidArgument(', '                      "out_backprop must be positive for all dimension, got:",', '                      out_backprop.dim_size(i)));', '    }', '']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `FractionalAvgPoolGrad` does not fully validate the input `orig_input_tensor_shape`. This results in an overflow that results in a `CHECK` failure which can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 03a659d7be9a1154fdf5eeac221e5950fec07dad. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.10.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.9.1, TensorFlow 2.8.1, and TensorFlow 2.7.2, as these are also affected and still in supported range. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

code_evidence: Input 0 is only checked to be a 1-D tensor of 4 elements; the individual dimension values are not validated for positivity or product overflow before use.
The four raw int64 dimension values are read directly into in_batch/in_rows/in_cols/in_depth (only zero is rejected).
These values are fed into TensorShape::AddDim and then used to allocate the temporary tensor via forward_input_or_allocate_temp.
The flat buffer is mapped with in_cols * in_rows * in_batch as the column count, so an overflowing product produces an inconsistent/too-small shape.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked shape leads to a TensorFlow CHECK/assertion failure reachable from user-supplied input, matching CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion). It is not a memory-safety bug; the supported impact is process abort/DoS.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: orig_input_tensor_shape values are not validated for positivity or multiplication overflow before building in_shape and allocating the temp tensor. A crafted shape whose dimension product overflows int64 yields an invalid TensorShape/allocation, causing a CHECK failure (reachable assertion) that aborts the process. Consequence is denial of service, not memory corruption.

commit_msg:
USB: serial: console: fix use-after-free on disconnect

A clean-up patch removing two redundant NULL-checks from the console
disconnect handler inadvertently also removed a third check. This could
lead to the struct usb_serial being prematurely freed by the console
code when a driver accepts but does not register any ports for an
interface which also lacks endpoint descriptors.

Fixes: 0e517c93dc02 ("USB: serial: console: clean up sanity checks")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>     # 4.11
Reported-by: Andrey Konovalov <andreyknvl@google.com>
Acked-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (serial->port[0] == usbcons_info.port) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (serial->port[0] && serial->port[0] == usbcons_info.port) {']}
description: The usb_serial_console_disconnect function in drivers/usb/serial/console.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.8 allows local users to cause a denial of service (use-after-free and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted USB device, related to disconnection and failed setup.

code_evidence: Line 3 dereferences serial->port[0] without first checking that port[0] is non-NULL, then compares it to usbcons_info.port. If the pointer is NULL and usbcons_info.port is also NULL, the branch is entered, and lines 4-5 call usb_serial_console_exit() and usb_serial_put(serial), releasing the serial structure.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing NULL guard causes premature freeing of serial, and subsequent uses of the freed object constitute use-after-free (CWE-416). This is a lifetime/ownership flaw, not merely a NULL-pointer dereference, since the released object remains reachable.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the disconnect handler treats a NULL port[0] as a match against usbcons_info.port and proceeds to release the serial. Trigger: a driver that accepts an interface but registers no ports (port[0] NULL) is disconnected. Consequence: usb_serial_put() prematurely frees the struct usb_serial while other code still references it, yielding a use-after-free/crash.

its CPDF_ColorSpace, from code attempting to recover from a failed decoder

commit_msg:
Follow the following steps:
 # ip netns add net1
 # export MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=0
 # ip netns list
then Segmentation fault (core dumped) will occur.

In get_netnsid_from_name func, answer is freed before
rta_getattr_u32(tb[NETNSA_NSID]), where tb[] refers to answer`s
content. If we set MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=0, mmap will be adoped to
malloc memory, which will be freed immediately after calling free
func.  So reading tb[NETNSA_NSID] will access the released memory
after free(answer).

Here, we will call get_netnsid_from_name(tb[NETNSA_NSID]) before free(answer).

Fixes: 86bf43c7c2f ("lib/libnetlink: update rtnl_talk to support malloc buff at run time")
Reported-by: Huiying Kou <kouhuiying@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Zhiqiang Liu <liuzhiqiang26@huawei.com>
Acked-by: Phil Sutter <phil@nwl.cc>
Signed-off-by: Stephen Hemminger <stephen@networkplumber.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint len, fd;', '\t\tgoto err_out;', '\t\tgoto err_out;', '\t\tfree(answer);', '\t\treturn rta_getattr_u32(tb[NETNSA_NSID]);', 'err_out:', '\treturn -1;'], 'added_lines': ['\tint len, fd, ret = -1;', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t\tgoto out;', '\t\tret = rta_getattr_u32(tb[NETNSA_NSID]);', 'out:', '\treturn ret;']}
description: iproute2 before 5.1.0 has a use-after-free in get_netnsid_from_name in ip/ipnetns.c. NOTE: security relevance may be limited to certain uses of setuid that, although not a default, are sometimes a configuration option offered to end users. Even when setuid is used, other factors (such as C library configuration) may block exploitability.

code_evidence: When tb[NETNSA_NSID] is set, line 35 frees the netlink reply buffer 'answer' before line 36 reads the attribute via rta_getattr_u32(tb[NETNSA_NSID]); tb[] entries point into the memory owned by 'answer'.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code dereferences a pointer into memory that was freed one line earlier, matching CWE-416 use after free. The fix reads the value before free(answer), confirming the ordering defect rather than a separate double-free or buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the reply buffer is released while an attribute pointer into it is still dereferenced. Trigger: a successful RTM_GETNSID response containing NETNSA_NSID, with malloc routed to mmap (MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=0) so free() returns pages immediately. Consequence: rta_getattr_u32 reads freed memory, causing a crash or disclosure of stale data.

commit_msg:
Because group consistency is non-atomic between parent (filedesc) and children
(inherited) events, it is possible for PERF_FORMAT_GROUP read() to try and sum
non-matching counter groups -- with non-sensical results.

Add group_generation to distinguish the case where a parent group removes and
adds an event and thus has the same number, but a different configuration of
events as inherited groups.

This became a problem when commit fa8c269353d5 ("perf/core: Invert
perf_read_group() loops") flipped the order of child_list and sibling_list.
Previously it would iterate the group (sibling_list) first, and for each
sibling traverse the child_list. In this order, only the group composition of
the parent is relevant. By flipping the order the group composition of the
child (inherited) events becomes an issue and the mis-match in group
composition becomes evident.

That said; even prior to this commit, while reading of a group that is not
equally inherited was not broken, it still made no sense.

(Ab)use ECHILD as error return to indicate issues with child process group
composition.

Fixes: fa8c269353d5 ("perf/core: Invert perf_read_group() loops")
Reported-by: Budimir Markovic <markovicbudimir@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20231018115654.GK33217@noisy.programming.kicks-ass.net
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t/*', '\t * By locking the child_mutex of the leader we effectively', '\t * lock the child list of all siblings.. XXX explain how.', '\t */'], 'added_lines': []}
description:
A heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Linux Kernel Performance Events (perf) component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

If perf_read_group() is called while an event's sibling_list is smaller than its child's sibling_list, it can increment or write to memory locations outside of the allocated buffer.

We recommend upgrading past commit 32671e3799ca2e4590773fd0e63aaa4229e50c06.

code_evidence: values is allocated with event->read_size bytes via kzalloc and values[0] is initialized to 1 + leader->nr_siblings.

The loop iterates over leader->child_list and calls __perf_read_group_add(child, read_format, values) for each child without verifying that the child's sibling_list size matches the leader's group composition.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is writing beyond the allocated values buffer due to a group-composition mismatch. This directly matches CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write); it is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the writes corrupt memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The buffer size is derived from the leader's read_size and nr_siblings, but the child loop writes into values using the child's own group composition. When a child has a larger sibling_list than the leader, __perf_read_group_add increments/writes past the allocated buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write and memory corruption.

commit_msg:
ovl: verify upper dentry before unlink and rename

Unlink and rename in overlayfs checked the upper dentry for staleness by
verifying upper->d_parent against upperdir.  However the dentry can go
stale also by being unhashed, for example.

Expand the verification to actually look up the name again (under parent
lock) and check if it matches the upper dentry.  This matches what the VFS
does before passing the dentry to filesytem's unlink/rename methods, which
excludes any inconsistency caused by overlayfs.

Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tolddentry = ovl_dentry_upper(old);', '\tnewdentry = ovl_dentry_upper(new);', '\tif (newdentry) {', '\t\t\tnewdentry = opaquedir;', '\t\t\topaquedir = NULL;', '\t\t\tdget(newdentry);', '\t\tnewdentry = lookup_one_len(new->d_name.name, new_upperdir,', '\t\t\t\t\t   new->d_name.len);', '\t\terr = PTR_ERR(newdentry);', '\t\tif (IS_ERR(newdentry))', '\t\t\tgoto out_unlock;', '\t}', '', '\terr = -ESTALE;', '\tif (olddentry->d_parent != old_upperdir)', '\t\tgoto out_dput;', '\tif (newdentry->d_parent != new_upperdir)', '\t\tgoto out_dput;'], 'added_lines': ['', '\tolddentry = lookup_one_len(old->d_name.name, old_upperdir,', '\t\t\t\t   old->d_name.len);', '\terr = PTR_ERR(olddentry);', '\tif (IS_ERR(olddentry))', '\t\tgoto out_unlock;', '', '\terr = -ESTALE;', '\tif (olddentry != ovl_dentry_upper(old))', '\t\tgoto out_dput_old;', '', '\tnewdentry = lookup_one_len(new->d_name.name, new_upperdir,', '\t\t\t\t   new->d_name.len);', '\terr = PTR_ERR(newdentry);', '\tif (IS_ERR(newdentry))', '\t\tgoto out_dput_old;', '', '\terr = -ESTALE;', '\tif (ovl_dentry_upper(new)) {', '\t\t\tif (newdentry != opaquedir)', '\t\t\t\tgoto out_dput;', '\t\t\tif (newdentry != ovl_dentry_upper(new))', '\t\t\t\tgoto out_dput;', '\t\tif (!d_is_negative(newdentry) &&', '\t\t    (!new_opaque || !ovl_is_whiteout(newdentry)))', '\t\t\tgoto out_dput;', '\t}', '', 'out_dput_old:', '\tdput(olddentry);']}
description: fs/overlayfs/dir.c in the OverlayFS filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 4.6 does not properly verify the upper dentry before proceeding with unlink and rename system-call processing, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) via a rename system call that specifies a self-hardlink.

code_evidence: After lock_rename, the code derives olddentry/newdentry from ovl_dentry_upper() and, when newdentry is non-NULL, just dget()s it; only d_parent is compared to old_upperdir/new_upperdir. A dentry can be stale via unhashed state, so the name is not re-looked-up and the actual upper entry is not validated against the requested name before the rename proceeds.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code accepts a derived input (the cached upper dentry) without validating that it still corresponds to the requested name, matching CWE-20's improper validation of required input properties. A related CWE-362 race is not the label because the supported defect is the missing validation, though staleness arises from concurrent changes.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the upper dentry is trusted without re-looking-up the name under the parent lock, so a stale/unhashed dentry passes the d_parent-only check. Trigger: rename with a self-hardlink causes an inconsistent upper dentry to be used in vfs_rename. Consequence: kernel crash (DoS).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void', '    size_t root_len;', '', '        wcscpy(dest_path, rest);', '        return;', '    root_len = wcslen(root);', '    wcscpy(dest_path, root);', '    if(root_len) {', "        dest_path[root_len] = L'\\\\';", '        root_len++;', '    wcscpy(dest_path+root_len, rest);'], 'added_lines': ['static int', '        return wcscpy_s(dest_path, MAX_PATH, rest);', '    if (wcscpy_s(dest_path, MAX_PATH, root)) {', '        return -1;', '    }', '    if (dest_path[0] && wcscat_s(dest_path, MAX_PATH, L"\\\\")) {', '        return -1;', '', '    return wcscat_s(dest_path, MAX_PATH, rest);']}
description: Python Software Foundation CPython version From 3.2 until 3.6.4 on Windows contains a Buffer Overflow vulnerability in os.symlink() function on Windows that can result in Arbitrary code execution, likely escalation of privilege. This attack appears to be exploitable via a python script that creates a symlink with an attacker controlled name or location. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in 3.7.0 and 3.6.5.

code_evidence: When rest is absolute, wcscpy copies rest into dest_path with no bound on the copied length, so a long attacker-controlled path overflows the fixed-size destination.

Otherwise root_len is computed with wcslen, root is copied unbounded by wcscpy, a separator is written at dest_path[root_len], and rest is appended at dest_path+root_len via wcscpy, again without any size check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the function performs buffer copy operations (wcscpy) of input strings into a destination without checking input size against buffer capacity, producing a classic out-of-bounds write. It is a buffer-copy overflow, not merely an out-of-bounds read or an integer size-calculation error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded wcscpy copies of root and rest (and the manual separator write) into a fixed-size dest_path with no verification that the combined length fits. Trigger: an os.symlink call with an attacker-controlled long name or location. Consequence: writes past the end of the buffer, enabling memory corruption and potential arbitrary code execution.

description: Integer overflow in the php_raw_url_encode function in ext/standard/url.c in PHP before 5.5.34, 5.6.x before 5.6.20, and 7.x before 7.0.5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a long string to the rawurlencode function. NOTE: the vendor says "Not sure if this qualifies as security issue (probably not).

code_evidence: The loop index y is declared as a signed int (line 3) but indexes the output buffer str, which is allocated for 3*len bytes (line 5). Within the loop each character may expand to three output bytes via the '%' and hex writes (lines 13-15), so y advances up to 3 per input byte. With a long input, y can exceed the range representable by int, causing signed overflow before or during the writes and the final str[y]='\0' (line 24) and *new_length=y (line 26).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe index arithmetic is a numeric calculation/conversion error leading to overflow, which fits the CWE-189 numeric errors category. It is not primarily a buffer-size miscalculation itself; the flaw is the incorrectly typed index that overflows during encoding.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the output index y is a signed int, while the encoded output can be up to three times the input length. Trigger: passing a very long string to rawurlencode so that the accumulated index exceeds INT_MAX. Consequence: signed integer overflow yields undefined behavior and an out-of-bounds write/crash (denial of service); the patch widens x and y to size_t.

commit_msg:
media: fix airspy usb probe error path

Fix a memory leak on probe error of the airspy usb device driver.

The problem is triggered when more than 64 usb devices register with
v4l2 of type VFL_TYPE_SDR or VFL_TYPE_SUBDEV.

The memory leak is caused by the probe function of the airspy driver
mishandeling errors and not freeing the corresponding control structures
when an error occours registering the device to v4l2 core.

A badusb device can emulate 64 of these devices, and then through
continual emulated connect/disconnect of the 65th device, cause the
kernel to run out of RAM and crash the kernel, thus causing a local DOS
vulnerability.

Fixes CVE-2016-5400

Signed-off-by: James Patrick-Evans <james@jmp-e.com>
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 3.17+
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function's error path mishandles a memory leak by skipping v4l2_ctrl_handler_free on video_register_device failure, which is CWE-404/401 (resource leak), not an out-of-bounds buffer operation; no out-of-bounds read/write exists in the function.

code_evidence: At line 15 the guard is only obj_renumber.count(og)==0, and when the object maps to an object stream (line 17) the code recurses via enqueueObject at line 20 before any renumber entry is recorded. The only assignment obj_renumber[og] happens at line 25 in the else branch, so a self-referential object stream re-enters with the same og and count() stays 0.
The recursive call at line 20 is the loop body; without a marker written before recursion, the exit condition at line 15 is never satisfied for a cyclic object-stream mapping.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's recursion has an exit condition (obj_renumber.count(og)==0) that cannot be reached for self-referential object streams, matching CWE-835's infinite loop. This is recursion-driven nontermination, not a fixed iteration bound issue, but the unreachable-exit-condition pattern is the same.

evidence_lines.code:
object_queue.push_back(object);
obj_renumber[og] = next_objid++;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recursion at line 20 is performed before obj_renumber[og] is set, so cycles in object_to_object_stream are not detected. Trigger: a crafted PDF where an object stream references itself causes enqueueObject to recurse with the same ObjGen indefinitely. Supported consequence: unbounded recursion/CPU consumption, a DoS, rather than memory corruption.

avcodec/dxtory: fix src size checks

Fixes integer overflow
Fixes out of array read
Fixes: d104661bb59b202df7671fb19a00ca6c-asan_heap-oob_d6429d_5066_cov_1729501105_dxtory_mic.avi
Found-by: Mateusz "j00ru" Jurczyk and Gynvael Coldwind

description: A vulnerability was found in FFmpeg 2.0. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file libavcodec/dxtroy.c. The manipulation leads to integer coercion error. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

code_evidence: The size check computes avctx->width * avctx->height * 18 / 16 entirely in int arithmetic; the multiplication of width and height (and by 18) can exceed INT_MAX before the comparison, producing a wrapped/truncated value used as the required-size threshold.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is an incorrect numeric conversion/overflow in the size computation, matching CWE-681 (incorrect conversion between numeric types) as the arithmetic result is truncated rather than widened. The consequence is the downstream out-of-bounds read, but the primary weakness is the flawed integer size check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the required-size expression is evaluated as 32-bit int, so large width/height cause signed overflow and an incorrect (possibly negative or small) threshold. Trigger: a crafted packet with large dimensions passes the check despite being shorter than the loop's actual 18-byte-per-4x4-block consumption, leading to out-of-array reads in the AV_COPY32/src indexing.

A kernel crash occurrs when defragmented packet is fragmented
in ip_do_fragment().
In defragment routine, skb_orphan() is called and
skb->ip_defrag_offset is set. but skb->sk and
skb->ip_defrag_offset are same union member. so that

commit_msg:
Don't create our own temporary mount point for pivot_root

An attacker could pre-create /tmp/.bubblewrap-$UID and make it a
non-directory, non-symlink (in which case mounting our tmpfs would fail,
causing denial of service), or make it a symlink under their control
(potentially allowing bad things if the protected_symlinks sysctl is
not enabled).

Instead, temporarily mount the tmpfs on a directory that we are sure
exists and is not attacker-controlled. /tmp (the directory itself, not
a subdirectory) will do.

Fixes: #304
Bug-Debian: https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=923557
Signed-off-by: Simon McVittie <smcv@debian.org>

Closes: #305
Approved by: cgwalters
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  cleanup_free char *base_path = NULL;', '     We first try in /run, and if that fails, try in /tmp. */', '  base_path = xasprintf ("/run/user/%d/.bubblewrap", real_uid);', '  if (ensure_dir (base_path, 0755))', '    {', '      free (base_path);', '      base_path = xasprintf ("/tmp/.bubblewrap-%d", real_uid);', '      if (ensure_dir (base_path, 0755))', '        die_with_error ("Creating root mountpoint failed");', '    }', '   * dir if the user requested to bind mount something over / */'], 'added_lines': ['  const char *base_path = NULL;', "   * Because we use pivot_root, it won't appear to be mounted from", '   * the perspective of the sandboxed process, so we can use anywhere', '   * that is sure to exist, that is sure to not be a symlink controlled', "   * by someone malicious, and that we won't immediately need to", '   * access ourselves. */', '  base_path = "/tmp";', '   * dir if the user requested to bind mount something over / (or', '   * over /tmp, now that we use that for base_path). */']}
description: bubblewrap.c in Bubblewrap before 0.3.3 misuses temporary directories in /tmp as a mount point. In some particular configurations (related to XDG_RUNTIME_DIR), a local attacker may abuse this flaw to prevent other users from executing bubblewrap or potentially execute code.

code_evidence: The code builds a mount-point path from the process's real_uid via xasprintf("/tmp/.bubblewrap-%d", real_uid) and only checks it with ensure_dir(), which does not verify that the existing path is a directory and not a symlink.
The resulting base_path is then handed directly to mount("tmpfs", base_path, ...) and chdir(base_path); there is no stat/lstat or ownership/type check on the path before use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes a path derived from environment/attacker-controlled state and fails to validate required properties (existence as a real, non-symlink directory) before mounting/chdir, matching CWE-20's improper input validation. It is not a mere transformation/filtering issue; the missing safety check is the defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the attacker-influenced /tmp path is trusted without validating its type or ownership. Trigger: a local attacker pre-creates /tmp/.bubblewrap-$UID as a non-directory (mount fails, DoS) or as a symlink under their control (redirecting the mount/chdir). Consequence: denial of service against bubblewrap and potentially unauthorized file/namespace manipulation.

Whenever a generated column is used, assume that all columns are used.

Also set the high-order', '  ** bit if the column is a generated column, as that adds dependencies', '  ** that are difficult to track, so we assume that all columns are used.', '    assert( pExpr->y.pTab!=0 );', '    if( pExpr->y.pTab->tabFlags & TF_HasGenerated ){', '      Column *pCol = pExpr->y.pTab->aCol + pExpr->iColumn;', '      if( pCol->colFlags & COLFLAG_GENERATED ) n = BMS-1;', '    }']}
description: lookupName in resolve.c in SQLite 3.30.1 omits bits from the colUsed bitmask in the case of a generated column, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact.

code_evidence: The colUsed bitmask is updated by computing n = pExpr->iColumn, clamping n to BMS-1 only when n>=BMS, then OR-ing a single bit ((Bitmask)1)<<n into pMatch->colUsed. There is no handling for generated columns: if the referenced column is a generated column, only its own bit is set, omitting the bits for the columns the generated expression depends on.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reduces a column index to a single bit position, clamping values at BMS-1 and discarding information about generated-column dependencies; this is an incorrect conversion/truncation of column-number data into the bitmask, matching CWE-681.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the index-covering optimization derives colUsed from the single referenced column index, converting/truncating the column number to a bit position without accounting for generated-column dependencies. Trigger: a query references a generated column in a table whose generated expression depends on other columns. Consequence: the colUsed mask omits dependency bits, so a covering-index decision can be wrong and yield an incorrect result or denial of service.

commit_msg:
net: vmxnet: use g_new for pkt initialisation

When network transport abstraction layer initialises pkt, the maximum
fragmentation count is not checked. This could lead to an integer
overflow causing a NULL pointer dereference. Replace g_malloc() with
g_new() to catch the multiplication overflow.

Reported-by: Li Qiang <liqiang6-s@360.cn>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Acked-by: Dmitry Fleytman <dmitry@daynix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    p->vec = g_malloc((sizeof *p->vec) *', '        (max_frags + NET_TX_PKT_PL_START_FRAG));', '    p->raw = g_malloc((sizeof *p->raw) * max_frags);'], 'added_lines': ['    p->vec = g_new(struct iovec, max_frags + NET_TX_PKT_PL_START_FRAG);', '    p->raw = g_new(struct iovec, max_frags);']}
description: Integer overflow in the net_tx_pkt_init function in hw/net/net_tx_pkt.c in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (QEMU process crash) via the maximum fragmentation count, which triggers an unchecked multiplication and NULL pointer dereference.

code_evidence: Allocation sizes are computed as (sizeof *p->vec) * (max_frags + NET_TX_PKT_PL_START_FRAG) and (sizeof *p->raw) * max_frags, where max_frags is an attacker-influenced uint32_t count. The multiplications are performed without any overflow check or upper bound on max_frags before being passed to g_malloc.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is precisely an integer overflow/wraparound in a size computation used for memory allocation (CWE-190), not a generic NULL dereference: the NULL dereference is only the downstream consequence of the wrapped size.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unchecked multiplication of an element size by the guest-controlled max_frags count. Trigger: supplying a sufficiently large fragmentation count makes the product wrap to a small value, so g_malloc returns an undersized (or NULL) buffer; subsequent iovec writes and packet handling then dereference or overrun it, causing a QEMU crash.

commit_msg:
UDP IPv6 packets auto flowlabels are using a 32bit secret
(static u32 hashrnd in net/core/flow_dissector.c) and
apply jhash() over fields known by the receivers.

Attackers can easily infer the 32bit secret and use this information
to identify a device and/or user, since this 32bit secret is only
set at boot time.

Really, using jhash() to generate cookies sent on the wire
is a serious security concern.

Trying to change the rol32(hash, 16) in ip6_make_flowlabel() would be
a dead end. Trying to periodically change the secret (like in sch_sfq.c)
could change paths taken in the network for long lived flows.

Let's switch to siphash, as we did in commit df453700e8d8
("inet: switch IP ID generator to siphash")

Using a cryptographically strong pseudo random function will solve this
privacy issue and more generally remove other weak points in the stack.

Packet schedulers using skb_get_hash_perturb() benefit from this change.

Fixes: b56774163f99 ("ipv6: Enable auto flow labels by default")
Fixes: 42240901f7c4 ("ipv6: Implement different admin modes for automatic flow labels")
Fixes: 67800f9b1f4e ("ipv6: Call skb_get_hash_flowi6 to get skb->hash in ip6_make_flowlabel")
Fixes: cb1ce2ef387b ("ipv6: Implement automatic flow label generation on transmit")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reported-by: Jonathan Berger <jonathann1@walla.com>
Reported-by: Amit Klein <aksecurity@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Benny Pinkas <benny@pinkas.net>
Cc: Tom Herbert <tom@herbertland.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\thash = ___skb_get_hash(skb, &keys, hashrnd);'], 'added_lines': ['\thash = ___skb_get_hash(skb, &keys, &hashrnd);']}
description: The flow_dissector feature in the Linux kernel 4.3 through 5.x before 5.3.10 has a device tracking vulnerability, aka CID-55667441c84f. This occurs because the auto flowlabel of a UDP IPv6 packet relies on a 32-bit hashrnd value as a secret, and because jhash (instead of siphash) is used. The hashrnd value remains the same starting from boot time, and can be inferred by an attacker. This affects net/core/flow_dissector.c and related code.

code_evidence: Line 5 initializes the flow-hash secret via __flow_hash_secret_init(). Line 6 passes the global 'hashrnd' into ___skb_get_hash to derive the packet hash. Line 7 stores that hash as the software hash on the skb, which feeds auto IPv6 flowlabel generation and schedulers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function consumes a long-lived, low-entropy secret to produce a value exposed on the wire, matching CWE-330's use of insufficiently random values in a security context. The weakness is the weak/predictable secret behind the hash, not merely a hash collision (CWE-328).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the packet hash that becomes the wire-visible flowlabel is derived from a 32-bit secret 'hashrnd' set once at boot and hashed with jhash over receiver-known fields. Trigger: an attacker observes flowlabels and infers the fixed secret. Consequence: device/user tracking via predictable flowlabels; the hash is not unpredictable to observers.

description: In FreeRDP less than or equal to 2.0.0, there is an out-of-bound read in ntlm_read_NegotiateMessage. This has been fixed in 2.1.0.

code_evidence: After the header and message-type checks, line 21 calls Stream_Read_UINT32(s, message->NegotiateFlags) to read 4 bytes without first verifying that the stream has 4 bytes remaining; the patch adds that guard immediately before this line.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe operation is a read past the end of the stream's backing buffer, not a write. The missing Stream_GetRemainingLength(s) < 4 constraint is the direct cause, and the patch adds exactly this bound check before the read.

evidence_lines.code: Stream_Read_UINT32(s, message->NegotiateFlags);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function consumes a 4-byte NegotiateFlags field from a caller-supplied SecBuffer with no remaining-length check. Trigger: a truncated or short NegotiateMessage that passes the header and message-type checks but has fewer than 4 bytes left. Consequence: Stream_Read_UINT32 reads past the end of the intended buffer, producing an out-of-bounds read of attacker-influenced length.

commit_msg:
Decoder: Fix stack underflow in CAVLC 4x4 parse functions

Bug: 26399350
Change-Id: Id768751672a7b093ab6e53d4fc0b3188d470920e
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    WORD16 i2_level_arr[16];'], 'added_lines': ['    // To avoid error check at 4x4 level, allocating for 3 extra levels(16+3)', '    // since u4_trailing_ones can at the max be 3. This will be required when', '    // u4_total_coeff is less than u4_trailing_ones', '    WORD16 ai2_level_arr[19];//', '    WORD16 *i2_level_arr = &ai2_level_arr[3];']}
description: Multiple stack-based buffer underflows in decoder/ih264d_parse_cavlc.c in mediaserver in Android 6.x before 2016-04-01 allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted media file, aka internal bug 26399350.

code_evidence: Line 11 declares a 16-element level array; line 18 sets i = u4_total_coeff - 1, then lines 27-28 write trailing-one levels into i2_level_arr[i--] for each of u4_trailing_ones iterations. If u4_total_coeff < u4_trailing_ones, i starts below zero and this loop writes to negative indices, i.e. before the array start.

Later, lines 139-142 read i2_level_arr[k--] for k down to 0 and copy into pi2_coeff_data, so the earlier out-of-bounds writes also propagate into coefficient data; line 121 computes u4_scan_pos from u4_total_coeff + u4_total_zeroes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes outside the bounds of a fixed-size stack buffer due to a missing count constraint, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation. The patch enlarging the array to 19 with a +3 offset confirms the underflow; this is a buffer-bounds error rather than, e.g., an integer overflow or use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 4x4 level array is sized 16 with no guard ensuring u4_total_coeff >= u4_trailing_ones. When a crafted bitstream yields more trailing ones than total coefficients, the decrementing index in lines 27-28 goes negative and writes before the stack buffer. Trigger: malformed CAVLC input; consequence: stack-based memory corruption, potentially code execution or denial of service.

commit_msg:
memory: fix return value handing of guest_remove_page()

Despite the description in mm.h, guest_remove_page() previously returned 0 for
paging errors.

Switch guest_remove_page() to having regular 0/-error semantics, and propagate
the return values from clear_mmio_p2m_entry() and mem_sharing_unshare_page()
to the callers (although decrease_reservation() is the only caller which
currently cares).

This is part of XSA-222.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            if ( !guest_remove_page(a->domain, gmfn + j) )'], 'added_lines': ['            if ( guest_remove_page(a->domain, gmfn + j) )']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate memory allocations during certain P2M operations, which allows guest OS users to obtain privileged host OS access, aka XSA-222.

code_evidence: Line 16 copies a guest-supplied gmfn from the extent list into a kernel variable; failure of the copy aborts via goto out (line 17).
Lines 32-34 iterate over the extent and previously treated guest_remove_page() success (0) as failure, aborting the loop with goto out when the page was actually removed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to correctly validate/interpret the return value of guest_remove_page() as an error indicator, so the guest-controlled operation proceeds on a wrong assumption about the result. This improper validation of a derived result supports CWE-20; it is not a bounds or type-confusion issue.

evidence_lines.code:
if ( unlikely(__copy_from_guest_offset(&gmfn, a->extent_list, i, 1)) )
goto out;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The guest controls extent_list entries and extent_order. Because guest_remove_page()'s 0-on-success return was misinterpreted by the negated check, a successful removal aborted decrease_reservation() early, leaving the operation partially performed and the guest's reservation accounting inconsistent. The fix inverts the condition to test for a nonzero error.

commit_msg: dns: fix crash issue
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['int dns_add_rr_nested_memcpy(struct dns_rr_nested *rr_nested, void *data, int data_len)'], 'added_lines': ['int dns_add_rr_nested_memcpy(struct dns_rr_nested *rr_nested, const void *data, int data_len)']}
description: SmartDNS through 41 before 56d0332 allows an out-of-bounds write because of a stack-based buffer overflow in the _dns_encode_domain function in the dns.c file, via a crafted DNS request.

code_evidence: Lines 3-5 only reject NULL pointers and non-positive lengths; data_len is a caller-supplied signed int with no upper bound tied to the actual size of data.
Lines 6-8 check remaining space with _dns_left_len(&rr_nested->context) < data_len, then line 9 performs memcpy(rr_nested->context.ptr, data, data_len) and line 10 advances ptr by data_len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function copies data_len bytes into rr_nested->context.ptr after only a length-accounting check, so a mismatch between accounted and actual buffer size yields a write past the intended buffer, matching CWE-787. A mere read overflow (CWE-125) is not supported because memcpy writes into the destination.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The guard compares data_len against the remaining length returned by _dns_left_len, but if that remaining-length computation or the context's declared size is inconsistent with the actual destination buffer, the check passes while memcpy still copies data_len bytes past the destination end. The trigger is a caller passing a data_len larger than the true destination allocation; the consequence is a heap/stack out-of-bounds write corrupting adjacent memory, potentially crashing or allowing code execution.

commit_msg: core(persistence): added null ptr checks
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (!ptr)', '            CV_PARSE_ERROR_CPP("Invalid input");', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in OpenCV before 4.1.1. There is a NULL pointer dereference in the function cv::XMLParser::parse at modules/core/src/persistence.cpp.

code_evidence: skipSpaces accepts a raw char* ptr and immediately enters an infinite loop that dereferences *ptr at line 5 without any prior null validation.

After fs->gets() returns, the code checks !ptr at line 22, showing the author is aware the buffer accessor can yield NULL; the same defensive check is absent for the incoming ptr parameter before the first dereference.

The fix adds exactly such a check, confirming the target. A related out-of-bounds issue is not indicated here.

If a malformed or truncated persistence stream causes the caller to pass an invalid/NULL buffer pointer, the dereference crashes, yielding a denial of service. The root cause is a missing null check on the input pointer; the crash is the consequence.

commit_msg:
xt_compat_match/target_from_user doesn't check that zeroing the area
to start of next rule won't write past end of allocated ruleset blob.

Remove this code and zero the entire blob beforehand.

Reported-by: syzbot+cfc0247ac173f597aaaa@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Reported-by: Andy Nguyen <theflow@google.com>
Fixes: 9fa492cdc160c ("[NETFILTER]: x_tables: simplify compat API")
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tmemset(newinfo->entries, 0, size);']}
description: A heap out-of-bounds write affecting Linux since v2.6.19-rc1 was discovered in net/netfilter/x_tables.c. This allows an attacker to gain privileges or cause a DoS (via heap memory corruption) through user name space

code_evidence: newinfo is allocated with xt_alloc_table_info(size) where size derives from user-controlled compatr->size and is later adjusted by check_compat_entry_size_and_hooks; the allocated entries region is left uninitialized.

entry1 = newinfo->entries and pos = entry1 set the write cursor to the start of the allocated blob; compat_copy_entry_from_user then copies each compat entry into newinfo using pos and size, advancing the cursor within the blob.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function writes translated entries through pos into newinfo->entries without ensuring the writes stay within the allocated buffer, producing an out-of-bounds write. This is a direct bounds/overflow issue in the write target, not merely an information disclosure or use-after-free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the destination entries region is not zeroed and the copy cursor pos is not bounded against the actual allocated end when translating entries, so a crafted compat ruleset can cause compat_copy_entry_from_user to write past the allocated table blob. Trigger: user-supplied compatr->size/entry layout through the compat setsockopt path. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, memory corruption and possible privilege escalation or DoS.

commit_msg:
patch 8.2.4009: reading one byte beyond the end of the line

Problem:    Reading one byte beyond the end of the line.
Solution:   Check for NUL byte first.
description: vim is vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read

code_evidence: At line 147 the condition `p == eap->cmd && p[0] == p[1] && (*p == '+' || *p == '-')` dereferences p[1] without first verifying that p[0] is not NUL. When eap->cmd points at a one-character command line whose terminator is NUL, p[0] is NUL and p[1] reads one byte beyond the allocated string. The fix inserts `p[0] != NUL` before comparing p[0] and p[1].
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory past the end of the command-line buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not a write or integer issue; the defect is an unchecked read of p[1] before the NUL guard.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the increment/decrement detection reads p[1] before checking whether p[0] is the NUL terminator. Trigger: an ex command line whose command begins with a single character followed by NUL (e.g., '+'). Consequence: a one-byte out-of-bounds read of the buffer, which can crash or expose adjacent memory.

std::make_shared<std::vector<uint8_t>>(begin, end) constructs a copy over the range [begin, end); when len exceeds the remaining bytes, end is past data.end(), so the copy reads out of bounds before GapData::Parse is reached.

commit_msg: [codec,nsc] fix input length validation
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tBYTE* rle = context->Planes;', '\t\t\tif (!nsc_rle_decode(rle, context->priv->PlaneBuffers[i],'], 'added_lines': ['\tconst BYTE* rle = context->Planes;', '\tsize_t rleSize = context->PlanesSize;', '', '\t\tif (rleSize < planeSize)', '\t\t\treturn FALSE;', '\t\t\tif (!nsc_rle_decode(rle, rleSize, context->priv->PlaneBuffers[i],', '\t\t\t\treturn FALSE;', '', '\t\t\tif (rleSize < originalSize)']}
description: FreeRDP is a free implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), released under the Apache license. Affected versions are subject to an Out-Of-Bounds Read in the `nsc_rle_decompress_data` function. The Out-Of-Bounds Read occurs because it processes `context->Planes` without  checking if it contains data of sufficient length. Should an attacker be able to leverage this vulnerability they may be able to cause a crash. This issue has been addressed in versions 2.11.0 and 3.0.0-beta3. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: rle points at context->Planes with no size captured; only WINPR_ASSERT(rle) checks non-nullness, not buffer length.
The loop iterates four planes using attacker-influenced planeSize/originalSize; the rle cursor is advanced by planeSize at line 29, so reads trust these counts without validating remaining data.

In the planeSize<originalSize branch, nsc_rle_decode reads from rle with no bound on rle relative to PlaneBuffersLength; in the else branch, CopyMemory reads originalSize bytes from rle without confirming the source holds that many bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read that can extend beyond the intended source buffer, matching CWE-125's definition of reading past the end of a buffer. The weakness is bounded read, not a write overflow (CWE-787) or integer issue, since the missing constraint is on source length before decoding/copying.

evidence_lines.code:
BYTE* rle = context->Planes;
WINPR_ASSERT(rle);

commit_msg:
perf: Fix race in swevent hash

There's a race on CPU unplug where we free the swevent hash array
while it can still have events on. This will result in a
use-after-free which is BAD.

Simply do not free the hash array on unplug. This leaves the thing
around and no use-after-free takes place.

When the last swevent dies, we do a for_each_possible_cpu() iteration
anyway to clean these up, at which time we'll free it, so no leakage
will occur.

Reported-by: Sasha Levin <sasha.levin@oracle.com>
Tested-by: Sasha Levin <sasha.levin@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@redhat.com>
Cc: Frederic Weisbecker <fweisbec@gmail.com>
Cc: Jiri Olsa <jolsa@redhat.com>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Stephane Eranian <eranian@google.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Vince Weaver <vincent.weaver@maine.edu>
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': []}
description: Race condition in kernel/events/core.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by leveraging incorrect handling of an swevent data structure during a CPU unplug operation.

code_evidence: mutex_lock(&swhash->hlist_mutex) guards the check of swevent_hlist_deref(swhash) and the cpu_online(cpu) test, then increments hlist_refcount under the lock.

The lock is released at exit via mutex_unlock, so the reference count and hash pointer are only synchronized within this mutex scope; CPU unplug teardown path is not serialized by the same lock, so the check-then-use on the hash array can race with free.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits: concurrent code sequences access the shared swevent hash/hlist_refcount without exclusive synchronization across the unplug path, creating a timing window where the resource is freed while in use, i.e., a race condition.

evidence_lines.code:
exit:
mutex_unlock(&swhash->hlist_mutex);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the swevent hash lifetime is managed by hlist_refcount and the hash pointer, but CPU unplug can free the hash array while this function holds a reference or is about to dereference it, because the unplug path is not serialized against the hlist_mutex critical section. Trigger: concurrent CPU unplug with swevent creation. Consequence: use-after-free of the swevent hash, enabling privilege escalation or DoS.

commit_msg:
gvariant-serialiser: Check offset table entry size is minimal

The entries in an offset table (which is used for variable sized arrays
and tuples containing variable sized members) are sized so that they can
address every byte in the overall variant.

The specification requires that for a variant to be in normal form, its
offset table entries must be the minimum width such that they can
address every byte in the variant.

That minimality requirement was not checked in
`g_variant_is_normal_form()`, leading to two different byte arrays being
interpreted as the normal form of a given variant tree. That kind of
confusion could potentially be exploited, and is certainly a bug.

Fix it by adding the necessary checks on offset table entry width, and
unit tests.

Spotted by William Manley.

Signed-off-by: Philip Withnall <pwithnall@endlessos.org>

Fixes: #2794
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  if (out.length > 0 && gvs_calculate_total_size (last_end, out.length) != value.size)', '    return out;  /* offset size not minimal */', '']}
description: A flaw was found in GLib. GVariant deserialization fails to validate that the input conforms to the expected format, leading to denial of service.

code_evidence: gvs_get_offset_size derives offset_size from value.size, then the last offset is read and validated only against last_end <= value.size and offsets_array_size % offset_size == 0. out.length is computed as offsets_array_size / out.offset_size and is_normal is set TRUE without verifying that offset_size is the minimal width needed to address the data. No check ties the chosen offset width back to the actual data size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing minimality constraint lets attacker-supplied input drive parsing into an inconsistent state that is accepted as normal, and the described impact is deserialization DoS, matching CWE-400's uncontrolled resource/availability scope. It is a validation gap rather than out-of-bounds access (CWE-125).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the frame-offset parser accepts offset-table entries wider than the minimum required by the variant size, so malformed input is declared normal. Trigger: a crafted serialized GVariant whose offset table uses a non-minimal width. Consequence: multiple distinct byte arrays map to the same normal-form tree, enabling ambiguity and denial-of-service via deserialization confusion.

Security: more cmsgpack fixes by @soloestoy.

@soloestoy sent me this additional fixes, after searching for similar

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    luaL_checkstack(L, 3, "in function mp_encode_lua_table_as_map");']}
description: Memory Corruption was discovered in the cmsgpack library in the Lua subsystem in Redis before 3.2.12, 4.x before 4.0.10, and 5.x before 5.0 RC2 because of stack-based buffer overflows.

code_evidence: The function iterates a Lua table via lua_next in two passes without reserving Lua stack slots; each iteration pushes values (lua_next pushes key/value, plus lua_pushvalue(-2)), and the nested mp_encode_lua_type calls push further values. No luaL_checkstack guards these pushes before the second traversal performs the encoding.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked stack pushes in the iteration loop write past the intended Lua stack buffer, matching CWE-787's out-of-bounds write. It is not merely a logic error; the missing luaL_checkstack constraint directly permits writes beyond the stack boundary, consistent with the described stack-based buffer overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is unbounded Lua stack growth during table encoding: each lua_next iteration and nested encode pushes values without ensuring stack space. Trigger is a deeply nested or large Lua table passed to cmsgpack encoding; the stack overflows, corrupting adjacent memory. Consequence is memory corruption potentially leading to code execution or crash.

commit_msg:
Disallow namespace nodes in XPointer ranges

Namespace nodes must be copied to avoid use-after-free errors.
But they don't necessarily have a physical representation in a
document, so simply disallow them in XPointer ranges.

Found with afl-fuzz.

Fixes CVE-2016-4658.

description: xpointer.c in libxml2 before 2.9.5 (as used in Apple iOS before 10, OS X before 10.12, tvOS before 10, and watchOS before 3, and other products) does not forbid namespace nodes in XPointer ranges, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (use-after-free and memory corruption) via a crafted XML document.

code_evidence: The first switch accepts XPATH_POINT, XPATH_RANGE and XPATH_NODESET ends, but for POINT/RANGE it only breaks, so no check rejects namespace node types carried in end->user / end->user2.
The second switch copies end->user (or end->user2) directly into ret->user2 and end->index into ret->index2 without validating that the node type has a physical document representation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing node-type constraint lets an attacker-controlled endpoint reach memory operations that act outside valid buffer boundaries, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory operation class. The concrete consequence (use-after-free) is a downstream effect; the code-level defect is the unvalidated acceptance of the node reference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function accepts an XPointer end object referencing a namespace node and stores it unvalidated in the new range object. Namespace nodes have no physical buffer representation, so later range processing dereferences/copies memory based on an invalid node reference, triggering a use-after-free and memory corruption. The trigger is a crafted XML document that supplies a namespace node as the range endpoint.

commit_msg:
rpmsg: virtio: Fix possible double free in rpmsg_probe()

vch will be free in virtio_rpmsg_release_device() when
rpmsg_ns_register_device() fails. There is no need to call kfree() again.

Fix this by changing error path from free_vch to free_ctrldev.

Fixes: c486682ae1e2 ("rpmsg: virtio: Register the rpmsg_char device")
Signed-off-by: Hangyu Hua <hbh25y@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Arnaud Pouliquen <arnaud.pouliquen@foss.st.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220426060536.15594-2-hbh25y@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Mathieu Poirier <mathieu.poirier@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tgoto free_vch;', 'free_vch:', '\tkfree(vch);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t/* vch will be free in virtio_rpmsg_release_device() */', '\t\t\tgoto free_ctrldev;']}
description: rpmsg_probe in drivers/rpmsg/virtio_rpmsg_bus.c in the Linux kernel before 5.18.4 has a double free.

code_evidence: Line 71 sets rpdev_ns->dev.release = virtio_rpmsg_release_device, so the namespace device's release callback owns freeing the containing vch.
When rpmsg_ns_register_device fails at line 72, line 74 jumps to free_vch, which at line 83 calls kfree(vch) directly, freeing the same object that the release callback also frees.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees the same vch allocation twice through two paths (explicit kfree and the device release callback), matching CWE-415. This is a direct double free rather than a use-after-free, since the defect is the redundant free call itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path frees vch via kfree while the registered device release callback (virtio_rpmsg_release_device) also frees the vch allocation. Trigger: rpmsg_ns_register_device returns an error after the release callback is set, causing both the explicit kfree and the release-time free to act on the same address, resulting in a double free and possible memory corruption.

commit_msg:
USB: check usb_get_extra_descriptor for proper size

When reading an extra descriptor, we need to properly check the minimum
and maximum size allowed, to prevent from invalid data being sent by a
device.

Reported-by: Hui Peng <benquike@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Mathias Payer <mathias.payer@nebelwelt.net>
Co-developed-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Hui Peng <benquike@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mathias Payer <mathias.payer@nebelwelt.net>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tUSB_DT_OTG, (void **) &desc);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tUSB_DT_OTG, (void **) &desc, sizeof(*desc));']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.19.9. The USB subsystem mishandles size checks during the reading of an extra descriptor, related to __usb_get_extra_descriptor in drivers/usb/core/usb.c.

code_evidence: Line 8 declares desc as a pointer initialized to NULL, and lines 11-13 call __usb_get_extra_descriptor without passing the destination buffer size, so the callee cannot bound how many bytes it writes through the (void **)&desc output.

commit_msg:
Fix #196 and #199: Out of bound reads security issues

Check args before calling memmove() and memset() in remap_struct()
function to avoid out of bound reads which would possibly lead to
unknown code execution and/or sadf command crash.

Signed-off-by: Sebastien GODARD <sysstat@users.noreply.github.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t     act[p]->fsize, act[p]->msize);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t     act[p]->fsize, act[p]->msize, act[p]->msize);']}
description: An issue was discovered in sysstat 12.1.1. The remap_struct function in sa_common.c has an out-of-bounds read during a memmove call, as demonstrated by sadf.

code_evidence: The loop iterates j from 0 to nr_value*act[p]->nr2 and calls remap_struct on the buffer at offset j*act[p]->msize, passing act[p]->fsize as the source size and act[p]->msize as the destination size. The patched call adds a third size argument (act[p]->msize) so remap_struct can bound its memmove/memset; the pre-patch call lacked this bound, allowing remap_struct to read past the end of the fsize-sized record within the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the flaw is reading past the end of an intended buffer during the remap operation. It is not CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write) since the supported consequence is a read overrun from the memmove/memset source region.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: remap_struct is invoked without a destination-buffer bound, so its internal memmove/memset can read beyond the record boundary. Trigger: a crafted sa/sadf data file yielding fsize and msize values where the remap operation exceeds the copied record. Consequence: out-of-bounds read, potentially leading to information disclosure or a sadf crash.

commit_msg:
Because group consistency is non-atomic between parent (filedesc) and children
(inherited) events, it is possible for PERF_FORMAT_GROUP read() to try and sum
non-matching counter groups -- with non-sensical results.

Add group_generation to distinguish the case where a parent group removes and
adds an event and thus has the same number, but a different configuration of
events as inherited groups.

This became a problem when commit fa8c269353d5 ("perf/core: Invert
perf_read_group() loops") flipped the order of child_list and sibling_list.
Previously it would iterate the group (sibling_list) first, and for each
sibling traverse the child_list. In this order, only the group composition of
the parent is relevant. By flipping the order the group composition of the
child (inherited) events becomes an issue and the mis-match in group
composition becomes evident.

That said; even prior to this commit, while reading of a group that is not
equally inherited was not broken, it still made no sense.

(Ab)use ECHILD as error return to indicate issues with child process group
composition.

Fixes: fa8c269353d5 ("perf/core: Invert perf_read_group() loops")
Reported-by: Budimir Markovic <markovicbudimir@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20231018115654.GK33217@noisy.programming.kicks-ass.net
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstruct perf_event *sub;', '\treturn 0;'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct perf_event *sub, *parent;', '\t/*', '\t * Verify the grouping between the parent and child (inherited)', '\t * events is still in tact.', '\t *', '\t * Specifically:', '\t *  - leader->ctx->lock pins leader->sibling_list', '\t *  - parent->child_mutex pins parent->child_list', '\t *  - parent->ctx->mutex pins parent->sibling_list', '\t *', '\t * Because parent->ctx != leader->ctx (and child_list nests inside', '\t * ctx->mutex), group destruction is not atomic between children, also', '\t * see perf_event_release_kernel(). Additionally, parent can grow the', '\t * group.', '\t *', '\t * Therefore it is possible to have parent and child groups in a', '\t * different configuration and summing over such a beast makes no sense', '\t * what so ever.', '\t *', '\t * Reject this.', '\t */', '\tparent = leader->parent;', '\tif (parent &&', '\t    (parent->group_generation != leader->group_generation ||', '\t     parent->nr_siblings != leader->nr_siblings)) {', '\t\tret = -ECHILD;', '\t\tgoto unlock;', '\t}', 'unlock:', '\treturn ret;']}
description:
A heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Linux Kernel Performance Events (perf) component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

If perf_read_group() is called while an event's sibling_list is smaller than its child's sibling_list, it can increment or write to memory locations outside of the allocated buffer.

We recommend upgrading past commit 32671e3799ca2e4590773fd0e63aaa4229e50c06.

code_evidence: values[n++] advances the output index for the leader fields gated by read_format (count, ID, lost) without any bound check against the buffer size.

The sibling loop repeats values[n++] for every event in leader's sibling_list, so the number of writes depends on the runtime group size; a child group with a larger sibling_list than the parent causes n to exceed the allocated buffer.
The function unconditionally returns 0 after unlocking, providing no error path to reject mismatched parent/child group composition.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because values[n++] writes past the end of the intended output buffer when the event group size exceeds the buffer's capacity. This is a direct out-of-bounds write, not merely an integer or logic error; the mis-sized loop bound is the cause, the memory write is the supported consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
raw_spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ctx->lock, flags);
return 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the write count is driven by the leader's sibling_list while the buffer was sized for the caller's group; no validation that inherited child group composition matches the parent group exists. Trigger: reading a group whose child sibling_list is larger than the leader's, causing values[n++] to write past the allocated buffer. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write corrupting adjacent memory, enabling local privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
checkpath: fix CVE-2018-21269

This walks the directory path to the file we are going to manipulate to make
sure that when we create the file and change the ownership and permissions
we are working on the same file.
Also, all non-terminal symbolic links must be owned by root. This will
keep a non-root user from making a symbolic link as described in the
bug. If root creates the symbolic link, it is assumed to be trusted.

On non-linux platforms, we no longer follow non-terminal symbolic links
by default. If you need to do that, add the -s option on the checkpath
command line, but keep in mind that this is not secure.

This fixes #201.

description: checkpath in OpenRC through 0.42.1 might allow local users to take ownership of arbitrary files because a non-terminal path component can be a symlink.
