The main loop passes each user-supplied argv[optind] path directly to do_check without any symlink-aware constraint; writable mode calls is_writable on the same raw path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because access is performed on a filename without preventing it from resolving through a link to an unintended resource. This is link following, not merely a race condition (CWE-367), since the missing constraint is link resolution itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function hands attacker-influenced path arguments to do_check/is_writable with no option or parameter to reject non-terminal symlinks, so path resolution follows links. Trigger: a local user supplies a path whose non-terminal component is a symlink they control. Consequence: file ownership/permission changes operate on the link target, enabling takeover of arbitrary files.

commit_msg:
CVE-2021-43825

Response filter manager crash

Signed-off-by: Yan Avlasov <yavlasov@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (!filter_manager_.remoteComplete()) {'], 'added_lines': ['  if (!filter_manager_.remoteDecodeComplete()) {']}
description: Envoy is an open source edge and service proxy, designed for cloud-native applications. Sending a locally generated response must stop further processing of request or response data. Envoy tracks the amount of buffered request and response data and aborts the request if the amount of buffered data is over the limit by sending 413 or 500 responses. However when the buffer overflows while response is processed by the filter chain the operation may not be aborted correctly and result in accessing a freed memory block. If this happens Envoy will crash resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: encodeHeaders checks filter_manager_.remoteComplete() to decide whether the request is still in flight; when false it may mark the connection Closing and increments downstream_rq_response_before_rq_complete_ before continuing with response_encoder_->encodeHeaders at line 77.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The changed line controls whether encoding continues after the stream may be destroyed; the fix uses remoteDecodeComplete() to correctly detect that remote decode is unfinished. Continuing to reference the freed stream/filter manager is a use-after-free (CWE-416), not merely a logic error, because the supported consequence is access to freed memory.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the guard uses remoteComplete(), which can report completion based on a state that does not reflect that remote decode processing has actually finished, so response encoding proceeds while the filter manager/stream is still being torn down. Trigger: a locally generated response (e.g., buffer-overflow 413/500) is encoded while the request is incomplete; the guard fails to abort, and the stream object is freed. Consequence: subsequent filter-chain/response processing touches freed memory, causing a crash and denial of service.

commit b86dab054059b970111b5516ae548efaae5b3aae upstream.

When k_ascii is invoked several times in a row there is a potential for
signed integer overflow:

UBSAN: Undefined behaviour in drivers/tty/vt/keyboard.c:888:19 signed integer overflow:
10 * 1111111111 cannot be represented in type 'int'
CPU: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 5.6.11 #1
Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS Bochs 01/01/2011
Call Trace:
 <IRQ>
 __dump_stack lib/dump_stack.c:77 [inline]
 dump_stack+0xce/0x128 lib/dump_stack.c:118

While it can be worked around by using check_mul_overflow()/
check_add_overflow(), it is better to introduce a separate flag to
signal that number pad is being used to compose a symbol, and
change type of the accumulator from signed to unsigned, thus
avoiding undefined behavior when it overflows.

Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>

Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tint base;', '\tif (npadch == -1)', '\t\tnpadch = value;', '\telse', '\t\tnpadch = npadch * base + value;'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned int base;', '\tif (!npadch_active) {', '\t\tnpadch_value = 0;', '\t\tnpadch_active = true;', '\t}', '', '\tnpadch_value = npadch_value * base + value;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel 4.4 through 5.7.1. drivers/tty/vt/keyboard.c has an integer overflow if k_ascii is called several times in a row, aka CID-b86dab054059. NOTE: Members in the community argue that the integer overflow does not lead to a security issue in this case.

code_evidence: Line 3 declares the multiplier as a signed int, so the accumulation is performed in signed arithmetic.
Lines 12-15: when npadch is already set, the accumulator is multiplied by base (10 or 16) and incremented by value with no bound; repeated k_ascii calls grow npadch without any overflow check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function computes npadch * base + value in signed int arithmetic assuming the result stays larger, so a too-large value wraps or triggers undefined behavior, matching CWE-190. This is not merely an input-validation issue; the weakness is the unchecked arithmetic on the accumulator.

evidence_lines.code: int base;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the signed int accumulator npadch is repeatedly multiplied by base and added to value without checking representability. Trigger: invoking k_ascii several times in a row (e.g., holding the numpad ASCII composition keys) makes npadch exceed INT_MAX. Consequence: signed integer overflow, which is undefined behavior (observed via UBSAN) and can yield a wrapped negative value rather than the intended accumulated number.

commit_msg:
drivers: net: slip: fix NPD bug in sl_tx_timeout()

When a slip driver is detaching, the slip_close() will act to
cleanup necessary resources and sl->tty is set to NULL in
slip_close(). Meanwhile, the packet we transmit is blocked,
sl_tx_timeout() will be called. Although slip_close() and
sl_tx_timeout() use sl->lock to synchronize, we don`t judge
whether sl->tty equals to NULL in sl_tx_timeout() and the
null pointer dereference bug will happen.

   (Thread 1)                 |      (Thread 2)
                              | slip_close()
                              |   spin_lock_bh(&sl->lock)
                              |   ...
...                           |   sl->tty = NULL //(1)
sl_tx_timeout()               |   spin_unlock_bh(&sl->lock)
  spin_lock(&sl->lock);       |
  ...                         |   ...
  tty_chars_in_buffer(sl->tty)|
    if (tty->ops->..) //(2)   |
    ...                       |   synchronize_rcu()

We set NULL to sl->tty in position (1) and dereference sl->tty
in position (2).

This patch adds check in sl_tx_timeout(). If sl->tty equals to
NULL, sl_tx_timeout() will goto out.

Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Jiri Slaby <jirislaby@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220405132206.55291-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (!netif_running(dev))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!netif_running(dev) || !sl->tty)']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A NULL pointer dereference may occur while a slip driver is in progress to detach in sl_tx_timeout in drivers/net/slip/slip.c. This issue could allow an attacker to crash the system or leak internal kernel information.

code_evidence: The timeout path enters only when netif_queue_stopped(dev) is true and then guards solely on netif_running(dev); it does not verify that sl->tty is still non-NULL before proceeding.
After the guard, sl->tty is dereferenced via tty_chars_in_buffer(sl->tty) and again in clear_bit(...&sl->tty->flags), with no intervening NULL check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer it assumes valid (sl->tty) without a NULL check, matching CWE-476. This is distinct from a race-only use-after-free, since the defect is the missing NULL constraint on a pointer that is legitimately set to NULL during detach.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: slip_close() sets sl->tty to NULL while holding sl->lock, and a pending transmit timeout later runs sl_tx_timeout(); although both take sl->lock, the timeout path never revalidates sl->tty after acquiring it. With the device still netif_running but tty detached, the dereferences of sl->tty at the warning and clear_bit lines hit NULL, causing a crash/DoS.

description: An issue was discovered in JerryScript 1.0. There is a heap-based buffer over-read in the lit_read_code_unit_from_utf8 function via a RegExp("[\\u0020") payload, related to re_parse_char_class in parser/regexp/re-parser.c.

code_evidence: When ch is 'x', the branch calls lit_read_code_unit_from_hex(input_curr_p, 2, &code_unit) without first verifying that two hex digits remain before input_end_p; the same unchecked read occurs for 'u' with four digits.

The missing bounds checks before lit_read_code_unit_from_hex and lit_utf8_peek_next are the direct cause; this is a read overrun, not a write overflow (CWE-787).

Trigger: a truncated payload such as RegExp("[\u0020") drives the parser to read hex digits and peek past input_end_p. commit_msg:
Apply data offset for list-of-pointers at access time rather than ListReader creation time.

Baking this offset into `ptr` reduced ops needed at access time but made the interpretation of `ptr` inconsistent depending on what type of list was expected.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      ptr + upgradeBound<uint64_t>(index) * step / BITS_PER_BYTE), nestingLimit);'], 'added_lines': ['  // If the list elements have data sections we need to skip those. Note that for pointers to be', '  // present at all (which already must be true if we get here), then `structDataSize` must be a', "  // whole number of words, so we don't have to worry about unaligned reads here.", '  auto offset = structDataSize / BITS_PER_BYTE;', '      ptr + offset + upgradeBound<uint64_t>(index) * step / BITS_PER_BYTE), nestingLimit);']}
description: Cap'n Proto is a data interchange format and remote procedure call (RPC) system. Cap'n Proro prior to versions 0.7.1, 0.8.1, 0.9.2, and 0.10.3, as well as versions of Cap'n Proto's Rust implementation prior to 0.13.7, 0.14.11, and 0.15.2 are vulnerable to out-of-bounds read due to logic error handling list-of-list. This issue may lead someone to remotely segfault a peer by sending it a malicious message, if the victim performs certain actions on a list-of-pointer type. Exfiltration of memory is possible if the victim performs additional certain actions on a list-of-pointer type. To be vulnerable, an application must perform a specific sequence of actions, described in the GitHub Security Advisory. The bug is present in inlined code, therefore the fix will require rebuilding dependent applications. Cap'n Proto has C++ fixes available in versions 0.7.1, 0.8.1, 0.9.2, and 0.10.3. The `capnp` Rust crate has fixes available in versions 0.13.7, 0.14.11, and 0.15.2.

code_evidence: getPointerElement computes the pointer address as ptr + index*step/BITS_PER_BYTE without accounting for the list's structDataSize data-section offset. For list-of-pointer types whose elements carry a data section, this base is wrong, so the returned PointerReader points before the actual pointer element.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function derives an unchecked element address and reads a WirePointer through it; the missing offset causes reads outside the intended element buffer, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. It is a read-positioning logic error rather than a write overflow (CWE-787).

evidence_lines.code:
return PointerReader(segment, capTable, reinterpret_cast<const WirePointer*>(
ptr + upgradeBound<uint64_t>(index) * step / BITS_PER_BYTE), nestingLimit);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the element address omits the structDataSize offset, making ptr interpretation inconsistent for list-of-pointer elements with data sections. Trigger: a crafted message with a list-of-list/list-of-pointer type processed by this accessor. Consequence: the PointerReader reads a WirePointer from an unintended location, yielding out-of-bounds reads (crash or possible memory exfiltration).

description: In function lys_node_free() in libyang <= v1.0.225, it asserts that the value of node->module can't be NULL. But in some cases, node->module can be null, which triggers a reachable assertion (CWE-617).

code_evidence: retval is set to the calloc'd container (line 19) before read_yin_common() attaches module/parent metadata; if that call fails (line 23) control jumps to error.
The error label calls lys_node_free(retval, NULL, 0) with a NULL context argument; the surrounding parsing code obtains ctx from module->ctx (line 5).
The fix changes this call to lys_node_free(ctx, retval, NULL, 0), passing the explicitly required context for nodes whose module/context is not yet set.

It is not a memory-corruption issue; the defect is the reachable assertion and resulting abort.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path frees a partially initialized node without passing the required context, so lys_node_free() reaches its assertion that node->module is non-NULL. Trigger: any parse failure in read_yin_common(), lys_node_addchild(), or later subnode handling on a container lacking module assignment. Consequence: the assertion aborts the process, giving a reachable crash/DoS rather than a clean parse error.

commit_msg:
PR24689, string table corruption

The testcase in the PR had a e_shstrndx section of type SHT_GROUP.
hdr->contents were initialized by setup_group rather than being read
from the file, thus last byte was not zero and string dereference ran
off the end of the buffer.

	PR 24689
	* elfcode.h (elf_object_p): Check type of e_shstrndx section.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      if (i_ehdrp->e_shstrndx >= elf_numsections (abfd))'], 'added_lines': ['      if (i_ehdrp->e_shstrndx >= elf_numsections (abfd)', '\t  || i_shdrp[i_ehdrp->e_shstrndx].sh_type != SHT_STRTAB)']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.32. There is a heap-based buffer over-read in _bfd_doprnt in bfd.c because elf_object_p in elfcode.h mishandles an e_shstrndx section of type SHT_GROUP by omitting a trailing '\0' character.

code_evidence: At 182-191 the code checks only that e_shstrndx is within the section count; if it is in range it keeps the index, otherwise it resets to SHN_UNDEF. It never verifies that the referenced section is actually a string table (SHT_STRTAB).

At 223-232, when e_shstrndx is nonzero and e_shoff is nonzero, the section headers are processed via bfd_section_from_shdr and _bfd_elf_setup_sections using the unvalidated string-table index, so a section of a different type (e.g. SHT_GROUP initialized by setup_group without a trailing NUL) is treated as a string table.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The omitted SHT_STRTAB type check allows a string dereference to read past the end of a buffer, which is exactly CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). The fix adds sh_type != SHT_STRTAB to the sanity check, confirming the missing constraint rather than a write-side issue (CWE-787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: elf_object_p accepts an e_shstrndx pointing to a non-SHT_STRTAB section. Trigger: a crafted ELF whose e_shstrndx selects a SHT_GROUP section whose contents lack a terminating NUL. The section is later dereferenced as a string table, so a string read runs past the buffer, causing a heap-based out-of-bounds read (crash/info leak).

commit_msg:
Fix memory leak in xmlSchemaValidateStream

When ctxt->schema is NULL, xmlSchemaSAXPlug->xmlSchemaPreRun
alloc a new schema for ctxt->schema and set vctxt->xsiAssemble
to 1. Then xmlSchemaVStart->xmlSchemaPreRun initialize
vctxt->xsiAssemble to 0 again which cause the alloced schema
can not be freed anymore.

Found with libFuzzer.

Signed-off-by: Zhipeng Xie <xiezhipeng1@huawei.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    vctxt->xsiAssemble = 0;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: xmlSchemaPreRun in xmlschemas.c in libxml2 2.9.10 allows an xmlSchemaValidateStream memory leak.

code_evidence: Line 7 unconditionally resets vctxt->xsiAssemble to 0 at the start of xmlSchemaPreRun. When vctxt->schema is NULL (line 14), the function sets xsiAssemble to 1 (line 16) and allocates a new schema via xmlSchemaNewSchema (line 22), assigning ownership through pctxt->ownsConstructor = 1 (line 29).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function controls ownership/release of a heap-allocated schema through the xsiAssemble flag; resetting that flag causes the allocation to be untracked and never released, matching CWE-401's missing release of memory after effective lifetime. This is a resource-lifetime tracking defect, not an out-of-bounds or use-after-free weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: xmlSchemaPreRun overwrites the xsiAssemble flag that xmlSchemaSAXPlug set to 1 when it allocated ctxt->schema. A second xmlSchemaPreRun invocation resets the flag to 0 before the NULL-schema branch re-sets it, so the previously allocated schema is no longer marked for release. Trigger: validating a stream where the schema is plugged then pre-run again; consequence: the allocated schema is never freed, leaking memory (DoS/resource consumption).

is stored as an optional, and is cleared whenever a non-const pointer or
reference to a HeaderEntry is accessed. The cached value can be set with
refreshByteSize() which performs an iteration over the HeaderMap to sum
the size of each key and value in the HeaderMap.

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: In the is_device_private_entry branch, vmf->page is obtained from the swap entry via pfn_swap_entry_to_page(entry) at [25], then immediately dereferenced through vmf->page->pgmap->ops->migrate_to_ram(vmf) at [26] without taking a page reference or holding the PTL. The page (and its pgmap) can be concurrently freed by migration or memunmap_pages(), so the dereference of pgmap->ops uses freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the function dereferences a struct page and its pgmap after they may have been freed, matching reuse of freed memory. The fix confirms this by taking get_page() under the PTL before the callback.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no reference is held on the device-private page while calling migrate_to_ram(). Trigger: a concurrent migration or device unbind frees the page/pgmap between pfn_swap_entry_to_page() and the callback dereference. Consequence: use-after-free of the struct page and pgmap, leading to an invalid function pointer call and kernel crash.

description: Unicorn Engine v2.0.0-rc7 and below was discovered to contain a NULL pointer dereference via qemu_ram_free.

code_evidence: memory_map allocates a MemoryRegion with g_new, then calls memory_region_init_ram(uc, ram, size, perms), which may fail to populate ram->ram_block when mapping a large memory region. The only guard checks ram->addr == -1; the function then returns NULL without freeing ram, and downstream use of the partially initialized region (e.g. qemu_ram_free on close) can dereference the missing ram_block.

Consequence: a NULL pointer dereference (crash) when the incomplete MemoryRegion is later freed/used, plus a leaked ram allocation.

description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The implementation of `SparseTensorSliceDataset` has an undefined behavior: under certain condition it can be made to dereference a `nullptr` value. The 3 input arguments to `SparseTensorSliceDataset` represent a sparse tensor. However, there are some preconditions that these arguments must satisfy but these are not validated in the implementation. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Only indices is checked to be a matrix; values and dense_shape are checked for vector shape only after num_indices/num_values are computed via NumElements().
The empty-tensor check compares num_indices == num_values only when one is zero, but does not enforce values count equals indices rows or dense_shape length equals indices columns.
values vector check reports indices shape in its error, but more importantly no cross-shape constraint ties values length to indices dimension 0.
dense_shape vector check exists, but no constraint ties dense_shape length to indices dimension 1, and no check that dense_shape has at least one element.

The loop reads indices->matrix<int64_t>()(i, 0) and dim_size(0) assuming a valid 2-D indices matrix with a batch column; later TensorShape(dense_shape->vec<int64_t>()) assumes dense_shape has elements.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsupported consequence is a NULL pointer dereference from unvalidated tensor shapes reaching code that assumes valid dimensions. This matches CWE-476 as a crash/DoS, rather than an input validation weakness alone.

errors::InvalidArgument(
"Input values should be a vector but received shape ",

dense_shape->shape().DebugString()));

for (int64_t i = 0; i < indices->dim_size(0); ++i) {
int64_t next_batch_index = indices->matrix<int64_t>()(i, 0);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: preconditions relating indices, values, and dense_shape are not validated (matching dimensions, non-empty dense_shape). Trigger: a sparse-tensor argument set with inconsistent shapes or an empty dense_shape. The downstream SparseTensor::Create/loop then indexes using unvalidated dimensions, leading to out-of-bounds or nullptr dereference and a crash/DoS.

description: The AllowCrossRendererResourceLoad function in extensions/browser/url_request_util.cc in Google Chrome before 53.0.2785.89 on Windows and OS X and before 53.0.2785.92 on Linux does not properly use an extension's manifest.json web_accessible_resources field for restrictions on IFRAME elements, which makes it easier for remote attackers to conduct clickjacking attacks, and trick users into changing extension settings, via a crafted web site, a different vulnerability than CVE-2016-5162.

code_evidence: Lines 24-27 allow any frame resource type (including subframes/IFRAMEs) when not a guest, setting *allowed = true and returning before any web_accessible_resources check.
Lines 47-51 permit all loads whenever the extension has any web accessible resources, without verifying the specific resource_path was declared in manifest.json.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-254 (7PK - Security Features) covers improper access control/security feature enforcement. The code fails to enforce the manifest.json web_accessible_resources restriction for IFRAME navigations, which is an access-control weakness in an intended security feature.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function's access control for extension resources is too permissive: frame navigations are unconditionally allowed (lines 24-27), and resources are allowed if any web_accessible_resources exist rather than if the specific path is listed (lines 47-51). A crafted site can therefore navigate an IFRAME to a non-whitelisted extension page, enabling clickjacking and tricking users into changing extension settings.

commit_msg:
__vmx_handle_exit() uses vcpu->run->internal.ndata as an index for
an array access.  Since vcpu->run is (can be) mapped to a user address
space with a writer permission, the 'ndata' could be updated by the
user process at anytime (the user process can set it to outside the
bounds of the array).
So, it is not safe that __vmx_handle_exit() uses the 'ndata' that way.

Fixes: 1aa561b1a4c0 ("kvm: x86: Add "last CPU" to some KVM_EXIT information")
Signed-off-by: Reiji Watanabe <reijiw@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Jim Mattson <jmattson@google.com>
Message-Id: <20210413154739.490299-1-reijiw@google.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel in versions before 5.12. The value of internal.ndata, in the KVM API, is mapped to an array index, which can be updated by a user process at anytime which could lead to an out-of-bounds write. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data integrity and system availability.

code_evidence: Line 43 sets vcpu->run->internal.ndata = 3, then line 48 increments it and line 49 writes data[3]. Line 52 then indexes data using the user-writable vcpu->run->internal.ndata as the array index, incrementing it post-write.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an array write indexed by an attacker-controllable value lacking a bounds check, directly matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). This is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the operation is a store into data[].
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is using the user-mapped vcpu->run->internal.ndata value directly as an array index for data[] without bounding it. A user process sharing the KVM run page can modify ndata between the assignments, causing data[ndata++] to write outside the internal.data array, corrupting adjacent memory.

commit_msg: Check that `type` isn't an empty string.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            if (type.empty()) {', '                throw Error(kerInvalidXmpText, type);', '            }']}
description: Exiv2 is a command-line utility and C++ library for reading, writing, deleting, and modifying the metadata of image files. An out-of-bounds read was found in Exiv2 versions v0.27.4 and earlier. The out-of-bounds read is triggered when Exiv2 is used to read the metadata of a crafted image file. An attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability to cause a denial of service, if they can trick the victim into running Exiv2 on a crafted image file. The bug is fixed in version v0.27.5.

code_evidence: find_first_of(' ') returns npos when buf contains no space; type is then buf.substr(5, npos-5), which yields the remainder of the string and may be empty.
With type empty, type[0] and type[type.length()-1] index element 0 of an empty std::string, reading memory before/at an invalid position (undefined behavior).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe access to type[0] and type[type.length()-1] on an empty std::string reads outside the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. The later empty check at line 13 is a guard against invalid type values, not a bounds check on these accesses, so it does not prevent the read.

evidence_lines.code:
std::string::size_type pos = buf.find_first_of(' ');
type = buf.substr(5, pos-5);

if (type[0] == '"') type = type.substr(1);
if (type[type.length()-1] == '"') type = type.substr(0, type.length()-1);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code assumes the substring after "type=" is non-empty, but buf.substr(5, pos-5) can produce an empty string when pos is npos or the space immediately follows. Trigger: a crafted XMP text buffer beginning with "type=" and lacking a type token. Consequence: type[0] and type[length()-1] on the empty string perform an out-of-bounds read, causing undefined behavior and potential denial of service.

The vivid_fb_ioctl() code fails to initialize the 16 _reserved bytes of
struct fb_vblank after the ->hcount member. Add an explicit

description: The vivid_fb_ioctl function in drivers/media/platform/vivid/vivid-osd.c in the Linux kernel through 4.3.3 does not initialize a certain structure member, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory via a crafted application.

code_evidence: A stack-allocated struct fb_vblank is declared uninitialized at line 6. commit_msg:
DNP3: fix reachable assertion and buffer over-read/overflow.

A DNP3 packet using a link layer header that specifies a zero length can
trigger an assertion failure if assertions are enabled.  Assertions are
enabled unless Bro is compiled with the NDEBUG preprocessor macro
defined.  The default configuration of Bro will define this macro and so
disables assertions, but using the --enable-debug option in the
configure script will enable assertions.  When assertions are disabled,
or also for certain length values, the DNP3 parser may attempt to pass a
negative value as the third argument to memcpy (number of bytes to copy)
and result in a buffer over-read or overflow.

Reported by Travis Emmert.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['bool DNP3_Base::AddToBuffer(Endpoint* endp, int target_len, const u_char** data, int* len)', '\t\treturn true;', '\treturn endp->buffer_len == target_len;'], 'added_lines': ['int DNP3_Base::AddToBuffer(Endpoint* endp, int target_len, const u_char** data, int* len)', '\t\treturn 1;', '', '\tif ( *len < 0 )', '\t\t{', '\t\treporter->AnalyzerError(analyzer, "dnp3 negative input length: %d", *len);', '\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t}', '', '\tif ( target_len < endp->buffer_len )', '\t\t{', '\t\treporter->AnalyzerError(analyzer, "dnp3 invalid target length: %d - %d",', '\t\t                        target_len, endp->buffer_len);', '\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t}', '', '\tif ( endp->buffer_len + to_copy > MAX_BUFFER_SIZE )', '\t\t{', '\t\treporter->AnalyzerError(analyzer, "dnp3 buffer length exceeded: %d + %d",', '\t\t                        endp->buffer_len, to_copy);', '\t\treturn -1;', '\t\t}', '\tif ( endp->buffer_len == target_len )', '\t\treturn 1;', '', '\treturn 0;']}
description: analyzer/protocol/dnp3/DNP3.cc in Bro before 2.3.2 does not properly handle zero values of a packet length, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow or buffer over-read if NDEBUG; otherwise assertion failure) via a crafted DNP3 packet.

code_evidence: Line 5 computes to_copy = min(*len, target_len - endp->buffer_len) without validating that *len is non-negative or that target_len - endp->buffer_len is a sane, non-negative bound; a zero or malformed DNP3 link-layer length can yield a negative to_copy. Line 6 then passes that value as the size argument to memcpy into endp->buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe memcpy reads from and writes to memory outside the intended buffer bounds, which is the definition of CWE-119. The missing length validation lets an attacker-controlled count drive the out-of-bounds operation; this is a buffer-boundary error rather than a simple integer issue alone.

evidence_lines.code:
int to_copy = min(*len, target_len - endp->buffer_len);
memcpy(endp->buffer + endp->buffer_len, *data, to_copy);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: AddToBuffer performs memcpy with a byte count derived from attacker-controlled packet length fields with no lower-bound or capacity check, so a crafted DNP3 packet with a zero/invalid length produces a negative size_t in memcpy. This causes an out-of-bounds read from *data and/or an out-of-bounds write into endp->buffer, leading to a crash or memory corruption (or an assertion failure when assertions are enabled).

commit_msg:
Fixed aggregation methods of Promise ctor with array-like object.

Previously, while iterating over an array-like object the methods may be
resolved with INVALID values. INVALID value is a special internal type which
should never be visible by ordinary functions.

The fix is to ensure that absent elements are represented by undefined value.

The following methods were fixed Promise.all(), Promise.allSettled(),
    Promise.any(), Promise.race().

This closes #483 issue on Github.

commit_msg:
Fix NULL pointer deref in outputSWF_TEXT_RECORD

In outputSWF_TEXT_RECORD, the array offset is stored in a
signed int, while (&(trec->GlyphEntries[i]))->GlyphIndex[0]
returns an unsigned 32 bit number.

This may lead to an integer overflow when reading the offset
from the GlyphIndex array, and further to a buffer overflow
when doing buffer[i]=fi->fontcodeptr[off] with negative off.

In this commit, we change the type of off to unsigned long so
we are guaranteed to be able to store 32 unsigned integers.

This commit fixes CVE-2018-6315 (fixes #101).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['     int off=(&(trec->GlyphEntries[i]))->GlyphIndex[0];'], 'added_lines': ['     unsigned long off=(&(trec->GlyphEntries[i]))->GlyphIndex[0];']}
description: The outputSWF_TEXT_RECORD function (util/outputscript.c) in libming through 0.4.8 is vulnerable to an integer overflow and resultant out-of-bounds read, which may allow attackers to cause a denial of service or unspecified other impact via a crafted SWF file.

code_evidence: Line 45 reads a 32-bit unsigned GlyphIndex[0] into a signed int off, so values >= 0x80000000 become negative. Line 46 then compares this negative off against the unsigned fontcodearrsize, and line 47 uses off as an index into fontcodeptr without a lower-bound check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Storing an unsigned 32-bit value in a signed int is an integer conversion/wraparound that yields a negative offset, which the subsequent bounds check fails to reject. This integer overflow directly enables the out-of-bounds access, matching CWE-190; the out-of-bounds read is the consequence, not the root weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a 32-bit unsigned glyph index is narrowed into a signed int, producing a negative value via wraparound. Trigger: a crafted SWF glyph entry with GlyphIndex[0] >= 2^31. The negative off passes the off<fontcodearrsize check and is used in buffer[i]=fi->fontcodeptr[off], causing an out-of-bounds read (and possible write) rather than a valid lookup.

commit_msg:
[CVE-2017-0196] Fixing an heap overread during slice.

The MissingItem check is happening on the array in a loop. It is possible that we get called into script and that mutates the array. So the Array's head is newly created with length.
However the loop is still performing over the old length.
Fixed this by checking the length In IsMissingItem function.
Added a unittest.

description: An information disclosure vulnerability in Microsoft scripting engine allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory via a crafted web site, aka "Microsoft Browser Information Disclosure Vulnerability."

code_evidence: The loop bound is only newLen, so index i + start can exceed pArr->length if pArr was mutated (length reduced) by script during IsMissingItem/DirectGetItemAtFull calls.
IsMissingItem and DirectGetItemAtFull are invoked with i + start without revalidating against the current pArr->length, and any retrieved element is copied into pnewArr via SetItem.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The direct weakness is an out-of-bounds heap read, but the supported consequence here is disclosure of sensitive process memory, matching CWE-200's confidentiality impact rather than a data-integrity error.

if (pArr->DirectGetItemAtFull(i + start, &element))
pnewArr->SetItem(i, element, PropertyOperation_None);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop trusts a stale newLen/start-derived bound while pArr can be reallocated/mutated through script callbacks, so reads at i + start run past the array's current length. Trigger: an array with missing values whose length shrinks during iteration. Consequence: out-of-bounds heap reads that can disclose process memory into the resulting array.

description: There is a heap overflow problem in video/SDL_pixels.c in SDL (Simple DirectMedia Layer) 2.x to 2.0.18 versions. By crafting a malicious .BMP file, an attacker can cause the application using this library to crash, denial of service or Code execution.

commit_msg:
xenoprof: limit consumption of shared buffer data

Since a shared buffer can be written to by the guest, we may only read
the head and tail pointers from there (all other fields should only ever
be written to). Furthermore, for any particular operation the two values
must be read exactly once, with both checks and consumption happening
with the thus read values. (The backtrace related xenoprof_buf_space()
use in xenoprof_log_event() is an exception: The values used there get
re-checked by every subsequent xenoprof_add_sample().)

Since that code needed touching, also fix the double increment of the
lost samples count in case the backtrace related xenoprof_add_sample()
invocation in xenoprof_log_event() fails.

Where code is being touched anyway, add const as appropriate, but take
the opportunity to entirely drop the now unused domain parameter of
xenoprof_buf_space().

This is part of XSA-313.

Reported-by: Ilja Van Sprundel <ivansprundel@ioactive.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Wei Liu <wl@xen.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static int xenoprof_buf_space(struct domain *d, xenoprof_buf_t * buf, int size)', '    int head, tail;', '', '    head = xenoprof_buf(d, buf, event_head);', '    tail = xenoprof_buf(d, buf, event_tail);', ''], 'added_lines': ['static int xenoprof_buf_space(int head, int tail, int size)']}
description: An issue was discovered in xenoprof in Xen through 4.13.x, allowing guest OS users (without active profiling) to obtain sensitive information about other guests. Unprivileged guests can request to map xenoprof buffers, even if profiling has not been enabled for those guests. These buffers were not scrubbed.

code_evidence: xenoprof_buf_space() reads event_head and event_tail from the shared xenoprof_buf_t via xenoprof_buf(d, buf, ...) and computes free space from them; the function itself performs no validation of the buffer contents and no initialization of the shared buffer before use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-909 (Missing Initialization of Resource) fits because the shared xenoprof buffer is used without being initialized/scrubbed, letting uninitialized or stale contents be exposed or misinterpreted; the described impact is sensitive information disclosure, consistent with the resource-initialization weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the free-space calculation consumes head/tail values taken directly from a guest-writable shared buffer without ensuring the buffer region was initialized/scrubbed for this guest. A guest that maps an unscrubbed xenoprof buffer can influence or observe these fields, leading to disclosure of residual data from other guests (and the commit notes the values must be read exactly once for consistency checks).

commit_msg:
The syzbot fuzzer has found two (!) races in the USB character device
registration and deregistration routines.  This patch fixes the races.

The first race results from the fact that usb_deregister_dev() sets
usb_minors[intf->minor] to NULL before calling device_destroy() on the
class device.  This leaves a window during which another thread can
allocate the same minor number but will encounter a duplicate name
error when it tries to register its own class device.  A typical error
message in the system log would look like:

    sysfs: cannot create duplicate filename '/class/usbmisc/ldusb0'

The patch fixes this race by destroying the class device first.

The second race is in usb_register_dev().  When that routine runs, it
first allocates a minor number, then drops minor_rwsem, and then
creates the class device.  If the device creation fails, the minor
number is deallocated and the whole routine returns an error.  But
during the time while minor_rwsem was dropped, there is a window in
which the minor number is allocated and so another thread can
successfully open the device file.  Typically this results in
use-after-free errors or invalid accesses when the other thread closes
its open file reference, because the kernel then tries to release
resources that were already deallocated when usb_register_dev()
failed.  The patch fixes this race by keeping minor_rwsem locked
throughout the entire routine.

Reported-and-tested-by: syzbot+30cf45ebfe0b0c4847a1@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Alan Stern <stern@rowland.harvard.edu>
CC: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/Pine.LNX.4.44L0.1908121607590.1659-100000@iolanthe.rowland.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tdevice_destroy(usb_class->class, MKDEV(USB_MAJOR, intf->minor));'], 'added_lines': ['\tdevice_destroy(usb_class->class, MKDEV(USB_MAJOR, intf->minor));']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.2.10, there is a race condition bug that can be caused by a malicious USB device in the USB character device driver layer, aka CID-303911cfc5b9. This affects drivers/usb/core/file.c.

code_evidence: The function clears usb_minors[intf->minor] under minor_rwsem (lines 7-9) and only afterwards calls device_destroy() at line 10, outside the lock. This ordering leaves a window in which the minor is free for reuse while the class device still exists.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code sequence requires exclusive access to usb_minors and the class device, but the release is split across a lock boundary, allowing an interfering concurrent sequence to act on the shared resource. This is exactly a race condition; it is not merely a missing NULL check because the defect is the timing/ordering of synchronized state updates.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shared minor slot and its class device are released non-atomically, with device_destroy() outside minor_rwsem. Trigger: a concurrent usb_register_dev() thread allocates the just-freed minor during that window and hits a duplicate sysfs name; similarly, readers may observe an inconsistent state. Supported consequence: registration failure and race-induced instability, matching the commit's duplicate-name report.

commit_msg:
res_pjsip_header_funcs: Duplicate new header value, don't copy.

When updating an existing header the 'update' code incorrectly
just copied the new value into the existing buffer. If the
new value exceeded the available buffer size memory outside
of the buffer would be written into, potentially causing
a crash.

This change makes it so that the 'update' now duplicates
the new header value instead of copying it into the existing
buffer.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpj_strcpy2(&((pjsip_generic_string_hdr *) hdr)->hvalue, data->header_value);'], 'added_lines': ['\tpj_pool_t *pool = data->channel->session->inv_session->dlg->pool;', '\tpj_strdup2(pool, &((pjsip_generic_string_hdr *) hdr)->hvalue, data->header_value);']}
description: Asterisk is an open source private branch exchange and telephony toolkit. In Asterisk versions 18.20.0 and prior, 20.5.0 and prior, and 21.0.0; as well as ceritifed-asterisk 18.9-cert5 and prior, the 'update' functionality of the PJSIP_HEADER dialplan function can exceed the available buffer space for storing the new value of a header. By doing so this can overwrite memory or cause a crash. This is not externally exploitable, unless dialplan is explicitly written to update a header based on data from an outside source. If the 'update' functionality is not used the vulnerability does not occur. A patch is available at commit a1ca0268254374b515fa5992f01340f7717113fa.

code_evidence: Line 18 copies data->header_value into the existing hvalue buffer via pj_strcpy2, which performs no destination-capacity check; the buffer was allocated for the prior header value and may be smaller than the new value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the code copies an input buffer to an output buffer without verifying that the input size is smaller than the output, producing a classic out-of-bounds write. The fix replaces the copy with a pool allocation (pj_strdup2), confirming the missing size constraint rather than an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence_lines.code: pj_strcpy2(&((pjsip_generic_string_hdr *) hdr)->hvalue, data->header_value);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unbounded string copy into a previously allocated header buffer. Trigger: the PJSIP_HEADER update path supplies a new header value longer than the existing hvalue allocation. Consequence: writes past the buffer end, corrupting memory or crashing; the commit notes this is only reachable if dialplan feeds external data into the update.

commit_msg:
ext4: zero out the unused memory region in the extent tree block

This commit zeroes out the unused memory region in the buffer_head
corresponding to the extent metablock after writing the extent header
and the corresponding extent node entries.

This is done to prevent random uninitialized data from getting into
the filesystem when the extent block is synced.

This fixes CVE-2019-11833.

Signed-off-by: Sriram Rajagopalan <sriramr@arista.com>
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@kernel.org
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t ext_size = 0;', '\t/* zero out unused area in the extent block */', '\text_size = sizeof(struct ext4_extent_header) +', '\t\tsizeof(struct ext4_extent) * le16_to_cpu(neh->eh_entries);', '\tmemset(bh->b_data + ext_size, 0, inode->i_sb->s_blocksize - ext_size);', '\t\t/* zero out unused area in the extent block */', '\t\text_size = sizeof(struct ext4_extent_header) +', '\t\t   (sizeof(struct ext4_extent) * le16_to_cpu(neh->eh_entries));', '\t\tmemset(bh->b_data + ext_size, 0,', '\t\t\tinode->i_sb->s_blocksize - ext_size);']}
description: fs/ext4/extents.c in the Linux kernel through 5.1.2 does not zero out the unused memory region in the extent tree block, which might allow local users to obtain sensitive information by reading uninitialized data in the filesystem.

code_evidence: The newly allocated metablock buffer is initialized only for the header fields (eh_entries, eh_max, eh_magic, eh_depth) and the moved extent entries; the remainder of the block is left untouched.

At the leaf level, m entries are memmove'd into the buffer and eh_entries is set to m, but bytes beyond the first sizeof(header)+m*sizeof(extent) are never written before the checksum is computed and the buffer is marked uptodate and dirtied.

The same pattern repeats for intermediate index blocks: only the first index and the m moved indices are populated, leaving the rest of the block uninitialized before ext4_extent_block_csum_set and ext4_handle_dirty_metadata.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 fits because the function uses and persists a resource (the metablock buffer) whose unused region was never initialized. This is not merely an information-exposure sink (CWE-200); the underlying defect is missing initialization of allocated memory, which the added memset at the split sites directly addresses.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the extent split path allocates a fresh metadata block and writes only the used header/entry region, leaving the unused tail uninitialized. Trigger: a local user performing an extent-tree split causes the partially initialized buffer to be synced to disk, so stale kernel heap contents are persisted. Supported consequence: disclosure of uninitialized kernel memory via the filesystem (CVE-2019-11833).

commit_msg:
usbip_host updates device status without holding lock from stub probe,
disconnect and rebind code paths. When multiple requests to import a
device are received, these unprotected code paths step all over each
other and drive fails with NULL-ptr deref and use-after-free errors.

The driver uses a table lock to protect the busid array for adding and
deleting busids to the table. However, the probe, disconnect and rebind
paths get the busid table entry and update the status without holding
the busid table lock. Add a new finer grain lock to protect the busid
entry. This new lock will be held to search and update the busid entry
fields from get_busid_idx(), add_match_busid() and del_match_busid().

match_busid_show() does the same to access the busid entry fields.

commit_msg:
9pfs: local: set the path of the export root to "."

The local backend was recently converted to using "at*()" syscalls in order
to ensure all accesses happen below the shared directory. This requires that
we only pass relative paths, otherwise the dirfd argument to the "at*()"
syscalls is ignored and the path is treated as an absolute path in the host.
This is actually the case for paths in all fids, with the notable exception
of the root fid, whose path is "/". This causes the following backend ops to
act on the "/" directory of the host instead of the virtfs shared directory
when the export root is involved:
- lstat
- chmod
- chown
- utimensat

ie, chmod /9p_mount_point in the guest will be converted to chmod / in the
host for example. This could cause security issues with a privileged QEMU.

All "*at()" syscalls are being passed an open file descriptor. In the case
of the export root, this file descriptor points to the path in the host that
was passed to -fsdev.

The fix is thus as simple as changing the path of the export root fid to be
"." instead of "/".

This is CVE-2017-7471.

Cc: qemu-stable@nongnu.org
Reported-by: Léo Gaspard <leo@gaspard.io>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kurz <groug@kaod.org>
Reviewed-by: Eric Blake <eblake@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Maydell <peter.maydell@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        v9fs_path_sprintf(target, "%s", name);'], 'added_lines': ['    } else if (strcmp(name, "/")) {', '        v9fs_path_sprintf(target, "%s", name);', '        /* We want the path of the export root to be relative, otherwise', '         * "*at()" syscalls would treat it as "/" in the host.', '         */', '        v9fs_path_sprintf(target, "%s", ".");']}
description: Quick Emulator (Qemu) built with the VirtFS, host directory sharing via Plan 9 File System (9pfs) support, is vulnerable to an improper access control issue. It could occur while accessing files on a shared host directory. A privileged user inside guest could use this flaw to access host file system beyond the shared folder and potentially escalating their privileges on a host.

code_evidence: When dir_path is NULL (the export root fid), the function builds target solely from name; before the fix name is "/", so target becomes the host absolute path "/". This string is later passed to *at() syscalls, whose dirfd is ignored for absolute paths, redirecting operations (lstat/chmod/chown/utimensat) to the host root instead of the shared directory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function assigns the export root an overly broad host path, letting unintended actors (guest users) act on resources outside the intended shared directory, matching incorrect permission/access scoping for a critical resource. It is not merely a missing check; the constructed path itself widens the accessible resource.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the export-root path is constructed as an absolute host path ("/") rather than a relative one, so *at() dirfd confinement is bypassed. Trigger: a guest accesses the 9p mount root (e.g., chmod /9p_mount_point). Supported consequence: backend operations act on the host "/" directory, allowing a privileged guest to modify host filesystem permissions/ownership beyond the shared folder.

description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In PJSIP before version 2.11.1, there are a couple of issues found in the SSL socket. First, a race condition between callback and destroy, due to the accepted socket having no group lock. Second, the SSL socket parent/listener may get destroyed during handshake. Both issues were reported to happen intermittently in heavy load TLS connections. They cause a crash, resulting in a denial of service. These are fixed in version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: SSLLogErrors(action, ret, err, len, ssock) is invoked with ssock, then ssock->last_err is written unconditionally. The patch adds an if (ssock) guard before dereferencing, indicating ssock may be NULL when this error path runs concurrently with socket destruction.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function participates in a race between error reporting and concurrent socket destruction on a shared resource lacking exclusive access. The NULL guard only mitigates the crash; the underlying concurrent access to ssock without synchronization is CWE-362, not an isolated NULL pointer dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error-handling path dereferences ssock without a validity check while another thread may destroy the SSL socket/listener during handshake. Trigger: concurrent teardown racing with an SSL error callback. Consequence: NULL dereference/crash, a denial of service; the missing group lock in the accepted socket makes this window reachable.

description: atm_tc_enqueue in net/sched/sch_atm.c in the Linux kernel through 6.1.4 allows attackers to cause a denial of service because of type confusion (non-negative numbers can sometimes indicate a TC_ACT_SHOT condition rather than valid classification results).

code_evidence: tcf_classify returns an action code in result, but the code only rejects negative values (line 19). Non-negative action codes such as TC_ACT_SHOT are treated as classification results, so res.class is cast to struct atm_flow_data * (line 21) even when it is not a valid flow pointer; lookup_flow is only used when res.class is NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The same value in result/res.class is interpreted as an action code by the filter but as a flow classification pointer by atm_tc_enqueue; using that resource as an incompatible type is exactly CWE-843 type confusion, not merely a NULL-pointer check omission.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of tcf_classify is assumed to be a classification result once it is non-negative, without distinguishing action codes from valid class pointers. Trigger: a filter returns TC_ACT_SHOT (a non-negative value) with res.class not holding a valid atm_flow_data pointer. Consequence: the invalid pointer is dereferenced as a flow (e.g., flow->vcc, flow->q), giving a denial of service via crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Prevent division by 0.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 370962554
Change-Id: I0b9b62f4d8e1046dd88f9433f8dfeaf61a901680
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, channels_in != 0);', '      TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, channels_in != 0);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. TFLite's convolution code(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/09c73bca7d648e961dd05898292d91a8322a9d45/tensorflow/lite/kernels/conv.cc) has multiple division where the divisor is controlled by the user and not checked to be non-zero. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 68 sets channels_in from filter->dims->data[3], a value derived from the model's filter tensor and thus attacker/model-controlled. Line 170 divides NumElements(input) by channels_in without first checking channels_in is non-zero, so a filter with zero input channels triggers integer division by zero.
Line 209 performs the same unsafeguarded division NumElements(input) / channels_in in the hybrid per-channel path, again using channels_in from line 68 with no zero check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-369 (Divide By Zero) directly describes the operation: a user-influenced dimension is used as the divisor without a non-zero constraint. This is a straightforward division-by-zero, not a different arithmetic weakness such as overflow, since the fault is the zero divisor itself.

evidence_lines.code:

commit_msg:
evtchn/x86: enforce correct upper limit for 32-bit guests

The recording of d->max_evtchns in evtchn_2l_init(), in particular with
the limited set of callers of the function, is insufficient. Neither for
PV nor for HVM guests the bitness is known at domain_create() time, yet
the upper bound in 2-level mode depends upon guest bitness. Recording
too high a limit "allows" x86 32-bit domains to open not properly usable
event channels, management of which (inside Xen) would then result in
corruption of the shared info and vCPU info structures.

Keep the upper limit dynamic for the 2-level case, introducing a helper
function to retrieve the effective limit. This helper is now supposed to
be private to the event channel code. The used in do_poll() and
domain_dump_evtchn_info() weren't consistent with port uses elsewhere
and hence get switched to port_is_valid().

Furthermore FIFO mode's setup_ports() gets adjusted to loop only up to
the prior ABI limit, rather than all the way up to the new one.

Finally a word on the change to do_poll(): Accessing ->max_evtchns
without holding a suitable lock was never safe, as it as well as
->evtchn_port_ops may change behind do_poll()'s back. Using
port_is_valid() instead widens some the window for potential abuse,
until we've dealt with the race altogether (see XSA-343).

This is XSA-342.

Reported-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Fixes: 48974e6ce52e ("evtchn: use a per-domain variable for the max number of event channels")
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Stefano Stabellini <sstabellini@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if ( port > d->max_evtchn_port || port >= d->max_evtchns )'], 'added_lines': ['    if ( port > d->max_evtchn_port || port >= max_evtchns(d) )']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.14.x. Out of bounds event channels are available to 32-bit x86 domains. The so called 2-level event channel model imposes different limits on the number of usable event channels for 32-bit x86 domains vs 64-bit or Arm (either bitness) ones. 32-bit x86 domains can use only 1023 channels, due to limited space in their shared (between guest and Xen) information structure, whereas all other domains can use up to 4095 in this model. The recording of the respective limit during domain initialization, however, has occurred at a time where domains are still deemed to be 64-bit ones, prior to actually honoring respective domain properties. At the point domains get recognized as 32-bit ones, the limit didn't get updated accordingly. Due to this misbehavior in Xen, 32-bit domains (including Domain 0) servicing other domains may observe event channel allocations to succeed when they should really fail. Subsequent use of such event channels would then possibly lead to corruption of other parts of the shared info structure. An unprivileged guest may cause another domain, in particular Domain 0, to misbehave. This may lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) for the entire system. All Xen versions from 4.4 onwards are vulnerable. Xen versions 4.3 and earlier are not vulnerable. Only x86 32-bit domains servicing other domains are vulnerable. Arm systems, as well as x86 64-bit domains, are not vulnerable.

code_evidence: Line 3 bounds the requested port only against d->max_evtchns, the statically recorded limit, and returns -ENOSPC at line 4 otherwise.
When port_is_valid() is false, lines 15-27 allocate a group and an event-channel bucket and increment valid_evtchns for a port that may exceed the effective 32-bit limit.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function permits a port index beyond the effective array limit, after which event-channel state is written out of bounds, matching CWE-787. The root cause is the stale/missing upper-bound constraint, not merely an information leak or race.

evidence_lines.code:
if ( port > d->max_evtchn_port || port >= d->max_evtchns )
return -ENOSPC;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The check uses the domain-wide max_evtchns recorded at domain creation rather than the bitness-dependent effective limit. A 32-bit x86 guest servicing other domains can therefore allocate an event channel above 1023; later use writes into the shared info/vCPU structures beyond their intended bounds.

commit_msg:
gnutls: prevent buffer overflow in get_cert_name

The test suite for ocserv calls openconnect with a certificate that has
a name that is 84 bytes in length. The buffer passed to get_cert_name is
currently 80 bytes.

The gnutls_x509_crt_get_dn_by_oid function will update the buffer size
parameter if the buffer is too small.

http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/gnutls_x509_crt_get_dn_by_oid.3.html

RETURNS
       GNUTLS_E_SHORT_MEMORY_BUFFER if the provided buffer is not long
       enough, and in that case the  buf_size will be updated with the
       required size. GNUTLS_E_REQUESTED_DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE if there are no
       data in the current index. On success 0 is returned.

Use a temporary variable to avoid clobbering the namelen variable that is
passed to get_cert_name.

Bug: https://bugs.gentoo.org/721570
Signed-off-by: Sergei Trofimovich <slyfox@gentoo.org>
Signed-off-by: Mike Gilbert <floppym@gentoo.org>

We need to avoid clobbering the original', '\t * length variable. */', '\tsize_t nl = namelen;', '\t\t\t\t\t  0, 0, name, &nl)) {', '\t\tnl = namelen;', '\t\tif (gnutls_x509_crt_get_dn(cert, name, &nl)) {', '\t\t\tname[namelen-1] = 0;', '\t\t\tsnprintf(name, namelen-1, "<unknown>");', '\t\t\treturn -EINVAL;', '\t\t}']}
description: OpenConnect 8.09 has a buffer overflow, causing a denial of service (application crash) or possibly unspecified other impact, via crafted certificate data to get_cert_name in gnutls.c.

code_evidence: The function passes the caller-supplied name buffer and the length variable namelen directly to gnutls_x509_crt_get_dn_by_oid and gnutls_x509_crt_get_dn. GnuTLS writes the DN into name and, on GNUTLS_E_SHORT_MEMORY_BUFFER, overwrites namelen with the required size.
On failure, name[namelen-1] and snprintf(name, namelen-1, ...) use the possibly-clobbered namelen, so the index and copy length can exceed the actual buffer size.

name[namelen-1] = 0;
snprintf(name, namelen-1, "<unknown>");

commit_msg:
outline: fix overflows in outline processing

This commit enforces strict invariant on ASS_Outline
to contain point coordinates into predetermined range.

Fixes https://github.com/libass/libass/issues/431.

Later add_line/add_quadratic/add_cubic (lines 26-42) operate on these coordinates, so the range invariant established here is what prevents arithmetic on unvalidated coordinates.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void SoftHEVC::setDecodeArgs(ivd_video_decode_ip_t *ps_dec_ip,', '    uint8_t *pBuf;', '    if (outHeader) {', '        pBuf = outHeader->pBuffer;', '    } else {', '        pBuf = mFlushOutBuffer;', '    }', '', '    return;'], 'added_lines': ['bool SoftHEVC::setDecodeArgs(ivd_video_decode_ip_t *ps_dec_ip,', '    uint8_t *pBuf;', '    if (outHeader) {', '        if (outHeader->nAllocLen < sizeY + (sizeUV * 2)) {', '            android_errorWriteLog(0x534e4554, "27569635");', '            return false;', '        }', '        pBuf = outHeader->pBuffer;', '    } else {', '        // mFlushOutBuffer always has the right size.', '        pBuf = mFlushOutBuffer;', '    }', '', '    return true;']}
description: libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-06-01 allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, as demonstrated by obtaining Signature or SignatureOrSystem access, aka internal bug 27833616.

code_evidence: sizeY and sizeUV are derived from the decoder's output dimensions (line 6, 27) and then used to lay out three output planes inside the caller-supplied buffer.

When outHeader is non-NULL, pBuf is taken directly from outHeader->pBuffer (line 23) and the plane pointers pBuf, pBuf+sizeY, pBuf+sizeY+sizeUV are written (lines 31-33) without checking outHeader->nAllocLen against the required sizeY + 2*sizeUV.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts buffer-size metadata but omits the required validation of that input before use, which is improper input validation (CWE-20). The missing check on nAllocLen is the validated-property gap; the resulting overflow is the consequence rather than a separate weakness label.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size of the external output buffer (outHeader->nAllocLen) is never validated against the computed plane sizes before the buffer is used. Trigger: a crafted stream/application supplies an output buffer whose allocation is smaller than sizeY + 2*sizeUV. Consequence: the decoder writes decoded planes past the buffer end, causing an out-of-bounds write that can corrupt memory and potentially enable privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
(for 4.9.3) CVE-2018-14882/ICMP6 RPL: Add a missing bounds check

Moreover:
Add and use *_tstr[] strings.
Update four tests outputs accordingly.
Fix a space.

Wang Junjie of 360 ESG Codesafe Team had independently identified this
vulnerability in 2018 by means of fuzzing and provided the packet capture
file for the test.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ND_PRINT((ndo,"[|icmp6]"));'], 'added_lines': ['    ND_PRINT((ndo, "%s", mldv2_tstr));']}
description: The ICMPv6 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.3 has a buffer over-read in print-icmp6.c.

code_evidence: Loop over ngroups extracted from the packet; before reading a group record it checks len < group + 20 and bails out via return at line 19.
For each group, nsrcs is read from packet bytes and the check len < group + 20 + (nsrcs * sizeof(struct in6_addr)) guards the source addresses, returning at line 28 when insufficient.
Inner loop reads each source address at bp[group + 20 + j*sizeof(struct in6_addr)] after ND_TCHECK2 on that offset, bounded by the prior length check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads data at computed offsets (bp[group+...], source addresses) beyond the intended buffer when bounds checks fail, matching CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. The diff only changes the truncation message; the underlying over-read is in the length-check logic, not a write (contrast CWE-787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser relies on length checks (len < group + 20 and len < group + 20 + nsrcs*16) before indexing packet buffers. Trigger: a crafted ICMPv6 MLDv2 report with ngroups/nsrcs values or truncated payload where the arithmetic check is insufficient, so the loop indexes past the captured/declared length. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of packet memory (buffer over-read), potentially leaking memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
btrfs: merge btrfs_find_device and find_device

Both btrfs_find_device() and find_device() does the same thing except
that the latter does not take the seed device onto account in the device
scanning context. We can merge them.

Signed-off-by: Anand Jain <anand.jain@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tNULL);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tNULL, true);']}
description: fs/btrfs/volumes.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1 allows a btrfs_verify_dev_extents NULL pointer dereference via a crafted btrfs image because fs_devices->devices is mishandled within find_device, aka CID-09ba3bc9dd15.

code_evidence: The function takes RCU read lock and calls btrfs_find_device() with fs_info->fs_devices, devid and optional uuid, passing NULL for the new seed-device parameter.
The returned dev pointer is checked only for NULL; once non-NULL, dev->devid, dev->bytes_used, dev->total_bytes and dev->uuid are dereferenced directly.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The evidence directly supports CWE-476: the code dereferences dev fields without validating that the device structure and its members are valid, and the described flaw is a NULL pointer dereference in find_device handling. This is a NULL-dereference issue rather than an out-of-bounds or use-after-free weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: btrfs_find_device may return a device object that was not fully initialized/validated when seed devices are mishandled, so the non-NULL result can still contain a NULL or invalid internal pointer. Trigger: a crafted btrfs image exposing a malformed fs_devices->devices list, reached via the dev-info ioctl. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference during the dereferences at lines 20-23, causing a kernel crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
XRA: Fix an infinite loop

C compilers don't care what size a value was on the wire. Use
naturally-sized ints, including in dissect_message_channel_mb where we
would otherwise overflow and loop infinitely.

Fixes #19100
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  guint16 offset = 0;'], 'added_lines': ['  int offset = 0;']}
description: XRA dissector infinite loop in Wireshark 4.0.0 to 4.0.5 and 3.6.0 to 3.6.13 allows denial of service via packet injection or crafted capture file

code_evidence: offset is declared as guint16 (line 3) and drives the loop condition on line 9 and the advancement offset += mb_length on line 46. mb_length is guint16 initialized to 1000 and, in the default case, assigned 5 + 256*(mb_nibble2 & 0x01) + mb_byte2 (line 37), which can exceed 65535 and wrap when stored in the 16-bit mb_length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The loop's exit condition (tvb_reported_length_remaining(tvb, offset) > 0) becomes unreachable because offset cannot progress past the wrapped value, matching CWE-835's infinite loop with availability impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the 16-bit offset and mb_length truncate a computed length. A crafted packet with an unrecognized mb_type and large nibble/byte values makes the computed length wrap, so offset advances by a small or zero amount and never reaches the reported remaining length. The loop condition stays true, causing CPU exhaustion and denial of service.

Split the xt_compat_match/xt_compat_target into smaller type-safe functions
performing just one operation. Handle all alignment and size-related
conversions centrally in these function instead of requiring each module to
implement a full-blown conversion function. Replace ->compat callback by
->compat_from_user and ->compat_to_user callbacks, responsible for
converting just a single private structure.

Signed-off-by: Patrick McHardy <kaber@trash.net>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (t->u.kernel.target->compat)', '\t\tt->u.kernel.target->compat(t, NULL, &off, COMPAT_CALC_SIZE);', '\telse', '\t\txt_compat_target(t, NULL, &off, COMPAT_CALC_SIZE);'], 'added_lines': ['\toff += xt_compat_target_offset(t->u.kernel.target);']}
description: A heap out-of-bounds write affecting Linux since v2.6.19-rc1 was discovered in net/netfilter/x_tables.c. This allows an attacker to gain privileges or cause a DoS (via heap memory corruption) through user name space

code_evidence: off is initialized to 0 and accumulated by IPT_MATCH_ITERATE and the target compat/size calculation at lines 11-14. newinfo->size is then decremented by off at line 15, and off is used in compat_add_offset and to adjust hook_entry/underflow offsets at lines 16-25. The size computed for the new table depends on the per-entry compat size offset derived from the target's compat handler.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the flawed size accounting in compat_calc_entry leads to a heap buffer that is smaller than the data written during compat table translation, i.e., a write past the end of the allocated buffer. This is an out-of-bounds write rather than a mere integer issue because the size miscalculation directly yields the overflow write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the size adjustment for a compat entry is computed from the target's compat conversion (or xt_compat_target fallback) and applied via newinfo->size -= off and offset updates. If the computed off is inconsistent with the actual translated entry layout, the allocated newinfo size is too small, and subsequent writes into the translated table overflow the heap buffer. Trigger: loading a compat iptables ruleset with a target whose compat size calculation mismatches the copied layout. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write enabling privilege escalation or DoS.

commit_msg:
Fix global buffer overflow in printMP3Headers.

The printMP3Headers function in util/listmp3.c processes mp3 files
without checking their bitrate values. This leads to bitrate_idx = 15
being used as index in mp2l23_bitrate_table[bitrate_idx] while
mp2l23_bitrate_table has only 14 elements.

In this commit we add a check rejecting mp3 files declaring invalid
bitrates.

This commit fixes CVE-2017-16898 (fixes: #75).

description: The printMP3Headers function in util/listmp3.c in libming v0.4.8 or earlier is vulnerable to a global buffer overflow, which may allow attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted file, a different vulnerability than CVE-2016-9264.

code_evidence: Line 40 extracts bitrate_idx directly from the frame header bits via (flags & MP3_BITRATE) >> MP3_BITRATE_SHIFT, so an attacker-controlled file can supply any 4-bit value up to 15.
Line 81 then uses bitrate_idx unguarded to index mp2l23_bitrate_table, which has only 14 entries, so bitrate_idx==15 reads one element past the array boundary.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an array read at index 15 on a 14-element table, an operation outside the buffer's intended boundary, matching CWE-119. The added check confirms the missing bound was the defect; the narrower CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read) is a child, but the target label CWE-119 is directly supported.

commit_msg:
mm/rmap: Fix anon_vma->degree ambiguity leading to double-reuse

anon_vma->degree tracks the combined number of child anon_vmas and VMAs
that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

anon_vma_clone() then assumes that for any anon_vma attached to
src->anon_vma_chain other than src->anon_vma, it is impossible for it to
be a leaf node of the VMA tree, meaning that for such VMAs ->degree is
elevated by 1 because of a child anon_vma, meaning that if ->degree
equals 1 there are no VMAs that use the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

This assumption is wrong because the ->degree optimization leads to leaf
nodes being abandoned on anon_vma_clone() - an existing anon_vma is
reused and no new parent-child relationship is created.  So it is
possible to reuse an anon_vma for one VMA while it is still tied to
another VMA.

This is an issue because is_mergeable_anon_vma() and its callers assume
that if two VMAs have the same ->anon_vma, the list of anon_vmas
attached to the VMAs is guaranteed to be the same.  When this assumption
is violated, vma_merge() can merge pages into a VMA that is not attached
to the corresponding anon_vma, leading to dangling page->mapping
pointers that will be dereferenced during rmap walks.

Fix it by separately tracking the number of child anon_vmas and the
number of VMAs using the anon_vma as their ->anon_vma.

Fixes: 7a3ef208e662 ("mm: prevent endless growth of anon_vma hierarchy")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Acked-by: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz>
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Root anon_vma is never reused:', '\t\t    anon_vma != src->anon_vma && anon_vma->degree < 2)', '\t\tdst->anon_vma->degree++;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t * Reuse existing anon_vma if it has no vma and only one', '\t\t * anon_vma child.', '\t\t * Root anon_vma is never reused:', '\t\t    anon_vma->num_children < 2 &&', '\t\t    anon_vma->num_active_vmas == 0)', '\t\tdst->anon_vma->num_active_vmas++;']}
description: mm/rmap.c in the Linux kernel before 5.19.7 has a use-after-free related to leaf anon_vma double reuse.

code_evidence: The reuse condition trusts anon_vma->degree < 2 (combined child-anon_vma and VMA count) as proof the anon_vma is unused by any VMA, so an anon_vma still referenced by another VMA can be assigned to dst->anon_vma and its degree incremented.
Because leaf nodes are abandoned on clone, degree does not distinguish an anon_vma with no active VMAs from one still attached to another VMA, so the check at [18,19,20] can reuse a shared anon_vma.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The described and patched defect yields stale page->mapping references to freed anon_vma memory that are later dereferenced, matching CWE-416 use after free; it is not merely a logic error because the supported consequence is access to freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
if (dst->anon_vma)
dst->anon_vma->degree++;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: degree conflates child anon_vmas with active VMAs, so an anon_vma still in use can be reused as dst->anon_vma. Trigger: cloning an anon_vma_chain where the candidate has degree < 2 but a live VMA reference. Consequence: vma_merge() merges pages into a VMA not attached to the matching anon_vma, producing dangling page->mapping pointers dereferenced during rmap walks (use-after-free).

if (offset + new_byte_length > buffer_byte_length) {
