commit_msg:
passthrough: quarantine PCI devices

When a PCI device is assigned to an untrusted domain, it is possible for
that domain to program the device to DMA to an arbitrary address. The
IOMMU is used to protect the host from malicious DMA by making sure that
the device addresses can only target memory assigned to the guest. However,
when the guest domain is torn down the device is assigned back to dom0,
thus allowing any in-flight DMA to potentially target critical host data.

This patch introduces a 'quarantine' for PCI devices using dom_io. When
the toolstack makes a device assignable (by binding it to pciback), it
will now also assign it to DOMID_IO and the device will only be assigned
back to dom0 when the device is made unassignable again. Whilst device is
assignable it will only ever transfer between dom_io and guest domains.
dom_io is actually only used as a sentinel domain for quarantining purposes;
it is not configured with any IOMMU mappings. Assignment to dom_io simply
means that the device's initiator (requestor) identifier is not present in
the IOMMU's device table and thus any DMA transactions issued will be
terminated with a fault condition.

In addition, a fix to assignment handling is made for VT-d.  Failure
during the assignment step should not lead to a device still being
associated with its prior owner. Hand the device to DomIO temporarily,
until the assignment step has completed successfully.  Remove the PI
hooks from the source domain then earlier as well.

Failure of the recovery reassign_device_ownership() may not go silent:
There e.g. may still be left over RMRR mappings in the domain assignment
to which has failed, and hence we can't allow that domain to continue
executing.

NOTE: This patch also includes one printk() cleanup; the
      "XEN_DOMCTL_assign_device: " tag is dropped in iommu_do_pci_domctl(),
      since similar printk()-s elsewhere also don't log such a tag.

This is XSA-302.

Signed-off-by: Paul Durrant <paul.durrant@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Ian Jackson <ian.jackson@eu.citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    pdev = pci_get_pdev_by_domain(hardware_domain, seg, bus, devfn);', '    return pdev ? 0 : -EBUSY;'], 'added_lines': ['    int rc = 0;', '', '    pdev = pci_get_pdev(seg, bus, devfn);', '', '    if ( !pdev )', '        rc = -ENODEV;', '    /*', '     * If the device exists and it is not owned by either the hardware', '     * domain or dom_io then it must be assigned to a guest, or be', '     * hidden (owned by dom_xen).', '     */', '    else if ( pdev->domain != hardware_domain &&', '              pdev->domain != dom_io )', '        rc = -EBUSY;', '', '    return rc;']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.12.x allowing attackers to gain host OS privileges via DMA in a situation where an untrusted domain has access to a physical device. This occurs because passed through PCI devices may corrupt host memory after deassignment. When a PCI device is assigned to an untrusted domain, it is possible for that domain to program the device to DMA to an arbitrary address. The IOMMU is used to protect the host from malicious DMA by making sure that the device addresses can only target memory assigned to the guest. However, when the guest domain is torn down, or the device is deassigned, the device is assigned back to dom0, thus allowing any in-flight DMA to potentially target critical host data. An untrusted domain with access to a physical device can DMA into host memory, leading to privilege escalation. Only systems where guests are given direct access to physical devices capable of DMA (PCI pass-through) are vulnerable. Systems which do not use PCI pass-through are not vulnerable.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only checks PCI device ownership under a lock and returns status codes; it performs no OS command construction or execution, so it cannot support CWE-78.

Later the project computation reads CUR.zp0.cur_x[CUR.GS.rp0] and CUR.zp0.cur_y[CUR.GS.rp0], again indexing zp0 with the unchecked rp0.

commit_msg: Guard binary expressions from too much recursion.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tSAVEREC();', '\tINCREC();', '\tPOPREC();']}
description: jsparse.c in Artifex MuJS through 1.0.2 does not properly maintain the AST depth for binary expressions, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive recursion) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: equality() parses a left operand via relational() then enters a 'loop:' label that, on each accepted equality operator (TK_EQ, TK_NE, TK_STRICTEQ, TK_STRICTNE), builds a binary node and jumps back to 'loop' without any depth accounting; the recursive relational() call on each iteration is guarded only by the input's chain of operators.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the parser fails to control recursion depth for binary expressions, allowing attacker-supplied input to drive excessive stack consumption. This is uncontrolled recursion, not merely a memory leak or integer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the iterative operator loop repeatedly invokes the recursive relational() parser for each chained equality operator while maintaining no AST/recursion depth counter. A crafted file with a very long binary-expression chain triggers unbounded recursion depth, exhausting the program stack (DoS).

commit_msg:
evtchn: avoid NULL derefs

Commit fbbd5009e6 ("evtchn: refactor low-level event channel port ops")
added a de-reference of the struct evtchn pointer for a port without
first making sure the bucket pointer is non-NULL. This de-reference is
actually entirely unnecessary, as all relevant callers (beyond the
problematic do_poll()) already hold the port number in their hands, and
the actual leaf functions need nothing else.

For FIFO event channels there's a second problem in that the ordering
of reads and updates to ->num_evtchns and ->event_array[] was so far
undefined (the read side isn't always holding the domain's event lock).
Add respective barriers.

This is XSA-221.

Reported-by: Ankur Arora <ankur.a.arora@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static bool_t evtchn_fifo_is_pending(struct domain *d,', '                                     const struct evtchn *evtchn)', '    word = evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, evtchn->port);'], 'added_lines': ['static bool_t evtchn_fifo_is_pending(struct domain *d, evtchn_port_t port)', '    word = evtchn_fifo_word_from_port(d, port);']}
description: Xen through 4.8.x does not validate the port numbers of polled event channel ports, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and host OS crash) or possibly obtain sensitive information, aka XSA-221.

code_evidence: The function receives a struct evtchn pointer (line 2) and immediately dereferences it via evtchn->port at line 5 without any NULL check on evtchn. The only guard present (line 6) checks the returned word pointer, not the incoming evtchn pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the function dereferences a pointer (evtchn->port) that is expected valid but can be NULL; the fix removes the dereference by taking the port number directly. This is a NULL-dereference weakness rather than a generic input-validation issue, since the crash stems from the unchecked pointer access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: evtchn_fifo_is_pending trusts the caller-supplied evtchn pointer and reads evtchn->port unconditionally. Trigger: a caller such as do_poll() passing a port with no valid evtchn/bucket lookup, yielding a NULL struct evtchn pointer. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference causing a host OS crash (DoS), as described in XSA-221.

commit_msg:
There are multiple refcounting bugs related to multi-BSSID:
 - In bss_ref_get(), if the BSS has a hidden_beacon_bss, then
   the bss pointer is overwritten before checking for the
   transmitted BSS, which is clearly wrong. Fix this by using
   the bss_from_pub() macro.

 - In cfg80211_bss_update() we copy the transmitted_bss pointer
   from tmp into new, but then if we release new, we'll unref
   it erroneously. We already set the pointer and ref it, but
   need to NULL it since it was copied from the tmp data.

 - In cfg80211_inform_single_bss_data(), if adding to the non-
   transmitted list fails, we unlink the BSS and yet still we
   return it, but this results in returning an entry without
   a reference. We shouldn't return it anyway if it was broken
   enough to not get added there.

This fixes CVE-2022-42720.

Reported-by: Sönke Huster <shuster@seemoo.tu-darmstadt.de>
Tested-by: Sönke Huster <shuster@seemoo.tu-darmstadt.de>
Fixes: a3584f56de1c ("cfg80211: Properly track transmitting and non-transmitting BSS")
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif (__cfg80211_unlink_bss(rdev, res))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (__cfg80211_unlink_bss(rdev, res)) {', '\t\t\t\tres = NULL;', '\t\t\t}', '', '\t\tif (!res)', '\t\t\treturn NULL;']}
description: Various refcounting bugs in the multi-BSS handling in the mac80211 stack in the Linux kernel 5.1 through 5.19.x before 5.19.16 could be used by local attackers (able to inject WLAN frames) to trigger use-after-free conditions to potentially execute code.

code_evidence: When cfg80211_add_nontrans_list() fails, __cfg80211_unlink_bss(rdev, res) removes res from the BSS list, which drops its reference. The function then falls through to trace_cfg80211_return_bss(&res->pub) and returns &res->pub, handing back a pointer to an entry whose reference was released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Returning a pointer to an object whose reference was dropped by unlinking leads to access of freed memory, matching CWE-416. This is a lifetime/reference-counting flaw, not merely a NULL dereference or missing check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: on the non-transmitted list insertion failure path, the BSS is unlinked (releasing its reference) but still returned to the caller. Trigger: a locally injected WLAN frame causing cfg80211_add_nontrans_list() to fail. Consequence: the caller uses the returned cfg80211_bss after it may have been freed, yielding a use-after-free (CVE-2022-42720).

description: mspack/lzxd.c in libmspack 0.5alpha, as used in ClamAV 0.99.2, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted CHM file.

code_evidence: In the LZX_BLOCKTYPE_UNCOMPRESSED case, rundest is set to &window[window_posn] and window_posn is advanced by this_run without checking that window_posn + this_run stays within lzx->window_size. The copy loop then writes i bytes (up to this_run) to rundest via lzx->sys->copy, with i_ptr and this_run controlled by the crafted CHM stream.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a write to a memory location outside the intended window buffer boundary, which is exactly CWE-119's improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer. The added guard in the patch confirms the missing bounds constraint; the specific heap-overflow descendant is not needed since the target is CWE-119.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the uncompressed-block path lacks a bounds check before writing this_run bytes at window[window_posn]. Trigger: a crafted CHM file makes this_run large enough that window_posn + this_run exceeds window_size. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write past the window buffer, causing crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg: Fix for CVE-2023-28366
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcontext->msgs_in.inflight_maximum = db.config->max_inflight_messages;', '\tcontext->msgs_in.inflight_quota = db.config->max_inflight_messages;'], 'added_lines': ['\tcontext->msgs_in.inflight_maximum = 1;', '\tcontext->msgs_in.inflight_quota = 1;']}
description: The broker in Eclipse Mosquitto 1.3.2 through 2.x before 2.0.16 has a memory leak that can be abused remotely when a client sends many QoS 2 messages with duplicate message IDs, and fails to respond to PUBREC commands. This occurs because of mishandling of EAGAIN from the libc send function.

code_evidence: context__init initializes both msgs_in and msgs_out inflight_maximum and inflight_quota from db.config->max_inflight_messages, so the inbound message store is permitted to hold many in-flight QoS 2 messages per client. The patch instead caps msgs_in to 1, indicating the inbound inflight store is the resource that grows unboundedly.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unbounded inbound inflight allocation retains memory that is not released after use, matching CWE-401's missing release of memory after effective lifetime. This is a memory-exhaustion leak rather than a write past bounds (CWE-787) or use-after-free (CWE-416).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the inbound inflight message store is sized by the configurable max_inflight_messages, so a client sending many QoS 2 messages with duplicate IDs and withholding PUBREC accumulates inbound message records. Each record retains allocated memory that is never released while the client keeps the session open, causing memory consumption until exhaustion.

commit_msg:
x509: excessive resource use verifying policy constraints

A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions
of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Fixes CVE-2023-0464

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Shane Lontis <shane.lontis@oracle.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20569)

description:
A security vulnerability has been identified in all supported versions

of OpenSSL related to the verification of X.509 certificate chains
that include policy constraints.  Attackers may be able to exploit this
vulnerability by creating a malicious certificate chain that triggers
exponential use of computational resources, leading to a denial-of-service
(DoS) attack on affected systems.

Policy processing is disabled by default but can be enabled by passing
the `-policy' argument to the command line utilities or by calling the
`X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_policies()' function.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only links policy nodes during certificate policy-tree construction; it performs no certificate validation decision, and the patch merely threads a tree pointer. The demonstrated consequence is resource exhaustion (DoS), not improper certificate validation as described by CWE-295.

Signed-off-by: Chen Hong <chenhong3@huawei.com>

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tport->serio = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['\tspin_lock_irq(&i8042_lock);', '\tport->serio = NULL;', '\tspin_unlock_irq(&i8042_lock);', '\t * We need to make sure that interrupt handler finishes using', '\t * our serio port before we return from this function.']}
description: drivers/input/serio/i8042.c in the Linux kernel before 4.12.4 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact because the port->exists value can change after it is validated.

code_evidence: i8042_stop() reads port from serio->port_data, clears port->exists, synchronizes the AUX/KBD IRQs, then sets port->serio to NULL. The clearing of port->exists and port->serio is not performed under i8042_lock, so the interrupt handler's view of the port can change between its checks.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unsynchronized state teardown enables a NULL pointer to reach serio_interrupt(), matching CWE-476 (dereference of a pointer expected to be valid but NULL). This is a NULL dereference, not merely a race condition, because the supported impact is the crash from dereferencing NULL.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: port->exists is cleared without holding i8042_lock while port->serio is still non-NULL (and set to NULL only after synchronize_irq). If i8042_interrupt() reads port->exists as true, then i8042_stop() clears it and completes synchronization, the handler may then call serio_interrupt() with a NULL serio pointer. Trigger: concurrent stop and IRQ handling. Consequence: NULL pointer dereference and system crash (DoS).

commit_msg: .https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/543
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (sun_info.maplength > GetBlobSize(image))', '          ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"InsufficientImageDataInFile");']}
description: In ImageMagick 7.0.6-1, a memory exhaustion vulnerability was found in the function ReadSUNImage in coders/sun.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service.

code_evidence: maplength is read directly from the file header (line 78) and, for depth<24, becomes image->colors (line 101) or maplength/3 when maptype is RMT_EQUAL_RGB (line 106). AcquireImageColormap then allocates that attacker-controlled count (line 107), with failure only reported after allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This matches CWE-770: the function allocates a resource (colormap memory) on behalf of an untrusted file without restricting the requested size. A related CWE such as CWE-789 (excessive memory allocation) would describe the consequence, but the missing size restriction on the allocation is the target weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the colormap allocation size is derived from the untrusted maplength header field without bounding it against the actual blob size or a resource limit. A crafted SUN file with a huge maplength triggers AcquireImageColormap to attempt an arbitrarily large allocation, exhausting memory and causing denial of service.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (highest_num_seen == 0 ||', '\t\t    highest_num_seen < pinfo->fd->num) {', '\t\t\thighest_num_seen = pinfo->fd->num;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (transfer_info->req == NULL) {']}
description: In Wireshark 2.2.0 to 2.2.4 and 2.0.0 to 2.0.10, there is an LDSS dissector crash, triggered by packet injection or a malformed capture file. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-ldss.c by ensuring that memory is allocated for a certain data structure.

code_evidence: The request structure is allocated only when highest_num_seen is 0 or below the current frame number; on later frames the condition is false, so transfer_info->req is never allocated, yet line 34 dereferences transfer_info->req->file unconditionally.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to validate the state of its conversation-derived data (whether req was already/ever allocated) before use, i.e., missing an input/state constraint check; the fix replaces the heuristic with an explicit NULL check. This improper validation of derived state leading to a crash fits CWE-20, though the lower-level NULL dereference is the concrete manifestation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: allocation of transfer_info->req is gated on a packet-number heuristic rather than on the pointer being NULL. Trigger: a second or later WILLSEND pull packet within the same conversation where highest_num_seen >= pinfo->fd->num skips the allocation. Consequence: transfer_info->req remains NULL and is dereferenced at line 34 (and later at 125/126), causing a NULL-pointer crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
rgw:  make init env methods return an error

Since web frontends may signal an error when requests are malformed or so, let
us double check this and raise errors early. The current user of this is
civetweb frontend; which can potentially return null from `parse_http_headers`
when a HTTP header without a ":" is supplied at which point headers.value is
null which can lead to undefined behaviour later in RGW.

Fixes: http://tracker.ceph.com/issues/23039
Signed-off-by: Abhishek Lekshmanan <abhishek@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void BasicClient::init(CephContext *cct) {', '  init_env(cct);'], 'added_lines': ['[[nodiscard]] int BasicClient::init(CephContext *cct) {', '  int init_error = init_env(cct);', '', '  if (init_error != 0)', '    return init_error;', '  return init_error;']}
description: In Ceph before 12.2.3 and 13.x through 13.0.1, the rgw_civetweb.cc RGWCivetWeb::init_env function in radosgw doesn't handle malformed HTTP headers properly, allowing for denial of service.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: BasicClient::init only calls init_env and iterates the environment map; it contains no pointer dereference of a possibly NULL value, so the NULL-pointer weakness is in the unrelated init_env function.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13040/MPTCP: Clean up printing DSS suboption.

Do the length checking inline; that means we print stuff up to the point
at which we run out of option data.

First check to make sure we have at least 4 bytes of option, so we have
flags to check.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Kim Gwan Yeong.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        if (!(opt_len == 12 && flags & TH_SYN) &&', '            !(opt_len == 24 && flags & TH_ACK))'], 'added_lines': ['        if (!(opt_len == 12 && (flags & TH_SYN)) &&', '            !(opt_len == 24 && (flags & TH_ACK)))']}
description: The MPTCP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-mptcp.c, several functions.

code_evidence: The guard accepts only opt_len values of 12, 16, or 24 depending on flags; any other length returns 0 before parsing. With the parenthesized flag tests, the length check is evaluated correctly, so mpj fields are only read when opt_len matches a valid suboption size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the relevant defect class is reading fields from opt beyond the supplied option length. The function's inline length check is the constraint preventing that out-of-bounds read; the patch corrects the guard rather than introducing a different weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!(opt_len == 12 && flags & TH_SYN) &&
!(opt_len == 16 && (flags & (TH_SYN | TH_ACK)) == (TH_SYN | TH_ACK)) &&
!(opt_len == 24 && flags & TH_ACK))
return 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is that the length validation must gate all subsequent reads of the variable-length opt buffer; the corrected guard ensures opt_len is 12, 16, or 24 before mp_join_print dereferences mpj. Trigger would be a malformed DSS/MP_JOIN suboption with a short opt_len; without the constraint, reads such as mpj->addr_id or EXTRACT_32BITS(mpj->u.syn.token) could read past the option buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13034/PGM: Add a bounds check.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s), modified
so the capture file won't be rejected as an invalid capture.

Move a return to make the code a bit cleaner (i.e., make it more obvious
that if we don't have enough of the PGM header, we just print the source
and destination IP addresses, mark it as incomplete PGM, and don't try
to look at the PGM header).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\treturn;', '\t\t\treturn;', '\t\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t}', '\t\treturn;', '\t    ND_TCHECK_16BITS(bp);']}
description: The PGM parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-pgm.c:pgm_print().

code_evidence: After advancing bp past the source address and two 16-bit fields, the code dereferences EXTRACT_16BITS(bp) in the switch without first verifying that two bytes remain within the captured packet buffer; the added ND_TCHECK_16BITS(bp) in the patch confirms this read was previously unchecked.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe EXTRACT_16BITS(bp) reads beyond the intended captured buffer before any length check; this is a read overrun, not an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: bp is advanced by attacker-controlled PGM NAK option lengths and then read via EXTRACT_16BITS without a bounds test. Trigger: a truncated PGM NAK packet whose captured data ends before the group address family field. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read past the snapshot buffer, leaking memory or crashing the parser.

description: udp_gro_receive_segment in net/ipv4/udp_offload.c in the Linux kernel 5.x before 5.0.13 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (slab-out-of-bounds memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact via UDP packets with a 0 payload, because of mishandling of padded packets, aka the "GRO packet of death" issue.

code_evidence: Only a zero-checksum guard is applied before the UDP header is pulled; no validation of the UDP length field against the actual skb payload length occurs.
skb_gro_pull advances past the UDP header and recomputes checksum without verifying that the claimed length matches skb_gro_len(skb).
The aggregation loop compares uh->len and uh2->len and calls skb_gro_receive(p, skb) directly, so a padded/zero-payload packet with a mismatched length reaches GRO merging and gso_size derivation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing length check allows GRO merging to write past the intended skb buffer, matching out-of-bounds write with integrity/availability impact. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the crash report shows a load, but the unchecked aggregation drives the buffer-length miscalculation underlying the write.

evidence_lines.code:
skb_gro_pull(skb, sizeof(struct udphdr));
skb_gro_postpull_rcsum(skb, uh, sizeof(struct udphdr));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function never constrains the UDP header length against the real payload, so zero-payload padded packets are aggregated. Trigger: a remote UDP packet with a 0 payload/incorrect length enters udp_gro_receive_segment and is merged via skb_gro_receive. Consequence: skb_gro_receive/derived gso_size computes beyond the buffer, causing a slab-out-of-bounds write/memory corruption and host DoS.

description: tools/tiffcrop.c in libtiff 4.0.6 reads an undefined buffer in readContigStripsIntoBuffer() because of a uint16 integer overflow. Reported as MSVR 35100.

code_evidence: Line 7 declares nstrips and strips_per_sample as uint16, so the strip count and per-sample strip count are truncated to 16 bits.
Line 46 assigns TIFFNumberOfStrips(in) into the uint16 nstrips, and line 47 computes strips_per_sample = nstrips / spp in 16-bit arithmetic.
Line 63 loops j over strips_per_sample, and line 68 computes strip = (s * strips_per_sample) + j for TIFFReadEncodedStrip.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the uint16 nstrips/strips_per_sample truncate an integer count that can exceed 65535, causing wraparound that alters the read loop bounds. This is integer overflow driving a buffer/loop-size defect, not a separate out-of-bounds write.

evidence_lines.code: uint16 bps, nstrips, planar, strips_per_sample;

nstrips = TIFFNumberOfStrips(in);
strips_per_sample = nstrips /spp;

for (j = 0; (j < strips_per_sample) && (result == 1); j++)
strip = (s * strips_per_sample) + j;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The strip count from TIFFNumberOfStrips is stored in a uint16, so a file with more than 65535 strips wraps nstrips and strips_per_sample to a small value. The loop then reads only a truncated subset of strips, leaving parts of the destination buffer uninitialized; the caller subsequently processes this undefined buffer.

commit_msg:
ALSA: timer: Fix leak in events via snd_timer_user_ccallback

The stack object “r1” has a total size of 32 bytes. Its field
“event” and “val” both contain 4 bytes padding. These 8 bytes
padding bytes are sent to user without being initialized.

Signed-off-by: Kangjie Lu <kjlu@gatech.edu>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

description: sound/core/timer.c in the Linux kernel through 4.6 does not initialize certain r1 data structures, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory via crafted use of the ALSA timer interface, related to the (1) snd_timer_user_ccallback and (2) snd_timer_user_tinterrupt functions.

code_evidence: Line 7 declares a stack struct snd_timer_tread r1 that is never zero-initialized before line 13 returns early or lines 14-16 assign only event, tstamp and val. The padding bytes of r1 remain uninitialized, and line 18 appends the whole struct to the user-readable timer queue, exposing stack memory contents.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly transfers a partially initialized stack structure to a user-accessible queue, revealing uninitialized memory contents; this is an information exposure of kernel stack data to an unauthorized local actor, matching CWE-200.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack object r1 is populated field-by-field without clearing padding, so uninitialized kernel stack bytes persist. Trigger: a local user enables tread and passes the filter check, causing snd_timer_user_append_to_tqueue to copy r1, including padding, into the queue readable by the user. Consequence: disclosure of sensitive kernel stack memory.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  NOTE_EATEN_LENGTH(new_length);', '    if (total_length < 0)', '        return length;', '    NOTE_EATEN_LENGTH(new_length);'], 'added_lines': ['  CHECK_LENGTH_ADVANCE_OFFSET(new_length);', '  /* XXX Add a bounds check for number_of_elements? */', '    CHECK_LENGTH_ADVANCE_OFFSET(new_length);']}
description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.4 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.12, epan/dissectors/packet-wccp.c had a large loop that was addressed by ensuring that a calculated length was monotonically increasing.

code_evidence: number_of_elements is read directly from the packet via tvb_get_ntohl(tvb, offset) with no upper-bound check (only the prior length<4 check guards the 4-byte read). The loop at line 24 iterates i from 0 to number_of_elements, and each iteration calls dissect_wccp2_web_cache_value_element and updates total_length via length - new_length. The removed check (total_length < 0 return length) previously bounded progress; the patch replaces it with CHECK_LENGTH_ADVANCE_OFFSET(new_length), which only guards per-element advancement, not the element count, as the added comment 'XXX Add a bounds check for number_of_elements?' acknowledges.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-834 covers performing a loop without sufficiently limiting iteration count. Here the loop count comes from packet data and is bounded only by the field width, matching the class; the resource-consumption impact is the supported consequence, not a separate memory-safety weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an attacker-controlled 32-bit element count drives a loop with no cap on iterations, and the loop's per-iteration progress is not tied to the remaining buffer length. Trigger: a crafted WCCP packet with a large number_of_elements and elements that consume little or no length. Consequence: excessive iteration consuming CPU (DoS), and total_length/offset accounting that can underflow or stall.

description: FreeRDP is a free implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), released under the Apache license. Affected versions are subject to an Out-Of-Bounds Read in the `nsc_rle_decompress_data` function. The Out-Of-Bounds Read occurs because it processes `context->Planes` without  checking if it contains data of sufficient length. Should an attacker be able to leverage this vulnerability they may be able to cause a crash. This issue has been addressed in versions 2.11.0 and 3.0.0-beta3. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

code_evidence: The function dereferences and advances the input pointer `in` at line 6 (`*in++`) without any input-length parameter or bound check. Line 16 reads `*in` again, line 18/19 advance and read `*in` for the run-length marker, and the multi-byte branch at lines 26-30 reads four more bytes via `*in++`. The function receives no `inSize`/length argument, so none of these reads are constrained. Line 50's `memcpy(out, in, 4)` likewise copies four bytes from `in` with only `outSize`/`left` checks (line 48), never validating remaining input.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads memory past the end of the intended input buffer at multiple dereferences and in the final memcpy, matching the description of reading data past the end of a buffer. It is not CWE-787 since the flaw is reading, not writing, out of bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decoder consumes the compressed input buffer through sequential pointer reads without tracking remaining input length. Trigger: a truncated or malformed RLE stream causes `in` to advance past the allocated buffer while loops continue. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds read, leaking adjacent memory or causing a crash/DoS.

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.2.3. There is a use-after-free caused by a malicious USB device in the drivers/media/usb/dvb-usb/dvb-usb-init.c driver.

code_evidence: Line 4 initializes name as a pointer to a static literal; line 7 reassigns it to d->desc->name, a pointer owned by the dvb_usb_device. Trigger: a malicious USB device whose descriptors are populated so the d != NULL && d->desc != NULL branch is taken. Consequence: info() reads freed memory, yielding a use-after-free that may crash or leak memory contents.

commit_msg:
If a non-transmitted BSS shares enough information (both
SSID and BSSID!) with another non-transmitted BSS of a
different AP, then we can find and update it, and then
try to add it to the non-transmitted BSS list. We do a
search for it on the transmitted BSS, but if it's not
there (but belongs to another transmitted BSS), the list
gets corrupted.

Since this is an erroneous situation, simply fail the
list insertion in this case and free the non-transmitted
BSS.

This fixes CVE-2022-42721.

commit_msg:
ax25: fix NPD bug in ax25_disconnect

The ax25_disconnect() in ax25_kill_by_device() is not
protected by any locks, thus there is a race condition
between ax25_disconnect() and ax25_destroy_socket().
when ax25->sk is assigned as NULL by ax25_destroy_socket(),
a NULL pointer dereference bug will occur if site (1) or (2)
dereferences ax25->sk.

ax25_kill_by_device()                | ax25_release()
  ax25_disconnect()                  |   ax25_destroy_socket()
    ...                              |
    if(ax25->sk != NULL)             |     ...
      ...                            |     ax25->sk = NULL;
      bh_lock_sock(ax25->sk); //(1)  |     ...
      ...                            |
      bh_unlock_sock(ax25->sk); //(2)|

This patch moves ax25_disconnect() into lock_sock(), which can
synchronize with ax25_destroy_socket() in ax25_release().

description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. This flaw allows an attacker to crash the Linux kernel by simulating amateur radio from the user space, resulting in a null-ptr-deref vulnerability and a use-after-free vulnerability.

code_evidence: sk = s->sk is captured and sock_hold(sk) taken, then ax25_list_lock is released at line 14. lock_sock(sk) at line 15 does not synchronize with ax25_destroy_socket(), which can set ax25->sk = NULL and free the socket. ax25_disconnect(s, ENETUNREACH) at line 19 is invoked after release_sock(sk) at line 18, outside the socket lock, so it can operate on a socket/sk that has been torn down and freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function references socket state (ax25->sk) after the lock protecting its lifetime is dropped, allowing the socket to be freed before ax25_disconnect() uses it. This is a use-after-free (CWE-416); the NULL pointer dereference is a downstream symptom of the freed/cleared pointer, not a separate root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: ax25_disconnect() runs after release_sock() without holding lock_sock, so it races with ax25_destroy_socket() freeing the socket and clearing ax25->sk. Trigger: device teardown via ax25_kill_by_device concurrent with ax25_release; consequence is a use-after-free/NULL dereference crash in ax25_disconnect().

commit_msg: Fixed memory leak reported in #462.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['            (void) inflateEnd(&stream);', '      (void) inflateEnd(&stream);']}
description: In ImageMagick 7.0.5-5, a memory leak was found in the function ReadPSDChannel in coders/psd.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted file.

code_evidence: inflateInit(&stream) is called at line 46, establishing a zlib stream whose internal state must be freed with inflateEnd. On inflate failure the error branch at lines 53-58 frees compact_pixels and pixels and returns MagickFalse without calling inflateEnd, leaking the zlib stream. After the loop the function also proceeds past line 61 without releasing the stream; the patch adds inflateEnd at both sites. The trigger is a crafted PSD whose compressed channel data makes inflate return an error other than Z_OK/Z_STREAM_END.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because a resource (the zlib stream) is allocated for a bounded lifetime but not released after that lifetime ends, matching the missing-release pattern and its availability impact rather than a buffer error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the zlib stream initialized by inflateInit is never terminated on the error path (and normally after the loop). Trigger: crafted file causing inflate to fail. Consequence: the stream's allocated internal buffers are leaked per occurrence, enabling memory-consumption denial of service.

commit_msg:
It's possible for a request to invalidate a fscache_cookie will come in
while we're already processing an invalidation. If that happens we
currently take an extra access reference that will leak. Only call
__fscache_begin_cookie_access if the FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE bit
was previously clear.

Also, ensure that we attempt to clear the bit when the cookie is
"FAILED" and put the reference to avoid an access leak.

Fixes: 85e4ea1049c7 ("fscache: Fix invalidation/lookup race")
Suggested-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (test_and_clear_bit(FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE, &cookie->flags))', '\t\t\tfscache_end_cookie_access(cookie, fscache_access_invalidate_cookie_end);', '']}
description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been rated as problematic. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file fs/fscache/cookie.c of the component IPsec. The manipulation leads to memory leak. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The associated identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211931.

code_evidence: In the FAILED state the machine only relinquishes or withdraws when n_accesses is zero and a DO_RELINQUISH/DO_WITHDRAW bit is set; it does not clear FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE or end the access reference taken when invalidation began.
The added block at lines 66-67 clears DO_INVALIDATE and calls fscache_end_cookie_access, releasing the extra access reference; without it that reference is never dropped.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is failure to release a tracked resource (the access reference) after its effective lifetime, matching CWE-401's missing-release semantics. It is not an out-of-bounds or use-after-free issue; the leak directly causes the cookie to remain indefinitely accessible.

evidence_lines.code:
if (test_and_clear_bit(FSCACHE_COOKIE_DO_INVALIDATE, &cookie->flags))
fscache_end_cookie_access(cookie, fscache_access_invalidate_cookie_end);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the FAILED state path breaks out without balancing the access reference acquired for a pending invalidation. Trigger: a request invalidates a cookie while an invalidation is already in progress, leaving the DO_INVALIDATE bit set and the extra access reference held. Consequence: the reference is leaked, keeping the cookie's access count nonzero so relinquish/withdraw processing stalls.

commit_msg:
[media] media: info leak in __media_device_enum_links()

These structs have holes and reserved struct members which aren't
cleared.  I've added a memset() so we don't leak stack information.

Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Laurent Pinchart <laurent.pinchart@ideasonboard.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\t\tmemset(&pad, 0, sizeof(pad));', '\t\t\tmemset(&link, 0, sizeof(link));']}
description: drivers/media/media-device.c in the Linux kernel before 3.11, as used in Android before 2016-08-05 on Nexus 5 and 7 (2013) devices, does not properly initialize certain data structures, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information via a crafted application, aka Android internal bug 28750150 and Qualcomm internal bug CR570757, a different vulnerability than CVE-2014-1739.

code_evidence: Stack struct media_pad_desc pad is declared at [11] and passed uninitialized to media_device_kpad_to_upad at [12], which fills only selected members; copy_to_user at [13] copies sizeof(pad) bytes, including padding and reserved fields that were never written.

Similarly, stack struct media_link_desc link is declared at [21] and only .source [24,25], .sink [26,27] and .flags [28] are assigned before the full sizeof(*ulink) buffer is copied to user space at [29], leaving padding and reserved members with stale stack contents.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function explicitly transfers partially initialized structures to an unprivileged user, exposing sensitive stack data; this is a direct information-exposure mistake, matching CWE-200. It is not an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) since the copied region is within the struct's bounds; the flaw is missing initialization.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: stack-allocated descriptor structs are only partially initialized and then copied whole to user space. Trigger: any local process calling the media links enumeration ioctl with pad/link buffers. Consequence: uninitialized stack bytes (padding and reserved members) are disclosed to the caller, leaking kernel memory.

commit_msg: Fix bug #79465 - use unsigneds as indexes.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t*dest = os_toebcdic[(char) php_htoi(data + 1)];'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t*dest = os_toebcdic[(unsigned char) php_htoi(data + 1)];']}
description: In PHP versions 7.2.x below 7.2.30, 7.3.x below 7.3.17 and 7.4.x below 7.4.5, if PHP is compiled with EBCDIC support (uncommon), urldecode() function can be made to access locations past the allocated memory, due to erroneously using signed numbers as array indexes.

code_evidence: Line 9-10 accepts a '%XX' escape after isxdigit checks, then line 14 indexes os_toebcdic with (char) php_htoi(data + 1). Casting the conversion result to signed char allows negative index values, so the lookup table is read before its start.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read of os_toebcdic at a negative signed index, which is an out-of-bounds read past the start of the intended buffer, matching CWE-125. It is not merely an integer-sign issue; the supported consequence is the OOB read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the EBCDIC table index is computed from a signed char, so byte values above 127 become negative indexes. Trigger: urldecode() on a percent-encoded byte >= 0x80 when PHP is built with EBCDIC support. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read of os_toebcdic, potentially disclosing adjacent memory or crashing.

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.20.15. The nfc_llcp_build_tlv function in net/nfc/llcp_commands.c may return NULL. If the caller does not check for this, it will trigger a NULL pointer dereference. This will cause denial of service. This affects nfc_llcp_build_gb in net/nfc/llcp_core.c.

code_evidence: nfc_llcp_build_tlv returns a pointer that may be NULL; version_tlv is assigned here and its length is immediately accumulated without a NULL check.
lto_tlv is assigned from nfc_llcp_build_tlv and gb_len is updated without verifying lto_tlv is non-NULL.
wks_tlv is likewise assigned and used for length accumulation with no NULL check.
miux_tlv is assigned and miux_length accumulated without a NULL check.
The TLV pointers are passed directly to memcpy as source arguments; if any allocation returned NULL, memcpy reads from address 0.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences pointers (version_tlv, lto_tlv, wks_tlv, miux_tlv) that can be NULL in memcpy, matching CWE-476. This is a missing NULL check on a fallible allocator result, not an out-of-bounds or use-after-free issue.

lto_tlv = nfc_llcp_build_tlv(LLCP_TLV_LTO, &local->lto, 1, &lto_length);
gb_len += lto_length;

wks_tlv = nfc_llcp_build_tlv(LLCP_TLV_WKS, (u8 *)&wks, 2, &wks_length);
gb_len += wks_length;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller assumes nfc_llcp_build_tlv succeeds and never checks the returned pointers before using them. Trigger: an allocation failure inside nfc_llcp_build_tlv returns NULL, and execution continues to the memcpy calls. Consequence: a NULL source pointer is dereferenced in memcpy, causing a kernel crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
win: fix unsavory rwlock fallback implementation

Before this patch an uv_mutex_t (backed by a critical section) could be
released by a tread different from the thread that acquired it, which is
not allowed. This is fixed by using a semaphore instead.

Note that the affected code paths were used on Windows XP and Windows
Server 2003 only.

Fixes: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/515
PR-URL: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/516
Reviewed-By: Ben Noordhuis <info@bnoordhuis.nl>
Reviewed-By: Saúl Ibarra Corretgé <saghul@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  uv_mutex_lock(&rwlock->fallback_.write_mutex_);'], 'added_lines': ['  DWORD r = WaitForSingleObject(rwlock->fallback_.write_lock_.sem, INFINITE);', '  if (r != WAIT_OBJECT_0)', '    uv_fatal_error(GetLastError(), "WaitForSingleObject");']}
description: The uv_rwlock_t fallback implementation for Windows XP and Server 2003 in libuv before 1.7.4 does not properly prevent threads from releasing the locks of other threads, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (deadlock) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging a race condition.

code_evidence: The writer-lock acquisition relies entirely on uv_mutex_lock(&rwlock->fallback_.write_mutex_) to establish exclusive access to the shared rwlock state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the acquisition sequence fails to preserve exclusive, atomic access to a shared resource across concurrent threads, allowing an interfering sequence to violate exclusivity. It is a race condition rather than a simple deadlock (CWE-833): the deadlock is the consequence of the synchronization flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The mutex backing the fallback rwlock can be released by a thread other than the one that acquired it, so exclusivity over the shared lock state is not guaranteed. A concurrent interfering sequence can unlock or re-enter the lock, breaking atomicity and enabling deadlock (availability impact). The cause is the improper synchronization primitive, not the lock call itself; the trigger is concurrent thread interaction under the XP/2003 fallback path.

commit_msg:
PyACL - Fixing integer overflows that occur when resizing ACLs

Fixes #1700
CVE-2021-32559
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        unsigned short required_size = pacl->AclSize + sizeof(ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE) + (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid);', '        pacl_padded->AclSize = required_size;'], 'added_lines': ['        unsigned int required_size = pacl->AclSize + sizeof(ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE) + GetLengthSid(psid);', '        // max ACL size is USHRT_MAX', '        if (required_size > USHRT_MAX)', '            return PyErr_Format(PyExc_OverflowError, "%s: adding ACE would put ACL over size limit", funcname);', '        pacl_padded->AclSize = (unsigned short)required_size;']}
description: An integer overflow exists in pywin32 prior to version b301 when adding an access control entry (ACE) to an access control list (ACL) that would cause the size to be greater than 65535 bytes. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could crash the vulnerable process.

code_evidence: Line 19 computes the resized ACL size into an unsigned short: pacl->AclSize + sizeof(ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE) + (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid). Both the accumulator and the SID length are narrowed to 16 bits, so a sum exceeding 65535 wraps around to a small value.
Line 20 then passes this wrapped required_size to malloc, and line 25 stores it into pacl_padded->AclSize, so the allocated and recorded ACL size no longer matches the required size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size calculation wraps in an unsigned short, producing a smaller-than-expected value used for allocation and size assignment. This is integer wraparound affecting a memory-allocation size, not a missing bounds check alone.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned short required_size = pacl->AclSize + sizeof(ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE) + (unsigned short)GetLengthSid(psid);
pacl_padded = (ACL *)malloc(required_size);
pacl_padded->AclSize = required_size;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ACL size arithmetic is performed in a 16-bit unsigned type, so adding an ACE whose total would exceed USHRT_MAX wraps to a small value. Trigger: an ACL large enough that the required size exceeds 65535. Consequence: malloc allocates a too-small buffer and AclSize records the truncated size, leading to undersized allocation and potential out-of-bounds writes when the ACE is added, crashing the process.

commit_msg:
rxrpc: Fix race between conn bundle lookup and bundle removal [ZDI-CAN-15975]

After rxrpc_unbundle_conn() has removed a connection from a bundle, it
checks to see if there are any conns with available channels and, if not,
removes and attempts to destroy the bundle.

Whilst it does check after grabbing client_bundles_lock that there are no
connections attached, this races with rxrpc_look_up_bundle() retrieving the
bundle, but not attaching a connection for the connection to be attached
later.

There is therefore a window in which the bundle can get destroyed before we
manage to attach a new connection to it.

Fix this by adding an "active" counter to struct rxrpc_bundle:

 (1) rxrpc_connect_call() obtains an active count by prepping/looking up a
     bundle and ditches it before returning.

 (2) If, during rxrpc_connect_call(), a connection is added to the bundle,
     this obtains an active count, which is held until the connection is
     discarded.

 (3) rxrpc_deactivate_bundle() is created to drop an active count on a
     bundle and destroy it when the active count reaches 0.  The active
     count is checked inside client_bundles_lock() to prevent a race with
     rxrpc_look_up_bundle().

 (4) rxrpc_unbundle_conn() then calls rxrpc_deactivate_bundle().

Fixes: 245500d853e9 ("rxrpc: Rewrite the client connection manager")
Reported-by: zdi-disclosures@trendmicro.com # ZDI-CAN-15975
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Tested-by: zdi-disclosures@trendmicro.com
cc: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
cc: linux-afs@lists.infradead.org
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\trxrpc_deactivate_bundle(bundle);']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernel's RxRPC network protocol, within the processing of RxRPC bundles. This issue results from the lack of proper locking when performing operations on an object. This may allow an attacker to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel.

code_evidence: rxrpc_prep_call() looks up or creates a bundle and returns it at line 12; on success the code proceeds toward attaching the call/connection to that bundle.

rxrpc_wait_for_channel() at line 18 may wait on the bundle's channel_lock, and the wait_failed path at lines 30-32 removes the call from the bundle's wait list, showing the bundle is shared and concurrently mutated.

Before the fix, the out_put_bundle path only calls rxrpc_put_bundle(bundle) at line 25; the added rxrpc_deactivate_bundle() call (diff) drops the active count that prevents bundle destruction while this lookup/attach is in progress.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is a timing window where a shared bundle object is modified/destroyed by another concurrent code sequence before this sequence completes its attach, violating exclusivity/atomicity via improper synchronization (missing active-count protection). This matches CWE-362; the use-after-free is the consequence, not a separate primary weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
out_put_bundle:
rxrpc_put_bundle(bundle);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: rxrpc_connect_call() obtains a bundle reference but, before attaching a connection, releases it via rxrpc_put_bundle() without holding an active count, so a concurrent rxrpc_unbundle_conn() can observe no attached connections and destroy the bundle. Trigger: concurrent unbundle/lookup on the same bundle. Consequence: use-after-free of the bundle, potentially leading to kernel memory corruption or privilege escalation.

in usb_register_driver, there is already cleanup using driver_unregister.
No need call cpia2_usb_cleanup on module exit.

Reported-by: Hulk Robot <hulkci@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: YueHaibing <yuehaibing@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcpia2_usb_init();', '\treturn 0;'], 'added_lines': ['\treturn cpia2_usb_init();']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.1.6, there is a use-after-free in cpia2_exit() in drivers/media/usb/cpia2/cpia2_v4l.c that will cause denial of service, aka CID-dea37a972655.

code_evidence: cpia2_init calls cpia2_usb_init() and then unconditionally returns 0, discarding the init result. If cpia2_usb_init fails inside usb_register_driver, its error path already calls driver_unregister, freeing the driver's kobject memory; the module is still treated as successfully loaded, so cpia2_exit later calls cpia2_usb_cleanup and driver_unregister again on the already-freed driver object, producing the reported use-after-free in sysfs_remove_file_ns.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the freed driver object is referenced again during cpia2_exit/cleanup after the failed registration's internal driver_unregister already released it. This is a stale-pointer reuse, not merely a missing error check; the missing propagation of cpia2_usb_init's result is the cause enabling the later access to freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
cpia2_usb_init();
return 0;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of cpia2_usb_init() is ignored, so a failed registration is not propagated to module loading. Trigger: usb_register_driver fails internally and frees the driver memory while init still returns success. Consequence: module exit performs cleanup on the freed driver, causing a use-after-free read and denial of service.

commit_msg: erecursion detection
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      clone_info=CloneImageInfo(draw_info->image_info);'], 'added_lines': ['      clone_info=AcquireImageInfo();', '      clone_info->recursion_depth=draw_info->image_info->recursion_depth;']}
description: A vulnerability was discovered in ImageMagick where a specially created SVG file loads itself and causes a segmentation fault. This flaw allows a remote attacker to pass a specially crafted SVG file that leads to a segmentation fault, generating many trash files in "/tmp," resulting in a denial of service. When ImageMagick crashes, it generates a lot of trash files. These trash files can be large if the SVG file contains many render actions. In a denial of service attack, if a remote attacker uploads an SVG file of size t, ImageMagick generates files of size 103*t. If an attacker uploads a 100M SVG, the server will generate about 10G.

code_evidence: When an ImagePrimitive has text, CloneImageInfo copies the caller's image_info, preserving its recursion_depth, then the referenced file or inline data is read via ReadInlineImage or ReadImage without checking or incrementing recursion_depth before recursion. The patch replaces CloneImageInfo with AcquireImageInfo and explicitly propagates recursion_depth, enabling a depth check elsewhere; the function itself performs no validation of the self-referential input before recursing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function processes attacker-supplied SVG image references without validating the recursion/depth property required for safe processing, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The missing constraint on recursion_depth, not a memory-safety primitive, is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ImagePrimitive path accepts an SVG-embedded reference and reads it recursively without validating a recursion limit in this function. Trigger: a crafted SVG whose image reference resolves to itself. Consequence: unbounded recursion and repeated rendering, leading to segmentation fault and excessive /tmp file generation (denial of service).

commit_msg: Lock down search_path in SPI calls
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t/* Lock down search_path */', '\tres = SPI_exec("SET LOCAL search_path TO pg_catalog, pg_temp", 0);', '\tif (res < 0)', '\t\tereport(ERROR, (errcode(ERRCODE_INTERNAL_ERROR), (errmsg("could not set search_path"))));', '']}
description:
TimescaleDB, an open-source time-series SQL database, has a privilege escalation vulnerability in versions 2.8.0 through 2.9.2. During installation, TimescaleDB creates a telemetry job that is runs as the installation user. The queries run as part of the telemetry data collection were not run with a locked down `search_path`, allowing malicious users to create functions that would be executed by the telemetry job, leading to privilege escalation. In order to be able to take advantage of this vulnerability, a user would need to be able to create objects in a database and then get a superuser to install TimescaleDB into their database. When TimescaleDB is installed as trusted extension, non-superusers can install the extension without help from a superuser.

Version 2.9.3 fixes this issue. As a mitigation, the `search_path` of the user running the telemetry job can be locked down to not include schemas writable by other users. The vulnerability is not exploitable on instances in Timescale Cloud and Managed Service for TimescaleDB due to additional security provisions in place on those platforms.

code_evidence: Lines 16-17 capture the caller's user ID and security context, then switch execution to BOOTSTRAP_SUPERUSERID with SECURITY_LOCAL_USERID_CHANGE, running subsequent work with elevated privileges.
Lines 18-35 parse the caller-supplied subscription_cmd and accept only SUBSCRIPTION statement node types, but the command text is still executed unchanged.
Lines 36-38 connect to SPI and run the same subscription_cmd via SPI_execute while the elevated user ID is in effect, before privileges are restored at line 45.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-269 fits because the function assigns elevated privileges (BOOTSTRAP_SUPERUSERID) to execution of user-influenced SQL without constraining the privilege sphere via a locked search_path, enabling the caller to gain superuser capabilities. This is improper privilege management rather than merely a generic injection label.

evidence_lines.code:
GetUserIdAndSecContext(&save_userid, &save_sec_context);
SetUserIdAndSecContext(BOOTSTRAP_SUPERUSERID, save_sec_context | SECURITY_LOCAL_USERID_CHANGE);

parsetree_list = pg_parse_query(subscription_cmd);
}

if (SPI_connect() != SPI_OK_CONNECT)
res = SPI_execute(subscription_cmd, false , 0 );

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function executes caller-supplied SQL under BOOTSTRAP_SUPERUSERID without restricting the search_path, so object-name resolution inside the SPI-executed command can be influenced by schemas the caller controls. Trigger: a non-superuser able to create objects installs/uses the extension and supplies a subscription command whose unqualified references resolve to attacker-defined functions. Consequence: attacker code runs with superuser privileges, i.e., privilege escalation.

description: A heap-based buffer overflow was discovered in upx, during the generic pointer 'p' points to an inaccessible address in func get_le64().

code_evidence: Line 6 computes chains = &buckets[nbucket] and line 7 indexes buckets[m] with m = hash % nbucket before any check; nbucket is attacker-controlled from the hash table header. Line 8's bounds check occurs only after these pointers are formed.

Line 29 forms hasharr = &buckets[n_bucket] and line 41 reads buckets[h % n_bucket] before the n_bitmask check on line 30. Line 50 indexes hasharr[bucket - symbias], and the loop on lines 58-59 reads get_te32(hp) while comparing hp to file_image[file_size] rather than the hash table's actual end.

The weakness is missing length validation on attacker-controlled table counts leading to out-of-bounds memory access; the patch confirms this by adding !nbucket/!n_bucket/!n_bitmask guards.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: hash-table counts (nbucket, n_bucket, n_bitmask) from the ELF are used to compute offsets and index arrays before validating them against the file image bounds. Trigger: a crafted DT_HASH/DT_GNU_HASH with oversized counts or symbias. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads (and pointer arithmetic) past the file_image buffer, causing the reported heap-based overflow/inaccessible-address crash in get_le64.

commit_msg:
PS interpreter - check the Implementation of a Pattern before use

Bug #700141 "Type confusion in setpattern"

As the bug thread says, we were not checking that the Implementation
of a pattern dictionary was a structure type, leading to a crash when
we tried to treat it as one.

Here we make the st_pattern1_instance and st_pattern2_instance
structures public definitions and in zsetcolor we check the object
stored under the Implementation key in the supplied dictionary to see if
its a t_struct or t_astruct type, and if it is that its a
st_pattern1_instance or st_pattern2_instance structure.

If either check fails we throw a typecheck error.

We need to make the st_pattern1_instance and st_pattern2_instance
definitions public as they are defined in the graphics library and we
need to check in the interpreter.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ', '        pgs->color_component_map.color_map[k] = '], 'added_lines': ['', '        pgs->color_component_map.color_map[k] =']}
description: In Artifex Ghostscript through 9.25, the setpattern operator did not properly validate certain types. A specially crafted PostScript document could exploit this to crash Ghostscript or, possibly, execute arbitrary code in the context of the Ghostscript process. This is a type confusion issue because of failure to check whether the Implementation of a pattern dictionary was a structure type.

code_evidence: Line 4 casts pcc->pattern to gs_pattern2_instance_t* without checking that the pattern object is actually a pattern2 instance; line 5 immediately dereferences pinst->templat.Shading->params.ColorSpace, treating the cast result as valid.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-704 fits because the code converts a generic pattern pointer to a specific structure type without verifying the object's actual type, and the subsequent field access relies on that incorrect conversion. This is incorrect type conversion rather than a mere null check or bounds issue.

evidence_lines.code:
gs_pattern2_instance_t * pinst = (gs_pattern2_instance_t *)pcc->pattern;
gs_color_space * pcs = pinst->templat.Shading->params.ColorSpace;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function blindly trusts the runtime type of pcc->pattern and performs an unchecked downcast to gs_pattern2_instance_t. If a caller supplies a client color whose pattern is not a pattern2 instance (e.g., a different pattern type), the dereferences in lines 4-5 yield type-confused memory access, causing a crash or potentially exploitable behavior. The commit message confirms the missing Implementation type check was the trigger.

commit_msg:
Use req::strndup in php_mb_parse_encoding_list to prevent oob memory write.

Summary:
Fix out of bounds write access in mb_detect_encoding.  Using strndup in
php_mb_parse_encoding_list will cause strings with embedded nulls to be
unexpectedly shortened.  The expected length of the string is tracked in
value_length but since strndup may copy fewer characters when there are
mbedded null this can lead to oob writes into tmpstr.

I've found a couple other places in this file that use strndup and replaced
them with req::strndup as well.  The use of strndup in mb_send_mail also seemed
to be a leak.

This replaces uses of strndup with req::strndup which can handle embedded
nulls properly.

It looks like I also accidentally fixed t11337047 at the same time.  Adding it to the list of tasks.

Reviewed By: paulbiss

Differential Revision: D3360065

fbshipit-source-id: 99776cf9105e3789883380bf30240009eec52cec
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      to_r = strndup(to.data(), to_len);'], 'added_lines': ['      to_r = req::strndup(to.data(), to_len);', '  if (to_r != to.data()) {', '    req::free(to_r);', '  }']}
description: Out-of-bounds write in the (1) mb_detect_encoding, (2) mb_send_mail, and (3) mb_detect_order functions in Facebook HHVM before 3.15.0 allows attackers to have unspecified impact via unknown vectors.

code_evidence: to_len is taken from to.size(), then strndup(to.data(), to_len) is used to allocate to_r. The loop then indexes to_r[to_len-1] and writes to_r[to_len-1]='\0' while decrementing to_len, assuming the copied buffer is exactly to_len bytes. If to contains an embedded null, strndup stops early and returns a shorter allocation, so the indexed writes at high offsets exceed the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the trimming loop writes past the end of the heap buffer returned by strndup; the write offset is derived from the original length rather than the actual allocated length.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code assumes strndup copies to_len bytes, but strndup truncates at the first embedded null. Trigger: a 'To' value containing an embedded null byte. The trimming loop then writes to_r[to_len-1] beyond the shorter allocation, causing an out-of-bounds write and potential memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Fixed bit stream access to make sure that it is not read beyond the allocated size.

Bug: 25765591

Change-Id: I98c23a3c3f84f6710f29bffe5ed73adcf51d47f6
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    while (impeg2d_bit_stream_nxt(ps_stream,MB_ESCAPE_CODE_LEN) == MB_ESCAPE_CODE)'], 'added_lines': ['    while (impeg2d_bit_stream_nxt(ps_stream,MB_ESCAPE_CODE_LEN) == MB_ESCAPE_CODE &&', '            ps_stream->u4_offset < ps_stream->u4_max_offset)']}
description: libmpeg2 in libstagefright in Android 6.x before 2016-03-01 allows attackers to obtain sensitive information, and consequently bypass an unspecified protection mechanism, via crafted Bitstream data, as demonstrated by obtaining Signature or SignatureOrSystem access, aka internal bug 25765591.

code_evidence: The while loop calls impeg2d_bit_stream_nxt to peek MB_ESCAPE_CODE_LEN bits and flushes those bits each iteration, but the loop condition checks only the peeked value, never the stream offset against u4_max_offset. A crafted bitstream consisting of repeated escape codes keeps the condition true, so the loop repeatedly advances u4_offset past the allocated buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-254 covers bypass of security features; the out-of-bounds read leaks memory that can expose Signature-level data, enabling bypass of an unspecified protection mechanism, matching the described impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the escape-code loop lacks a bounds check on ps_stream->u4_offset relative to u4_max_offset. Trigger: attacker-supplied Bitstream data containing a long run of MB_ESCAPE_CODE values. Consequence: the bitstream accessor reads beyond the allocated buffer, exposing adjacent memory contents (sensitive information disclosure).

description: ihex.c in GNU Binutils before 2.26 contains a stack buffer overflow when printing bad bytes in Intel Hex objects.

code_evidence: The loop at 360-369 reads one byte past the option payload using *((char *) eopt + offset + len) for len from sizeof(*eopt) up to option->size; the byte is then printed via %c or octal escape.

The size check at 227-233 validates option->size against the section size and advances offset, but the read loop uses the signed char cast, so bytes 0x80-0xFF become negative and are mishandled by ISPRINT/printf.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a read/print operation on memory beyond the intended buffer boundary due to the signed-char datum and unbounded escape formatting, matching CWE-119 improper restriction of operations within memory bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the option data byte is loaded as signed char, and the loop reads within option->size but the signedness causes incorrect escape handling and out-of-bounds access when printing corrupt MIPS option bytes. Trigger: a crafted ELF with a MIPS options section containing non-ASCII bytes. Consequence: stack buffer overflow / memory access outside intended bounds while printing, potentially crashing readelf or executing code.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/1735
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel & (size_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel << (size_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel | (size_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel >> (size_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel ^ (size_t) (value+0.5));'], 'added_lines': ['      result=(MagickRealType) ((ssize_t) pixel & (ssize_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((ssize_t) pixel << (ssize_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((ssize_t) pixel | (ssize_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((ssize_t) pixel >> (ssize_t) (value+0.5));', '      result=(MagickRealType) ((ssize_t) pixel ^ (ssize_t) (value+0.5));']}
description: In /MagickCore/statistic.c, there are several areas in ApplyEvaluateOperator() where a size_t cast should have been a ssize_t cast, which causes out-of-range values under some circumstances when a crafted input file is processed by ImageMagick. Red Hat Product Security marked this as Low severity because although it could potentially lead to an impact to application availability, no specific impact was shown in this case. This flaw affects ImageMagick versions prior to 6.9.10-69.

code_evidence: Bitwise And: casts pixel and (value+0.5) to size_t before the & operation, so negative operator arguments are wrapped to large unsigned values.
LeftShift: shifts a size_t-converted pixel by a size_t-converted, unbounded shift count, allowing oversized shift amounts.
Or: size_t casts of pixel and (value+0.5) again reinterpret negative inputs as huge unsigned integers.
RightShift: size_t shift count derived from (value+0.5) can exceed the operand width.
Xor: size_t casts of pixel and (value+0.5) wrap negative values before the bitwise operation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an integer conversion/wraparound: values are assumed non-negative and cast to size_t, so negative inputs become out-of-range unsigned numbers, matching CWE-190's wraparound description. It is not merely a signedness mismatch; the wrapped value directly drives shift/bitwise computation and the resulting out-of-range result.

evidence_lines.code: result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel & (size_t) (value+0.5));
result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel << (size_t) (value+0.5));
result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel | (size_t) (value+0.5));
result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel >> (size_t) (value+0.5));
result=(MagickRealType) ((size_t) pixel ^ (size_t) (value+0.5));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The bitwise/shift operators in ApplyEvaluateOperator convert pixel and the user-supplied value to size_t, so negative or out-of-range operator arguments wrap to large unsigned values. For shifts this yields an out-of-range shift count; the result is then cast back to MagickRealType and used in pixel evaluation, producing undefined/incorrect values that can destabilize processing of crafted input.

commit_msg:
libarchive: Skip files with symlinks in parents

Currently, it is still possible that some files are extracted outside of
the destination dir in case of malicious archives. The checks from commit
21dfcdbf can be still bypassed in certain cases. See GNOME/file-roller#108
for more details. After some investigation, I am convinced that it would be
best to simply disallow symlinks in parents. For example, `tar` fails to
extract such files with the `ENOTDIR` error. Let's do the same here.

Fixes: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/file-roller/-/issues/108

The tar', "\t\t * cmd fails to extract such archives with ENOTDIR. Let's skip", '\t\t * those files here for sure. This is most probably malicious,', '\t\t * or corrupted archive.', '\t\t */', '\t\tif (_g_file_contains_symlinks_in_path (relative_path, extract_data->destination, symlinks)) {', '\t\t\tg_warning ("Skipping \'%s\' file as it has symlink in parents.", relative_path);', '\t\t\t\tif (load_data->error == NULL)', '\t\t\t\t\tg_hash_table_add (symlinks, g_object_ref (file));', '\tg_hash_table_unref (symlinks);']}
description: fr-archive-libarchive.c in GNOME file-roller through 3.38.0, as used by GNOME Shell and other software, allows Directory Traversal during extraction because it lacks a check of whether a file's parent is a symlink in certain complex situations. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2020-11736.

code_evidence: After computing relative_path from the archive entry [46,47], the code only rejects paths deemed external to the destination [54-59] and then builds file as a child of destination [60]; no check verifies that an intermediate parent component is a symlink, so an earlier-extracted symlink parent can redirect the later write.

When a symlink entry is created [216,217], the code records it in external_links only if _symlink_is_external_to_destination returns true [232,233]; symlinks pointing within the destination are not tracked, so downstream _g_path_is_external_to_destination cannot detect them as parent components.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-59 fits because the extraction accesses files by pathname without preventing symlink resolution in parent components, so the path resolves to an unintended resource outside the destination. This is link following during file access, distinct from merely computing a path string.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: extraction resolves archive-controlled paths without checking whether parent directories are symlinks, and only external-pointing symlinks are recorded. Trigger: a malicious archive first extracts a symlink parent, then a file whose relative path traverses that symlink. Consequence: the file write (g_file_replace or directory creation) follows the link and lands outside the destination directory.

description: WavPack 5.3.0 has an out-of-bounds write in WavpackPackSamples in pack_utils.c because of an integer overflow in a malloc argument. NOTE: some third-parties claim that there are later "unofficial" releases through 5.3.2, which are also affected.

code_evidence: Line 5 copies config->num_channels into num_chans with no upper bound; the pre-patch guard only rejects zero (lines 11-14), so arbitrarily large channel counts pass validation.

The stream loop at line 123 iterates on num_chans, calling realloc with (wpc->current_stream + 1) * sizeof(...) at line 127 and malloc at line 124 for each stream. Line 166 decrements num_chans and line 167 breaks only at NEW_MAX_STREAMS - 1, so wpc->current_stream and the multiplication operands can grow large before the post-loop check at line 186.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the missing bound on num_chans lets a size calculation used for realloc/malloc wrap to a small value, which is the integer overflow underlying the out-of-bounds write. It is distinct from a plain buffer overflow (CWE-787): the arithmetic wrap is the root cause, with memory corruption as the consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: num_chans is accepted without an upper bound, so the stream-allocation loop can drive current_stream and allocation-size arithmetic toward overflow. Trigger: a caller supplies a very large config->num_channels. The multiplication (current_stream + 1) * sizeof(wpc->streams[0]) can wrap to a small value, causing an undersized allocation followed by indexed writes to wpc->streams[current_stream], an out-of-bounds write.

commit_msg:
[misc] Fix use-after-free in net_bind()

Thanks to Ba Jinsheng for reporting this bug

description: OwnTone (aka owntone-server) through 28.1 has a use-after-free in net_bind() in misc.c.

code_evidence: servinfo is released via freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 48, but the loop pointer ptr is still used afterward: the check at line 49 (!ptr) and then getsockname(fd, ptr->ai_addr, &ptr->ai_addrlen) at line 54 dereference ptr->ai_addr, which points into the freed addrinfo list.

The getsockname call writes into ptr->ai_addr/ai_addrlen memory belonging to the freed servinfo allocation; the subsequent error path at lines 55-58 does not fix the dangling access since the write already occurred.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because memory owned by servinfo is freed and then referenced/written through ptr->ai_addr after freeaddrinfo(). This is a genuine use-after-free, not merely a NULL/error-handling bug or an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: net_bind() frees the addrinfo list with freeaddrinfo() yet continues to use the loop's ptr->ai_addr as the output buffer for getsockname(). Trigger: any successful bind (ptr non-NULL after the loop) reaches line 54 and writes through the dangling pointer into freed memory. Supported consequence: memory corruption/UAF write, potentially crash or integrity impact depending on reuse of the freed chunk.
