commit_msg:
Treat usages of arguments.callee as unknown callsites

Summary:
arguments.callee in non-strict mode are indirect references to the current function. As such,
make sure that call site inference bails if there's any possibility such a reference is made. This
is inexact by nature, so the analysis needs to be conservative.

nocommit until a solution is decided.

Reviewed By: neildhar

Differential Revision: D44674327

fbshipit-source-id: c118b23d91ffe872e65dea0560b3c622802c2eef
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  // Non-strict functions can be aliased in multiple ways (', '  // arguments.callee, Function.prototype.caller etc). Do not try to identify', '  // the callsites for those.', '  if (!F->isStrictMode()) {', '    return false;', '  }', '']}
description: A use-after-free related to unsound inference in the bytecode generation when optimizations are enabled for Hermes prior to commit da8990f737ebb9d9810633502f65ed462b819c09 could have been used by an attacker to achieve remote code execution. Note that this is only exploitable in cases where Hermes is used to execute untrusted JavaScript. Hence, most React Native applications are not affected.

code_evidence: The loop walks F->getUsers() and only accepts users that are direct CallInst callsites, inserting them into callSites.
For CreateFunctionInst users, it inspects each sub-user; any non-CallInst or non-direct call makes it return false, otherwise the call is recorded.
Any other user kind (line 18-19) causes an immediate false return, so inference bails for unhandled aliasing forms.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit and description tie the unsound inference to a use-after-free exploitable for code execution, matching CWE-416's reuse of freed memory. The function itself performs the inference whose missing strict-mode guard is the root cause; the UAF is the downstream consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function infers callsites from use-def users without accounting for non-strict functions, whose arguments.callee/Function.prototype.caller can create indirect references. Trigger: a non-strict function whose callsite is inferred as direct while an indirect reference exists, so bytecode generation optimizes based on an unsound callsite set. Supported consequence: stale/incorrect optimization assumptions, enabling the use-after-free described for Hermes optimizations.

description: In SkSampler::Fill of SkSampler.cpp, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an integer overflow. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation. Product: Android Versions: Android-7.0 Android-7.1.1 Android-7.1.2 Android-8.0 Android-8.1 Android ID: A-78354855

code_evidence: When count exceeds kCount, the code computes size64 = sk_64_mul(count, sizeof(T)), narrows it to size_t, and only then checks size != size64 to call sk_out_of_memory(). The allocation size passed to sk_malloc_throw is this narrowed size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The multiplication of an attacker-influenced count by an element size is the classic integer-overflow-in-size-calculation pattern (CWE-190), which then yields an undersized allocation and out-of-bounds write. The check is on the narrowed value rather than the full-width product, so the overflow/wraparound is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the product of count and sizeof(T) is computed in 64-bit but cast to size_t and validated only after narrowing. If count is large enough that the multiplication or narrowing produces a small size, the equality check may not detect truncation consistently, and the subsequent loop constructs count T objects into a buffer sized for fewer elements, writing out of bounds.

commit_msg:
libxl: restore passing "readonly=" to qemu for SCSI disks

A read-only check was introduced for XSA-142, commit ef6cb76026 ("libxl:
relax readonly check introduced by XSA-142 fix") added the passing of
the extra setting, but commit dab0539568 ("Introduce COLO mode and
refactor relevant function") dropped the passing of the setting again,
quite likely due to improper re-basing.

Restore the readonly= parameter to SCSI disks.  For IDE disks this is
supposed to be rejected; add an assert.  And there is a bare ad-hoc
disk drive string in libxl__build_device_model_args_new, which we also
update.

This is XSA-266.

Reported-by: Andrew Reimers <andrew.reimers@orionvm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Ian Jackson <Ian.Jackson@eu.citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    char *common = GCSPRINTF("if=none,cache=writeback");'], 'added_lines': ['    char *common = GCSPRINTF("if=none,readonly=%s,cache=writeback",', '                             disk->readwrite ? "off" : "on");']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen 4.7 through 4.10.x. libxl fails to pass the readonly flag to qemu when setting up a SCSI disk, due to what was probably an erroneous merge conflict resolution. Malicious guest administrators or (in some situations) users may be able to write to supposedly read-only disk images. Only emulated SCSI disks (specified as "sd" in the libxl disk configuration, or an equivalent) are affected. IDE disks ("hd") are not affected (because attempts to make them readonly are rejected). Additionally, CDROM devices (that is, devices specified to be presented to the guest as CDROMs, regardless of the nature of the backing storage on the host) are not affected; they are always read only. Only systems using qemu-xen (rather than qemu-xen-traditional) as the device model version are vulnerable. Only systems using libxl or libxl-based toolstacks are vulnerable. (This includes xl, and libvirt with the libxl driver.) The vulnerability is present in Xen versions 4.7 and later. (In earlier versions, provided that the patch for XSA-142 has been applied, attempts to create read only disks are rejected.) If the host and guest together usually support PVHVM, the issue is exploitable only if the malicious guest administrator has control of the guest kernel or guest kernel command line.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only builds a qemu drive option string and does not itself expose sensitive information; the readonly flag omission is a missing security constraint leading to unauthorized write access, not an information disclosure.

description: Amanda 3.5.1 allows privilege escalation from the regular user backup to root. The SUID binary located at /lib/amanda/rundump will execute /usr/sbin/dump as root with controlled arguments from the attacker which may lead to escalation of privileges, denial of service, and information disclosure.

code_evidence: The program selects dump_program based on argv[0] (the xfsdump branch at line 54-55 assigns XFSDUMP) without validating options in this branch; the else chain leads to other dump programs.
The remaining argv elements are appended as individual strings via quote_string and joined into cmdline, but the actual execution uses argv directly.
execve(dump_program, argv, env) executes the chosen program as root (after become_root at lines 40-42) passing attacker-controlled argv, so arguments are not neutralized before execution.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function builds and executes a command (execve) using externally influenced argv without neutralizing special elements, matching CWE-77 command injection. The missing validate_xfsdump_options call in the xfsdump branch is the specific neutralization gap; this is a command-language injection rather than a shell-string injection.

evidence_lines.code: execve(dump_program, argv, env);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the SUID rundump binary becomes root and then execve's a dump program with attacker-supplied argv, without validating the xfsdump option set in the xfsdump branch. Trigger: a regular user invokes rundump with a crafted argv selecting xfsdump and injecting options that the downstream dump/xfsdump interprets as commands or privileged operations. Consequence: privilege escalation to root, denial of service, or information disclosure.

commit_msg:
driver: secure: use consttime_memequal for memory comparison

Do  not  use memcmp() to compare security critical data, such as
cryptographic secrets, because the required CPU time depends on the
number of equal bytes.
Instead, a function that performs comparisons in constant time is required.
Warning: consttime_memequal returns 0 if data are NOT equal, and 1 if they are
equal.

Signed-off-by: Eugen Hristev <eugen.hristev@microchip.com>
Reviewed-by: Nicolas Ferre <nicolas.ferre@microchip.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (memcmp(cmac, computed_cmac, AT91_AES_BLOCK_SIZE_BYTE))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!consttime_memequal(cmac, computed_cmac, AT91_AES_BLOCK_SIZE_BYTE))']}
description: A timing side channel was discovered in AT91bootstrap before 3.9.2. It can be exploited by attackers with physical access to forge CMAC values and subsequently boot arbitrary code on an affected system.

code_evidence: cmac points at the stored CMAC appended after the padded data (line 17), and line 18 compares it against computed_cmac with memcmp over AT91_AES_BLOCK_SIZE_BYTE; on any mismatch line 19 jumps to exit, so the function returns -1 and skips decryption. The comparison result therefore directly controls a distinct success/failure path observable by the caller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The memcmp-based tag check makes the function's timing and response depend on how much of the supplied CMAC matches the computed one, an observable discrepancy exploitable to recover or forge the authentication value; CWE-203 captures this observable behavioral difference. It is distinct from a missing check, since a comparison is present but implemented non-constant-time.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the CMAC tag check uses memcmp, whose execution time depends on the number of leading equal bytes. Trigger: an attacker who can supply crafted data and observe the time until the failure return can iteratively guess the expected CMAC. Supported consequence: the CMAC comparison leaks information about the secret tag, enabling forgery of CMAC values and acceptance of attacker-chosen code.

commit_msg: x B1101, AVI: fix crash with some invalid streams
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (Size_Complete%2 && !IsNotWordAligned)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (Size_Complete%2 && !IsNotWordAligned && File_Offset+Buffer_Offset+Element_Offset+Size_Complete<File_Size)']}

commit_msg:
Since the tee subsystem does not keep a strong reference to its idle
shared memory buffers, it races with other threads that try to destroy a
shared memory through a close of its dma-buf fd or by unmapping the
memory.

In tee_shm_get_from_id() when a lookup in teedev->idr has been
successful, it is possible that the tee_shm is in the dma-buf teardown
path, but that path is blocked by the teedev mutex. Since we don't have
an API to tell if the tee_shm is in the dma-buf teardown path or not we
must find another way of detecting this condition.

Fix this by doing the reference counting directly on the tee_shm using a
new refcount_t refcount field. dma-buf is replaced by using
anon_inode_getfd() instead, this separates the life-cycle of the
underlying file from the tee_shm. tee_shm_put() is updated to hold the
mutex when decreasing the refcount to 0 and then remove the tee_shm from
teedev->idr before releasing the mutex. This means that the tee_shm can
never be found unless it has a refcount larger than 0.

Fixes: 967c9cca2cc5 ("tee: generic TEE subsystem")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Reviewed-by: Lars Persson <larper@axis.com>
Reviewed-by: Sumit Garg <sumit.garg@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Patrik Lantz <patrik.lantz@axis.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void tee_shm_release(struct tee_shm *shm)', '\tstruct tee_device *teedev = shm->ctx->teedev;', '', '\tif (shm->flags & TEE_SHM_DMA_BUF) {', '\t\tmutex_lock(&teedev->mutex);', '\t\tidr_remove(&teedev->idr, shm->id);', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&teedev->mutex);', '\t}', ''], 'added_lines': ['static void tee_shm_release(struct tee_device *teedev, struct tee_shm *shm)']}
description: A use-after-free exists in drivers/tee/tee_shm.c in the TEE subsystem in the Linux kernel through 5.15.11. This occurs because of a race condition in tee_shm_get_from_id during an attempt to free a shared memory object.

code_evidence: tee_shm_release removes the shared memory from teedev->idr under teedev->mutex, but that removal happens only in the release path, after the object is already being torn down.
The final teardown (teedev_ctx_put, kfree(shm), tee_device_put) is not synchronized with the idr removal, so another thread can still find the shm via idr lookup while it is being freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's idr removal and object teardown form a concurrent sequence lacking exclusive access to the shared shm/idr state, enabling a timing window where an interfering lookup accesses the resource mid-teardown, matching CWE-362.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the teedev->idr lookup and the tee_shm teardown are not made mutually exclusive, because the shm is removed from the idr only inside the release path while a concurrent lookup can still find it. Trigger: a thread calls tee_shm_get_from_id during a close/unmap of the same shm. Consequence: the lookup returns a shm that is concurrently freed, giving a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
[folly] Add additional overflow checks to IOBuf - CVE-2021-24036

Summary:
As per title

CVE-2021-24036

Reviewed By: jan

Differential Revision: D27938605

fbshipit-source-id: 7481c54ae6fbb7b67b15b3631d5357c2f7043f9c

description: Passing an attacker controlled size when creating an IOBuf could cause integer overflow, leading to an out of bounds write on the heap with the possibility of remote code execution. This issue affects versions of folly prior to v2021.07.22.00. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 4.80.5, all versions between 4.81.0 and 4.102.1, all versions between 4.103.0 and 4.113.0, and versions 4.114.0, 4.115.0, 4.116.0, 4.117.0, 4.118.0 and 4.118.1.

code_evidence: The DCHECK at [10,11,12] only validates the userData/freeFn/STORE_SIZE relationship; it does not constrain the caller-supplied capacity, offset, or length, and DCHECK is compiled out in release builds.
At [27,28,29,30,31,32,33] the attacker-influenced capacity and offset are passed directly into the IOBuf constructor, which computes the buffer end from them without any prior bounds check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing constraint lets size arithmetic in IOBuf construction wrap, matching CWE-190's integer overflow/wraparound when a computed value is assumed valid. Contrast CWE-122 (heap overflow): the wraparound is the root cause, and the out-of-bounds write is its consequence.

InternalConstructor(),
packFlagsAndSharedInfo(0, &storage->shared),
static_cast<uint8_t*>(buf),

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: takeOwnership accepts attacker-controlled capacity/offset without validating them against kMaxIOBufSize or checking arithmetic on the pointer/size before constructing the IOBuf. Trigger: a caller passes a size near the integer maximum. The constructor's pointer/size arithmetic can wrap, producing an undersized allocation while the recorded length remains large, supporting an out-of-bounds heap write.

commit_msg:
Bug#24388746: PRIVILEGE ESCALATION AND RACE CONDITION USING CREATE TABLE

During REPAIR TABLE of a MyISAM table, a temporary data file (.TMD)
is created. When repair finishes, this file is renamed to the original
.MYD file. The problem was that during this rename, we copied the
stats from the old file to the new file with chmod/chown. If a user
managed to replace the temporary file before chmod/chown was executed,
it was possible to get an arbitrary file with the privileges of the
mysql user.

This patch fixes the problem by not copying stats from the old
file to the new file. This is not needed as the new file was
created with the correct stats. This fix only changes server
behavior - external utilities such as myisamchk still does
chmod/chown.

No test case provided since the problem involves synchronization
with file system operations.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t      char * name, int rep_quick)', '\t\t\t    (param->testflag & T_BACKUP_DATA ?', '\t\t\t     MYF(MY_REDEL_MAKE_BACKUP): MYF(0))) ||'], 'added_lines': ['\t      char * name, int rep_quick, my_bool no_copy_stat)', '      myf flags= 0;', '      if (param->testflag & T_BACKUP_DATA)', '        flags |= MY_REDEL_MAKE_BACKUP;', '      if (no_copy_stat)', '        flags |= MY_REDEL_NO_COPY_STAT;', '                            flags) ||']}
description: Race condition in Oracle MySQL before 5.5.52, 5.6.x before 5.6.33, 5.7.x before 5.7.15, and 8.x before 8.0.1; MariaDB before 5.5.52, 10.0.x before 10.0.28, and 10.1.x before 10.1.18; Percona Server before 5.5.51-38.2, 5.6.x before 5.6.32-78-1, and 5.7.x before 5.7.14-8; and Percona XtraDB Cluster before 5.5.41-37.0, 5.6.x before 5.6.32-25.17, and 5.7.x before 5.7.14-26.17 allows local users with certain permissions to gain privileges by leveraging use of my_copystat by REPAIR TABLE to repair a MyISAM table.

code_evidence: After a successful repair, the code closes the temporary file, resets new_file to -1, and then calls change_to_newfile(share->data_file_name, MI_NAME_DEXT, DATA_TMP_EXT, ...) to rename the .TMD temp file over the .MYD data file; on this pre-patch path the rename is performed without any no-copy-stat protection and no atomicity guarantee between closing the temp file and the rename.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is CWE-362: a shared filesystem resource (the temp file path) is accessed in a non-atomic close-then-rename sequence, and an interfering code sequence can modify it in the timing window. The patch adds a no_copy_stat flag to change_to_newfile to avoid the vulnerable stat copy, confirming the race on the shared path rather than a mere path-traversal issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the temp file is closed and then separately renamed over the original data file, with no exclusive access to the temp file path during that window; the rename helper also copies old-file stats (chmod/chown) onto the new file. Trigger: a concurrent local user replaces the .TMD path between the close and the rename/stat-copy. Consequence: the attacker-chosen file receives the mysql user's ownership/permissions, enabling privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
When running concurrent iptables rules replacement with data, the per CPU
sequence count is checked after the assignment of the new information.
The sequence count is used to synchronize with the packet path without the
use of any explicit locking. If there are any packets in the packet path using
the table information, the sequence count is incremented to an odd value and
is incremented to an even after the packet process completion.

The new table value assignment is followed by a write memory barrier so every
CPU should see the latest value. If the packet path has started with the old
table information, the sequence counter will be odd and the iptables
replacement will wait till the sequence count is even prior to freeing the
old table info.

However, this assumes that the new table information assignment and the memory
barrier is actually executed prior to the counter check in the replacement
thread. If CPU decides to execute the assignment later as there is no user of
the table information prior to the sequence check, the packet path in another
CPU may use the old table information. The replacement thread would then free
the table information under it leading to a use after free in the packet
processing context-

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual
address 000000000000008e
pc : ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
lr : ip6t_do_table+0x5b8/0x89c
ip6t_do_table+0x5d0/0x89c
ip6table_filter_hook+0x24/0x30
nf_hook_slow+0x84/0x120
ip6_input+0x74/0xe0
ip6_rcv_finish+0x7c/0x128
ipv6_rcv+0xac/0xe4
__netif_receive_skb+0x84/0x17c
process_backlog+0x15c/0x1b8
napi_poll+0x88/0x284
net_rx_action+0xbc/0x23c
__do_softirq+0x20c/0x48c

This could be fixed by forcing instruction order after the new table
information assignment or by switching to RCU for the synchronization.

Fixes: 80055dab5de0 ("netfilter: x_tables: make xt_replace_table wait until old rules are not used anymore")
Reported-by: Sean Tranchetti <stranche@codeaurora.org>
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Subash Abhinov Kasiviswanathan <subashab@codeaurora.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

description: An issue was discovered in netfilter in the Linux kernel before 5.10. There can be a use-after-free in the packet processing context, because the per-CPU sequence count is mishandled during concurrent iptables rules replacement. This could be exploited with the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability in an unprivileged namespace. NOTE: cc00bca was reverted in 5.12.

uwbd_start() calls kthread_run() and checks that the return value is

commit_msg:
Unsquashfs: additional write outside destination directory exploit fix

An issue on github (https://github.com/plougher/squashfs-tools/issues/72)
showed how some specially crafted Squashfs filesystems containing
invalid file names (with '/' and '..') can cause Unsquashfs to write
files outside of the destination directory.

Since then it has been shown that specially crafted Squashfs filesystems
that contain a symbolic link pointing outside of the destination directory,
coupled with an identically named file within the same directory, can
cause Unsquashfs to write files outside of the destination directory.

Specifically the symbolic link produces a pathname pointing outside
of the destination directory, which is then followed when writing the
duplicate identically named file within the directory.

This commit fixes this exploit by explictly checking for duplicate
filenames within a directory.  As directories in v2.1, v3.x, and v4.0
filesystems are sorted, this is achieved by checking for consecutively
identical filenames.  Additionally directories are checked to
ensure they are sorted, to avoid attempts to evade the duplicate
check.

Version 1.x and 2.0 filesystems (where the directories were unsorted)
are sorted and then the above duplicate filename check is applied.

Signed-off-by: Phillip Lougher <phillip@squashfs.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif(sBlk_3->s_minor == 0)', '\t\tneeds_sorting = TRUE;', '']}
description: squashfs_opendir in unsquash-2.c in Squashfs-Tools 4.5 allows Directory Traversal, a different vulnerability than CVE-2021-40153. A squashfs filesystem that has been crafted to include a symbolic link and then contents under the same filename in a filesystem can cause unsquashfs to first create the symbolic link pointing outside the expected directory, and then the subsequent write operation will cause the unsquashfs process to write through the symbolic link elsewhere in the filesystem.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function only reads a v2 superblock and sets needs_sorting for minor version 0; it contains no file access, symlink handling, or directory traversal logic that directly supports link following.

commit_msg:
Fix qpress directory traversal vulnerability (#6)

A bad actor user can prepare the payload as:

```
mkdir -p AAAAAAAAA/secure_file_priv_dir
touch AAAAAAAAA/secure_file_priv_dir/evil.so
qpress -r AAAAAAAAA payload.qp
Then edit the payload.qp in a hex editor or sed to replace AAAAAAAAA with ../../../
(example: sed -i 's/AAAAAAAAA/..\/..\/..\//' payload.qp)
```

Fix bug by checking the directory and reject the command if find the attempt to traversal

Test: see example above and try to reproduce it. Before fix you can observe

commit_msg:
mm/demotion: fix NULL vs IS_ERR checking in memory_tier_init

alloc_memory_type() returns error pointers on error instead of NULL.  Use
IS_ERR() to check the return value to fix this.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20221110030751.1627266-1-linmq006@gmail.com
Fixes: 7b88bda3761b ("mm/demotion/dax/kmem: set node's abstract distance to MEMTIER_DEFAULT_DAX_ADISTANCE")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: "Huang, Ying" <ying.huang@intel.com>
Cc: Aneesh Kumar K.V <aneesh.kumar@linux.ibm.com>
Cc: Wei Xu <weixugc@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (!default_dram_type)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (IS_ERR(default_dram_type))']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 6.2, mm/memory-tiers.c misinterprets the alloc_memory_type return value (expects it to be NULL in the error case, whereas it is actually an error pointer). NOTE: this is disputed by third parties because there are no realistic cases in which a user can cause the alloc_memory_type error case to be reached.

code_evidence: alloc_memory_type() is called and its result stored in default_dram_type; the code then tests only `!default_dram_type` before panicking, so an error pointer returned by the allocator passes the check as non-NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the guard fails to detect the error condition, allowing a pointer that is not a valid object to be dereferenced later. This is a NULL/error-pointer check flaw; it is not a missing NULL check but a wrong error-encoding test.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of alloc_memory_type() is checked against NULL rather than with IS_ERR(), although the callee returns ERR_PTR() values on failure. Trigger: an allocation failure inside alloc_memory_type() yields an error pointer that survives the guard at line 15. Consequence: the invalid pointer is treated as a valid memory tier and used by later initialization, leading to an invalid dereference/crash rather than the intended panic; user reachability is limited, as the description notes.

commit_msg:
Track byteSize of HeaderMap internally.

Introduces a cached byte size updated internally in HeaderMap. The value
is stored as an optional, and is cleared whenever a non-const pointer or
reference to a HeaderEntry is accessed. The cached value can be set with
refreshByteSize() which performs an iteration over the HeaderMap to sum
the size of each key and value in the HeaderMap.

Signed-off-by: Asra Ali <asraa@google.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    appendToHeader(entry->value(), buf);'], 'added_lines': ['    const uint64_t added_size = appendToHeader(entry->value(), buf);', '    addSize(added_size);']}
description: Upon receiving each incoming request header data, Envoy will iterate over existing request headers to verify that the total size of the headers stays below a maximum limit. The implementation in versions 1.10.0 through 1.11.1 for HTTP/1.x traffic and all versions of Envoy for HTTP/2 traffic had O(n^2) performance characteristics. A remote attacker may craft a request that stays below the maximum request header size but consists of many thousands of small headers to consume CPU and result in a denial-of-service attack.

code_evidence: addCopy looks up an existing inline entry for key and, when found, formats value into a 32-byte stack buffer and appends it to the entry's value via appendToHeader before returning.
When no entry exists, a new HeaderString key and integer value are created and inserted with insertByKey; this path also grows the map without any size accounting or limit check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs resource-consuming header growth without enforcing a maximum, matching CWE-400's uncontrolled consumption of a limited resource. It is not a logic/authorization flaw; the supported impact is availability via resource exhaustion.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: addCopy grows header storage (append to existing value or insertion of a new entry) without tracking or bounding accumulated header size, so repeated calls with many small distinct keys or repeated appends expand the map unbounded. Trigger: a request carrying many small headers; consequence: CPU and memory consumption scaling with header count, enabling denial of service.

description: The IEEE 802.11 dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.11 and 2.0.x before 2.0.3 does not properly restrict element lists, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (deep recursion and application crash) via a crafted packet, related to epan/dissectors/packet-capwap.c and epan/dissectors/packet-ieee80211.c.

code_evidence: The TFS subelement branch sets s_offset/s_end from the packet-supplied len and loops while s_offset < s_end, calling add_tagged_field on each nested subelement.

The nested call result tlen only guards against zero; the loop advances s_offset by tlen without restricting which element IDs may be recursively processed, so attacker-chosen subelement IDs can re-enter nested dissection.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts structured packet input and fails to validate which element IDs are permissible for recursive processing, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The recursion depth is the consequence, not the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dissector does not constrain the set of subelement IDs accepted inside a TFS subelement before recursively calling add_tagged_field on packet data. Trigger: a crafted 802.11 packet with nested TFS subelements. Consequence: unbounded recursion leading to stack exhaustion and application crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
more bio_map_user_iov() leak fixes

we need to take care of failure exit as well - pages already
in bio should be dropped by analogue of bio_unmap_pages(),
since their refcounts had been bumped only once per reference
in bio.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (ret < local_nr_pages) {', '\tfor (j = 0; j < nr_pages; j++) {', '\t\tif (!pages[j])', '\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\tput_page(pages[j]);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct bio_vec *bvec;', '\t\tif (unlikely(ret < local_nr_pages)) {', '\t\t\tfor (j = cur_page; j < page_limit; j++) {', '\t\t\t\tif (!pages[j])', '\t\t\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t\t\tput_page(pages[j]);', '\t\t\t}', '\tbio_for_each_segment_all(bvec, bio, j) {', '\t\tput_page(bvec->bv_page);']}
description: The bio_map_user_iov and bio_unmap_user functions in block/bio.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.8 do unbalanced refcounting when a SCSI I/O vector has small consecutive buffers belonging to the same page. The bio_add_pc_page function merges them into one, but the page reference is never dropped. This causes a memory leak and possible system lockup (exploitable against the host OS by a guest OS user, if a SCSI disk is passed through to a virtual machine) due to an out-of-memory condition.

code_evidence: Lines 40-42 pin user pages via get_user_pages_fast into pages[cur_page..]; when the partial-failure check at line 43 fires, control jumps to out_unmap.

The out_unmap handler at lines 72-75 walks pages[] only up to nr_pages and stops at the first NULL entry; pages already merged into the bio by bio_add_pc_page (lines 55-58) are not in pages[] contiguously and their references are not released.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to release a bounded kernel resource (pinned page references) on an error path, and repeated invocation exhausts memory, matching CWE-400's loss-of-reference/error-condition resource-exhaustion pattern. It is not a bounds bug; the defect is uncontrolled accumulation of unreleased references.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path releases page references by scanning the flat pages[] array rather than the bio's segments, so pages whose references were consumed by bio_add_pc_page (consecutive small buffers merged into one bvec) are never put. Trigger: a SCSI I/O vector with small consecutive buffers in the same page followed by a get_user_pages_fast shortfall. The pinned page references leak, accumulating until memory exhaustion and potential system lockup.

commit_msg:
By validating length fields from server responses, out of boundary
accesses and endless loops can be mitigated.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Reviewed-by: Matthieu Herrb <matthieu@herrb.eu>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    if (f->length > nbytes)'], 'added_lines': ['    char *end = NULL;', '\tend = (char *)f + nbytes;', '\t    if ((char *)f + sizeof(*f) > end ||', '\t        f->length == 0 || f->length > nbytes)', '\t\tif ((char *)f + sizeof(*strf) > end)', '\t\t    goto out;']}
description: Multiple integer overflows in X.org libXi before 1.7.7 allow remote X servers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds memory access or infinite loop) via vectors involving length fields.

code_evidence: nbytes is derived from the server-controlled rep.length via a left shift; the guard rep.length < (INT_MAX >> 2) prevents the shift itself from wrapping, and nbytes is used to size the Xmalloc buffer.
strf->num_syms_supported is taken from the server response and multiplied by sizeof(KeySym) to accumulate size; no bound on num_syms_supported is enforced here.
size is checked against INT_MAX only after accumulation, so the per-iteration addition from line 55-56 can wrap before the check.
The wrapped num_syms_supported value also drives the length and memcpy size for the destination buffer, so an overflowed count yields an undersized allocation followed by an oversized copy.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer overflow in the size calculation used for allocation and copying, matching CWE-190. It is distinct from a simple out-of-bounds read because the arithmetic wraparound of the computed length is the root cause enabling the memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: size is accumulated from the untrusted num_syms_supported field using multiplication and addition without prior bounds, and the INT_MAX check occurs only after the sum. Trigger: a malicious X server returns a feedback with a large num_syms_supported. Consequence: the multiplication/addition wraps, size becomes small, a too-small buffer is allocated, and the later memcpy using the same count causes an out-of-bounds write.

description: Multiple integer overflows in the (1) sycc422_to_rgb and (2) sycc444_to_rgb functions in fxcodec/codec/fx_codec_jpx_opj.cpp in PDFium, as used in Google Chrome before 48.0.2564.82, allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted PDF document.

commit_msg:
The old ALLOCSP/FREESP ioctls in XFS can be used to preallocate space at
the end of files, just like fallocate and RESVSP.  Make the behavior
consistent with the other ioctls.

Reported-by: Kirill Tkhai <ktkhai@virtuozzo.com>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Sandeen <sandeen@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\tbf->l_start - XFS_ISIZE(ip), 0);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\tbf->l_start - XFS_ISIZE(ip),', '\t\t\t\tXFS_BMAPI_PREALLOC);']}
description: A data leak flaw was found in the way XFS_IOC_ALLOCSP IOCTL in the XFS filesystem allowed for size increase of files with unaligned size. A local attacker could use this flaw to leak data on the XFS filesystem otherwise not accessible to them.

code_evidence: When the requested start offset exceeds the current file size, xfs_alloc_file_space is called with the byte count bf->l_start - XFS_ISIZE(ip) and a final flag argument of 0, i.e. no XFS_BMAPI_PREALLOC.
Immediately after, iattr.ia_size is set to bf->l_start and passed to xfs_vn_setattr_size, which grows the inode to the unaligned requested size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The size passed to allocation (bf->l_start - XFS_ISIZE(ip)) and the size later exposed via iattr.ia_size derive from the same user-controlled value but are handled inconsistently, so the allocated extent range does not match the logical file size. This incorrect size/range calculation is the direct cause of the data exposure, fitting CWE-131 rather than a pure bounds-check weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the extent allocation is not marked as preallocation, so the newly allocated region is treated as real file data rather than unwritten extents, while the subsequent setattr extends i_size to the attacker-chosen bf->l_start. Trigger: a local user invokes the ALLOCSP/FREESP ioctl with an unaligned l_start beyond the current size. Consequence: the gap between the allocated blocks and the new i_size exposes stale on-disk blocks, leaking data not accessible to the attacker.

commit_msg:
net: ll_temac: Fix TX BD buffer overwrite

Just as the initial check, we need to ensure num_frag+1 buffers available,
as that is the number of buffers we are going to use.

This fixes a buffer overflow, which might be seen during heavy network
load. Complete lockup of TEMAC was reproducible within about 10 minutes of
a particular load.

Fixes: 84823ff80f74 ("net: ll_temac: Fix race condition causing TX hang")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v5.4+
Signed-off-by: Esben Haabendal <esben@geanix.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (temac_check_tx_bd_space(lp, num_frag))'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (temac_check_tx_bd_space(lp, num_frag + 1))']}
description: drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx/ll_temac_main.c in the Linux kernel before 5.12.13 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and lockup) by sending heavy network traffic for about ten minutes.

code_evidence: Line 10 sets num_frag to the number of fragments; line 13 checks BD space for num_frag + 1 buffers, the head descriptor plus one per fragment.
After stopping the queue, lines 17-19 re-check space using only num_frag, so the wake path can proceed with one fewer buffer than the loop in lines 41-44 needs to write.
The loop advances tx_bd_tail and writes cur_p->phys/len for each fragment, wrapping at tx_bd_num; without the +1 reservation the last write can overrun the BD ring.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Writes into a fixed-size descriptor array exceed its bounds because the size/space check is off by one; this is an out-of-bounds write stemming from an incorrect buffer-count check, matching CWE-120's unchecked-size write pattern.

evidence_lines.code:
num_frag = skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags;
if (temac_check_tx_bd_space(lp, num_frag + 1)) {

smp_mb();
return NETDEV_TX_BUSY;

for (ii = 0; ii < num_frag; ii++) {
cur_p = &lp->tx_bd_v[lp->tx_bd_tail];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The re-check after queue stop under-counts required descriptors by one, so a heavy-load race lets the fragment loop write past the TX BD array. This corrupts adjacent memory and can lock up the TEMAC device.

commit_msg:
Ensure raw tagnames are safe exiting internalEntityParser

It is possible to concoct a situation in which parsing is
suspended while substituting in an internal entity, so that
XML_ResumeParser directly uses internalEntityProcessor as
its processor.  If the subsequent parse includes some unclosed
tags, this will return without calling storeRawNames to ensure
that the raw versions of the tag names are stored in memory other
than the parse buffer itself.  If the parse buffer is then changed
or reallocated (for example if processing a file line by line),
badness will ensue.

This patch ensures storeRawNames is always called when needed
after calling doContent.  The earlier call do doContent does
not need the same protection; it only deals with entity
substitution, which cannot leave unbalanced tags, and in any
case the raw names will be pointing into the stored entity
value not the parse buffer.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    return doContent(parser, parser->m_parentParser ? 1 : 0, parser->m_encoding,', '                     s, end, nextPtr,', '                     (XML_Bool)! parser->m_parsingStatus.finalBuffer,', '                     XML_ACCOUNT_DIRECT);'], 'added_lines': ['    result = doContent(parser, parser->m_parentParser ? 1 : 0,', '                       parser->m_encoding, s, end, nextPtr,', '                       (XML_Bool)! parser->m_parsingStatus.finalBuffer,', '                       XML_ACCOUNT_DIRECT);', '    if (result == XML_ERROR_NONE) {', '      if (! storeRawNames(parser))', '        return XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY;', '    }', '    return result;']}
description: libexpat before 2.4.9 has a use-after-free in the doContent function in xmlparse.c.

code_evidence: doContent is invoked on the internal entity buffer (textStart..textEnd), and its result only returns early when parsing is suspended, without storing raw tag names.
On suspension, entity->processed is advanced and the function returns while raw tag-name pointers may still reference the entity text buffer rather than stable memory.

After entity processing completes, the final branch calls doContent again on the main buffer (s..end); if unclosed tags remain and storeRawNames was never called, raw names can point into a buffer that is later reallocated or changed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is use of memory through pointers that were not relocated to stable storage before the underlying buffer is freed or reallocated, which is a use-after-free (CWE-416). This is not merely a buffer over-read; the stale raw-name pointers are dereferenced after the buffer's lifetime ends.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the internalEntityProcessor path can return after doContent without storeRawNames, leaving raw tag-name pointers referencing the parse/entity buffer. Trigger: parsing is suspended during internal entity substitution and the subsequent parse leaves unclosed tags, so the buffer is later modified or reallocated. Consequence: dangling pointers to freed/reallocated memory are used, yielding a use-after-free.

commit_msg:
Disallow division by zero FPE in tf.raw_ops.SparseDenseCwiseDiv

PiperOrigin-RevId: 383959809
Change-Id: Ibe88458bdf66a686c93e354b8255dec94285c560
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': ['    bool op_is_div = false;', '    if (absl::StrContains(ctx->op_kernel().type_string_view(), "Div")) {', '      op_is_div = true;', '    }', '      if (op_is_div) {                                                         \\', '        OP_REQUIRES(ctx, dense_gathered_flat(i) != 0,                          \\', '                    errors::InvalidArgument(                                   \\', '                        "SparseDenseCwiseDiv cannot divide by zero,"           \\', '                        "but input dense tensor contains zero "));             \\', '      }                                                                        \\']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.SparseDenseCwiseDiv` is vulnerable to a division by 0 error. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/a1bc56203f21a5a4995311825ffaba7a670d7747/tensorflow/core/kernels/sparse_dense_binary_op_shared.cc#L56) uses a common class for all binary operations but fails to treat the division by 0 case separately. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit d9204be9f49520cdaaeb2541d1dc5187b23f31d9. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: dense_gathered_flat(i) = rhs_ref.coeff(idx) gathers the dense divisor values for each sparse index; output_values->flat<T>().binaryExpr(dense_gathered_flat, typename Functor::func()) then applies the operation (division for SparseDenseCwiseDiv) elementwise, using those gathered values as the divisor.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs elementwise division where the divisor comes from user-controlled dense tensor entries, and a zero divisor is not rejected, directly matching CWE-369 (divide by zero). This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read, which is already guarded by FastBoundsCheck.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The gathered dense operands are used as divisors in the binary expression without checking for zero. If the input dense tensor contains a zero at a gathered position, the elementwise division computes a division by zero, triggering a floating-point exception/crash (availability impact). The root cause is the missing zero check before the division; the crash is the consequence.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12996/PIMv2: Make sure PIM TLVs have the right length.

We do bounds checks based on the TLV length, so if the TLV's length is
too short, and we don't check for that, we could end up fetching data
past the end of the TLV - including past the length of the captured data
in the packet.

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Forcepoint's security
researchers Otto Airamo & Antti Levomäki.

Add tests using the capture files supplied by the reporter(s).

description: The PIMv2 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-pim.c:pimv2_print().

code_evidence: The option type and length are read from the packet into otype and olen; the only bound check is ND_TCHECK2(bp[0], 4 + olen), which validates the declared option region but not the minimum sizes required by each option type.
For PIMV2_HELLO_OPTION_HOLDTIME, EXTRACT_16BITS(bp) reads two bytes with no check that olen is at least 2.
For PIMV2_HELLO_OPTION_GENID, EXTRACT_32BITS(bp) reads four bytes with no check that olen is at least 4.
For PIMV2_HELLO_OPTION_REFRESH_CAP, the code dereferences *bp, *(bp+1) and EXTRACT_16BITS(bp+2), reading up to four bytes without verifying olen covers them.
bp is advanced by olen, so a too-short TLV causes the next iteration to parse bytes that belong to the following data, extending the over-read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory beyond the intended option/TLV boundary, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not a write or an integer overflow; the defect is an unchecked read length gated by attacker-controlled olen.

evidence_lines.code: bp += olen;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: per-option fixed-size reads are performed on bp using the TLV's declared olen without enforcing the minimum length each option requires. Trigger: a captured PIMv2 Hello packet whose option length is smaller than the field being extracted. Consequence: the parser reads past the end of the option and potentially past the captured packet buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
Fix packet length handling.

Treat the packet length as unsigned - it shouldn't be negative in the
file.  If it is, that'll probably cause the sscanf to fail, so we'll
report the file as bad.

Check it against WTAP_MAX_PACKET_SIZE to make sure we don't try to
allocate a huge amount of memory, just as we do in other file readers.

Use the now-validated packet size as the length in
ws_buffer_assure_space(), so we are certain to have enough space, and
don't allocate too much space.

Merge the header and packet data parsing routines while we're at it.

Bug: 12395
Change-Id: Ia70f33b71ff28451190fcf144c333fd1362646b2
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/15172
Reviewed-by: Guy Harris <guy@alum.mit.edu>

commit_msg:
Fixed bug #72227: imagescale out-of-bounds read

Ported from https://github.com/libgd/libgd/commit/4f65a3e4eedaffa1efcf9ee1eb08f0b504fbc31a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static inline int _setEdgePixel(const gdImagePtr src, unsigned int x, unsigned int y, gdFixed coverage, const int bgColor) '], 'added_lines': ['static inline int _setEdgePixel(const gdImagePtr src, unsigned int x, unsigned int y, gdFixed coverage, const int bgColor)']}
description: gd_interpolation.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.1.1, as used in PHP before 5.5.36, 5.6.x before 5.6.22, and 7.x before 7.0.7, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted image that is mishandled by the imagescale function.

code_evidence: Line 4 indexes src->tpixels[y][x] without any bounds check on x or y, directly reading a pixel from the source image buffer. Line 5 then uses that value to build the blended color, so the out-of-bounds read propagates into the returned result.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an unchecked array read of src->tpixels[y][x], which is exactly the out-of-bounds read pattern of CWE-125. The bug is a missing bounds constraint on the read, not a write overflow (CWE-787) or a null-pointer dereference.

evidence_lines.code:
register int c = src->tpixels[y][x];
c = c | (( (int) (gd_fxtof(gd_mulfx(coverage, f_127)) + 50.5f)) << 24);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: _setEdgePixel trusts caller-supplied x and y coordinates and dereferences src->tpixels[y][x] with no validation against the image dimensions. Trigger: a crafted image processed through imagescale produces edge coordinates outside the allocated row/column range. Consequence: reading memory past the intended buffer, supporting an out-of-bounds read (DoS or potential information disclosure).

description: Multiple integer overflows in the (1) pixops_composite_nearest, (2) pixops_composite_color_nearest, and (3) pixops_process functions in pixops/pixops.c in gdk-pixbuf before 2.33.1 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted image, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: The loop index i, x position, step values x_step/y_step, and coordinate variables xmax/xstart/xstop/x_pos/y_pos are all declared as int. x_step and y_step are computed as (1 << SCALE_SHIFT) / scale_x with double scale values, then used in coordinate and offset arithmetic.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an improper numeric calculation (integer overflow in coordinate/step arithmetic), which matches the CWE-189 Numeric Errors category rather than a bounds-checking weakness; the missing range constraint on scale-derived ints is the numeric error that enables the overflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: 32-bit int step and coordinate variables can overflow when scale_x/scale_y are small, making x_step/y_step or subsequent products exceed int range. Trigger: a crafted image yielding extreme scale factors. The overflowed coordinates feed INNER_LOOP pointer/index arithmetic, causing out-of-bounds access and a heap buffer overflow or crash.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['#ifdef LIBRAW_LIBRARY_BUILD', '  if(!image)', '    throw LIBRAW_EXCEPTION_IO_CORRUPT;', '#endif']}
description: An off-by-one error within the "LibRaw::kodak_ycbcr_load_raw()" function (internal/dcraw_common.cpp) in LibRaw versions prior to 0.18.7 can be exploited to cause a heap-based buffer overflow and subsequently cause a crash.

code_evidence: pixel is allocated with calloc(raw_width, 3*sizeof *pixel), giving a buffer of raw_width*3 bytes; its size depends on raw_width, not width/height.
The decode loop indexes pixel[width*2*(row & 1) + col], pixel[width + (col & -2)] and pixel[width + (col & -2)+1] using width, while the allocation uses raw_width.
The computed values are then written through image[row*width+col][c] inside FORC3, so the destination index depends on width and height.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function performs buffer indexing and writes based on unchecked dimension arithmetic, allowing memory outside the intended buffer to be modified. The related read at pixel[] is part of the same root cause, but the image[row*width+col][c] store is the out-of-bounds write that anchors this label.

evidence_lines.code:
pixel = (uchar *) calloc (raw_width, 3*sizeof *pixel);
merror (pixel, "kodak_c603_load_raw()");
FORC3 image[row*width+col][c] = curve[LIM(rgb[c],0,255)];

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the mismatch between the pixel buffer size (raw_width*3) and the index computations driven by width; when width exceeds raw_width or the row/column terms exceed the allocated region, the pixel reads go out of bounds and feed rgb values into the image write at [row*width+col][c]. The trigger is crafted dimensions/raw_width in the Kodak C603 path; the supported consequence is out-of-bounds memory access leading to corruption or crash.

description: Multiple heap-based buffer overflows in parser.c in libming 0.4.7 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (listswf application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted SWF file. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-9831.

commit_msg:
dmg: sanitize chunk length and sectorcount (CVE-2014-0145)

Chunk length and sectorcount are used for decompression buffers as well
as the bdrv_pread() count argument.  Ensure that they have reasonable
values so neither memory allocation nor conversion from uint64_t to int
will cause problems.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Wolf <kwolf@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Max Reitz <mreitz@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                if (s->sectorcounts[i] > DMG_SECTORCOUNTS_MAX) {', '                    error_report("sector count %" PRIu64 " for chunk %u is "', '                                 "larger than max (%u)",', '                                 s->sectorcounts[i], i, DMG_SECTORCOUNTS_MAX);', '                    ret = -EINVAL;', '                    goto fail;', '                }', '', '', '                if (s->lengths[i] > DMG_LENGTHS_MAX) {', '                    error_report("length %" PRIu64 " for chunk %u is larger "', '                                 "than max (%u)",', '                                 s->lengths[i], i, DMG_LENGTHS_MAX);', '                    ret = -EINVAL;', '                    goto fail;', '                }']}
description: Multiple buffer overflows in QEMU before 1.7.2 and 2.x before 2.0.0, allow local users to cause a denial of service (crash) or possibly execute arbitrary code via a large (1) L1 table in the qcow2_snapshot_load_tmp in the QCOW 2 block driver (block/qcow2-snapshot.c) or (2) uncompressed chunk, (3) chunk length, or (4) number of sectors in the DMG block driver (block/dmg.c).

code_evidence: The loop reads attacker-controlled sectorcounts[i] and lengths[i] from the DMG image without any upper bound ([94,98] and [105,109]). It then derives max_compressed_size from lengths[i] ([110,111,112]) and max_sectors_per_chunk from sectorcounts[i] ([113,114,115]).
These unbounded maximums directly size the allocation buffers at [120,121]: compressed_chunk = g_malloc(max_compressed_size + 1) and uncompressed_chunk = g_malloc(512 * max_sectors_per_chunk).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked sizes lead to out-of-bounds memory operations during decompression, i.e., reads/writes outside the allocated chunk buffers, matching CWE-119. The specific root cause is integer overflow/improper size validation (CWE-190/CWE-20), but the supported consequence is improper restriction of operations within memory buffer bounds.

evidence_lines.code:
s->compressed_chunk = g_malloc(max_compressed_size + 1);
s->uncompressed_chunk = g_malloc(512 * max_sectors_per_chunk);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: chunk length and sectorcount fields are trusted without range validation, so they flow into buffer-size computations. Trigger: a crafted DMG image with an oversized length or sectorcount. This causes integer overflow in the allocation size (512 * max_sectors_per_chunk or max_compressed_size + 1) and/or undersized decompression buffers, so later decompression reads/writes outside the intended buffer, leading to crash or possible code execution.

code_evidence: Line 48 obtains the page count and line 49 guards only pcount > 0, not the result of GetPage. Line 50 calls sourceDoc->GetPage(0) and immediately invokes GetMediaBox() on the returned pointer without any NULL check; the subsequent lines only read width/height from the resulting rect.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences a pointer expected to be valid without verifying it is non-NULL, matching CWE-476's null pointer dereference. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read, since the defect is the missing NULL check on the returned page pointer before method invocation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: When a crafted PDF parses successfully but GetPage(0) yields a NULL PdfPage pointer, the unchecked dereference at line 50 invokes GetMediaBox through a null pointer, causing undefined behavior and a segmentation fault (denial of service). The pcount > 0 guard does not ensure the page object exists.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-13042/HNCP: add DHCPv6-Data bounds checks

hncp_print_rec() validates each HNCP TLV to be within the declared as
well as the on-the-wire packet space. However, dhcpv6_print() in the same
file didn't do the same for the DHCPv6 options within the HNCP
DHCPv6-Data TLV value, which could cause an out-of-bounds read when
decoding an invalid packet. Add missing checks to dhcpv6_print().

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Bhargava Shastry,
SecT/TU Berlin.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (i + 4 > length)', '            return -1;', '        if (i + 4 + optlen > length)', '            return -1;']}
description: The HNCP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-hncp.c:dhcpv6_print().

code_evidence: The loop iterates while i < length, but immediately reads a 4-byte TLV header via EXTRACT_16BITS(tlv) and EXTRACT_16BITS(tlv + 2) without first verifying that i + 4 <= length.

value is set to tlv + 4 and later consumed by handlers (e.g., ip6addr_string over optlen bytes, ns_nprint up to value + optlen), and i advances by 4 + optlen, so a declared optlen exceeding the remaining buffer drives reads past cp + length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads past the intended buffer end (cp + length) when parsing TLV headers and option values, which is exactly CWE-125. It is not CWE-787 because no out-of-bounds write occurs; the defect is a read overrun.

evidence_lines.code: i += 4 + optlen;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing bounds checks on the DHCPv6 option header and on the declared optlen before dereferencing tlv/value. Trigger: an HNCP DHCPv6-Data TLV whose value ends mid-header or whose optlen overruns the declared length. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of packet memory during decoding, potentially crash or disclosure.

description: Integer overflow in the jpc_pi_nextcprl function in jpc_t2cod.c in JasPer before 1.900.20 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via a crafted file, which triggers use of an uninitialized value.

code_evidence: pi->xstep and pi->ystep are computed as hsamp/vsamp multiplied by (1 << (prcwidthexpn + numrlvls - 1)); the shift uses a signed int literal 1 and attacker-influenced exponent fields from the crafted codestream.
The same signed-int shift pattern recurs inside the rlvlno loop for xstep/ystep; these derived step values then drive the loops at [37,38,39,40] that advance pi->x/pi->y.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a signed-integer shift/multiply calculation whose result can wrap because the code assumes the computed step stays representable; that is CWE-190. The uninitialized-value use is the downstream consequence, not a separate memory-safety root cause here.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shift operand is a signed 32-bit int literal, so when (prcwidthexpn + numrlvls - 1) reaches or exceeds the int width the left shift overflows/wraps, producing a bogus or zero step. Trigger: a crafted JPC file with large precision/level fields. Consequence: corrupted xstep/ystep lead to invalid iteration/geometry, yielding use of uninitialized data downstream.

commit_msg:
Make extensions use a correct same-origin check.

GURL::GetOrigin does not do the right thing for all types of URLs.

BUG=573317

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1658913002

Cr-Commit-Position: refs/heads/master@{#373381}
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if (attached() && (params.url.GetOrigin() != url_.GetOrigin())) {'], 'added_lines': ['  if (attached() && !url::IsSameOriginWith(params.url, url_)) {']}
description: The Extensions subsystem in Google Chrome before 50.0.2661.75 incorrectly relies on GetOrigin method calls for origin comparisons, which allows remote attackers to bypass the Same Origin Policy and obtain sensitive information via a crafted extension.

code_evidence: Line 4 gates the origin check on attached() and compares params.url.GetOrigin() against url_.GetOrigin(); when the origins differ, lines 5-6 report a bad message to the render process host.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-284 fits because the origin-equality check is the access-control gate for extension view guest navigation; its incorrect comparison fails to restrict access to an unauthorized origin, permitting a cross-origin actor to reach protected content. This is an enforcement failure in the access check rather than an authentication flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the access decision relies on GURL::GetOrigin, which does not yield a correct origin for all URL types, so the equality comparison can treat distinct origins as matching. Trigger: a crafted extension navigation whose URL type makes GetOrigin return a misleading value. Consequence: the EVG_BAD_ORIGIN rejection is skipped, allowing a cross-origin navigation to proceed and enabling Same Origin Policy bypass and sensitive-information disclosure.

commit_msg:
x86/traps: Fix %dr6 handing in #DB handler

Most bits in %dr6 accumulate, rather than being set directly based on the
current source of #DB.  Have the handler follow the manuals guidance, which
avoids leaking hypervisor debugging activities into guest context.

This is part of XSA-260 / CVE-2018-8897

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    v->arch.debugreg[6] = read_debugreg(6);'], 'added_lines': ['    unsigned long dr6;', '', '    /* Stash dr6 as early as possible. */', '    dr6 = read_debugreg(6);', '', '    /*', '     * At the time of writing (March 2018), on the subject of %dr6:', '     *', '     * The Intel manual says:', '     *   Certain debug exceptions may clear bits 0-3. The remaining contents', '     *   of the DR6 register are never cleared by the processor. To avoid', '     *   confusion in identifying debug exceptions, debug handlers should', '     *   clear the register (except bit 16, which they should set) before', '     *   returning to the interrupted task.', '     *', '     * The AMD manual says:', '     *   Bits 15:13 of the DR6 register are not cleared by the processor and', '     *   must be cleared by software after the contents have been read.', '     *', '     * Some bits are reserved set, some are reserved clear, and some bits', '     * which were previously reserved set are reused and cleared by hardware.', '     * For future compatibility, reset to the default value, which will allow', '     * us to spot any bit being changed by hardware to its non-default value.', '     */', '    write_debugreg(6, X86_DR6_DEFAULT);', '    v->arch.debugreg[6] |= (dr6 & ~X86_DR6_DEFAULT);', '    v->arch.debugreg[6] &= (dr6 | ~X86_DR6_DEFAULT);']}
description: A statement in the System Programming Guide of the Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual (SDM) was mishandled in the development of some or all operating-system kernels, resulting in unexpected behavior for #DB exceptions that are deferred by MOV SS or POP SS, as demonstrated by (for example) privilege escalation in Windows, macOS, some Xen configurations, or FreeBSD, or a Linux kernel crash. The MOV to SS and POP SS instructions inhibit interrupts (including NMIs), data breakpoints, and single step trap exceptions until the instruction boundary following the next instruction (SDM Vol. 3A; section 6.8.3). (The inhibited data breakpoints are those on memory accessed by the MOV to SS or POP to SS instruction itself.) Note that debug exceptions are not inhibited by the interrupt enable (EFLAGS.IF) system flag (SDM Vol. 3A; section 2.3). If the instruction following the MOV to SS or POP to SS instruction is an instruction like SYSCALL, SYSENTER, INT 3, etc. that transfers control to the operating system at CPL < 3, the debug exception is delivered after the transfer to CPL < 3 is complete. OS kernels may not expect this order of events and may therefore experience unexpected behavior when it occurs.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function handles debug-register state synchronously on a single CPU exception path; it contains no concurrent code sequence or shared-resource synchronization, so CWE-362 is not supported.

commit_msg:
Trap for overly large input to XmlRPCPP which could cause problems with int <-> size_t conversions.

 - In XmlRpcClient, XmlRpcServerConnection and XmlRpcSocket, recognize when incoming or outgoing data is too large, generate an error and discard the data when practical.
 - Use the safe strtol() rather than atoi() to decode an incoming content-length header, and generate an error if the length is invalid or too large.
 - In XmlRpcUtil, prevent attempts to parse overly large XML input.
 - Add tests where they can reasonably be inserted into existing test routines.

Although this fix could be cleaner the update is written to make the update ABI compatible.

This fix addresses CVE-2020-16124 / Integer overflow in ros_comm.

Signed-off-by: Sid Faber <sid.faber@canonical.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  // Watch for integer overrun', '  if (s.length() > size_t(__INT_MAX__)) {', '    XmlRpcUtil::error("XmlRpcSocket::nbRead: text size (%u) exceeds the maximum allowed size (%s).",', '                      s.length(), __INT_MAX__);', '    s.clear();', '    return false;', '  }']}
description: Integer Overflow or Wraparound vulnerability in the XML RPC library of OpenRobotics ros_comm communications packages allows unauthenticated network traffic to cause unexpected behavior. This issue affects: OpenRobotics ros_comm communications packages Noetic and prior versions. Fixed in https://github.com/ros/ros_comm/pull/2065.

code_evidence: The loop repeatedly calls read() into a 4096-byte buffer and appends each chunk to the caller-provided std::string s via s.append(readBuf, n), with no bound on the accumulated length.
The loop exits only on wouldBlock or eof, then returns true; nothing checks whether s.length() has grown beyond a safe limit before returning success.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The patch adds exactly this guard (s.length() > size_t(__INT_MAX__)) to nbRead, confirming the function is where oversized input accumulates and where an int/size_t conversion overflow is possible. CWE-190 fits because a length value can exceed the integer representation assumed by downstream logic; it is not merely a buffer overflow (CWE-120), since the append is bounded per chunk but the total size is unchecked.

evidence_lines.code:
}
return true;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded accumulation of network input into s, whose length can grow past the range used for int/size_t conversions elsewhere. Trigger: an unauthenticated peer streams an arbitrarily large XML-RPC message. Supported consequence: the oversized length can overflow int<->size_t conversions and cause unexpected behavior/DoS; nbRead itself performs no size check.

commit_msg:
cifs: Fix use-after-free in SMB2_write

There is a KASAN use-after-free:
BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in SMB2_write+0x1342/0x1580
Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880b6a8e450 by task ln/4196

Should not release the 'req' because it will use in the trace.

Fixes: eccb4422cf97 ("smb3: Add ftrace tracepoints for improved SMB3 debugging")

Signed-off-by: ZhangXiaoxu <zhangxiaoxu5@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <stfrench@microsoft.com>
CC: Stable <stable@vger.kernel.org> 4.18+
Reviewed-by: Pavel Shilovsky <pshilov@microsoft.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tcifs_small_buf_release(req);'], 'added_lines': ['\tcifs_small_buf_release(req);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.0.10. SMB2_write in fs/cifs/smb2pdu.c has a use-after-free.

code_evidence: cifs_send_recv is called with rqst, whose rq_iov[0].iov_base points to req (set at line 38). After the send/recv completes, line 45 releases req via cifs_small_buf_release(req).
Subsequently, in the rc path line 48 and success path line 56, trace_smb3_write_err/trace_smb3_write_done dereference req->PersistentFileId, reading freed memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function frees req then dereferences it through req->PersistentFileId in the trace calls, which is exactly reuse of memory after it has been freed, matching CWE-416. The fix moves the release after the trace calls, confirming the ordering defect rather than an unrelated issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The request buffer req is freed immediately after cifs_send_recv returns, but the tracepoints later in both the error and success branches read req->PersistentFileId. Trigger: any SMB2_write call reaching the trace calls after the release. Consequence: use-after-free read (KASAN report in SMB2_write), potentially leading to memory corruption or crash.

description: In ImageMagick 7.0.6-1, a memory exhaustion vulnerability was found in the function ReadPCXImage in coders/pcx.c, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service.

code_evidence: Lines 126-131 read the attacker-controlled planes byte and only reject planes==0 or (bits_per_pixel*planes)>=64; there is no upper bound on planes itself before allocations.
Lines 149-154 read bytes_per_line and other header fields from the file without constraining their magnitude.
Lines 164-172 compute pcx_packets = rows*bytes_per_line*planes with only overflow sanity checks, not size limits.
Lines 173-184 pass the derived pcx_packets to AcquireQuantumMemory and AcquireVirtualMemory, so the allocation size is driven by unvalidated header values.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory based on attacker-controlled file metadata with no restriction on the resulting allocation size, matching CWE-770 (allocation without limits). This is distinct from an integer overflow: overflow checks exist, but the absence of an allocation cap is the weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the PCX header fields (planes, bytes_per_line, dimensions) are trusted to size allocations without a cap. Trigger: a crafted PCX/DCX file with large header values reaches AcquireQuantumMemory/AcquireVirtualMemory at lines 173-175. Consequence: excessive memory allocation, leading to memory exhaustion and denial of service.

commit_msg:
There is a small race window at snd_pcm_oss_sync() that is called from
OSS PCM SNDCTL_DSP_SYNC ioctl; namely the function calls
snd_pcm_oss_make_ready() at first, then takes the params_lock mutex
for the rest.  When the stream is set up again by another thread
between them, it leads to inconsistency, and may result in unexpected
results such as NULL dereference of OSS buffer as a fuzzer spotted
recently.

The fix is simply to cover snd_pcm_oss_make_ready() call into the same
params_lock mutex with snd_pcm_oss_make_ready_locked() variant.

Reported-and-tested-by: butt3rflyh4ck <butterflyhuangxx@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Jaroslav Kysela <perex@perex.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/CAFcO6XN7JDM4xSXGhtusQfS2mSBcx50VJKwQpCq=WeLt57aaZA@mail.gmail.com
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220905060714.22549-1-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\terr = snd_pcm_oss_make_ready(substream);', '\t\tif (err < 0)', '\t\t\treturn err;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\terr = snd_pcm_oss_make_ready_locked(substream);', '\t\tif (err < 0)', '\t\t\tgoto unlock;']}
description: A race condition flaw was found in the Linux kernel sound subsystem due to improper locking. It could lead to a NULL pointer dereference while handling the SNDCTL_DSP_SYNC ioctl. A privileged local user (root or member of the audio group) could use this flaw to crash the system, resulting in a denial of service condition

code_evidence: snd_pcm_oss_make_ready(substream) is called at line 15 before params_lock is acquired; the mutex is only taken at line 19. The shared runtime->oss state can be modified by another thread in between, and the make_ready result is used without holding the lock that protects the rest of the function.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 fits because the function fails to properly acquire the lock around the snd_pcm_oss_make_ready operation that accesses shared stream state, allowing a race. The weakness is improper lock coverage, not merely a generic race, since the rest of the function is correctly guarded by params_lock.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the readiness check/update of the OSS PCM stream is performed outside runtime->oss.params_lock, so a concurrent SNDCTL_DSP_SYNC or stream re-setup can change the stream state between the check and the locked section. Trigger: two threads racing through snd_pcm_oss_sync. Consequence: inconsistent OSS buffer state leading to a NULL dereference and denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fix - memory leak when deleting client from client list

Signed-off-by: Rob White <rob@blue-wave.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t// Reset custom and client_type', '', '\t\tclient->cid = safe_calloc(SMALL_BUF);'], 'added_lines': ['\t// Reset custom, client_type and cpi_query', '', '\tif (!client->cpi_query) {', '\t\tclient->cpi_query = safe_calloc(STATUS_BUF);', '\t}', '\tclient->cid = safe_calloc(SMALL_BUF);', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in the captive portal in OpenNDS before version 10.1.3. It has multiple memory leaks due to not freeing up allocated memory. This may lead to a Denial-of-Service condition due to the consumption of all available memory.

code_evidence: client_reset unconditionally overwrites client->token (line 13), client->custom (line 18), and client->client_type (line 19) with fresh safe_calloc allocations, and inside the cid block overwrites client->cid (line 29); none of the prior allocations referenced by these pointers are freed before reassignment, so the old buffers become unreachable.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Overwriting owning pointers with fresh allocations without releasing the prior memory is the classic CWE-401 missing-release pattern; the leaked buffers are never tracked again. This is not a use-after-free or double-free, since the old memory is simply orphaned rather than accessed or freed twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: existing heap buffers owned by the client struct are replaced by new allocations without a prior free, losing the only pointer to them. Trigger: repeated calls to client_reset (e.g., on client re-authentication or reset). Consequence: each reset leaks the previous token, custom, client_type and cid buffers, and repeated resets exhaust memory, supporting the described DoS.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12896/ISAKMP: Do bounds checks in isakmp_rfc3948_print().

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Kamil Frankowicz.

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [''], 'added_lines': ['\tND_TCHECK(bp[0]);', '\tND_TCHECK(bp[3]);']}
description: The ISAKMP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isakmp.c:isakmp_rfc3948_print().

code_evidence: Line 6 dereferences bp[0] before any bounds check when length == 1, and the check is evaluated after the pointer read.
Lines 10-12 only guard the later four-byte comparison by requiring length >= 4; they do not protect the earlier bp[0] access.
Line 13 reads bp[0] through bp[3] based on the length < 4 guard, but the function never verifies the captured buffer is at least 4 bytes long via ND_TCHECK.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads packet bytes without confirming the buffer extends that far, matching CWE-125's out-of-bounds read. The patch adds ND_TCHECK(bp[0]) and ND_TCHECK(bp[3]), confirming the missing length checks are the defect; this is a read, not a write (CWE-787).

evidence_lines.code: if(length == 1 && bp[0]==0xff) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is missing capture-buffer bounds validation: the code dereferences bp[0] (line 6) and bp[3] (line 13) relying only on the packet's declared length, not the actual captured data size. A truncated capture with a consistent length field triggers reads past the end of the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read.

commit_msg:
EogErrorMessageArea: Make sure error messages are valid UTF8

GMarkup requires valid UTF8 input strings and would cause odd
looking messages if given invalid input. This could also trigger an
out-of-bounds write in glib before 2.44.1. Reported by kaslovdmitri.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=770143

description: Eye of GNOME (aka eog) 3.16.5, 3.17.x, 3.18.x before 3.18.3, 3.19.x, and 3.20.x before 3.20.4, when used with glib before 2.44.1, allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds write and crash) via vectors involving passing invalid UTF-8 to GMarkup.

code_evidence: Line 11 escapes only caption via g_markup_escape_text, and lines 12-13 interpolate the escaped caption into the localized error string; this path is already markup-safe.

Line 14 duplicates error->message verbatim with g_strdup and lines 15-18 pass it as message_details into create_error_message_area, which later feeds GMarkup; no UTF-8 validation or sanitization is applied to this attacker-influenced GError message.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The supported consequence is an out-of-bounds write in the downstream GMarkup parser reached via unvalidated error->message, matching CWE-787. It is not merely improper input validation (CWE-20); the memory-corrupting write is the specific weakness enabled by the missing UTF-8 constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error->message is forwarded to GMarkup without enforcing valid UTF-8, unlike caption which is escaped. Trigger: a GError whose message contains invalid UTF-8 bytes reaches this function. With glib before 2.44.1, GMarkup processing of that invalid input can write out of bounds, causing a crash or memory corruption; the function itself performs no bounds handling.

commit_msg: Fix vulnerability around urls crafter as http://host/../secret.foo

description: Platinum UPnP SDK 1.2.0 allows Directory Traversal in Core/PltHttpServer.cpp because it checks for /.. where it should be checking for ../ instead.

The weakness is the flawed filter, not merely a generic file-access error.
