description: An issue was discovered in box_code_apple.c:119 in Gpac MP4Box 0.8.0, allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service due to an invalid read on function ilst_item_Read.

code_evidence: Line 9 calls gf_isom_box_parse(&a, bs); the return value e is checked, but a is not validated before line 10 dereferences a->size when e is falsy.
Lines 14-17 only handle the error path (e nonzero); when e is GF_OK but a is NULL, execution falls through to line 18, which dereferences a->size via ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences pointer a (a->size) while only the error code e is validated, which is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476). This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read because the failure is a missing NULL check, not a size/offset constraint violation.

evidence_lines.code:
e = gf_isom_box_parse(&a, bs);
if (!e && ptr->size < a->size) {

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a successful parse result is assumed to leave a non-NULL, so a->size is dereferenced at lines 10 and 18 without a NULL check. Trigger: a crafted ilst item where gf_isom_box_parse returns GF_OK but does not populate a. Consequence: invalid read and crash (DoS), matching the reported issue in ilst_item_Read.

commit_msg: fix Division by zero in XMenuWidget() of MagickCore/widget.c
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        if (selection_info.height == 0)', '          break;', '        if (selection_info.height == 0)', '          break;', '        if (selection_info.height == 0)', '          break;']}
description: An issue was discovered with ImageMagick 7.1.0-4 via Division by zero in function ReadEnhMetaFile of coders/emf.c.

code_evidence: In the ButtonPress branch, after clearing InactiveWidgetState, the code computes id=(event.xbutton.y-top_offset)/(int) selection_info.height, using selection_info.height as the divisor.
In the EnterNotify branch, id=((event.xcrossing.y-top_offset)/(int) selection_info.height) divides by the same selection_info.height.
In the MotionNotify branch, id=(event.xmotion.y-top_offset)/(int) selection_info.height again uses selection_info.height as a divisor.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly divides by a dimension value (selection_info.height) that can be zero, matching CWE-369's pattern of division by zero on a physical dimension. The patch adds height==0 guards before each division, confirming the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: selection_info.height is assigned from the computed height (line 81/100) and can be zero if the font ascent+descent yields zero. The three event handlers then perform integer division by selection_info.height without a zero check, so a mouse event triggers a divide-by-zero crash (DoS).

commit_msg:
Validate min and max arguments to `QuantizedResizeBilinear`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 369765091
Change-Id: I33be8b78273ab7d08b97541692fe05cb7f94963a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    const float in_min = context->input(2).flat<float>()(0);', '    const float in_max = context->input(3).flat<float>()(0);'], 'added_lines': ['    const auto& in_min_tensor = context->input(2);', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, TensorShapeUtils::IsScalar(in_min_tensor.shape()),', '                errors::InvalidArgument("min must be a scalar"));', '    const float in_min = in_min_tensor.flat<float>()(0);', '    const auto& in_max_tensor = context->input(3);', '    OP_REQUIRES(context, TensorShapeUtils::IsScalar(in_max_tensor.shape()),', '                errors::InvalidArgument("max must be a scalar"));', '    const float in_max = in_max_tensor.flat<float>()(0);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can cause a heap buffer overflow in `QuantizedResizeBilinear` by passing in invalid thresholds for the quantization. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/50711818d2e61ccce012591eeb4fdf93a8496726/tensorflow/core/kernels/quantized_resize_bilinear_op.cc#L705-L706) assumes that the 2 arguments are always valid scalars and tries to access the numeric value directly. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Compute reads quantization thresholds directly from input tensors 2 and 3 via flat<float>()(0), with no shape or scalar validation before indexing element 0.
The resulting in_min and in_max are passed into ResizeBilinear<T>, which uses them for quantized interpolation over the output buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the missing scalar validation on the quantization thresholds leads to a heap buffer overflow write during bilinear resize. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the supported consequence is memory corruption from writing past the output buffer.

evidence_lines.code:
ResizeBilinear<T>(image_data, st.height_scale, st.width_scale, in_min,
in_max, half_pixel_centers_, &output_data);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function assumes inputs 2 and 3 are valid scalar float tensors and unconditionally indexes element 0. Trigger: a caller supplies a non-scalar or otherwise malformed threshold tensor. The unchecked read feeds ResizeBilinear, producing an out-of-bounds write into the output buffer, corrupting memory or crashing.

commit_msg:
sched/fair: Fix low cpu usage with high throttling by removing expiration of cpu-local slices

It has been observed, that highly-threaded, non-cpu-bound applications
running under cpu.cfs_quota_us constraints can hit a high percentage of
periods throttled while simultaneously not consuming the allocated
amount of quota. This use case is typical of user-interactive non-cpu
bound applications, such as those running in kubernetes or mesos when
run on multiple cpu cores.

This has been root caused to cpu-local run queue being allocated per cpu
bandwidth slices, and then not fully using that slice within the period.
At which point the slice and quota expires. This expiration of unused
slice results in applications not being able to utilize the quota for
which they are allocated.

The non-expiration of per-cpu slices was recently fixed by
'commit 512ac999d275 ("sched/fair: Fix bandwidth timer clock drift
condition")'. Prior to that it appears that this had been broken since
at least 'commit 51f2176d74ac ("sched/fair: Fix unlocked reads of some
cfs_b->quota/period")' which was introduced in v3.16-rc1 in 2014. That
added the following conditional which resulted in slices never being
expired.

if (cfs_rq->runtime_expires != cfs_b->runtime_expires) {
	/* extend local deadline, drift is bounded above by 2 ticks */
	cfs_rq->runtime_expires += TICK_NSEC;

Because this was broken for nearly 5 years, and has recently been fixed
and is now being noticed by many users running kubernetes
(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/67577) it is my opinion
that the mechanisms around expiring runtime should be removed
altogether.

This allows quota already allocated to per-cpu run-queues to live longer
than the period boundary. This allows threads on runqueues that do not
use much CPU to continue to use their remaining slice over a longer
period of time than cpu.cfs_period_us. However, this helps prevent the
above condition of hitting throttling while also not fully utilizing
your cpu quota.

This theoretically allows a machine to use slightly more than its
allotted quota in some periods. This overflow would be bounded by the
remaining quota left on each per-cpu runqueueu. This is typically no
more than min_cfs_rq_runtime=1ms per cpu. For CPU bound tasks this will
change nothing, as they should theoretically fully utilize all of their
quota in each period. For user-interactive tasks as described above this
provides a much better user/application experience as their cpu
utilization will more closely match the amount they requested when they
hit throttling. This means that cpu limits no longer strictly apply per
period for non-cpu bound applications, but that they are still accurate
over longer timeframes.

This greatly improves performance of high-thread-count, non-cpu bound
applications with low cfs_quota_us allocation on high-core-count
machines. In the case of an artificial testcase (10ms/100ms of quota on
80 CPU machine), this commit resulted in almost 30x performance
improvement, while still maintaining correct cpu quota restrictions.
That testcase is available at https://github.com/indeedeng/fibtest.

Fixes: 512ac999d275 ("sched/fair: Fix bandwidth timer clock drift condition")

(In other words, although this slice expiration would typically be seen with benign workloads, it is possible that an attacker could calculate how many stray requests are required to force an entire Kubernetes cluster into a low-performance state caused by slice expiration, and ensure that a DDoS attack sent that number of stray requests. commit_msg:
perf: Fix race in swevent hash

There's a race on CPU unplug where we free the swevent hash array
while it can still have events on. This will result in a
use-after-free which is BAD.

Simply do not free the hash array on unplug. This leaves the thing
around and no use-after-free takes place.

When the last swevent dies, we do a for_each_possible_cpu() iteration
anyway to clean these up, at which time we'll free it, so no leakage
will occur.

Reported-by: Sasha Levin <sasha.levin@oracle.com>
Tested-by: Sasha Levin <sasha.levin@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@redhat.com>
Cc: Frederic Weisbecker <fweisbec@gmail.com>
Cc: Jiri Olsa <jolsa@redhat.com>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Stephane Eranian <eranian@google.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Vince Weaver <vincent.weaver@maine.edu>
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

description: Race condition in kernel/events/core.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by leveraging incorrect handling of an swevent data structure during a CPU unplug operation.

code_evidence: Line 3 obtains this_cpu_ptr(&swevent_htable), the per-CPU swevent hash. Line 11 calls find_swevent_head to locate the target bucket, and lines 12-14 only WARN/return when head is NULL. Line 16 then inserts the event via hlist_add_head_rcu without any synchronization against concurrent CPU-hotplug teardown of swhash.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because a shared per-CPU swevent hash is accessed without proper synchronization against a concurrent hotplug sequence, creating a timing window that violates exclusivity. The code's null check only handles a missing head; it does not prevent the race with teardown, so this is a race condition rather than merely a null-pointer defect.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the add path looks up and uses the swevent hash head without excluding concurrent CPU-unplug code that frees the hash array. Trigger: a CPU unplug races with perf_swevent_add on that CPU, so find_swevent_head or the following hlist insertion operates on freed memory. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the swevent hash, enabling privilege escalation or denial of service.

commit_msg:
When going through execve(), zero out the NUMA fault statistics instead of
freeing them.

During execve, the task is reachable through procfs and the scheduler. A
concurrent /proc/*/sched reader can read data from a freed ->numa_faults
allocation (confirmed by KASAN) and write it back to userspace.
I believe that it would also be possible for a use-after-free read to occur
through a race between a NUMA fault and execve(): task_numa_fault() can
lead to task_numa_compare(), which invokes task_weight() on the currently
running task of a different CPU.

Another way to fix this would be to make ->numa_faults RCU-managed or add
extra locking, but it seems easier to wipe the NUMA fault statistics on
execve.

Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Petr Mladek <pmladek@suse.com>
Cc: Sergey Senozhatsky <sergey.senozhatsky@gmail.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>
Fixes: 82727018b0d3 ("sched/numa: Call task_numa_free() from do_execve()")
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190716152047.14424-1-jannh@google.com
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\ttask_numa_free(current);'], 'added_lines': ['\ttask_numa_free(current, false);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.2.6. On NUMA systems, the Linux fair scheduler has a use-after-free in show_numa_stats() because NUMA fault statistics are inappropriately freed, aka CID-16d51a590a8c.

code_evidence: After exec_binprm() succeeds, the function clears in_execve and then calls task_numa_free(current) at line 84. In the pre-patch code this call frees the task's NUMA fault statistics while the task remains reachable via procfs and the scheduler, so concurrent readers can access the freed allocation. The diff changes this call to task_numa_free(current, false) to zero the statistics instead of freeing them.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the freed ->numa_faults allocation is referenced after free by concurrent readers, matching the use-after-free pattern. The fix removes the free, confirming the defect is post-free access rather than a simple leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: execve frees the current task's ->numa_faults memory while the task is still observable by concurrent /proc/*/sched readers and NUMA fault paths. Trigger: a successful execve races with a reader such as show_numa_stats() or task_numa_compare(). Consequence: use-after-free read of the freed allocation, leaking data to userspace or causing memory corruption/crash.

nfp: flower: fix memory leak in nfp_flower_spawn_vnic_reprs

In nfp_flower_spawn_vnic_reprs in the loop if initialization or the
allocations fail memory is leaked. Appropriate releases are added.

Fixes: b94524529741 ("nfp: flower: add per repr private data for LAG offload")
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Jakub Kicinski <jakub.kicinski@netronome.com>

description: A memory leak in the nfp_flower_spawn_vnic_reprs() function in drivers/net/ethernet/netronome/nfp/flower/main.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.4 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption), aka CID-8ce39eb5a67a.

code_evidence: At [24-28], nfp_repr_alloc() succeeds and, if the subsequent kzalloc() at [29] fails, the code jumps to err_reprs_clean without freeing the allocated repr.
At [38-43], nfp_port_alloc() returns an error; the code frees repr at [41] but never releases the repr_priv allocated at [29], leaking it.
At [56-61], nfp_repr_init() fails; port and repr are freed at [59-60], but repr_priv allocated at [29] is not freed before jumping to err_reprs_clean.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory with nfp_repr_alloc/kzalloc and, on error branches, fails to release it, matching CWE-401's missing release after effective lifetime. This is a leak on exceptional paths, not a use-after-free or double free, since the memory remains allocated and unreferenced.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: allocation-failure and initialization-error paths inside the loop jump to err_reprs_clean without releasing per-iteration allocations (repr, and repr_priv stored in nfp_repr->app_priv). Trigger: kzalloc, nfp_port_alloc, or nfp_repr_init failing. Consequence: leaked kernel memory on each failing attempt, enabling memory-consumption denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 17 reads an attacker-controlled iv_size byte from the bitstream and stores it in ptr->key_info[3]. Line 18 reads 16 bytes into ptr->key_info+4 unconditionally. commit_msg:
(uid_t) -1 is still used as placeholder to mean "unset". This is OK, since
there should be no users with such number, see
https://systemd.io/UIDS-GIDS#special-linux-uids.

(uid_t) -1 is used as the default value in class initialization.

When a user or group above INT32_MAX is created, the numeric uid or
gid wraps around to negative when the value is assigned to gint, and
polkit gets confused. Let's accept such gids, except for -1.

A nicer fix would be to change the underlying type to e.g. uint32 to
not have negative values. But this cannot be done without breaking the
API, so likely new functions will have to be added (a
polkit_unix_user_new variant that takes a unsigned, and the same for
_group_new, _set_uid, _get_uid, _set_gid, _get_gid, etc.). This will
require a bigger patch.

Fixes https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/polkit/polkit/issues/74.

code_evidence: The PROP_UID property is declared with g_param_spec_int, so its value range and default are gint. The minimum is set to 0 and the default to 0, restricting uid input to non-negative int values and treating 0 as the unset placeholder. There is no validation that the incoming uid fits the accepted domain; the integer range is the only constraint applied to this property.

This is improper input validation (CWE-20), not merely a type-conversion defect.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the uid property accepts only a gint range and uses 0 as the unset sentinel, so large uids above INT_MAX cannot be represented and a wrapped negative value is indistinguishable from the placeholder. commit_msg:
ALSA: timer: Fix race among timer ioctls

ALSA timer ioctls have an open race and this may lead to a
use-after-free of timer instance object.  A simplistic fix is to make
each ioctl exclusive.  We have already tread_sem for controlling the
tread, and extend this as a global mutex to be applied to each ioctl.

The downside is, of course, the worse concurrency.  But these ioctls
aren't to be parallel accessible, in anyway, so it should be fine to
serialize there.

Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Tested-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&tu->tread_sem);', '      \tmutex_unlock(&tu->tread_sem);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: sound/core/timer.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4.1 uses an incorrect type of mutex, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (race condition, use-after-free, and system crash) via a crafted ioctl call.

code_evidence: The ioctl handler serializes itself only with mutex_lock(&tu->tread_sem) at line 9, then closes and clears the shared tu->timeri at lines 10-13 without holding a global ioctl lock.
At the __err label the same per-user tread_sem is released at line 50, so concurrent ioctls on the same file each take this mutex independently rather than being mutually exclusive.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's shared timer instance is protected by an inappropriate mutex, leaving a timing window where concurrent ioctl code sequences interfere, which is a race condition (CWE-362). The use-after-free is the resulting consequence rather than a separate memory-safety root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the handler uses tu->tread_sem, a mutex intended for the timer read path, instead of a global ioctl mutex, so different ioctl sequences can interleave. Trigger: a local user issues concurrent ioctl calls on the same timer file; one path closes and nulls tu->timeri while another accesses it, causing a race and use-after-free that can crash the system.

commit_msg:
Don't overflow the output length in EVP_CipherUpdate calls

CVE-2021-23840

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        /*', '         * final_used is only ever set if buf_len is 0. Therefore the maximum', '         * length output we will ever see from evp_EncryptDecryptUpdate is', '         * the maximum multiple of the block length that is <= inl, or just:', '         * inl & ~(b - 1)', '         * Since final_used has been set then the final output length is:', '         * (inl & ~(b - 1)) + b', '         * This must never exceed INT_MAX', '         */', '        if ((inl & ~(b - 1)) > INT_MAX - b) {', '            EVPerr(EVP_F_EVP_DECRYPTUPDATE, EVP_R_OUTPUT_WOULD_OVERFLOW);', '            return 0;', '        }']}
description: Calls to EVP_CipherUpdate, EVP_EncryptUpdate and EVP_DecryptUpdate may overflow the output length argument in some cases where the input length is close to the maximum permissable length for an integer on the platform. In such cases the return value from the function call will be 1 (indicating success), but the output length value will be negative. This could cause applications to behave incorrectly or crash. OpenSSL versions 1.1.1i and below are affected by this issue. Users of these versions should upgrade to OpenSSL 1.1.1j. OpenSSL versions 1.0.2x and below are affected by this issue. However OpenSSL 1.0.2 is out of support and no longer receiving public updates. Premium support customers of OpenSSL 1.0.2 should upgrade to 1.0.2y. Other users should upgrade to 1.1.1j. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1j (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1i). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2y (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2x).

code_evidence: b is the cipher block size (line 10). When final_used is set, a full block b is copied to out and outl is later adjusted (lines 41-43). evp_EncryptDecryptUpdate writes into out and sets *outl (line 46). When b > 1 and buf_len is 0, *outl is reduced by b and the trailing block is saved (lines 48-51). Finally, if fix_len, *outl += b (line 55), adding the saved block length back to the reported output length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked integer addition of block length b to *outl that can exceed INT_MAX and wrap negative, matching CWE-190. The added guard (inl & ~(b - 1)) > INT_MAX - b prevents this overflow; without it the arithmetic lacks the bound. This is an integer wraparound, not a buffer over-read or a signedness-only issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The reported output length *outl is computed as the update output plus b. With inl near INT_MAX, the update output can approach INT_MAX, so *outl += b (line 55) wraps to a negative value. The function still returns success, so callers trusting the negative length may mis-handle the buffer, causing incorrect behavior or a crash.

- Modified TileManager.cc to verify that malloc() has correctly allocated memory.
- Updated numerical types to std::size_t in RawTile.h, TileManager.cc, KakaduImage.cc, OpenJPEG.cc and Transforms.cc when allocating memory via new to avoid integer overflow - fixes remaining problems identified in https://github.com/ruven/iipsrv/issues/223.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if( obpc == 16 ) rawtile.data = new unsigned short[w * h * channels];', '  else if( obpc == 8 ) rawtile.data = new unsigned char[w * h * channels];', '  rawtile.dataLength = w*h*channels*(obpc/8);'], 'added_lines': ['  size_t np = (size_t) w * (size_t) h * (size_t) channels;', '  if( obpc == 16 ) rawtile.data = new unsigned short[np];', '  else if( obpc == 8 ) rawtile.data = new unsigned char[np];', '  rawtile.dataLength = np*(obpc/8);']}
description: IIPImage High Resolution Streaming Image Server prior to commit 882925b295a80ec992063deffc2a3b0d803c3195 is affected by an integer overflow in iipsrv.fcgi through malformed HTTP query parameters.

code_evidence: The allocation size w * h * channels is computed in unsigned int arithmetic before being passed to new[]; there is no cast or overflow check, so a large product wraps to a small value.
The same unchecked product w*h*channels*(obpc/8) sets rawtile.dataLength, so the recorded length can likewise wrap independently of the true buffer size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The flaw is an integer overflow in a size calculation that then governs memory allocation, matching CWE-190's allocation-size scope. It is not merely a buffer overflow (CWE-119); the wrap in the size computation is the primary defect, with the out-of-bounds write being its consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
if( obpc == 16 ) rawtile.data = new unsigned short[w * h * channels];
else if( obpc == 8 ) rawtile.data = new unsigned char[w * h * channels];
rawtile.dataLength = w*h*channels*(obpc/8);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is unsigned-int multiplication of attacker-influenced w, h and channels without widening or bounds checks; when the product exceeds UINT_MAX it wraps, yielding an undersized allocation and a wrapped dataLength. Trigger is a malformed request producing large dimensions, after which process() writes decoded pixel data into the too-small buffer, giving heap overflow and possible memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Fixed aggregation methods of Promise ctor with array-like object.

Previously, while iterating over an array-like object the methods may be
resolved with INVALID values. INVALID value is a special internal type which
should never be visible by ordinary functions.

The fix is to ensure that absent elements are represented by undefined value.

The following methods were fixed Promise.all(), Promise.allSettled(),
    Promise.any(), Promise.race().

This closes #483 issue on Github.

description: Nginx NJS v0.7.2 was discovered to contain a segmentation violation in the function njs_vmcode_interpreter at src/njs_vmcode.c.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function handles invalid values by substituting undefined; it contains no memory-freeing or post-free reference, so it does not support CWE-416.

commit_msg:
Fix #77177: Serializing or unserializing COM objects crashes

Firstly, we avoid returning NULL from the get_property handler, but
instead return an empty HashTable, which already prevents the crashes.
Secondly, since (de-)serialization obviously makes no sense for COM,
DOTNET and VARIANT objects (at least with the current implementation),
we prohibit it right away.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\treturn NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['\treturn &com_dotnet_object_properties;']}
description: ext/standard/var.c in PHP 5.x through 7.1.24 on Windows allows attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and application crash) because com and com_safearray_proxy return NULL in com_properties_get in ext/com_dotnet/com_handlers.c, as demonstrated by a serialize call on COM("WScript.Shell").

code_evidence: com_properties_get is a property-accessor handler that unconditionally returns NULL instead of a valid HashTable pointer. Any caller relying on this return value to read object properties receives a NULL pointer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Returning NULL from a handler whose contract implies a valid HashTable* directly produces a NULL pointer dereference in callers, matching CWE-476. The fix returns a real HashTable instead, confirming the NULL return was the defect rather than a different weakness such as improper input validation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the handler always returns NULL, so callers that dereference the returned HashTable* operate on a NULL pointer. Trigger: invoking serialization (serialize) on a COM object, which reaches this accessor through the property enumeration path. Supported consequence: NULL pointer dereference leading to an application crash (denial of service).

commit_msg:
Fix heap buffer overflow caused by rounding.

This was hard to fix. Due to the way we compute the pixels that influence an output pixel in resized images, for certain input configuration we might have issued a read to a pixel that is outside of boundary of the original image. This is because of floating errors that affected truncation results.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 369757871
Change-Id: If89425fff930983829a2168203c11858883eebc9
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    interpolation->lower[i] =', '        std::min(interpolation->lower[i], interpolation->upper[i]);']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can trigger a heap buffer overflow in `tf.raw_ops.QuantizedResizeBilinear` by manipulating input values so that float rounding results in off-by-one error in accessing image elements. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/44b7f486c0143f68b56c34e2d01e146ee445134a/tensorflow/core/kernels/quantized_resize_bilinear_op.cc#L62-L66) computes two integers (representing the upper and lower bounds for interpolation) by ceiling and flooring a floating point value. For some values of `in`, `interpolation->upper[i]` might be smaller than `interpolation->lower[i]`. This is an issue if `interpolation->upper[i]` is capped at `in_size-1` as it means that `interpolation->lower[i]` points outside of the image. Then, in the interpolation code(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/44b7f486c0143f68b56c34e2d01e146ee445134a/tensorflow/core/kernels/quantized_resize_bilinear_op.cc#L245-L264), this would result in heap buffer overflow. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: `in_f = std::floor(in)` yields the lower bound, clamped to at least 0 via `std::max(static_cast<int64>(in_f), 0)`.
`upper[i]` is computed independently as `std::min(std::ceil(in), in_size - 1)`, capped at `in_size - 1` but never reconciled with `lower[i]`.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an incorrect boundary value where a bound is off by one relative to the correct index, exactly CWE-193. The later heap overflow is the consequence, not the weakness itself; the missing constraint between lower and upper is the defect.

evidence_lines.code:
interpolation->upper[i] =
std::min(static_cast<int64>(std::ceil(in)), in_size - 1);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Because `lower` and `upper` are derived separately from flooring and ceiling the same float, float rounding can make `upper[i]` (capped at `in_size-1`) smaller than `lower[i]`, so `lower[i]` can exceed the valid image index range. This off-by-one index then feeds the interpolation step, producing an out-of-bounds heap read/write.

commit_msg:
Fix tf.raw_ops.DeleteSessionTensor vulnerability with invalid `handle`.

Check that `handle` input is actually a scalar before treating it as such.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 445228994
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(ctx, TensorShapeUtils::IsScalar(handle.shape()),', '                errors::InvalidArgument("`handle` must be scalar"));']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4, the implementation of `tf.raw_ops.DeleteSessionTensor` does not fully validate the input arguments. This results in a `CHECK`-failure which can be used to trigger a denial of service attack. Versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4 contain a patch for this issue.

code_evidence: Line 2 takes input 0 as `handle` without checking its shape. Line 3 immediately calls `handle.scalar<tstring>()()`, which assumes `handle` is a scalar tensor and reads its single element.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function processes an input whose required property (scalar shape) is never validated before use, matching CWE-20 improper input validation. The added `IsScalar` check confirms the missing constraint; the resulting crash is the consequence, not the weakness itself.

evidence_lines.code:
const Tensor& handle = ctx->input(0);
const string& name = handle.scalar<tstring>()();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: `Compute` dereferences `handle` as a scalar without first validating that the input tensor is scalar-shaped. Trigger: a caller supplies a non-scalar (e.g., empty or multi-element) `handle` tensor to `tf.raw_ops.DeleteSessionTensor`. Consequence: the scalar accessor fails a `CHECK`, aborting the process and causing a denial of service.

commit_msg:
Fix possible infinite loop in BN_mod_sqrt()

The calculation in some cases does not finish for non-prime p.

This fixes CVE-2022-0778.

Based on patch by David Benjamin <davidben@google.com>.

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <pauli@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
(cherry picked from commit 9eafb53614bf65797db25f467946e735e1b43dc9)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [' * Theory", algorithm 1.5.1). \'p\' must be prime!', '        /* find smallest  i  such that  b^(2^i) = 1 */', '        i = 1;', '        if (!BN_mod_sqr(t, b, p, ctx))', '            goto end;', '        while (!BN_is_one(t)) {', '            i++;', '            if (i == e) {', '                ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_BN, BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE);', '                goto end;', '            if (!BN_mod_mul(t, t, t, p, ctx))', '                goto end;'], 'added_lines': [' * Theory", algorithm 1.5.1). \'p\' must be prime, otherwise an error or', ' * an incorrect "result" will be returned.', '        /* Find the smallest i, 0 < i < e, such that b^(2^i) = 1. */', '        for (i = 1; i < e; i++) {', '            if (i == 1) {', '                if (!BN_mod_sqr(t, b, p, ctx))', '                    goto end;', '', '            } else {', '                if (!BN_mod_mul(t, t, t, p, ctx))', '                    goto end;', '            if (BN_is_one(t))', '                break;', '        }', '        /* If not found, a is not a square or p is not prime. */', '        if (i >= e) {', '            ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_BN, BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE);', '            goto end;']}
description: The BN_mod_sqrt() function, which computes a modular square root, contains a bug that can cause it to loop forever for non-prime moduli. Internally this function is used when parsing certificates that contain elliptic curve public keys in compressed form or explicit elliptic curve parameters with a base point encoded in compressed form. It is possible to trigger the infinite loop by crafting a certificate that has invalid explicit curve parameters. Since certificate parsing happens prior to verification of the certificate signature, any process that parses an externally supplied certificate may thus be subject to a denial of service attack. The infinite loop can also be reached when parsing crafted private keys as they can contain explicit elliptic curve parameters. Thus vulnerable situations include: - TLS clients consuming server certificates - TLS servers consuming client certificates - Hosting providers taking certificates or private keys from customers - Certificate authorities parsing certification requests from subscribers - Anything else which parses ASN.1 elliptic curve parameters Also any other applications that use the BN_mod_sqrt() where the attacker can control the parameter values are vulnerable to this DoS issue. In the OpenSSL 1.0.2 version the public key is not parsed during initial parsing of the certificate which makes it slightly harder to trigger the infinite loop. However any operation which requires the public key from the certificate will trigger the infinite loop. In particular the attacker can use a self-signed certificate to trigger the loop during verification of the certificate signature. This issue affects OpenSSL versions 1.0.2, 1.1.1 and 3.0. It was addressed in the releases of 1.1.1n and 3.0.2 on the 15th March 2022. Fixed in OpenSSL 3.0.2 (Affected 3.0.0,3.0.1). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1n (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1m). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2zd (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2zc).

code_evidence: Inside the outer while(1), the inner loop initializes i=1, squares b into t, then increments i and re-squares t while t is not one. The only exit is i==e, which raises BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE and jumps to end; otherwise it keeps squaring until t becomes one. When p is non-prime, b^(2^i) may never equal 1 for any i in range, so the loop can iterate without reaching a terminating condition.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function contains a loop whose exit condition (t == 1) is unreachable for certain non-prime inputs, matching CWE-835's infinite/unreachable-exit loop. The consequence is availability impact (CPU exhaustion), consistent with the weakness scope; this is not merely an incorrect-result bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop's termination depends on t reaching one, an assumption valid only for prime p; there is no independent bound on the number of squarings. Trigger: attacker-supplied non-prime modulus (e.g., explicit EC parameters in a certificate) reaching BN_mod_sqrt. Consequence: unbounded CPU consumption, a denial of service during certificate parsing.

commit_msg:
FTP: Fix buffer overflow in PORT parser, reported by Aaron Esau

Signed-off-by: Joachim Nilsson <troglobit@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tsprintf(addr, "%d.%d.%d.%d", a, b, c, d);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsnprintf(addr, sizeof(addr), "%d.%d.%d.%d", a, b, c, d);']}
description: An unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in common.c's handle_PORT in uftpd FTP server versions 2.10 and earlier can be abused to cause a crash and could potentially lead to remote code execution.

code_evidence: Line 4 declares a fixed 16-byte stack buffer addr (INET_ADDRSTRLEN). Line 11 parses six attacker-controlled integers from the PORT argument via sscanf without validating their magnitude. Line 12 writes the four values a-d into addr with unbounded sprintf, so large or negative integers expand far beyond 16 bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is a write past the end of an intended buffer, matching CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write. It is not merely a format-string issue (CWE-134) because the format is constant; the overflow stems from unconstrained width of the written data into a too-small destination.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded sprintf into a fixed-size stack buffer using unvalidated integer fields parsed from the client-supplied PORT command. Trigger: an unauthenticated client sends a PORT argument whose decimal values produce a string longer than INET_ADDRSTRLEN. Consequence: stack memory past addr is overwritten, causing a crash and potentially remote code execution.

commit_msg:
Decoder: Fixed incorrect use of mmco parameters.

Added extra structure to read mmco values and copied only once per
picture.

Bug: 65735716

Change-Id: I25b08a37bc78342042c52957774b089abce1a54b
(cherry picked from commit 3c70b9a190875938fc57164d9295a3ec791554df)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    dpb_commands_t *ps_dpb_cmds = ps_dec->ps_dpb_cmds;'], 'added_lines': ['    dpb_commands_t *ps_dpb_cmds = &(ps_dec->s_dpb_cmds_scratch);']}
description: A vulnerability in the Android media framework (libavc) related to incorrect use of mmco parameters. Product: Android. Versions: 7.0, 7.1.1, 7.1.2, 8.0, 8.1. Android ID: A-65735716.

code_evidence: The MMCO command value u4_mmco is read from the bitstream via ih264d_uev and drives a while loop that continues until END_OF_MMCO is seen.
Command count is bounded: if j >= MAX_REF_BUFS the function logs and returns -1 before indexing as_mmc_params[j], so the command array is not overflowed.
Each parsed command is stored into ps_mmc_params = &ps_dpb_cmds->as_mmc_params[j] and the loop advances j after fetching the next u4_mmco.
The parsed values (u4_diff_pic_num, u4_lt_idx, u4_max_lt_idx_plus1) are stored without range checks against the reference picture structures.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is the entry point that receives attacker-controlled MMCO values from the bitstream and stores them without checking that they satisfy required domain constraints (valid reference indices), which is improper input validation (CWE-20). The missing constraint is on the parsed parameter values, not merely on the loop count, which is already bounded.

evidence_lines.code:
ps_mmc_params = &ps_dpb_cmds->as_mmc_params[j];
ps_mmc_params->u4_mmco = u4_mmco;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: MMCO parameters parsed from the slice header are accepted without validating them against the current reference-picture set (e.g., diff_pic_num or long-term index bounds). Trigger: a crafted H.264 stream supplies MMCO commands whose parameters reference nonexistent or out-of-range pictures. Supported consequence: downstream DPB processing uses these unvalidated indices, leading to out-of-bounds access or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Bug #484 CVE-2018-17582 Check for corrupt PCAP files

* Check for packets that are larger than 262144 bytes
* Check for capture lengths that are greater than packet length

Example of a corrupt PCAP file ...

sudo src/tcpreplay -i ens33 --unique-ip -t --loop 4 get_next_paket_01
safe_pcap_next ERROR: Invalid packet length in send_packets.c:get_next_packet() line 1054: 8388670 is greater than maximum 262144
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    for (pkt_counter = 0; pcap_next_ex(pcap, &header, &packet) > 0; pkt_counter++){'], 'added_lines': ['    for (pkt_counter = 0; safe_pcap_next_ex(pcap, &header, &packet) > 0; pkt_counter++){']}
description: Tcpreplay v4.3.0 beta1 contains a heap-based buffer over-read. The get_next_packet() function in the send_packets.c file uses the memcpy() function unsafely to copy sequences from the source buffer pktdata to the destination (*prev_packet)->pktdata. This will result in a Denial of Service (DoS) and potentially Information Exposure when the application attempts to process a file.

code_evidence: Line 41 iterates with pcap_next_ex and no check that header->caplen or header->len is within a sane bound; lines 42-45 only warn when len > caplen and continue processing.

Lines 47-49 cast packet to ether_hdr and read iphdr at packet + SIZE_ETHERNET, then dereference iphdr->ip_hl without confirming caplen covers SIZE_ETHERNET plus an IPv4 header; lines 54-55 similarly read tcphdr->th_off past the captured data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads header fields from a packet buffer without confirming the buffer actually contains those bytes, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The later memcpy overflow would be CWE-787, but here the unsafe operation is the unchecked read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The loop accepts corrupt/truncated packets whose captured length is smaller than the headers it dereferences. Because packet buffer bounds are never validated against caplen before reading ethernet, IP and TCP header fields, a short packet causes reads past the end of the captured buffer. This yields a crash/DoS and possible information exposure from adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
The check_interval file in

  /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck<cpu number>

directory is a global timer value for MCE polling. If it is changed by one
CPU, mce_restart() broadcasts the event to other CPUs to delete and restart
the MCE polling timer and __mcheck_cpu_init_timer() reinitializes the
mce_timer variable.

If more than one CPU writes a specific value to the check_interval file
concurrently, mce_timer is not protected from such concurrent accesses and
all kinds of explosions happen. Since only root can write to those sysfs
variables, the issue is not a big deal security-wise.

However, concurrent writes to these configuration variables is void of
reason so the proper thing to do is to serialize the access with a mutex.

Boris:

 - Make store_int_with_restart() use device_store_ulong() to filter out
   negative intervals
 - Limit min interval to 1 second
 - Correct locking
 - Massage commit message

Signed-off-by: Seunghun Han <kkamagui@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Borislav Petkov <bp@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Cc: Tony Luck <tony.luck@intel.com>
Cc: linux-edac <linux-edac@vger.kernel.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20180302202706.9434-1-kkamagui@gmail.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tssize_t ret = device_store_int(s, attr, buf, size);'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned long old_check_interval = check_interval;', '\tssize_t ret = device_store_ulong(s, attr, buf, size);', '', '\tif (check_interval == old_check_interval)', '\t\treturn ret;', '', '\tif (check_interval < 1)', '\t\tcheck_interval = 1;', '', '\tmutex_lock(&mce_sysfs_mutex);', '\tmutex_unlock(&mce_sysfs_mutex);', '']}
description: Race condition in the store_int_with_restart() function in arch/x86/kernel/cpu/mcheck/mce.c in the Linux kernel through 4.15.7 allows local users to cause a denial of service (panic) by leveraging root access to write to the check_interval file in a /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck<cpu number> directory. NOTE: a third party has indicated that this report is not security relevant

code_evidence: store_int_with_restart() calls device_store_int() to update the global check_interval, then immediately invokes mce_restart() with no mutex or other lock protecting the sequence; concurrent writers can interleave between the store and the restart.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a race condition (CWE-362): a concurrent code sequence lacks exclusivity/atomicity over a shared resource (check_interval and mce_timer), and a timing window lets an interfering writer interleave, yielding a DoS crash. It is not merely an input-validation issue, since the unsafe operation is the unsynchronized concurrent access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is the absence of exclusive synchronization around the shared global check_interval and the mce_timer reinitialization performed by mce_restart(). When two CPUs write the check_interval sysfs file concurrently, the interfering sequence can modify check_interval and restart the timer while another writer is mid-sequence, corrupting timer state and causing a panic.

commit_msg:
Avoid races between check and use of the nested VMCB controls.  This
for example ensures that the VMRUN intercept is always reflected to the
nested hypervisor, instead of being processed by the host.  Without this
patch, it is possible to end up with svm->nested.hsave pointing to
the MSR permission bitmap for nested guests.

This bug is CVE-2021-29657.

Reported-by: Felix Wilhelm <fwilhelm@google.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 2fcf4876ada ("KVM: nSVM: implement on demand allocation of the nested state")
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tload_nested_vmcb_control(svm, &vmcb12->control);'], 'added_lines': []}
description: arch/x86/kvm/svm/nested.c in the Linux kernel before 5.11.12 has a use-after-free in which an AMD KVM guest can bypass access control on host OS MSRs when there are nested guests, aka CID-a58d9166a756. This occurs because of a TOCTOU race condition associated with a VMCB12 double fetch in nested_svm_vmrun.

code_evidence: Line 5 stores vmcb12_gpa in svm->nested.vmcb12_gpa, then line 6 loads nested VMCB controls from vmcb12->control. Lines 7-8 subsequently prepare save and control state, which re-reads the nested VMCB (including svm->nested.hsave selection) based on the same vmcb12. The loaded controls and later preparations are distinct reads of guest-controlled nested state.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-367 fits because a check/load of the nested VMCB control occurs before its later use, with the resource state changeable in between by the guest. This is a TOCTOU race rather than a mere logic error, since the inconsistency arises from the temporal gap between two accesses to the same guest-controlled VMCB.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function performs separate reads of the nested VMCB control fields: load_nested_vmcb_control consumes vmcb12->control, while nested_prepare_vmcb_control later derives state from the same VMCB. A nested guest can change the VMCB between these accesses, so the controls validated/loaded first become inconsistent with the state used afterward, allowing the VMRUN intercept to be processed by the host and hsave to point at the MSR permission bitmap.

More changes to mitigate:

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      strncat(params, gtk_entry_get_text(GTK_ENTRY(entry1)), PARAMS_LEN);', '      strncat(params, "/", PARAMS_LEN);', '      strncat(params, gtk_entry_get_text(GTK_ENTRY(entry2)), PARAMS_LEN);'], 'added_lines': ['      strncat(params, gtk_entry_get_text(GTK_ENTRY(entry1)), ETH_ASCII_ADDR_LEN);', '      strncat(params, "/", 1);', '      strncat(params, gtk_entry_get_text(GTK_ENTRY(entry2)), IP6_ASCII_ADDR_LEN);']}

Each strncat uses PARAMS_LEN as the count, so the destination buffer size is never accounted for; the concatenation can write past the end of params.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a buffer copy without checking the size of the destination: input from GUI fields is copied into a fixed buffer using PARAMS_LEN rather than the remaining capacity. That matches CWE-120's classic copy-into-fixed-buffer pattern, distinct from an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is unbounded concatenation: strncat limits only the number of source bytes copied, not the remaining space in params. When the entry1/entry2 text is long, the cumulative copy exceeds the destination, corrupting adjacent stack memory. commit_msg:
MBIM: stop pre sizing wmem arrays

In case of malformed packet, this can lead to an insane amount of
memory.
Instead let's use the automatic growth mecanism. This way the malformed
packet is caught by the dissection engine.

Bug: 14056
Change-Id: I7bf5b80a516210b341356f5d495f08d1dba05805
Reviewed-on: https://code.wireshark.org/review/23537
Reviewed-by: Pascal Quantin <pascal.quantin@gmail.com>
Petri-Dish: Pascal Quantin <pascal.quantin@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Petri Dish Buildbot <buildbot-no-reply@wireshark.org>
Reviewed-by: Michael Mann <mmann78@netscape.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        pair_list = wmem_array_sized_new(wmem_packet_scope(), sizeof(struct mbim_pair_list), elem_count);'], 'added_lines': ['        pair_list = wmem_array_new(wmem_packet_scope(), sizeof(struct mbim_pair_list));']}
description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.1 and 2.2.0 to 2.2.9, the MBIM dissector could crash or exhaust system memory. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-mbim.c by changing the memory-allocation approach.

code_evidence: The element count is read directly from the packet into elem_count without any bound check.

When elem_count is nonzero, wmem_array_sized_new preallocates an array sized by that attacker-controlled count before any packet data is validated, and the subtree length 8*elem_count is likewise derived from it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to constrain the amount of memory allocated in response to a packet-controlled count, leading to resource exhaustion/DoS. This is an allocation-sizing flaw (pre-sizing from untrusted input), not an out-of-bounds read, which is why CWE-400 rather than a memory-safety CWE applies.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an untrusted 32-bit element count from the MBIM packet is used to pre-size a wmem array allocation. A malformed packet declaring a huge count triggers an enormous allocation, exhausting system memory or crashing the dissector before the loop can detect truncated data; the crash is the consequence, not the cause.

commit_msg:
Reported-by: Li Qiang
Free the vertex array in error path.
This was introduced by this commit:
renderer: fix heap overflow in vertex elements state create.

I rewrote the code to not require the allocation in the first
place if we have an error, seems nicer.

Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['   struct vrend_vertex_element_array *v = CALLOC_STRUCT(vrend_vertex_element_array);', '', '   if (num_elements > PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS)', '      return EINVAL;'], 'added_lines': ['   struct vrend_vertex_element_array *v;', '   if (num_elements > PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS)', '      return EINVAL;', '', '   v = CALLOC_STRUCT(vrend_vertex_element_array);']}
description: Memory leak in the vrend_create_vertex_elements_state function in vrend_renderer.c in virglrenderer allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host memory consumption) via a large number of VIRGL_OBJECT_VERTEX_ELEMENTS commands.

code_evidence: Line 6 allocates v via CALLOC_STRUCT before any validation. Lines 11-14 check the returned pointer and then reject num_elements > PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS with EINVAL without freeing v, so the allocation leaks on that error path. The commit moves validation before allocation to avoid the leak.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-772 fits because the resource allocated at line 6 is never released after its effective lifetime ends on the early-return path at lines 13-14. This is a missing-release resource lifetime flaw, distinct from a generic memory-safety issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the size-limit check on num_elements returns EINVAL after v has already been allocated, and that error path omits FREE(v). Trigger: a guest repeatedly sends VIRGL_OBJECT_VERTEX_ELEMENTS commands with num_elements exceeding PIPE_MAX_ATTRIBS. Supported consequence: each rejected request leaks the vertex-element array allocation, enabling host memory exhaustion and denial of service.

commit_msg:
patch 9.0.0105: illegal memory access when pattern starts with illegal byte

Problem:    Illegal memory access when pattern starts with illegal byte.
Solution:   Do not match a character with an illegal byte.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tif (utf_fold(utf_ptr2char(p)) == cc)'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tint uc = utf_ptr2char(p);', '', '\t\t// Do not match an illegal byte.  E.g. 0xff matches 0xc3 0xbf,', '\t\t// not 0xff.', '\t\tif ((uc < 0x80 || uc != *p) && utf_fold(uc) == cc)']}
description: Out-of-bounds Read in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 9.0.0104.

code_evidence: The loop advances p by (*mb_ptr2len)(p) over a multibyte string, and within the enc_utf8 && c > 0x80 branch it decodes the current byte with utf_ptr2char(p) and compares it to cc.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The direct consequence is an illegal memory access reading past valid data when an illegal byte is decoded and matched, which fits CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not merely an encoding/logic error because the faulty match drives memory access beyond the intended buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: utf_ptr2char(p) is called on a byte that may be an illegal lead byte (e.g., 0xff), producing an invalid decoded value whose folded form can match cc. The loop then treats that position as a match, and the invalid byte is mishandled during subsequent multibyte processing, leading to an out-of-bounds read. The missing constraint is that the decoded value must correspond to the actual byte (uc < 0x80 || uc != *p).

commit_msg:
Fix #242: Double free in check_file_actlst()

Avoid freeing buffer() twice.

Signed-off-by: Sebastien GODARD <sysstat@users.noreply.github.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tbuffer = NULL;']}
description: sysstat through 12.2.0 has a double free in check_file_actlst in sa_common.c.

code_evidence: Line 30 frees buffer and line 31 sets buffer = NULL. Line 124 frees buffer again at the normal end of the function after the activity loop. If an error path is taken in the loop (goto format_error at lines 59, 71, 87, 101, 108), the handler at lines 146-149 frees buffer only if it is non-NULL; without the NULL reset the earlier free at line 30 would be followed by this free, or line 124 would free it a second time when the loop completes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 is the double free of the same memory address. The patch adds buffer = NULL after the free at line 30, confirming the missing constraint that the pointer must not be reused after being freed. This is not a use-after-free because the second operation is a free, not a dereference.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: buffer is freed at line 30 but the pointer is not cleared, so later free() calls at line 124 or in the format_error handler at line 148 can free the same allocation again. Trigger: any path reaching those frees after line 30. Supported consequence: a double free, corrupting heap metadata and risking memory modification or code execution.

commit_msg:
* tools/tiffcp.c: error out cleanly in cpContig2SeparateByRow and
cpSeparate2ContigByRow if BitsPerSample != 8 to avoid heap based overflow.
Fixes http://bugzilla.maptools.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2656 and
http://bugzilla.maptools.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2657
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t(void) TIFFGetField(in, TIFFTAG_PLANARCONFIG, &shortv);'], 'added_lines': ['\t(void) TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(in, TIFFTAG_PLANARCONFIG, &shortv);']}
description: LibTIFF version 4.0.7 is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow in the tools/tiffcp resulting in DoS or code execution via a crafted BitsPerSample value.

code_evidence: Line 7 retrieves TIFFTAG_PLANARCONFIG with TIFFGetField but ignores the return value, leaving shortv uninitialized when the tag is absent. Line 8 gates the error-out only on shortv != config && bitspersample != 8 && samplesperpixel > 1, so a missing tag bypasses the guard. The switch at line 42 then packs the uninitialized shortv into the dispatch key, selecting a copy routine without validating the actual planar configuration/bits-per-sample combination.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The dispatch driven by unvalidated field data routes the crafted image into copy routines that perform buffer operations outside intended bounds, matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds read/write within a memory buffer. The missing TIFFGetFieldDefaulted check is the enabling constraint failure; the resultant heap overflow is the supported consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the planar-config field is fetched without checking success, so shortv can hold arbitrary stack data. Trigger: a crafted TIFF lacking PLANARCONFIG but with BitsPerSample != 8 and multiple samples. The guard on line 8 fails to reject it, and the switch dispatches to a copy function (e.g. cpContig2SeparateByRow) that assumes 8-bit samples, producing an out-of-bounds heap read/write.

commit_msg:
If the target ring is configured with IOPOLL, then we always need to hold
the target ring uring_lock before posting CQEs. We could just grab it
unconditionally, but since we don't expect many target rings to be of this
type, make grabbing the uring_lock conditional on the ring type.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/io-uring/Y8krlYa52%2F0YGqkg@ip-172-31-85-199.ec2.internal/
Reported-by: Xingyuan Mo <hdthky0@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static int io_msg_ring_data(struct io_kiocb *req)', '\tif (io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, msg->user_data, msg->len, 0))', '\t\treturn 0;', '', '\treturn -EOVERFLOW;'], 'added_lines': ['static int io_msg_ring_data(struct io_kiocb *req, unsigned int issue_flags)', '\tint ret;', '\tret = -EOVERFLOW;', '\tif (target_ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL) {', '\t\tif (unlikely(io_double_lock_ctx(target_ctx, issue_flags)))', '\t\t\treturn -EAGAIN;', '\t\tif (io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, msg->user_data, msg->len, 0))', '\t\t\tret = 0;', '\t\tio_double_unlock_ctx(target_ctx);', '\t} else {', '\t\tif (io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, msg->user_data, msg->len, 0))', '\t\t\tret = 0;', '\t}', '\treturn ret;']}
description: A vulnerability was found due to missing lock for IOPOLL flaw in io_cqring_event_overflow() in io_uring.c in Linux Kernel. This flaw allows a local attacker with user privilege to trigger a Denial of Service threat.

code_evidence: io_msg_ring_data reads target_ctx from req->file->private_data and posts an auxiliary CQE via io_post_aux_cqe(target_ctx, ...) at lines 15-17 without acquiring target_ctx->uring_lock, even though the target ring may be configured with IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL, where posting CQEs requires holding that lock.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-667 covers failing to properly acquire a lock around a shared resource. Here the shared CQE ring is modified without the required uring_lock, matching improper locking rather than a mere overflow-return issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function posts a CQE to a target IOPOLL ring without holding the target ring's uring_lock. Trigger: a local user sends an io_uring message to an IOPOLL-configured target ring, causing concurrent unlocked CQE posting. Supported consequence: inconsistent ring state leading to denial of service.

commit_msg:
dd: harden functions against directory traversal issues

Test correctness of all accessed dump dir files in all dd* functions.
Before this commit, the callers were allowed to pass strings like
"../../etc/shadow" in the filename argument of all dd* functions.

Related: #1214457

Signed-off-by: Jakub Filak <jfilak@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (!str_is_correct_filename(name))', '    {', '        error_msg("Cannot load text. \'%s\' is not a valid file name", name);', '        if (!(flags & DD_LOAD_TEXT_RETURN_NULL_ON_FAILURE))', '            xfunc_die();', '    }']}
description: Directory traversal vulnerability in abrt-dbus in Automatic Bug Reporting Tool (ABRT) allows local users to read, write to, or change ownership of arbitrary files via unspecified vectors to the (1) NewProblem, (2) GetInfo, (3) SetElement, or (4) DeleteElement method.

code_evidence: The function takes a caller-supplied 'name', optionally rewrites it only for the literal 'release' case, then builds a path with concat_path_file(dd->dd_dirname, name) and passes it to load_text_file. No check rejects '..' or absolute components in 'name', so a value such as '../../etc/shadow' is joined to the dump directory and resolved outside it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The pathname is intended to identify a file under the dump directory, but special elements in 'name' are not neutralized, matching CWE-22 path traversal. This is not merely an information-exposure issue; the missing pathname restriction is the direct cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unvalidated external 'name' is concatenated to dd->dd_dirname without neutralizing path separators or '..'. Trigger: a caller passes a traversal string; the resulting full_path escapes the dump directory and load_text_file reads it, allowing arbitrary file disclosure (or failure/DoS on invalid paths).

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t    const u_char *p, const u_char *ep,', '\telse', '\tif (ep < p + totlen) {', '\t\treturn ep + 1;', '\t\telse', '\t\t\trawprint(ndo, (const uint8_t *)&p[2], 2);', '\t\tND_PRINT((ndo,"len=%d value=", EXTRACT_16BITS(&p[2])));', '\t\trawprint(ndo, (const uint8_t *)&p[4], EXTRACT_16BITS(&p[2]));'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t    const u_char *p, const u_char *ep2,', '\tND_TCHECK(p[0]);', '\telse {', '\t\tND_TCHECK_16BITS(&p[2]);', '\t}', '\tif (ep2 < p + totlen) {', '\t\treturn ep2 + 1;', '\tND_TCHECK_16BITS(&p[0]);', '\t\tND_TCHECK_16BITS(&p[2]);', '\t\telse {', '\t\t\tif (!rawprint(ndo, (const uint8_t *)&p[2], 2)) {', '\t\t\t\tND_PRINT((ndo,")"));', '\t\t\t\tgoto trunc;', '\t\t\t}', '\t\t}', '\t\tND_PRINT((ndo,"len=%d value=", totlen - 4));', '\t\tif (!rawprint(ndo, (const uint8_t *)&p[4], totlen - 4)) {', '\t\t\tND_PRINT((ndo,")"));', '\t\t\tgoto trunc;', '\t\t}', '', 'trunc:', '\treturn NULL;']}
description: The ISAKMP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isakmp.c, several functions.

code_evidence: Before reading p[0], the code dereferences it without any bounds check, and in the non-extended branch it computes totlen from EXTRACT_16BITS(&p[2]), reading two bytes at p[2] before verifying that p+2 is within the buffer.

The only length guard compares ep < p+totlen, but totlen itself was derived from unvalidated packet bytes, and the value/rawprint paths read p[2] and p[4] with lengths taken from the packet (EXTRACT_16BITS(&p[2])) without checking that these offsets remain below ep.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operations are reads past the end of the intended packet buffer, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). This is not CWE-787 because no out-of-bounds write occurs; the flaw is unchecked read access via EXTRACT_16BITS and rawprint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: attacker-controlled ISAKMP attribute length and value fields are dereferenced and used to size reads before validating that p[2], p[4] and the claimed payload stay within ep. Trigger: a truncated or malformed attribute where the header claims more bytes or the value pointer exceeds the captured buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of adjacent memory, leaking data or crashing the parser.

description: The gf_odf_desc_copy function in GPAC 1.0.1 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) via a crafted file in the MP4Box command.

code_evidence: entry is fetched from the sample description list and only null-checked at line 14; type is read from entry at line 17 and drives the second switch at line 18.
For MP4V the cast to GF_MPEGVisualSampleEntryBox and field access at line 39 assume the entry is a visual sample entry; the patch adds an internal_type check before this access.
For MP4A the cast to GF_MPEGAudioSampleEntryBox at line 86 and ase->esd access at line 87 similarly assume audio sample entry layout without validation.
LSR1 casts to GF_LASeRSampleEntryBox and dereferences ptr->lsr_config at lines 207-208/210 with no null check on lsr_config.
MH3D cases cast to GF_MPEGAudioSampleEntryBox and dereference ptr->cfg_mha at lines 228-233; cfg_mha is only null-checked at line 228 but the cast assumes audio layout.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences pointers obtained from a type-directed cast without validating the entry's actual internal_type, so a malformed file yields a NULL/invalid pointer dereference. This matches CWE-476; it is not merely an out-of-bounds read, since the crash stems from dereferencing an assumed-valid pointer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A crafted file can make a sample entry whose type matches a case in the second switch but whose internal_type/box layout does not match the expected sample entry class. The code then casts entry to the wrong structure and dereferences fields (e.g. esd, lsr_config, cfg_mha) that may be absent or invalid, causing a NULL pointer dereference and crash (DoS).

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. It is possible to trigger a null pointer dereference in TensorFlow by passing an invalid input to `tf.raw_ops.CompressElement`. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/47a06f40411a69c99f381495f490536972152ac0/tensorflow/core/data/compression_utils.cc#L34) was accessing the size of a buffer obtained from the return of a separate function call before validating that said buffer is valid. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 5dc7f6981fdaf74c8c5be41f393df705841fb7c5. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: In the size-accumulation loop, when the component dtype supports memcpy, the code calls DMAHelper::buffer(&component)->size() directly; the returned TensorBuffer* is dereferenced without a null check.
In the serialization loop, the same pointer is obtained into buffer and then buffer->data() and buffer->size() are dereferenced unconditionally before any validation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the root cause is dereferencing a pointer expected to be valid but which may be NULL, with no prior validation. The fix adds explicit buffer null checks, confirming the missing constraint rather than a distinct weakness such as buffer overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
if (DataTypeCanUseMemcpy(component.dtype())) {
total_size += DMAHelper::buffer(&component)->size();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: DMAHelper::buffer can return a null TensorBuffer* for a malformed component. The function dereferences that pointer both while computing total_size and while memcpy-ing component data, so an invalid input reaching CompressElement triggers a null pointer dereference, crashing the process (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fixed recursive async function calls.

Previously, PromiseCapability record was stored (function->context)
directly in function object during a function invocation.  This is
not correct, because PromiseCapability record should be linked to
current execution context.  As a result, function->context is
overwritten with consecutive recursive calls which results in
use-after-free.

This closes #451 issue on Github.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['njs_vmcode_await(njs_vm_t *vm, njs_vmcode_await_t *await)', '    njs_async_ctx_t     *ctx;', '    ctx = active->function->await;', '', '        ctx->capability = active->function->context;', '', '        active->function->context = NULL;'], 'added_lines': ['njs_vmcode_await(njs_vm_t *vm, njs_vmcode_await_t *await,', '    njs_promise_capability_t *pcap, njs_async_ctx_t *ctx)', '        ctx->capability = pcap;']}
description: njs through 0.7.0, used in NGINX, was discovered to contain a heap use-after-free in njs_await_fulfilled.

code_evidence: Line 22 reads the async context from the shared function object via active->function->await; when NULL, a new ctx is allocated. Lines 34-36 then bind ctx->capability from active->function->context and clear that field, so the capability record is stored on the function object rather than per execution context.
Lines 55 and 62 attach the same ctx to both fulfilled and rejected function contexts, so this ctx is the object later consumed by njs_await_fulfilled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the root cause is a stored pointer whose lifetime is not tied to the execution context that uses it, leaving a dangling capability reference after the owning invocation completes. This is a use-after-free rather than a simple memory leak or NULL dereference.

evidence_lines.code:
fulfilled->context = ctx;
rejected->context = ctx;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The capability is kept in function->context, a field shared by all invocations of the same function. A recursive async call overwrites or clears that field while an earlier invocation still references its ctx/capability, so the earlier handler later uses a capability that has been released. Trigger is a recursive async call; consequence is a heap use-after-free in njs_await_fulfilled.

commit_msg:
Check if output buffer is too small.

It really seems like libsodium (whose entire purpose is to make crypto
idiot-proof) making me mess with these details is a flaw in the API design.

Also, correct Hungarian.

description: Valve's Game Networking Sockets prior to version v1.2.0 improperly handles long encrypted messages in function AES_GCM_DecryptContext::Decrypt() when compiled using libsodium, leading to a Stack-Based Buffer Overflow and resulting in a memory corruption and possibly even a remote code execution.

code_evidence: Line 7 copies the caller's output-buffer size into a local variable, then line 8 passes pEncryptedDataAndTag directly to crypto_aead_aes256gcm_encrypt_afternm with that size as the capacity. Line 9 lets libsodium write the ciphertext plus authentication tag into the caller's buffer. No check confirms the buffer holds cbPlaintextData + crypto_aead_aes256gcm_ABYTES bytes; line 16 only writes back the resulting length.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function permits an out-of-bounds write into pEncryptedDataAndTag through the missing size constraint. This is distinct from an out-of-bounds read, since the overflowed region is the write destination.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the encryption routine writes plaintext length plus tag bytes into a caller-supplied buffer without validating that the supplied capacity is large enough. Trigger: a caller passes cbPlaintextData exceeding the actual buffer size relative to the advertised size. Consequence: libsodium writes past the buffer end, corrupting adjacent stack memory.

commit_msg:
x86/spec-ctrl: Add spec-ctrl=unpriv-mmio

Per Xen's support statement, PCI passthrough should be to trusted domains
because the overall system security depends on factors outside of Xen's
control.

As such, Xen, in a supported configuration, is not vulnerable to DRPW/SBDR.

However, users who have risk assessed their configuration may be happy with
the risk of DoS, but unhappy with the risk of cross-domain data leakage.  Such
users should enable this option.

On CPUs vulnerable to MDS, the existing mitigations are the best we can do to
mitigate MMIO cross-domain data leakage.

On CPUs fixed to MDS but vulnerable MMIO stale data leakage, this option:

 * On CPUs susceptible to FBSDP, mitigates cross-domain fill buffer leakage
   using FB_CLEAR.
 * On CPUs susceptible to SBDR, mitigates RNG data recovery by engaging the
   srb-lock, previously used to mitigate SRBDS.

Both mitigations require microcode from IPU 2022.1, May 2022.

This is part of XSA-404.

Signed-off-by: Andrew Cooper <andrew.cooper3@citrix.com>
Reviewed-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
