commit_msg:
net: ne2000: check ring buffer control registers

Ne2000 NIC uses ring buffer of NE2000_MEM_SIZE(49152)
bytes to process network packets. Registers PSTART & PSTOP
define ring buffer size & location. Setting these registers
to invalid values could lead to infinite loop or OOB r/w
access issues. Add check to avoid it.

Reported-by: Yang Hongke <yanghongke@huawei.com>
Tested-by: Yang Hongke <yanghongke@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Prasad J Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (s->stop <= s->start) {', '        return 1;', '    }']}
description: The ne2000_receive function in the NE2000 NIC emulation support (hw/net/ne2000.c) in QEMU before 2.5.1 allows local guest OS administrators to cause a denial of service (infinite loop and QEMU process crash) via crafted values for the PSTART and PSTOP registers, involving ring buffer control.

code_evidence: The ring-buffer geometry is taken directly from device registers: index from s->curpag and boundary from s->boundary, then avail is computed as boundary - index or as (s->stop - s->start) - (index - boundary).
The computed avail is compared against MAX_ETH_FRAME_SIZE + 4 to decide fullness; no check constrains stop and start before they are used in the subtraction.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is missing validation of input (device register values) before they are used in arithmetic that governs loop control and buffer bounds, matching CWE-20's improper input validation with an availability/DoS impact. It is not a mere transformation error; the code performs no safety check on start/stop at all.

evidence_lines.code:
if (avail < (MAX_ETH_FRAME_SIZE + 4))
return 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function derives available ring space from guest-controlled PSTART/PSTOP (s->start/s->stop) and boundary registers without validating that stop > start or that the values describe a consistent ring. Trigger: a guest sets PSTOP <= PSTART, making the (s->stop - s->start) term zero or negative, so avail misrepresents free space. Consequence: the caller's fullness/transmit loop can fail to terminate or index outside the 49152-byte ring, yielding a QEMU hang or crash (DoS).

commit_msg: Add packet boundary checks when decompressing IP addresses.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['static void'], 'added_lines': ['static bool', '    if((iphc_ptr - packetbuf_ptr) + postcount > packetbuf_datalen()) {', '      LOG_WARN("Insufficient packet data to decompress IP address\\n");', '      return false;', '    }', '', '  return true;']}
description: Contiki-NG is an operating system for internet-of-things devices. In versions 4.9 and prior, when processing the various IPv6 header fields during IPHC header decompression, Contiki-NG confirms the received packet buffer contains enough data as needed for that field. But no similar check is done before decompressing the IPv6 address. Therefore, up to 16 bytes can be read out of bounds on the line with the statement `memcpy(&ipaddr->u8[16 - postcount], iphc_ptr, postcount);`. The value of `postcount` depends on the address compression used in the received packet and can be controlled by the attacker. As a result, an attacker can inject a packet that causes an out-of-bound read. As of time of publication, a patched version is not available. As a workaround, one can apply the changes in Contiki-NG pull request #2509 to patch the system.

code_evidence: postcount derives from the caller-supplied pref_post_count low nibble (or 16 when 15) and is not bounded against the remaining packet buffer length.
When postcount > 0, memcpy reads postcount bytes from iphc_ptr into ipaddr without any check that iphc_ptr plus postcount stays within packetbuf_datalen().
iphc_ptr is then advanced by postcount, so the copy length and read source both scale with the attacker-influenced value.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe memcpy reads beyond the end of the intended packet buffer; the missing length check is the cause and the over-read is the direct consequence. It is a read, not a write, so CWE-787 does not apply.

evidence_lines.code:
if(postcount > 0) {
memcpy(&ipaddr->u8[16 - postcount], iphc_ptr, postcount);
iphc_ptr += postcount;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decompression copies postcount bytes from iphc_ptr with no constraint tying postcount to the remaining packet data. Trigger: an attacker sends a compressed IPv6 packet whose IPHC address field sets a postcount larger than the bytes actually present. Consequence: an out-of-bounds read of up to 16 bytes past the packet buffer into ipaddr, leaking adjacent memory.

commit_msg: added option to disable trivial auth methods
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (cli_opts.exit_on_trivial_auth && cli_ses.is_trivial_auth) {', '\t\tdropbear_exit("trivial authentication not allowed");', '\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in Dropbear through 2020.81. Due to a non-RFC-compliant check of the available authentication methods in the client-side SSH code, it is possible for an SSH server to change the login process in its favor. This attack can bypass additional security measures such as FIDO2 tokens or SSH-Askpass. Thus, it allows an attacker to abuse a forwarded agent for logging on to another server unnoticed.

code_evidence: recv_msg_userauth_success() unconditionally sets ses.authstate.authdone = 1 and advances cli_ses.state to USERAUTH_SUCCESS_RCVD upon receiving the server's userauth-success message. There is no validation of which authentication method was actually completed before marking authentication done; line 5 merely resets lastauthtype to AUTH_TYPE_NONE, discarding method context.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-287 fits because the function accepts a claimed authentication success without sufficiently proving the claimed identity/method was legitimately authenticated. This is improper authentication, not merely a protocol parsing bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the client trusts the server's success message and marks auth done without verifying the negotiated authentication method. Trigger: a malicious SSH server sends userauth success after a trivial or unexpected method. Consequence: authentication state is accepted, bypassing intended measures such as FIDO2/Askpass and enabling agent abuse.

description:
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's ipv4: igmp component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation.

A race condition can be exploited to cause a timer be mistakenly registered on a RCU read locked object which is freed by another thread.

We recommend upgrading past commit e2b706c691905fe78468c361aaabc719d0a496f1.

code_evidence: igmp_start_timer unconditionally calls refcount_inc(&im->refcnt) after mod_timer returns zero, without verifying that im is still referenced. If the group was concurrently dropped (ip_ma_put reaching zero), the increment operates on a freed ip_mc_list.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and increments a reference count on an ip_mc_list that another thread may have freed, which is exactly reuse of freed memory (CWE-416). The missing refcount_inc_not_zero guard distinguishes it from a mere race/refcount weakness: the object is already freed when accessed.

evidence_lines.code:
if (!mod_timer(&im->timer, jiffies+tv+2))
refcount_inc(&im->refcnt);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the timer is armed and the reference count incremented without any liveness check, so a concurrent igmp_stop_timer/ip_ma_put path can free im between the timer setup and the refcount_inc. Trigger: an IGMP query arriving while the device goes down and leaves the multicast group. Consequence: refcount addition on a freed object, i.e., use-after-free of the mc list entry, leading to memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
misc: sgi-gru: fix use-after-free error in gru_set_context_option, gru_fault and gru_handle_user_call_os

In some bad situation, the gts may be freed gru_check_chiplet_assignment.
The call chain can be gru_unload_context->gru_free_gru_context->gts_drop
and kfree finally. However, the caller didn't know if the gts is freed
or not and use it afterwards. This will trigger a Use after Free bug.

Fix it by introducing a return value to see if it's in error path or not.
Free the gts in caller if gru_check_chiplet_assignment check failed.

Fixes: 55484c45dbec ("gru: allow users to specify gru chiplet 2")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>
Acked-by: Dimitri Sivanich <sivanich@hpe.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20221110035033.19498-1-zyytlz.wz@163.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void gru_check_context_placement(struct gru_thread_state *gts)', '\t\treturn;', '\t\tgru_unload_context(gts, 1);'], 'added_lines': ['int gru_check_context_placement(struct gru_thread_state *gts)', '\tint ret = 0;', '\t/*', "\t * If gru or gts->ts_tgid_owner isn't initialized properly, return", '\t * success to indicate that the caller does not need to unload the', '\t * gru context.The caller is responsible for their inspection and', '\t * reinitialization if needed.', '\t */', '\t\treturn ret;', '\t\tret = -EINVAL;', '', '\treturn ret;']}
description: A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s SGI GRU driver in the way the first gru_file_unlocked_ioctl function is called by the user, where a fail pass occurs in the gru_check_chiplet_assignment function. This flaw allows a local user to crash or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

code_evidence: When gru_check_chiplet_assignment(gru, gts) fails, the function calls gru_unload_context(gts, 1). That chain (gru_free_gru_context -> gts_drop -> kfree) frees the gts object, but the function returns void, so the caller has no way to learn gts was freed and can dereference it afterward.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because gts memory is freed by gru_unload_context and then referenced by an unaware caller. This is a dangling-pointer reuse, not a simple NULL dereference or leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: gru_unload_context frees gts inside the failure branch, while the void return type hides the free from the caller. Trigger: a failed chiplet-assignment check during ioctl/fault handling. Consequence: the caller reuses the freed gts, causing a use-after-free (crash or potential privilege escalation).

commit_msg: Fix #12417/#12418 (arm assembler heap overflows)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tfor (i = j = 0; i < sizeof (buf) - 1 && str[i]; i++, j++) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tfor (i = j = 0; i < sizeof (buf) - 1 && str[j]; i++, j++) {']}
description: In radare2 through 3.1.3, the assemble function inside libr/asm/p/asm_arm_cs.c allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service (application crash via an r_num_calc out-of-bounds read) by crafting an arm assembly input because a loop uses an incorrect index in armass.c and certain length validation is missing in armass64.c, a related issue to CVE-2018-20459.

code_evidence: Loop condition at line 5 tests str[i] while the buffer index used for reading and copying is j (lines 6, 9). When str[j] == '#' (line 6), i-- and continue (line 7) decrement only i, so i and j diverge; j keeps advancing independently of the buffer bound check on i.
The resulting buf may be unterminated or misaligned; line 11 writes buf[i]=0 using the diverged i, and line 12 passes buf to arm_opcode_parse, which may read past the intended content.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the diverging indices cause reads past the end of the input string and the 128-byte buffer, directly matching out-of-bounds read. It is not a write overflow here since the copy is bounded by i < sizeof(buf)-1; the defect is reading with the unvalidated j.

evidence_lines.code:
buf[i] = 0;
arm_opcode_parse (&aop, buf);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop bound and termination check use i, but the input character is read via j, which is incremented in the for-update even when '#' causes i-- and continue. Trigger: an assembly string containing '#' characters makes j advance beyond the region validated and beyond the string terminator. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of str and of buf downstream in arm_opcode_parse, leading to crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
The file is not malformed per se, it just has a huge XRefStm chain
and we end up exhausting the stack space trying to parse them all.

Having more than 4096 XRefStm seems like won't really happen on real
life so break the flow at that point

Fixes #936
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['        // Arbitrary limit because otherwise we exhaust the stack', '        // calling readXRef + readXRefTable', '        if (followedXRefStm->size() > 4096) {', '            error(errSyntaxError, -1, "File has more than 4096 XRefStm, aborting");', '            ok = false;', '        }']}
description: Uncontrolled Recursion in pdfinfo, and pdftops in poppler 0.89.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via crafted input.

code_evidence: readXRefTable reads the trailer's XRefStm offset into pos2 and scans followedXRefStm for a duplicate; when ok remains true it pushes pos2 and recursively calls readXRef(&pos2, followedXRefStm, xrefStreamObjsNum) at line 118.

The only termination condition is duplicate detection against followedXRefStm; there is no depth or count limit before the recursive call, so a crafted chain of distinct XRefStm offsets drives unbounded recursion. A non-ok result only causes goto err0 after recursion returns.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because attacker-controlled trailer offsets cause recursion whose depth is not limited, consuming program stack. This is uncontrolled recursion rather than a simple loop, since the resource exhaustion arises from nested readXRef calls.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recursive descent through chained XRefStm offsets is guarded only by duplicate detection, not by a bound on chain length. Trigger: a PDF trailer whose XRefStm points to successive distinct offsets, each again containing an XRefStm. Consequence: each level adds a readXRef/readXRefTable stack frame, exhausting stack space and causing denial of service.

commit_msg: added some checks to snap handling
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tif(Unpacker.Error())'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif(Unpacker.Error() || NumParts < 1 || NumParts > CSnapshot::MAX_PARTS || Part < 0 | Part >= NumParts || PartSize < 0 || PartSize > MAX_SNAPSHOT_PACKSIZE)']}
description: The CClient::ProcessServerPacket method in engine/client/client.cpp in Teeworlds before 0.6.4 allows remote servers to write to arbitrary physical memory locations and possibly execute arbitrary code via vectors involving snap handling.

code_evidence: Line 193-194: after reading PartSize, NumParts and Part from the untrusted server packet, only Unpacker.Error() is checked before the snapshot data is used; the attacker-controlled Part, NumParts and PartSize are not range-validated.

Line 202: mem_copy writes PartSize bytes to (char*)m_aSnapshotIncommingData + Part*MAX_SNAPSHOT_PACKSIZE, so a negative/large Part or oversized PartSize indexes and writes outside the snapshot buffer. Line 203 also shifts 1<<Part, which is undefined for out-of-range Part.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the unchecked Part/PartSize values drive a buffer write outside the intended bounds of m_aSnapshotIncommingData. The added check in the patch confirms the missing bounds constraint, distinguishing it from a pure integer-overflow root cause.

evidence_lines.code:
if(Unpacker.Error())
return;

mem_copy((char*)m_aSnapshotIncommingData + Part*MAX_SNAPSHOT_PACKSIZE, pData, PartSize);
m_SnapshotParts |= 1<<Part;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing validation of Part, NumParts and PartSize extracted from the remote server's snap message. A malicious server supplies an out-of-range Part or oversized PartSize, causing the mem_copy at line 202 to write past m_aSnapshotIncommingData (and the shift at line 203 to misbehave), enabling arbitrary physical memory write and possible code execution.

The error page allows injecting snippets using the distinguished name of
untrusted certificates via the %D template parameter.
This patch quote information retrieved from  remote certificates using the
%ssl_subject, %ssl_ca_name and %ssl_cn error details formating codes.

Thanks to Nikolas Lohmann [eBlocker] for identifying the problem.

This is a Measurement Factory project

commit_msg:
Handle null return from iniparser_getstring

Fix handling of NULL returns from iniparser_getstring in
iniparser_getboolean, iniparser_getlongint and iniparser_getdouble,
avoiding a crash.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (str==INI_INVALID_KEY) return notfound ;'], 'added_lines': ['    if (str==NULL || str==INI_INVALID_KEY) return notfound ;']}
description: iniparser v4.1 is vulnerable to NULL Pointer Dereference in function iniparser_getlongint which misses check NULL for function iniparser_getstring's return.

code_evidence: Line 4 stores the return of iniparser_getstring into str, which may be NULL. Line 5 only checks for INI_INVALID_KEY and does not test str for NULL, so a NULL return passes through. Line 6 then passes str directly to strtol, which dereferences the pointer.

Verify that user applications are not using the kernel RPC message
handle to restrict them from directly attaching to guest OS on the
remote subsystem. This is a port of CVE-2019-2308 fix.

Fixes: c68cfb718c8f ("misc: fastrpc: Add support for context Invoke method")
Cc: Srinivas Kandagatla <srinivas.kandagatla@linaro.org>
Cc: Jonathan Marek <jonathan@marek.ca>

Signed-off-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210212192658.3476137-1-dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (handle == FASTRPC_INIT_HANDLE && !kernel) {', '\t\tdev_warn_ratelimited(fl->sctx->dev, "user app trying to send a kernel RPC message (%d)\\n",  handle);', '\t\treturn -EPERM;', '\t}']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 5.11.6. fastrpc_internal_invoke in drivers/misc/fastrpc.c does not prevent user applications from sending kernel RPC messages, aka CID-20c40794eb85. This is a related issue to CVE-2019-2308.

code_evidence: fastrpc_internal_invoke accepts a kernel flag and a handle from its caller and performs no check that a user-originated invocation (kernel == 0) is barred from using the reserved kernel RPC handle.
The handle is passed unchanged to fastrpc_invoke_send, so a user application can attach to the guest OS on the remote subsystem via the kernel message handle.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-862 fits because the function performs an action (sending an RPC with a privileged handle) without verifying that the actor is authorized for that handle; the missing kernel/user check is precisely missing authorization, not a memory-safety flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
static int fastrpc_internal_invoke(struct fastrpc_user *fl,  u32 kernel,
u32 handle, u32 sc,
struct fastrpc_invoke_args *args)
err = fastrpc_invoke_send(fl->sctx, ctx, kernel, handle);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function lacks an authorization check distinguishing user callers from kernel callers before honoring the handle. Trigger: a user-space app invokes with handle FASTRPC_INIT_HANDLE and kernel == 0. Consequence: bypass of the restriction, letting user applications use the kernel RPC message handle to attach directly to the remote guest OS.

commit_msg:
admin: Prevent access if any authentication agent isn't available

The backend currently allows to access and modify files without prompting
for password if any polkit authentication agent isn't available. This seems
isn't usually problem, because polkit agents are integral parts of
graphical environments / linux distributions. The agents can't be simply
disabled without root permissions and are automatically respawned. However,
this might be a problem in some non-standard cases.

This affects only users which belong to wheel group (i.e. those who are
already allowed to use sudo). It doesn't allow privilege escalation for
users, who don't belong to that group.

Let's return permission denied error also when the subject can't be
authorized by any polkit agent to prevent this behavior.

Closes: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gvfs/issues/355
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  is_authorized = polkit_authorization_result_get_is_authorized (result) ||', '    polkit_authorization_result_get_is_challenge (result);'], 'added_lines': ['  is_authorized = polkit_authorization_result_get_is_authorized (result);']}
description: An incorrect permission check in the admin backend in gvfs before version 1.39.4 was found that allows reading and modify arbitrary files by privileged users without asking for password when no authentication agent is running. This vulnerability can be exploited by malicious programs running under privileges of users belonging to the wheel group to further escalate its privileges by modifying system files without user's knowledge. Successful exploitation requires uncommon system configuration.

code_evidence: The function synchronously checks the caller's authorization for "org.gtk.vfs.file-operations" with POLKIT_CHECK_AUTHORIZATION_FLAGS_ALLOW_USER_INTERACTION, treating the returned result as the access decision.
is_authorized is computed as authorized OR challenge; a challenge result (authentication required but no agent available) is accepted as sufficient authorization.
Only when is_authorized is false does it fail with G_IO_ERROR_PERMISSION_DENIED; otherwise the job proceeds, so the OR with is_challenge lets the call through without completed authentication.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-863 fits because the function performs an authorization check but incorrectly accepts a challenge (unresolved authentication) as authorization, bypassing the intended access-control decision. This is incorrect authorization logic, not merely a missing check.

evidence_lines.code:
result = polkit_authority_check_authorization_sync (self->authority,
subject,
"org.gtk.vfs.file-operations",
NULL, POLKIT_CHECK_AUTHORIZATION_FLAGS_ALLOW_USER_INTERACTION,
NULL, &error);

is_authorized = polkit_authorization_result_get_is_authorized (result) ||
polkit_authorization_result_get_is_challenge (result);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the authorization decision conflates an outstanding authentication challenge with a granted authorization. Trigger: a wheel-group caller (or malicious program under such privileges) requests a file operation while no polkit authentication agent is available, causing polkit to return a challenge result. Consequence: the check returns authorized and the privileged file operation proceeds without a password, allowing modification of system files.

check null pointer in broken tiled file handling

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

commit_msg:
drm/amd/display: memory leak

In dcn*_clock_source_create when dcn20_clk_src_construct fails allocated
clk_src needs release.

Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tkfree(clk_src);']}
description: Memory leaks in *clock_source_create() functions under drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc in the Linux kernel before 5.3.8 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption). This affects the dce112_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce112/dce112_resource.c, the dce100_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce100/dce100_resource.c, the dcn10_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn10/dcn10_resource.c, the dcn20_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dcn20/dcn20_resource.c, the dce120_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce120/dce120_resource.c, the dce110_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce110/dce110_resource.c, and the dce80_clock_source_create() function in drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/dce80/dce80_resource.c, aka CID-055e547478a1.

code_evidence: clk_src is allocated with kzalloc and returned via &clk_src->base on success; allocation is only checked for NULL here.
The failure branch of dce112_clk_src_construct is entered when the constructor returns nonzero, meaning the allocated clk_src is not returned to the caller.
In the original function, this failure path executes BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER() and returns NULL without freeing clk_src, so the allocation pointer is lost.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because memory is allocated and then abandoned on an error path with no remaining reference for release. It is not a use-after-free or double-free: the defect is the missing free of a still-live allocation before returning NULL.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function allocates clk_src but the error branch after a failed dce112_clk_src_construct returns NULL without releasing it. Trigger: repeated calls where construction fails (e.g., malformed/invalid resource conditions). Supported consequence: unreclaimed heap memory accumulates, leading to resource-consumption DoS.

commit_msg: fixed #2356
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (vps->max_layer_id > MAX_LHVC_LAYERS) {'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (vps->max_layer_id >= MAX_LHVC_LAYERS) {', '\t\tvps->max_layer_id = 0;']}
description: GPAC MP4Box 2.1-DEV-rev644-g5c4df2a67 is vulnerable to buffer overflow in function gf_hevc_read_vps_bs_internal of media_tools/av_parsers.c:8039

code_evidence: Line 34 reads max_layer_id (6 bits, range 0-63) from the bitstream. Line 35 rejects only values strictly greater than MAX_LHVC_LAYERS, so max_layer_id == MAX_LHVC_LAYERS passes. commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

From GH #178 fuzzing

description: An issue was discovered in GNU LibreDWG through 0.9.3. Crafted input will lead to a heap-based buffer over-read in bit_write_TF in bits.c.

code_evidence: The loop at [20,22] advances i while byte[i] & 0x7f is zero, so i can reach 4 when all bytes are zero. Line [23] then reads byte[i] with i==4, which is within byte[5] (index 4), so no OOB here; the subsequent i-- can make i negative, and line [25] byte[i] &= 0x7f then reads/writes before the array start when the 0x40 bit is set.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the function reads (and then writes) byte[-1], i.e., before the beginning of the intended byte[5] buffer. This is an out-of-bounds read; the patch adds i > 0 to prevent the underflow.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the sign-bit test at [23] decrements i without checking i > 0, so when the loop terminates at i==0 with the 0x40 bit set, i becomes -1. Trigger: crafted input whose most significant encoded byte has bit 0x40 set. The consequence is an out-of-bounds access at byte[-1] on line [25] (and the negative index propagates into the write loop at [28]).

commit_msg:
Fix out-of-bounds read with 'xmllint --htmlout'

Make sure that truncated UTF-8 sequences don't cause an out-of-bounds
array access.

Thanks to @SuhwanSong and the Agency for Defense Development (ADD) for
the report.

Fixes #178.

This is a hack to at least avoid', '     * an out-of-bounds read.', '     */', '    memset(&buffer[sizeof(buffer)-4], 0, 4);']}
description: GNOME project libxml2 v2.9.10 has a global buffer over-read vulnerability in xmlEncodeEntitiesInternal at libxml2/entities.c. The issue has been fixed in commit 50f06b3e.

code_evidence: The function passes the global `buffer` directly to `xmlEncodeEntitiesReentrant` without first ensuring the buffer terminates on a complete UTF-8 sequence. When the buffer ends with a truncated multi-byte UTF-8 sequence, the encoder continues reading past the intended end of the buffer.

result = (char *) xmlEncodeEntitiesReentrant(NULL, BAD_CAST buffer);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no bound or UTF-8 boundary check before encoding, so a truncated trailing sequence causes the decoder to consume bytes beyond the buffer's valid data. Trigger: `buffer` contents ending mid-sequence; consequence is an out-of-bounds read (memory disclosure or crash), matching the commit's fix that zeroes the final four bytes to avoid the over-read.

commit_msg:
Merge pull request from GHSA-cv8x-p47p-99wr

* - Avoid SSL socket parent/listener getting destroyed during handshake by increasing parent's reference count.
- Add missing SSL socket close when the newly accepted SSL socket is discarded in SIP TLS transport.

* - Fix silly mistake: accepted active socket created without group lock in SSL socket.
- Replace assertion with normal validation check of SSL socket instance in OpenSSL verification callback (verify_cb()) to avoid crash, e.g: if somehow race condition with SSL socket destroy happens or OpenSSL application data index somehow gets corrupted.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t    pj_bool_t ret;', '\t    if (ret == PJ_FALSE)', '\t\treturn PJ_FALSE;\t', '\t    pj_bool_t ret;', '\t    if (ret == PJ_FALSE)', '\t\treturn PJ_FALSE;'], 'added_lines': ['\tpj_bool_t ret = PJ_TRUE;', '', '\t    }', '', '\t    /* Decrement ref count of parent */', '\t    if (ssock->parent->param.grp_lock) {', '\t\tpj_grp_lock_dec_ref(ssock->parent->param.grp_lock);', '\t\tssock->parent = NULL;', '', '', "\t/* Decrement ref count of parent and reset parent (we don't need it", '\t * anymore, right?).', '\t */', '\tif (ssock->parent->param.grp_lock) {', '\t    pj_grp_lock_dec_ref(ssock->parent->param.grp_lock);', '\t    ssock->parent = NULL;', '\t}', '', '\tif (ret == PJ_FALSE)', '\t    return PJ_FALSE;']}
description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In PJSIP before version 2.11.1, there are a couple of issues found in the SSL socket. First, a race condition between callback and destroy, due to the accepted socket having no group lock. Second, the SSL socket parent/listener may get destroyed during handshake. Both issues were reported to happen intermittently in heavy load TLS connections. They cause a crash, resulting in a denial of service. These are fixed in version 2.11.1.

code_evidence: The accept-complete callbacks are invoked with ssock->parent as an argument, but this parent pointer is not protected by any group lock or reference held during the handshake callback.

The callback return value is stored in a local ret and checked only after the callback returns; the callback itself may release or destroy the parent/listener while the handshake path still references it.
The on_accept_complete branch similarly reads ssock->parent and passes it to the application callback without synchronization against destruction.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a timing window in concurrent code where a shared resource (the parent/listener) is accessed without exclusive synchronization, matching CWE-362. It is not merely a missing null check; the defect is the unsynchronized concurrent access to the shared parent object.

evidence_lines.code:
(*ssock->param.cb.on_accept_complete2) 
(ssock->parent, ssock, (pj_sockaddr_t*)&ssock->rem_addr, 
pj_sockaddr_get_len((pj_sockaddr_t*)&ssock->rem_addr), 
status);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the accepted SSL socket's parent/listener is dereferenced during the handshake-complete callback without holding a reference count or group lock, so a concurrent destroy can free the parent. Trigger: heavy-load TLS accept/handshake races with socket destruction. Consequence: use-after-free/crash, a denial of service.

commit_msg:
xfs: don't fail when converting shortform attr to long form during ATTR_REPLACE

Kanda Motohiro reported that expanding a tiny xattr into a large xattr
fails on XFS because we remove the tiny xattr from a shortform fork and
then try to re-add it after converting the fork to extents format having
not removed the ATTR_REPLACE flag.  This fails because the attr is no
longer present, causing a fs shutdown.

This is derived from the patch in his bug report, but we really
shouldn't ignore a nonzero retval from the remove call.

Bugzilla: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=199119
Reported-by: kanda.motohiro@gmail.com
Reviewed-by: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tASSERT(retval == 0);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (retval)', '\t\t\treturn retval;', '\t\t/*', '\t\t * Since we have removed the old attr, clear ATTR_REPLACE so', "\t\t * that the leaf format add routine won't trip over the attr", '\t\t * not being around.', '\t\t */', '\t\targs->flags &= ~ATTR_REPLACE;']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 4.17, a local attacker able to set attributes on an xfs filesystem could make this filesystem non-operational until the next mount by triggering an unchecked error condition during an xfs attribute change, because xfs_attr_shortform_addname in fs/xfs/libxfs/xfs_attr.c mishandles ATTR_REPLACE operations with conversion of an attr from short to long form.

code_evidence: On the EEXIST path, the existing attr is removed via xfs_attr_shortform_remove, but the return value is only checked by ASSERT, which is compiled out in non-debug kernels, so a removal failure is silently ignored.
After removal, the ATTR_REPLACE flag is left set, so the subsequent shortform-to-extents conversion and leaf add path expects an attr that no longer exists.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code assumes removal cannot fail and ignores the nonzero retval, an improper check for an unusual condition (CWE-754), leading to filesystem shutdown. This is not merely an assertion failure; the unchecked error propagates into inconsistent state.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the exceptional return from xfs_attr_shortform_remove is not checked, and ATTR_REPLACE is not cleared after removing the old attr. Trigger: a local user performs an ATTR_REPLACE that converts a shortform attr to long form. The leaf add routine trips over the missing attr and shuts down the filesystem.

commit_msg:
Fix qpress directory traversal vulnerability

A bad actor user can prepare the payload as:

```
mkdir -p AAAAAAAAA/secure_file_priv_dir
touch AAAAAAAAA/secure_file_priv_dir/evil.so
qpress -r AAAAAAAAA payload.qp
Then edit the payload.qp in a hex editor or sed to replace AAAAAAAAA with ../../../
(example: sed -i 's/AAAAAAAAA/..\/..\/..\//' payload.qp)
```

Fix bug by checking the directory and reject the command if find the attempt to traversal

Test: see example above and try to reproduce it. Before fix you can observe
traversal. After fix - the error message(File path contains directory traversal
which is not allowed.) shown, no traversal observe.

All new code of the whole pull request, including one or several files
that are either new files or modified ones, are contributed under the BSD-new
license.  I am contributing on behalf of my employer Amazon Web Services,
Inc.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            try_aread(tmp, chunk_size + 1); // read file name'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif(NAME_BUFFER_SIZE < chunk_size + 1)', '            {', '                abort("File path string is bigger than buffer size");', '            }', '\t\t\t/* RDS security fix: https://rds-jira.amazon.com/browse/MMCP-231', '\t \t\tNeed to check if we try to decompress file or directory outside working directory', '\t \t\t*/', '\t        if(true == check_if_path_has_dir_traversal(tmp)) ', '            {', '\t            abort("Directory path contains directory traversal which is not allowed.");', '\t        }', '\t        /* End of RDS security fix*/', '            if(NAME_BUFFER_SIZE < chunk_size + 1)', '\t             {', '\t                 abort("File path string is bigger than buffer size");', '\t             }', "\t             try_aread(tmp, chunk_size + 1); // read file name to 'tmp' with size 'chunk_size + 1'", '\t         /* RDS security fix: https://rds-jira.amazon.com/browse/MMCP-231', '\t \t\t   Need to check if we try to decompress file or directory outside working directory', '\t \t\t*/', '\t         if(true == check_if_path_has_dir_traversal(tmp)) ', '\t         {', '\t             abort("File path contains directory traversal which is not allowed.");', '\t         }', '\t         /* End of RDS security fix*/']}
description: qpress before PierreLvx/qpress 20220819 and before version 11.3, as used in Percona XtraBackup and other products, allows directory traversal via ../ in a .qp file.

code_evidence: chunk_size is read from the archive and passed to try_aread(tmp, chunk_size + 1); the resulting tmp is concatenated into curdir, which is then used to create a directory at [24] (mkdir(curdir.c_str(), 509)).
In the 'F' branch, tmp is read from the archive and concatenated into buf2 = curdir + DELIM_STR + tmp; buf2 is passed to decompress_file(buf2) at [38] without neutralizing '../' elements.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function constructs pathnames from external archive input intended to stay under extract_dir but does not neutralize traversal elements, matching CWE-22; the fix's check_if_path_has_dir_traversal confirms this is the targeted weakness rather than a mere buffer issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: directory and file names read from the .qp archive are appended to the extraction path without rejecting '..' components, so a crafted payload can escape the restricted directory. Trigger: an archive entry whose name contains '../' (or an absolute path). Consequence: files or directories are created or overwritten outside the intended extraction directory, enabling unauthorized file write/code execution.

commit_msg:
Internal change

PiperOrigin-RevId: 411896058
Change-Id: Ia031058247e3cf382957a6662d3f9e1cbb481ca2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  ConvolutionDimensions dims = OpDimensionsFromInputs(', '      op_info.inputs(1).shape(), op_info, &found_unknown_shapes);'], 'added_lines': ['  TF_ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(ConvolutionDimensions dims,', '                      OpDimensionsFromInputs(op_info.inputs(1).shape(), op_info,', '                                             &found_unknown_shapes));']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The estimator for the cost of some convolution operations can be made to execute a division by 0. The function fails to check that the stride argument is strictly positive. Hence, the fix is to add a check for the stride argument to ensure it is valid. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: OpDimensionsFromInputs derives convolution dimensions (including iz, ix, iy) from the input tensor shape and op_info; the stride argument's validity is not checked here, and the return value is assigned directly without any error propagation.
The compute-cost expression multiplies dims.iz by an expression containing dims.ix, dims.iy and dims.batch; if the stride-derived dimension is zero, this arithmetic can divide by zero.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs arithmetic on dimensions whose derivation depends on an unchecked stride, and the commit specifically adds validation to prevent division by zero. This matches CWE-369 (Divide By Zero): an unexpected value reaches a calculation without proper detection, impacting availability via crash.

evidence_lines.code:
ConvolutionDimensions dims = OpDimensionsFromInputs(
op_info.inputs(1).shape(), op_info, &found_unknown_shapes);
ops = dims.iz * (dims.batch * dims.ix * dims.iy * 11 + 5 + rsqrt_cost);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the dimension/stride computation feeding this estimator does not reject a non-positive stride, so a zero dimension can reach the cost arithmetic. Trigger: a convolution op with a zero (or otherwise invalid) stride supplied by a crafted model. Consequence: division by zero inside the cost estimation, causing a crash/DoS rather than a wrong cost estimate.

commit_msg:
Merge to XFA: openjpeg: Fix potential bad precno value in opj_pi_next* functions.

TBR=thestig@chromium.org
BUG=571479

Original Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1585243003 .

(cherry picked from commit 0b56371b1e9683676cf191f2d9d41d40d47c3726)

Review URL: https://codereview.chromium.org/1590593002 .
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tif (pi->precno >= res->pw * res->ph) {', '\t\t\t\t\t\treturn OPJ_FALSE;', '\t\t\t\t\t}']}
description: pi.c in OpenJPEG, as used in PDFium in Google Chrome before 48.0.2564.109, does not validate a certain precision value, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted JPEG 2000 image in a PDF document, related to the opj_pi_next_rpcl, opj_pi_next_pcrl, and opj_pi_next_cprl functions.

code_evidence: Lines 59-63 compute prci/prcj from x/y coordinates and res->pdx/pdy, then cast the arithmetic result into pi->precno without verifying prci+prcj*res->pw stays below the resolution's precision count. Line 57 only rejects pw==0 or ph==0, not an out-of-range precno. Line 65 then uses pi->precno*pi->step_p to index pi->include, and line 66 dereferences pi->include[index]; the patch inserts the missing precno >= res->pw*res->ph guard just after line 63.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked precno causes a buffer index beyond pi->include's intended bounds, directly matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds memory buffer read/write. It is not merely an integer issue: the missing precision bound is the operative defect enabling the out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: a crafted JPEG 2000 geometry makes the computed precision index prci+prcj*res->pw exceed the valid precision grid, and no bound check constrains precno. Trigger: a crafted image reaching opj_pi_next_rpcl with inconsistent resolution/coordinate values. Consequence: the index at line 65 is out of range, so pi->include[index] at line 66 performs an out-of-bounds read (and subsequent write), supporting crash/DoS or memory disclosure/execution as described.

commit_msg:
Revert "NFSv4: Handle the special Linux file open access mode"

This reverts commit 44942b4e457beda00981f616402a1a791e8c616e.

After secondly opening a file with O_ACCMODE|O_DIRECT flags,
nfs4_valid_open_stateid() will dereference NULL nfs4_state when lseek().

Reproducer:
  1. mount -t nfs -o vers=4.2 $server_ip:/ /mnt/
  2. fd = open("/mnt/file", O_ACCMODE|O_DIRECT|O_CREAT)
  3. close(fd)
  4. fd = open("/mnt/file", O_ACCMODE|O_DIRECT)
  5. lseek(fd)

Reported-by: Lyu Tao <tao.lyu@epfl.ch>
Signed-off-by: ChenXiaoSong <chenxiaosong2@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Trond Myklebust <trond.myklebust@hammerspace.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\treturn nfs_open(inode, filp);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\topenflags--;']}
description: An issue was discovered in fs/nfs/dir.c in the Linux kernel before 5.16.5. If an application sets the O_DIRECTORY flag, and tries to open a regular file, nfs_atomic_open() performs a regular lookup. If a regular file is found, ENOTDIR should occur, but the server instead returns uninitialized data in the file descriptor.

code_evidence: When the access mode is the special Linux O_ACCMODE value 3 (via O_ACCMODE|O_DIRECT), the function bypasses normal open processing and calls nfs_open() directly, returning early before alloc_nfs_open_context and open_context setup.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function returns a file whose open state/context was never initialized through the normal path, and that uninitialized resource is later used, matching CWE-908 (Use of Uninitialized Resource). The defect is missing initialization of the resource, not merely a NULL check.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((openflags & O_ACCMODE) == 3)
return nfs_open(inode, filp);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the special access-mode branch short-circuits nfs4_file_open and returns an nfs_open() result without establishing the full NFSv4 open state. Trigger: an application opens a file with O_ACCMODE|O_DIRECT; the resulting file object lacks properly initialized open context/state, so a later operation (lseek) dereferences an uninitialized/NULL nfs4_state. Consequence: NULL dereference and crash (availability impact).

The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/dcba796a28364d6d7f003f6fe733d82726dda713/tensorflow/core/kernels/fractional_avg_pool_op.cc#L216) fails to validate that the pooling sequence arguments have enough elements as required by the `out_backprop` tensor shape. Trigger: caller supplies a pooling sequence tensor with too few elements while out_backprop has larger out_rows/out_cols. The out-of-range r+1/c+1 reads yield attacker-influenced indices, and coeffRef writes past the allocated temp buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow (memory corruption/crash).

commit_msg:
The current code performs the cancel of a delayed work at the late
stage of disconnection procedure, which may lead to the access to the
already cleared state.

This patch assures to call cancel_delayed_work_sync() at the beginning
of the disconnection procedure for avoiding that race.  The delayed
work object is now assigned in the common line6 object instead of its
derivative, so that we can call cancel_delayed_work_sync().

Along with the change, the startup function is called via the new
callback instead.  This will make it easier to port other LINE6
drivers to use the delayed work for startup in later patches.

Reported-by: syzbot+5255458d5e0a2b10bbb9@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 7f84ff68be05 ("ALSA: line6: toneport: Fix broken usage of timer for delayed execution")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tINIT_DELAYED_WORK(&line6->startup_work, line6_startup_work);']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.1.8. There is a NULL pointer dereference caused by a malicious USB device in the sound/usb/line6/driver.c driver.

code_evidence: line6 is card->private_data, then its fields are initialized; the delayed startup work is not initialized here in the before version.
private_init may fail and jump to error, which calls line6_disconnect(interface) while the delayed work was never initialized/cancelled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The target CWE-476 fits because the defect results in a NULL/invalid pointer dereference during the disconnect path due to the uninitialized delayed work, leading to a crash. The fix initializes the delayed work in line6_probe via INIT_DELAYED_WORK before any failure/disconnect handling.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The startup delayed work is not initialized at probe time, but a failure path (private_init error) invokes line6_disconnect, which operates on the uninitialized delayed work state. This race/ordering leads to dereferencing an invalid/NULL state, causing a crash (NULL pointer dereference) on malicious USB device disconnect.

commit_msg:
NetKVM: BZ#1169718: Checking the length only on read

Signed-off-by: Joseph Hindin <yhindin@rehat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                                               FALSE,']}
description: The NetKVM Windows Virtio driver allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (guest crash) via a crafted length value in an IP packet, as demonstrated by a value that does not account for the size of the IP options.

code_evidence: The function derives the IP length from the packet by calling PopulateIPLength with EthPayloadLength, which is peer-controlled, without checking that the length accounts for header size or IP options.

ParaNdis_CheckSumVerifyFlat is invoked with a parameter list that lacks a length/options validation flag (the patch adds FALSE here), so the parsing of the packet is performed without enforcing the length consistency.
The parsed header size (packetReview.XxpIpHeaderSize) is then used to compute VHeader->hdr_len, propagating the unchecked length into the virtio header.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is missing validation of a length value received from the network before it is used for parsing and header construction, matching CWE-20's improper input validation of a specified quantity. It is not a transformation/filtering issue; the length is trusted as-is.

evidence_lines.code: PopulateIPLength(reinterpret_cast<IPv4Header*>(IpHeader), static_cast<USHORT>(EthPayloadLength));
VHeader->hdr_len = (USHORT)(packetReview.XxpIpHeaderSize + IpHeaderOffset + PriorityHdrLen);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the packet's length field is used to populate and parse the IP header without validating it against the actual payload size or IP options. Trigger: a crafted IPv4 packet with a length value inconsistent with the header/options. Consequence: the derived header size is wrong and downstream processing can crash the guest (DoS).

commit_msg:
adapter: Fix storing discoverable setting

discoverable setting shall only be store when changed via Discoverable
property and not when discovery client set it as that be considered
temporary just for the lifetime of the discovery.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (adapter->discovery_discoverable)', '\t\tset_discovery_discoverable(adapter, false);'], 'added_lines': ['\tset_discovery_discoverable(adapter, false);']}
description: bluetoothd from bluez incorrectly saves adapters' Discoverable status when a device is powered down, and restores it when powered up. If a device is powered down while discoverable, it will be discoverable when powered on again. This could lead to inadvertent exposure of the bluetooth stack to physically nearby attackers.

code_evidence: On the last-client path, discovery_stop clears the adapter's discoverable state via set_discovery_discoverable(adapter, false) only when adapter->discovery_discoverable is set, then proceeds to stop discovery.
The early branch for remaining discovery clients removes the client and returns without touching the discoverable state, so the discoverable flag persists across discovery stop for non-final clients.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-863 fits because the state transition that should gate discoverable access is performed incorrectly: the reset is conditional and skipped on some paths, so the protection/authorization state is not correctly enforced. This is a state-handling authorization flaw, not merely a missing check or resource leak.

evidence_lines.code:
if (adapter->discovery_discoverable)
set_discovery_discoverable(adapter, false);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function conditionally resets the adapter's discoverable state based on an internal flag and per-client list position rather than authorization/state provenance, allowing the discoverable setting to remain active after discovery ends or the adapter powers down. Trigger: discovery stop or power-down while discoverable; consequence: the adapter is restored discoverable on power-up, exposing the Bluetooth stack to nearby actors.

commit_msg: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/1472
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (((MagickSizeType) image->columns*image->rows) > GetBlobSize(image))', '    ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"InsufficientImageDataInFile");']}
description: The cineon parsing component in ImageMagick 7.0.8-26 Q16 allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service (uncontrolled resource consumption) by crafting a Cineon image with an incorrect claimed image size. This occurs because ReadCINImage in coders/cin.c lacks a check for insufficient image data in a file.

code_evidence: Image dimensions are taken directly from the file's channel header: image->columns=cin.image.channel[0].pixels_per_line and image->rows=cin.image.channel[0].lines_per_image, with no validation against the actual blob size.
SetImageExtent allocates the pixel cache for the attacker-claimed columns/rows before any data-availability check.
The decode loop iterates y < image->rows and queues/reads each row; a large claimed row count drives repeated allocation and processing even when the file contains little pixel data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-400 fits because the function fails to constrain how much resource it consumes in response to input; the claimed dimensions drive allocation and processing without a size check. This is resource exhaustion, distinct from a memory-corruption overflow (CWE-787), since the issue is unbounded consumption rather than out-of-bounds writing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser trusts attacker-controlled pixels_per_line/lines_per_image and allocates the full image extent and row cache without checking that the file actually contains that much data. Trigger: a crafted Cineon file declaring a huge image size; the reader then allocates and processes up to rows*columns worth of pixels. Supported consequence: uncontrolled memory/CPU consumption leading to denial of service.

commit_msg:
Issue #718: Fix TALOS-CAN-152

If a 7-Zip archive declares a rediculously large number of substreams,
it can overflow an internal counter, leading a subsequent memory
allocation to be too small for the substream data.

Thanks to the Open Source and Threat Intelligence project at Cisco
for reporting this issue.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\tif (unpack_streams > SIZE_MAX - UMAX_ENTRY) {', '\t\t\t\treturn (-1);', '\t\t\t}']}
description: Integer overflow in the read_SubStreamsInfo function in archive_read_support_format_7zip.c in libarchive before 3.2.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a 7zip file with a large number of substreams, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

code_evidence: unpack_streams is initialized to 0 and accumulated across the numFolders loop by adding each attacker-controlled f[i].numUnpackStreams (parsed from the archive). The only per-entry check caps each value at UMAX_ENTRY, but the running sum is never checked before the +=, so many entries can wrap the size_t counter.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is an unchecked integer addition that can wrap the size_t counter, which is exactly CWE-190. The subsequent undersized allocation and out-of-bounds writes are consequences of that overflow, not a separate missing-bounds issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Each f[i].numUnpackStreams is bounded by UMAX_ENTRY, but the unchecked accumulation into unpack_streams can overflow size_t to a small value. That wrapped count is stored in ss->unpack_streams and drives the calloc sizes for unpackSizes/digestsDefined/digests, so the buffers are undersized; later loops write up to the real substream count, producing a heap-based buffer overflow.

commit_msg:
media: stv06xx: add missing descriptor sanity checks

Make sure to check that we have two alternate settings and at least one
endpoint before accessing the second altsetting structure and
dereferencing the endpoint arrays.

This specifically avoids dereferencing NULL-pointers or corrupting
memory when a device does not have the expected descriptors.

Note that the sanity checks in stv06xx_start() and pb0100_start() are
not redundant as the driver is mixing looking up altsettings by index
and by number, which may not coincide.

Fixes: 8668d504d72c ("V4L/DVB (12082): gspca_stv06xx: Add support for st6422 bridge and sensor")
Fixes: c0b33bdc5b8d ("[media] gspca-stv06xx: support bandwidth changing")
Cc: stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>     # 2.6.31
Cc: Hans de Goede <hdegoede@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\talt = &gspca_dev->dev->actconfig->intf_cache[0]->altsetting[1];'], 'added_lines': ['\tstruct usb_interface_cache *intfc;', '\tintfc = gspca_dev->dev->actconfig->intf_cache[0];', '', '\tif (intfc->num_altsetting < 2)', '\t\treturn -ENODEV;', '', '\talt = &intfc->altsetting[1];', '', '\tif (alt->desc.bNumEndpoints < 1)', '\t\treturn -ENODEV;', '']}
description: An issue was discovered in the stv06xx subsystem in the Linux kernel before 5.6.1. drivers/media/usb/gspca/stv06xx/stv06xx.c and drivers/media/usb/gspca/stv06xx/stv06xx_pb0100.c mishandle invalid descriptors, as demonstrated by a NULL pointer dereference, aka CID-485b06aadb93.

code_evidence: Line 5 unconditionally indexes intf_cache[0]->altsetting[1] without verifying that the interface cache has at least two alternate settings. Line 6 then dereferences alt->endpoint[0] without checking that the selected altsetting declares at least one endpoint, so a device descriptor with fewer altsettings or zero endpoints yields an invalid or NULL pointer that is immediately written through.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-476 fits because the unchecked descriptor-derived pointer (altsetting[1] or endpoint[0]) can be NULL or invalid and is dereferenced/written. This is a missing-validity-check NULL dereference rather than a pure out-of-bounds indexing weakness, since the descriptor expectation of a valid pointer is violated.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts USB descriptor layout and accesses altsetting[1] and endpoint[0] without validating num_altsetting or bNumEndpoints. Trigger: a device presenting malformed descriptors (fewer than two altsettings or no endpoints). Consequence: NULL/invalid pointer dereference and out-of-bounds write to wMaxPacketSize, causing kernel crash or memory corruption.

commit_msg:
Fix heap buffer overflow in tf.raw_ops.UnicodeEncode.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 371717714
Change-Id: If33443b28f158e58078f1268f6b92f2728d219e0
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    // Operation will treat first argument in input_splits as if it were zero', '    // regardless of its actual value since splits should begin with zero and', '    // end with the length of the input values vector.', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, input_splits_flat(0) == 0,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("First value in input_splits must be zero."));', '    OP_REQUIRES(context,', '                input_splits_flat(input_splits_flat.size() - 1) ==', '                    input_tensor_flat.size(),', '                errors::InvalidArgument("Last value in input_splits must be "', '                                        "equal to length of input_tensor."));', '      OP_REQUIRES(', '          context, input_splits_flat(i - 1) <= input_splits_flat(i),', '          errors::InvalidArgument(', '              "Values in input_splits must be equal or in ascending order."));', '      OP_REQUIRES(', '          context, input_splits_flat(i) <= input_tensor_flat.size(),', '          errors::InvalidArgument("Values in input_splits must be less than or "', '                                  "equal to input_tensor length."));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. An attacker can access data outside of bounds of heap allocated array in `tf.raw_ops.UnicodeEncode`. This is because the implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/472c1f12ad9063405737679d4f6bd43094e1d36d/tensorflow/core/kernels/unicode_ops.cc) assumes that the `input_value`/`input_splits` pair specify a valid sparse tensor. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: The loop iterates from i=1 while reading input_splits_flat(i), and the inner loop reads input_tensor_flat(idx) with idx advanced until it reaches input_splits_flat(i).
input_splits_flat is derived from the user-supplied input_splits tensor; its values are used directly as bounds into input_tensor_flat without any validation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked split value drives an index past the end of the flat values buffer, producing a read outside the intended buffer. This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the missing constraint is on split bounds, not a write past the buffer (CWE-787).

evidence_lines.code:
const Tensor& input_splits = context->input(1);
const auto input_splits_flat = input_splits.flat<SPLITS_TYPE>();

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the code trusts the input_splits/input_tensor pair to describe a valid sparse tensor, so split values may exceed input_tensor_flat.size(). Trigger: pass a splits tensor whose entries are larger than the flat values length. The inner loop then indexes input_tensor_flat(idx) beyond the allocated buffer, causing an out-of-bounds heap read.

description: OMPL v1.5.2 contains a memory leak in VFRRT.cpp

commit_msg:
l2tp: fix racy SOCK_ZAPPED flag check in l2tp_ip{,6}_bind()

Lock socket before checking the SOCK_ZAPPED flag in l2tp_ip6_bind().
Without lock, a concurrent call could modify the socket flags between
the sock_flag(sk, SOCK_ZAPPED) test and the lock_sock() call. This way,
a socket could be inserted twice in l2tp_ip6_bind_table. Releasing it
would then leave a stale pointer there, generating use-after-free
errors when walking through the list or modifying adjacent entries.

description: Race condition in the L2TPv3 IP Encapsulation feature in the Linux kernel before 4.8.14 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by making multiple bind system calls without properly ascertaining whether a socket has the SOCK_ZAPPED status, related to net/l2tp/l2tp_ip.c and net/l2tp/l2tp_ip6.c.

Lines 22-27 perform the bind-table lookup under l2tp_ip6_lock, release it, and only then call lock_sock(sk); the intervening window allows the socket state to change after the flag test.
Lines 57-61 add the socket to l2tp_ip6_bind_table and reset SOCK_ZAPPED while holding the write lock, so a second racing bind can pass the stale flag test and insert the same socket again.

if (!sock_flag(sk, SOCK_ZAPPED))
return -EINVAL;

commit_msg:
x86/fpu: Don't let userspace set bogus xcomp_bv

On x86, userspace can use the ptrace() or rt_sigreturn() system calls to
set a task's extended state (xstate) or "FPU" registers.  ptrace() can
set them for another task using the PTRACE_SETREGSET request with
NT_X86_XSTATE, while rt_sigreturn() can set them for the current task.
In either case, registers can be set to any value, but the kernel
assumes that the XSAVE area itself remains valid in the sense that the
CPU can restore it.

However, in the case where the kernel is using the uncompacted xstate
format (which it does whenever the XSAVES instruction is unavailable),
it was possible for userspace to set the xcomp_bv field in the
xstate_header to an arbitrary value.  However, all bits in that field
are reserved in the uncompacted case, so when switching to a task with
nonzero xcomp_bv, the XRSTOR instruction failed with a #GP fault.  This
caused the WARN_ON_FPU(err) in copy_kernel_to_xregs() to be hit.  In
addition, since the error is otherwise ignored, the FPU registers from
the task previously executing on the CPU were leaked.

Fix the bug by checking that the user-supplied value of xcomp_bv is 0 in
the uncompacted case, and returning an error otherwise.

The reason for validating xcomp_bv rather than simply overwriting it
with 0 is that we want userspace to see an error if it (incorrectly)
provides an XSAVE area in compacted format rather than in uncompacted
format.

Note that as before, in case of error we clear the task's FPU state.
This is perhaps non-ideal, especially for PTRACE_SETREGSET; it might be
better to return an error before changing anything.  But it seems the
"clear on error" behavior is fine for now, and it's a little tricky to
do otherwise because it would mean we couldn't simply copy the full
userspace state into kernel memory in one __copy_from_user().

This bug was found by syzkaller, which hit the above-mentioned
WARN_ON_FPU():

    WARNING: CPU: 1 PID: 0 at ./arch/x86/include/asm/fpu/internal.h:373 __switch_to+0x5b5/0x5d0
    CPU: 1 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/1 Not tainted 4.13.0 #453
    Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS Bochs 01/01/2011
    task: ffff9ba2bc8e42c0 task.stack: ffffa78cc036c000
    RIP: 0010:__switch_to+0x5b5/0x5d0
    RSP: 0000:ffffa78cc08bbb88 EFLAGS: 00010082
    RAX: 00000000fffffffe RBX: ffff9ba2b8bf2180 RCX: 00000000c0000100
    RDX: 00000000ffffffff RSI: 000000005cb10700 RDI: ffff9ba2b8bf36c0
    RBP: ffffa78cc08bbbd0 R08: 00000000929fdf46 R09: 0000000000000001
    R10: 0000000000000000 R11: 0000000000000000 R12: ffff9ba2bc8e42c0
    R13: 0000000000000000 R14: ffff9ba2b8bf3680 R15: ffff9ba2bf5d7b40
    FS:  00007f7e5cb10700(0000) GS:ffff9ba2bf400000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000
    CS:  0010 DS: 0000 ES: 0000 CR0: 0000000080050033
    CR2: 00000000004005cc CR3: 0000000079fd5000 CR4: 00000000001406e0
    Call Trace:
    Code: 84 00 00 00 00 00 e9 11 fd ff ff 0f ff 66 0f 1f 84 00 00 00 00 00 e9 e7 fa ff ff 0f ff 66 0f 1f 84 00 00 00 00 00 e9 c2 fa ff ff <0f> ff 66 0f 1f 84 00 00 00 00 00 e9 d4 fc ff ff 66 66 2e 0f 1f

Here is a C reproducer.  The expected behavior is that the program spin
forever with no output.  However, on a buggy kernel running on a
processor with the "xsave" feature but without the "xsaves" feature
(e.g. Sandy Bridge through Broadwell for Intel), within a second or two
the program reports that the xmm registers were corrupted, i.e. were not
restored correctly.  With CONFIG_X86_DEBUG_FPU=y it also hits the above
kernel warning.

    #define _GNU_SOURCE
    #include <stdbool.h>
    #include <inttypes.h>
    #include <linux/elf.h>
    #include <stdio.h>
    #include <sys/ptrace.h>
    #include <sys/uio.h>
    #include <sys/wait.h>
    #include <unistd.h>

    int main(void)
    {
        int pid = fork();
        uint64_t xstate[512];
        struct iovec iov = { .iov_base = xstate, .iov_len = sizeof(xstate) };

        if (pid == 0) {
            bool tracee = true;
            for (int i = 0; i < sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) && tracee; i++)
                tracee = (fork() != 0);
            uint32_t xmm0[4] = { [0 ... 3] = tracee ? 0x00000000 : 0xDEADBEEF };
            asm volatile("   movdqu %0, %%xmm0\n"
                         "   mov %0, %%rbx\n"
                         "1: movdqu %%xmm0, %0\n"
                         "   mov %0, %%rax\n"
                         "   cmp %%rax, %%rbx\n"
                         "   je 1b\n"
                         : "+m" (xmm0) : : "rax", "rbx", "xmm0");
            printf("BUG: xmm registers corrupted!  tracee=%d, xmm0=%08X%08X%08X%08X\n",
                   tracee, xmm0[0], xmm0[1], xmm0[2], xmm0[3]);
        } else {
            usleep(100000);
            ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, pid, 0, 0);
            wait(NULL);
            ptrace(PTRACE_GETREGSET, pid, NT_X86_XSTATE, &iov);
            xstate[65] = -1;
            ptrace(PTRACE_SETREGSET, pid, NT_X86_XSTATE, &iov);
            ptrace(PTRACE_CONT, pid, 0, 0);
            wait(NULL);
        }
        return 1;
    }

Note: the program only tests for the bug using the ptrace() system call.
The bug can also be reproduced using the rt_sigreturn() system call, but
only when called from a 32-bit program, since for 64-bit programs the
kernel restores the FPU state from the signal frame by doing XRSTOR
directly from userspace memory (with proper error checking).

description: The x86/fpu (Floating Point Unit) subsystem in the Linux kernel before 4.13.5, when a processor supports the xsave feature but not the xsaves feature, does not correctly handle attempts to set reserved bits in the xstate header via the ptrace() or rt_sigreturn() system call, allowing local users to read the FPU registers of other processes on the system, related to arch/x86/kernel/fpu/regset.c and arch/x86/kernel/fpu/signal.c.

code_evidence: In the uncompacted branch (XSAVES unavailable), user_regset_copyin copies the full userspace XSAVE buffer into xsave without validating the header's xcomp_bv field, so reserved bits remain attacker-controlled.
The subsequent masking only clears xfeatures and reserved bytes, not xcomp_bv; the corrupted state is retained and later restored by XRSTOR.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The ignored XRSTOR failure leaves stale FPU register state attributed to the attacker's task, exposing another process's register contents—an unauthorized read of sensitive data. This fits CWE-200 as an information exposure, though the underlying root cause is the missing validation of reserved bits.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: missing validation of reserved xcomp_bv bits when userspace supplies an uncompacted xstate via ptrace/rt_sigreturn. Trigger: nonzero xcomp_bv causes XRSTOR to fault; the restore error is ignored, so the task runs with the previously executing task's FPU registers. Consequence: FPU register contents of other processes are leaked to the attacker.

description: Poppler before 0.66.0 has an integer overflow in Parser::makeStream in Parser.cc.

code_evidence: length is taken from the untrusted stream dictionary 'Length' as an int or int64 without any bound check.
When xref provides a stream end, length is overwritten by the subtraction endPos - pos, which can also yield a negative or huge value.
pos + length is passed directly to lexer->setPos, and later length is used in makeSubStream(pos, gTrue, length, ...); no check ensures the addition stays within Goffset range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the unsafe operation is an unchecked integer addition of an untrusted length to a stream offset, whose wrapped result is consumed as a position/size. It is not merely a bounds-check omission; the direct arithmetic overflow is the defect.

lexer->setPos(pos + length);
length = lexer->getPos() - pos;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: attacker-controlled Length (or endPos - pos) is added to the current stream position without validating that pos + length fits in Goffset. A crafted PDF with a very large Length triggers signed integer overflow/wraparound, producing a bogus position and length that are then used to construct a substream. The supported consequence is incorrect offset/size handling leading to out-of-bounds access or denial of service.

commit_msg: Guard binary expressions from too much recursion.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tSAVEREC();', '\tINCREC();', '\tPOPREC();']}
description: jsparse.c in Artifex MuJS through 1.0.2 does not properly maintain the AST depth for binary expressions, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (excessive recursion) via a crafted file.

code_evidence: The parser loop at label `loop` repeatedly consumes '.', '[' and '(' tokens, each time calling `EXP2(...)` to build a new AST node and then `goto loop`, without any depth counter or recursion guard in the original function. Each iteration can invoke sub-parsers such as `identifiername`, `expression` and `arguments`, so nesting crafted binary/member/call expressions drives unbounded recursion.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits because the parser performs recursion without controlling its depth, consuming stack resources until failure. It is not merely a logic error; the missing bound on recursion is the weakness enabling availability impact.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function lacks any recursion-depth accounting while looping over postfix operators and descending into nested expression parsers. Trigger: a crafted input with deeply/chainedly nested member, index or call expressions. Consequence: excessive stack recursion during parsing, exhausting stack and causing denial of service.

commit_msg: Fix double free in pico_fragments_reassemble()

description: Double Free vulnerability in virtualsquare picoTCP v1.7.0 and picoTCP-NG v2.1 in modules/pico_fragments.c in function pico_fragments_reassemble, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code.

code_evidence: After reassembly, pico_transport_receive(full, proto) is called, and when it returns -1 the code calls pico_frame_discard(full) on the same frame. The transport receive path may already release or consume 'full', so the subsequent discard frees an already-freed frame.
