Trigger: pico_transport_receive returns -1 after having freed/consumed 'full'. Consequence: pico_frame_discard frees the same buffer twice, enabling memory corruption and potentially arbitrary code execution.

commit_msg:
evdns: fix searching empty hostnames

From #332:
  Here follows a bug report by **Guido Vranken** via the _Tor bug bounty program_. Please credit Guido accordingly.

  ## Bug report

  The DNS code of Libevent contains this rather obvious OOB read:

  ```c
  static char *
  search_make_new(const struct search_state *const state, int n, const char *const base_name) {
      const size_t base_len = strlen(base_name);
      const char need_to_append_dot = base_name[base_len - 1] == '.' ? 0 : 1;
  ```

  If the length of ```base_name``` is 0, then line 3125 reads 1 byte before the buffer. This will trigger a crash on ASAN-protected builds.

  To reproduce:

  Build libevent with ASAN:
  ```
  $ CFLAGS='-fomit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address' ./configure && make -j4
  ```
  Put the attached ```resolv.conf``` and ```poc.c``` in the source directory and then do:

  ```
  $ gcc -fsanitize=address -fomit-frame-pointer poc.c .libs/libevent.a
  $ ./a.out
  =================================================================
  ==22201== ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x60060000efdf at pc 0x4429da bp 0x7ffe1ed47300 sp 0x7ffe1ed472f8
  READ of size 1 at 0x60060000efdf thread T0
  ```

P.S. we can add a check earlier, but since this is very uncommon, I didn't add it.

Fixes: #332
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ["\tconst char need_to_append_dot = base_name[base_len - 1] == '.' ? 0 : 1;"], 'added_lines': ['\tchar need_to_append_dot;', '', '\tif (!base_len) return NULL;', "\tneed_to_append_dot = base_name[base_len - 1] == '.' ? 0 : 1;"]}
description: The search_make_new function in evdns.c in libevent before 2.1.6-beta allows attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via an empty hostname.

code_evidence: base_len is computed with strlen(base_name); if base_name is empty, base_len is 0. Line 4 then indexes base_name[base_len - 1], i.e. base_name[(size_t)-1], reading one byte before the buffer start.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads one byte before the intended buffer because a length-derived index underflows on empty input, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). It is not a write overflow; the defect is a read at an invalid pre-buffer offset.

evidence_lines.code:
const size_t base_len = strlen(base_name);
const char need_to_append_dot = base_name[base_len - 1] == '.' ? 0 : 1;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the index base_len - 1 underflows when strlen returns 0, so the '.' check dereferences memory before the supplied hostname. Trigger: an empty hostname reaching search_make_new. Supported consequence: an out-of-bounds read, which crashes ASAN-protected builds (denial of service) and may expose adjacent byte content.

commit_msg:
spi: gpio: prevent memory leak in spi_gpio_probe

In spi_gpio_probe an SPI master is allocated via spi_alloc_master, but
this controller should be released if devm_add_action_or_reset fails,
otherwise memory leaks. In order to avoid leak spi_contriller_put must
be called in case of failure for devm_add_action_or_reset.

Fixes: 8b797490b4db ("spi: gpio: Make sure spi_master_put() is called in every error path")
Signed-off-by: Navid Emamdoost <navid.emamdoost@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190930205241.5483-1-navid.emamdoost@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (status)'], 'added_lines': ['\tif (status) {', '\t\tspi_master_put(master);', '\t}']}
description: A memory leak in the spi_gpio_probe() function in drivers/spi/spi-gpio.c in the Linux kernel through 5.3.11 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by triggering devm_add_action_or_reset() failures, aka CID-d3b0ffa1d75d. NOTE: third parties dispute the relevance of this because the system must have already been out of memory before the probe began

code_evidence: spi_alloc_master() at line 10 allocates an SPI master and stores it in 'master'. The only guard is the NULL check at lines 11-12. At line 13 devm_add_action_or_reset() registers spi_gpio_put as a devres cleanup action; if that registration fails, the callback is never installed. The error branch at lines 14-15 returns 'status' without releasing 'master', so the allocation from line 10 is abandoned.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because an allocated object is not released on an error path, leaving memory unavailable for reuse. This is a missing release on failure, not a use-after-free (CWE-416) or double free, since no dangling pointer is dereferenced or freed twice.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the failure path of devm_add_action_or_reset() returns without a release for the master allocated by spi_alloc_master(), because the devres cleanup that would free it was not successfully registered. Trigger: devm_add_action_or_reset() returns nonzero during probe (e.g., allocation failure). Consequence: the master allocation is leaked, and repeated probe failures consume memory, supporting a resource-consumption DoS.

commit_msg:
x86: don't store possibly stale TLB flush time stamp

While the timing window is extremely narrow, it is theoretically
possible for an update to the TLB flush clock and a subsequent flush
IPI to happen between the read and write parts of the update of the
per-page stamp. Exclude this possibility by disabling interrupts
across the update, preventing the IPI to be serviced in the middle.

This is XSA-241.

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Suggested-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: George Dunlap <george.dunlap@citrix.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['        page_set_tlbflush_timestamp(page);', '        page_set_tlbflush_timestamp(page);'], 'added_lines': ['        set_tlbflush_timestamp(page);', '        set_tlbflush_timestamp(page);']}
description: An issue was discovered in Xen through 4.9.x allowing x86 PV guest OS users to execute arbitrary code on the host OS because of a race condition that can cause a stale TLB entry.

code_evidence: At line 13 the per-page TLB flush timestamp is updated before the type_info decrement at line 15, with only a write barrier (line 14) between them; no interrupt disabling protects the read-modify-write of the stamp.
The second branch similarly calls page_set_tlbflush_timestamp at line 21 then modifies type_info at line 23 with only smp_wmb at line 22, leaving the same window.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function updates a shared per-page resource without exclusive/atomic access, permitting an interfering concurrent code sequence (flush IPI) to modify it mid-update. This is the timing-window exclusivity violation defining CWE-362.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The TLB flush timestamp update is a non-atomic read-modify-write. An intervening flush IPI serviced between the read and write can store a newer timestamp, which is then overwritten by the stale value. This stale stamp can cause a subsequent TLB flush to be skipped, leaving a stale TLB entry usable.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (i >= strlen(s) - 1) return NULL;', '    h1 = s[i + 1], h2 = s[i + 2];'], 'added_lines': ['    h1 = s[i + 1];', '    if (!h1) {', "        *d = '\\0';", '        return NULL;', '    }', '    h2 = s[i + 2];']}
description: An issue was discovered in the libsofia-sip fork in drachtio-server before 0.8.19. It allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (daemon crash) via a crafted UDP message that causes a url_canonize2 heap-based buffer over-read because of an off-by-one error.

code_evidence: Loop scans s up to s[i] and i < n; when s[i] is '%', the code checks only i >= strlen(s) - 1 before reading h1 = s[i+1] and h2 = s[i+2].

The guard is off by one: it permits i == strlen(s) - 2, so h2 reads s[strlen(s)], the terminating NUL, and for i == strlen(s) - 1 it would read past the terminator; the later IS_HEX check then handles the bad byte.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is a maximum-boundary calculation that is one less than required for the two-character lookahead, exactly CWE-193. It is not a generic buffer overflow (CWE-119): the flaw is the incorrect index limit permitting the over-read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The bounds check uses strlen(s) - 1 instead of ensuring room for two hex digits, so a trailing '%' (or '%X' at end) makes h2 read one byte beyond the string. A crafted UDP URL reaching url_canonize2 with a '%' near the end triggers this out-of-bounds read, causing a daemon crash (heap-based buffer over-read).

Currently, only 24bpp without alphabits and 32bpp with 8 alphabits are
really supported. All other combinations will be rejected with a warning.

description: gd_tga.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted TGA file.

code_evidence: Lines 18-19 read attacker-controlled bits-per-pixel (header[16]) and alphabits (header[17]&0x0f) directly from the TGA header.

Lines 28-38 validate only tga->bits, accepting 8, 16, 24 and 32 while ignoring tga->alphabits entirely; unsupported bpp/alpha combinations (e.g. 8bpp, or 24bpp with alpha) pass the check and processing continues.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing constraint on the bpp/alphabits combination, and the supported consequence is reading past the intended pixel buffer (CWE-125). This is a validation gap enabling an OOB read, not merely a logic error; CWE-20 alone would not capture the read-past-buffer consequence.

tga->bits = header[16];

commit_msg:
tcp: preserve data source if a PDU uses it

If the previous TCP segments already form one or more PDUs, then the
data source of these segments must not be removed. Otherwise
get_field_data (epan/print.c) will fail to find the data source which
correspond to the fields within these PDUs.

Also tested with the capture referenced in v1.11.3-rc1-1525-g21e0a63b29
(bug 9169), the "tshark -Vr mem-leak.pcap" output remains unchanged.

description: In Wireshark 2.4.0 to 2.4.5, the TCP dissector could crash. This was addressed in epan/dissectors/packet-tcp.c by preserving valid data sources.

code_evidence: After reassembling a chained TCP PDU, the code computes old_len from next_tvb and last_fragment_len, then checks pinfo->desegment_len and desegment_offset<=old_len before calling remove_last_data_source(pinfo). The comment in the patch notes that if desegment_offset is 0, nothing was dissected and the data source should be removed; otherwise it must be preserved so get_field_data can still resolve fields. The guard here only tests desegment_offset<=old_len, not desegment_offset==0, so a PDU that already dissected fields (desegment_offset>0) can still reach remove_last_data_source.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts a derived offset property from dissector input and fails to validate it before a destructive operation, matching CWE-20's improper validation of a derived quantity/offset. The missing constraint is the desegment_offset==0 condition; the weakness is not a memory-safety primitive itself but unvalidated input state driving an unsafe state change.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the desegment_offset value (derived from dissector input on reassembled TCP data) is not validated against the boundary that distinguishes 'nothing dissected' from 'PDU fields already dissected'. Trigger: a reassembled TCP PDU with desegment_offset>0 satisfying desegment_offset<=old_len. Consequence: the valid data source is removed and get_field_data fails, causing the TCP dissector crash described in the advisory.

commit_msg:
A race condition may occur if the user physically removes the
USB device while calling open() for this device node.

This is a race condition between the ufx_ops_open() function and
the ufx_usb_disconnect() function, which may eventually result in UAF.

So, add a mutex to the ufx_ops_open() and ufx_usb_disconnect() functions
to avoid race contidion of krefs.

Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Helge Deller <deller@gmx.de>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (dev->virtualized)'], 'added_lines': ['\tmutex_lock(&disconnect_mutex);', '', '\tif (dev->virtualized) {', '\t\tmutex_unlock(&disconnect_mutex);', '\t}', '\tmutex_unlock(&disconnect_mutex);', '']}
description: drivers/video/fbdev/smscufx.c in the Linux kernel through 5.19.12 has a race condition and resultant use-after-free if a physically proximate attacker removes a USB device while calling open(), aka a race condition between ufx_ops_open and ufx_usb_disconnect.

code_evidence: ufx_ops_open checks dev->virtualized and returns -ENODEV, then increments dev->fb_count and calls kref_get(&dev->kref) with no lock protecting the check-then-act sequence against ufx_usb_disconnect.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs a concurrent check-and-modify on shared device state (virtualized, fb_count, kref) without exclusive synchronization, matching CWE-362's non-atomic sequence on a shared resource. The UAF is the resulting consequence, not the race itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The virtualized check and the subsequent fb_count increment and kref_get are not atomic with respect to device disconnect. A physically proximate attacker removing the USB device while open() runs lets ufx_usb_disconnect free the shared ufx_data concurrently, so the kref operations touch a released object, yielding use-after-free.

description: ImageMagick 7.0.7-17 Q16 x86_64 has memory leaks in coders/msl.c, related to MSLPopImage and ProcessMSLScript, and associated with mishandling of MSLPushImage calls.

code_evidence: CloneImage returns a newly allocated msl_image reference at line 13; this reference is passed by address into ProcessMSLScript at line 14. The only cleanup is the conditional DestroyImage at lines 15-16, which releases just the pointer currently stored in msl_image and only if non-NULL.

This is CWE-772 (missing release of resource), not merely a NULL check issue, because the defect is unreleased allocations rather than dereferencing.

commit_msg:
usb/redir: avoid dynamic stack allocation (CVE-2021-3527)

Use autofree heap allocation instead.

Fixes: 4f4321c11ff ("usb: use iovecs in USBPacket")
Reviewed-by: Philippe Mathieu-Daudé <philmd@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Philippe Mathieu-Daudé <philmd@redhat.com>
Message-Id: <20210503132915.2335822-3-kraxel@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            uint8_t buf[p->iov.size];'], 'added_lines': ['            g_autofree uint8_t *buf = g_malloc(p->iov.size);']}
description: A flaw was found in the USB redirector device (usb-redir) of QEMU. Small USB packets are combined into a single, large transfer request, to reduce the overhead and improve performance. The combined size of the bulk transfer is used to dynamically allocate a variable length array (VLA) on the stack without proper validation. Since the total size is not bounded, a malicious guest could use this flaw to influence the array length and cause the QEMU process to perform an excessive allocation on the stack, resulting in a denial of service.

code_evidence: The OUT branch builds an iso_packet header whose length is p->iov.size [77], then declares a variable-length array on the stack sized by that same guest-influenced value [79]. The array is filled by usb_packet_copy [80] and passed to usbredirparser_send_iso_packet [81,82] with no upper bound check on p->iov.size before the allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-770 fits because the function allocates a resource (stack space) sized by an actor-controlled value without imposing a limit on the allocation size, leading to resource exhaustion. This is the allocation-sizing weakness; the stack placement is the mechanism of the DoS rather than a separate CWE.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the stack VLA size is derived directly from p->iov.size without any cap. Trigger: a malicious guest submits an iso OUT packet with a large iov size while the stream is started, causing a large stack allocation; this can exhaust the stack and crash the QEMU process, a denial of service. The patch replaces the VLA with bounded heap allocation, though the size itself remains unvalidated.

commit_msg:
There are two invocation sites of hso_free_net_device. After
refactoring hso_create_net_device, this parameter is useless.
Remove the bailout in the hso_free_net_device and change the invocation
sites of this function.

Signed-off-by: Dongliang Mu <mudongliangabcd@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\thso_free_net_device(network_table[i], false);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\thso_free_net_device(network_table[i]);']}
description: hso_free_net_device in drivers/net/usb/hso.c in the Linux kernel through 5.13.4 calls unregister_netdev without checking for the NETREG_REGISTERED state, leading to a use-after-free and a double free.

code_evidence: The loop matches network_table[i] to the interface, stops the net queue, stops the device, cancels async work, and then calls hso_free_net_device(network_table[i], false). This teardown path is reached during hso_free_interface regardless of the net device's registration state; the freed/stopped device is not marked or cleared from network_table here, so a subsequent teardown or invocation can reach the same entry again.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-415 fits because the code path calls hso_free_net_device on the same network_table entry without a guard ensuring single free, allowing free() to be invoked twice on the same address. This is a double free, not merely a missing NULL check or an unregister-order bug.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: hso_free_interface tears down and frees each matching hso_net_device without verifying NETREG_REGISTERED state or clearing the network_table slot. Trigger: the interface free path runs (or runs again) while the entry still points to the device. Consequence: the same device memory is freed twice, giving use-after-free/double-free and potential memory corruption.

These are all references relative to the', '\t start of the current CU.  */', '      size_t total;', '', '      info_ptr = unit->info_ptr_unit;', '      total = info_ptr_end - info_ptr;', '      if (!die_ref || die_ref >= total)', '\t{', '\t  _bfd_error_handler', '\t    (_("Dwarf Error: Invalid abstract instance DIE ref."));', '\t  bfd_set_error (bfd_error_bad_value);', '\t  return FALSE;', '\t}', '      info_ptr += die_ref;']}
description: dwarf2.c in the Binary File Descriptor (BFD) library (aka libbfd), as distributed in GNU Binutils 2.29, miscalculates DW_FORM_ref_addr die refs in the case of a relocatable object file, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (find_abstract_instance_name invalid memory read, segmentation fault, and application crash).

code_evidence: For DW_FORM_ref_addr, info_ptr is computed as unit->sec_info_ptr + die_ref with only a zero check on die_ref; no upper bound against the section/CU end is enforced before info_ptr is used.
For the other ref forms, info_ptr is unit->info_ptr_unit + die_ref with no bounds check at all; die_ref is attacker-controlled from the DWARF, so info_ptr can point past the CU buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function dereferences and reads from a memory location computed outside the intended .debug_info/CU buffer boundary, which is exactly CWE-119's out-of-bounds buffer read. This is a direct buffer-boundary failure, not merely a type or arithmetic issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: die_ref (from DWARF attributes) is added to a base pointer without validating it against the buffer end for DW_FORM_ref_addr (and not even a zero check for ref1/2/4/8). Trigger: a crafted relocatable object with an out-of-range die ref. Consequence: _bfd_safe_read_leb128 and read_attribute read past the intended buffer, causing an invalid memory read and crash.

This was fixed in commit 35c94dc6acc418f1ad7f6241a6680e5327495793 (Aug 2017).

Line 8 declares a fixed 20-byte stack buffer desc, and line 28 copies descsz bytes into it without validating descsz <= 20; line 29 then iterates descsz times over desc.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-controlled descsz bytes into a fixed-size buffer without an effective upper bound, which is an out-of-bounds memory buffer operation, matching CWE-119. A stricter child such as CWE-121 (stack-based overflow) would also fit, but the target class is supported by the memcpy overflow.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void ntlm_write_message_fields_buffer(wStream* s, NTLM_MESSAGE_FIELDS* fields)'], 'added_lines': ['static void ntlm_write_message_fields_buffer(wStream* s, NTLM_MESSAGE_FIELDS* fields)']}
description: FreeRDP prior to version 2.0.0-rc4 contains several Out-Of-Bounds Reads in the NTLM Authentication module that results in a Denial of Service (segfault).

code_evidence: The guard only checks fields->Len > 0, then Stream_SetPosition(s, fields->BufferOffset) seeks to a caller-supplied offset and Stream_Write(s, fields->Buffer, fields->Len) copies fields->Len bytes from fields->Buffer. No check relates BufferOffset or Len to the stream's capacity, and no check confirms fields->Buffer actually holds Len bytes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is a read of fields->Buffer bounded only by an unvalidated length, which matches CWE-125 (reading past the end of an intended buffer). It is not a write overflow, since the vulnerable access is the source read in Stream_Write.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the missing validation that fields->Len is within the allocated size of fields->Buffer before Stream_Write reads it. A malformed NTLM message can set Len larger than the buffer, so the copy reads past its end; the resulting out-of-bounds read can segfault the process (DoS) and may disclose adjacent memory.

commit_msg:
CVE-2019-3557: Fix OOB read in readRecord on BZ2Files/OutputFiles

Summary:
These File subclasses return -1 on read errors which is not what is
expected for readImpl--this made File::readRecord behave unusually if the read
fails, causing it to read (size_t)(-1) bytes from its stream buffer; which,
unsurprisingly produces a out-of-bounds heap read.

Reviewed By: leikahing, jjgriego

Differential Revision: D13659395

fbshipit-source-id: 359ed6e3ff9f9cf49b752b666f51c4e0b3ce4b8a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      return -1;'], 'added_lines': ['      return 0;']}
description: The implementations of streams for bz2 and php://output improperly implemented their readImpl functions, returning -1 consistently. This behavior caused some stream functions, such as stream_get_line, to trigger an out-of-bounds read when operating on such malformed streams. The implementations were updated to return valid values consistently. This affects all supported versions of HHVM (3.30 and 3.27.4 and below).

code_evidence: BZ2_bzread returns a byte count; line 6 stores it in signed int len. On a read error it returns -1, so the len <= 0 branch sets EOF (line 8) but the len < 0 case returns -1 (line 10) instead of a non-negative count. The caller receives -1 as the number of bytes read.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the faulty -1 return is consumed as a length, producing an out-of-bounds read. The defect is the wrong error-signaling return value, not a bounds check in this function; a negative-size/overflow label would describe the numeric conversion, whereas the supported consequence here is reading beyond the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: readImpl propagates a negative error return (-1) where callers expect a non-negative byte count. Trigger: BZ2_bzread fails and returns -1; the caller then treats that value as a size, e.g. converting to size_t, and reads far past the stream buffer. Supported consequence: out-of-bounds heap read from the stream buffer.

commit_msg:
show_opcodes() is used both for dumping kernel instructions and for dumping
user instructions. If userspace causes #PF by jumping to a kernel address,
show_opcodes() can be reached with regs->ip controlled by the user,
pointing to kernel code. Make sure that userspace can't trick us into
dumping kernel memory into dmesg.

Fixes: 7cccf0725cf7 ("x86/dumpstack: Add a show_ip() function")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: Borislav Petkov <bp@suse.de>
Cc: "H. Peter Anvin" <hpa@zytor.com>
Cc: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: security@kernel.org
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20180828154901.112726-1-jannh@google.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['void show_opcodes(u8 *rip, const char *loglvl)', '\tif (probe_kernel_read(opcodes, rip - PROLOGUE_SIZE, OPCODE_BUFSIZE)) {'], 'added_lines': ['void show_opcodes(struct pt_regs *regs, const char *loglvl)', '\tunsigned long prologue = regs->ip - PROLOGUE_SIZE;', '\tbool bad_ip;', '\t/*', "\t * Make sure userspace isn't trying to trick us into dumping kernel", '\t * memory by pointing the userspace instruction pointer at it.', '\t */', '\tbad_ip = user_mode(regs) &&', '\t\t__chk_range_not_ok(prologue, OPCODE_BUFSIZE, TASK_SIZE_MAX);', '', '\tif (bad_ip || probe_kernel_read(opcodes, (u8 *)prologue,', '\t\t\t\t\tOPCODE_BUFSIZE)) {']}
description: A missing address check in the callers of the show_opcodes() in the Linux kernel allows an attacker to dump the kernel memory at an arbitrary kernel address into the dmesg log.

code_evidence: show_opcodes() takes a raw instruction-pointer value (rip) and computes rip - PROLOGUE_SIZE, then passes it directly to probe_kernel_read() to copy OPCODE_BUFSIZE bytes into opcodes. No check verifies that the address range belongs to the caller's context (e.g., userspace) before the read; only the return value of probe_kernel_read() is tested, and a successful read of kernel memory is printed to the log.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the function fails to validate that the supplied address input satisfies the property required for safe processing (being a userspace address when invoked for user mode), enabling the resulting kernel-memory disclosure.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the instruction pointer used for the memory dump is treated as a trusted kernel address without validating that it lies within the expected address space. Trigger: a userspace-controlled regs->ip (e.g., via a fault/jump to a kernel address) is passed in, causing probe_kernel_read() to read kernel memory at that address. Consequence: kernel memory contents are disclosed in the dmesg output.

description: Incomplete string comparison vulnerability exits in cvxopt.org cvxop <= 1.2.6 in APIs (cvxopt.cholmod.diag, cvxopt.cholmod.getfactor, cvxopt.cholmod.solve, cvxopt.cholmod.spsolve), which allows attackers to conduct Denial of Service attacks by construct fake Capsule objects.

code_evidence: PyCapsule path: after obtaining the capsule name via PyCapsule_GetName, line 24 uses strncmp(descr, "CHOLMOD FACTOR", 14), comparing only the first 14 bytes; a name sharing that prefix passes validation, and line 26 then retrieves the pointer using that attacker-controlled descr.
PyCObject path: line 30 similarly checks only the first 14 bytes of the description before line 32 casts the object to cholmod_factor*.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-697 (Incorrect Comparison) fits because the security check compares only a prefix of the descriptor rather than the complete expected value, so distinct strings are incorrectly treated as equal. This is a comparison-logic flaw, not merely a memory-safety consequence, which is why the incorrect comparison is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The factor validation performs a partial string comparison (first 14 bytes) instead of verifying the full expected capsule/object name. An attacker can construct a fake capsule/CObject whose name begins with "CHOLMOD FACTOR", bypassing the type check; the pointer is then cast to cholmod_factor* and dereferenced (e.g., L->xtype, L->n), enabling denial of service via crafted objects.

commit_msg:
driver: Sanitize data_size value returned from devices

We're using this value for some bounds checks and we should ensure that
we don't potentially get a data_size that's bigger than the arguments
array to avoid out of bounds reads.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (WARN_ONCE(response_report->data_size > ARRAY_SIZE(response_report->arguments),', '                  "Field data_size %d in response is bigger than arguments\\n",', '                  response_report->data_size)) {', "        /* Sanitize the value since at the moment callers don't respect the return code */", '        response_report->data_size = ARRAY_SIZE(response_report->arguments);', '        return -EINVAL;', '    }', '']}
description: OpenRazer is an open source driver and user-space daemon to control Razer device lighting and other features on GNU/Linux. Using a modified USB device an attacker can leak stack addresses of the `razer_attr_read_dpi_stages`, potentially bypassing KASLR. To exploit this vulnerability an attacker would need to access to a users keyboard or mouse or would need to convince a user to use a modified device. The issue has been patched in v3.5.1. Users are advised to upgrade and should be reminded not to plug in unknown USB devices.

code_evidence: usb_control_msg writes up to `size` (RAZER_USB_REPORT_LEN) bytes into the heap buffer `buf`, and the result is then copied wholesale into the caller's `response_report` with memcpy of sizeof(struct razer_report).

The only validation checks the returned `len` against 90 and sets result=1; it does not validate the device-supplied `data_size` field inside the report, and the function still returns the copied report to callers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing constraint on `data_size` lets downstream consumers read beyond the intended `arguments` buffer, which is exactly an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), not a write or type confusion. The patch's added WARN_ONCE/data_size clamp confirms this weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A modified USB device controls the report contents, including `data_size`, which is copied into `response_report` without any bounds check against `arguments`. Callers use this unvalidated `data_size` for bounds checks, so an oversized value lets them read past the `arguments` array, leaking stack memory (e.g., stack addresses to bypass KASLR).

commit_msg:
goption: Add a precondition to avoid GOptionEntry list overflow

If the calling code adds more option entries than `G_MAXSIZE` then
there’ll be an integer overflow. This seems vanishingly unlikely (given
that all callers use static option entry lists), but add a precondition
anyway.

Signed-off-by: Philip Withnall <withnall@endlessm.com>

Fixes: #2197
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '  g_return_if_fail (n_entries <= G_MAXSIZE - group->n_entries);']}
description: GNOME GLib before 2.65.3 has an integer overflow, that might lead to an out-of-bounds write, in g_option_group_add_entries. NOTE: the vendor's position is "Realistically this is not a security issue. The standard pattern is for callers to provide a static list of option entries in a fixed number of calls to g_option_group_add_entries()." The researcher states that this pattern is undocumented

code_evidence: Line 5 declares n_entries and group->n_entries as gsize; line 8 counts entries until a NULL long_name, so n_entries is attacker-influenced only if the list is non-static. Line 9 computes group->n_entries + n_entries as the element count passed to g_renew; if that sum wraps past G_MAXSIZE, g_renew allocates a too-small buffer. Line 11 then memcpy's sizeof(GOptionEntry) * n_entries bytes into that undersized buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the unsafe operation is an integer addition used as an allocation size that can wrap to a small value, and the patch adds a bound check specifically to prevent that wraparound. The resulting out-of-bounds write is a consequence of the overflow, not a separate CWE; the weakness is the unchecked size arithmetic.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the addition group->n_entries + n_entries in the allocation size is unchecked for wraparound. Trigger: a caller adds enough entries that the sum exceeds G_MAXSIZE. Consequence: g_renew allocates a wrapped, too-small buffer and memcpy at line 11 writes past it, causing an out-of-bounds write. The added precondition guards this sum before allocation, confirming the cause is the unchecked size calculation rather than the copy itself.

commit_msg:
ipv6: Prevent overrun when parsing v6 header options

The KASAN warning repoted below was discovered with a syzkaller
program.  The reproducer is basically:
  int s = socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_RAW, NEXTHDR_HOP);
  send(s, &one_byte_of_data, 1, MSG_MORE);
  send(s, &more_than_mtu_bytes_data, 2000, 0);

The socket() call sets the nexthdr field of the v6 header to
NEXTHDR_HOP, the first send call primes the payload with a non zero
byte of data, and the second send call triggers the fragmentation path.

The fragmentation code tries to parse the header options in order
to figure out where to insert the fragment option.  Since nexthdr points
to an invalid option, the calculation of the size of the network header
can made to be much larger than the linear section of the skb and data
is read outside of it.

This fix makes ip6_find_1stfrag return an error if it detects
running out-of-bounds.

description: The IPv6 fragmentation implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.11.1 does not consider that the nexthdr field may be associated with an invalid option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and BUG) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted socket and send system calls.

code_evidence: Line 6 declares unfrag_ip6hlen as unsigned int, but line 47 assigns it the return value of ip6_find_1stfragopt(), which can be negative on invalid nexthdr options; no sign check exists before use.

Lines 50-51 compute unfrag_len using the possibly huge wrapped unsigned value, and line 57 computes fptr from it; line 53 memmove and line 63 skb_segment then operate on this over-large length, reading beyond the skb's linear data.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function directly uses an unchecked computed header length to read skb data past the intended buffer region, matching CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read). The patch adds the missing negative-return check before the length is used, confirming the read overrun rather than a write overflow.

evidence_lines.code:
memmove(packet_start-frag_hdr_sz, packet_start, unfrag_len);
segs = skb_segment(skb, features);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of ip6_find_1stfragopt() is stored in an unsigned int without validating a negative error, so an invalid IPv6 nexthdr option causes size arithmetic to overflow/underflow into a large length. Trigger: attacker crafts a raw IPv6 socket with NEXTHDR_HOP and sends data triggering the fragmentation path. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of skb memory (KASAN slab-out-of-bounds), leading to crash/DoS.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (capacity > kMaxIOBufSize) {', '    throw_exception<std::bad_alloc>();', '  }', '']}
description: Passing an attacker controlled size when creating an IOBuf could cause integer overflow, leading to an out of bounds write on the heap with the possibility of remote code execution. This issue affects versions of folly prior to v2021.07.22.00. This issue affects HHVM versions prior to 4.80.5, all versions between 4.81.0 and 4.102.1, all versions between 4.103.0 and 4.113.0, and versions 4.114.0, 4.115.0, 4.116.0, 4.117.0, 4.118.0 and 4.118.1.

code_evidence: goodMallocSize(capacity) computes an allocation size from the caller-supplied capacity, and line 7 computes minSize as ((capacity + 7) & ~7) + sizeof(SharedInfo). If capacity is near SIZE_MAX, capacity + 7 wraps to a small value, so minSize becomes small. The comparison mallocSize < minSize then fails, so the checkedMalloc branch is skipped and control falls through to createSeparate(capacity).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size computation (capacity + 7) can wrap when capacity is near SIZE_MAX, and the logic assumes the rounded value stays larger than capacity. This is an integer overflow used to defeat a size check, distinct from a plain missing bounds check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the rounding arithmetic capacity + 7 (and the subsequent addition of sizeof(SharedInfo)) is performed without checking that capacity is bounded, so an attacker-controlled large capacity wraps to a small minSize. Trigger: a size close to SIZE_MAX passed to IOBuf::create. Consequence: the guard at line 8 is bypassed and an undersized allocation path is taken, enabling heap out-of-bounds writes.

commit_msg:
virtio-net: fix use after unmap/free for sg

When mergeable buffer is enabled, we try to set the num_buffers after
the virtqueue elem has been unmapped. This will lead several issues,
E.g a use after free when the descriptor has an address which belongs
to the non direct access region. In this case we use bounce buffer
that is allocated during address_space_map() and freed during
address_space_unmap().

Fixing this by storing the elems temporarily in an array and delay the
unmap after we set the the num_buffers.

This addresses CVE-2021-3748.

Reported-by: Alexander Bulekov <alxndr@bu.edu>
Fixes: fbe78f4f55c6 ("virtio-net support")
Cc: qemu-stable@nongnu.org
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    size_t offset, i, guest_offset;', '            return -1;', '            return -1;', '            return size;', '        /* signal other side */', '        virtqueue_fill(q->rx_vq, elem, total, i++);', '        g_free(elem);'], 'added_lines': ['    VirtQueueElement *elems[VIRTQUEUE_MAX_SIZE];', '    size_t lens[VIRTQUEUE_MAX_SIZE];', '    size_t offset, i, guest_offset, j;', '    ssize_t err;', '        if (i == VIRTQUEUE_MAX_SIZE) {', '            virtio_error(vdev, "virtio-net unexpected long buffer chain");', '            err = size;', '            goto err;', '        }', '', '            err = -1;', '            goto err;', '            err = -1;', '            goto err;', '            err = size;', '            goto err;', '        elems[i] = elem;', '        lens[i] = total;', '        i++;', '    for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {', '        /* signal other side */', '        virtqueue_fill(q->rx_vq, elems[j], lens[j], j);', '        g_free(elems[j]);', '    }', '', '', 'err:', '    for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {', '        g_free(elems[j]);', '    }', '', '    return err;']}
description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the virtio-net device of QEMU. It could occur when the descriptor's address belongs to the non direct access region, due to num_buffers being set after the virtqueue elem has been unmapped. A malicious guest could use this flaw to crash QEMU, resulting in a denial of service condition, or potentially execute code on the host with the privileges of the QEMU process.

code_evidence: Inside the receive loop, the popped element is filled and then immediately freed with g_free(elem) while the loop continues to process subsequent descriptors (lines 82-83).

After the loop, the mergeable header's num_buffers is written via iov_from_buf into mhdr_sg (lines 85-90), which was captured from the first element's scatter-gather list before that element was freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 applies because the function writes through mhdr_sg after the owning element was freed, i.e. references memory past its lifetime. The root cause is the premature free/unmap before the num_buffers write, not an out-of-bounds index (CWE-787) or a missing check.

evidence_lines.code:
virtqueue_fill(q->rx_vq, elem, total, i++);
g_free(elem);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The first descriptor's in_sg is copied into mhdr_sg, and the element is freed at line 83; later at line 87 iov_from_buf writes into that stale scatter-gather mapping. When the descriptor address is in a non-direct-access region, the mapped bounce buffer is freed on unmap, so the write at line 87 dereferences freed memory. Trigger: a mergeable, multi-buffer receive where the header element is freed before num_buffers is set. Consequence: use-after-free, enabling guest-triggered QEMU crash or potential host code execution.

commit_msg: properly cast double to size_t (https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/6341)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  page.width=(size_t) floor(page.width*image->resolution.x/delta.x+0.5);', '  page.height=(size_t) floor(page.height*image->resolution.y/delta.y+0.5);'], 'added_lines': ['  page.width=CastDoubleToUnsigned(page.width*image->resolution.x/delta.x+0.5);', '  page.height=CastDoubleToUnsigned(page.height*image->resolution.y/delta.y+0.5);']}
description: A vulnerability was found in ImageMagick. This security flaw ouccers as an undefined behaviors of casting double to size_t in svg, mvg and other coders (recurring bugs of CVE-2022-32546).

code_evidence: Lines 150-151 compute page.width and page.height by multiplying the size_t page dimensions by image->resolution.x/y and dividing by delta.x/y, then converting the double result directly to size_t with a C cast. The double result is unvalidated before conversion; a large resolution or invalid geometry can yield a value outside the size_t range.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Directly casting an unbounded computed value to size_t without a range check fits CWE-190: the conversion can wrap to a small/incorrect integer. It is not merely a formatting issue; the integer result is used as a size, matching overflow/wraparound semantics.

evidence_lines.code:
page.width=(size_t) floor(page.width*image->resolution.x/delta.x+0.5);
page.height=(size_t) floor(page.height*image->resolution.y/delta.y+0.5);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is an unchecked double-to-size_t conversion of a computed page dimension. Triggered by attacker-controlled resolution/geometry producing an out-of-range or negative double, the cast has undefined behavior and can yield a wrapped size_t, which is then used for the delegate -g geometry and image->page, causing incorrect dimensions or instability.

commit_msg:
Add heartbeat extension bounds check.

A missing bounds check in the handling of the TLS heartbeat extension
can be used to reveal up to 64k of memory to a connected client or
server.

Thanks for Neel Mehta of Google Security for discovering this bug and to
Adam Langley <agl@chromium.org> and Bodo Moeller <bmoeller@acm.org> for
preparing the fix (CVE-2014-0160)

description: The (1) TLS and (2) DTLS implementations in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1g do not properly handle Heartbeat Extension packets, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory via crafted packets that trigger a buffer over-read, as demonstrated by reading private keys, related to d1_both.c and t1_lib.c, aka the Heartbleed bug.

code_evidence: Line 8 reads the heartbeat type via *p++ and line 9 decodes the 16-bit payload length from p with n2s, without verifying that s->s3->rrec.length actually contains the claimed payload bytes. Line 10 sets pl to the start of the payload, and line 23 then does memcpy(bp, pl, payload), copying payload bytes from the record buffer into the response buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe memcpy reads beyond the intended record buffer due to an unchecked length, with the supported consequence of memory disclosure. It is an out-of-bounds read rather than an out-of-bounds write, since the copy destination is sized from the same payload value.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The root cause is that the attacker-controlled payload length from n2s is trusted without comparing 1 + 2 + payload + 16 against s->s3->rrec.length. When a crafted heartbeat request declares a payload larger than the received record, memcpy on line 23 reads past the end of the record buffer, and the over-read bytes are returned in the heartbeat response, leaking process memory.

commit_msg: Fixed bug #69090 (check cached files permissions)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['#ifndef ZEND_WIN32', '\thash_value ^= ZCG(root_hash);', '#endif']}
description: An issue was discovered in PHP 5.x and 7.x, when the configuration uses apache2handler/mod_php or php-fpm with OpCache enabled. With 5.x after 5.6.28 or 7.x after 7.0.13, the issue is resolved in a non-default configuration with the opcache.validate_permission=1 setting. The vulnerability details are as follows. In PHP SAPIs where PHP interpreters share a common parent process, Zend OpCache creates a shared memory object owned by the common parent during initialization. Child PHP processes inherit the SHM descriptor, using it to cache and retrieve compiled script bytecode ("opcode" in PHP jargon). Cache keys vary depending on configuration, but filename is a central key component, and compiled opcode can generally be run if a script's filename is known or can be guessed. Many common shared-hosting configurations change EUID in child processes to enforce privilege separation among hosted users (for example using mod_ruid2 for the Apache HTTP Server, or php-fpm user settings). In these scenarios, the default Zend OpCache behavior defeats script file permissions by sharing a single SHM cache among all child PHP processes. PHP scripts often contain sensitive information: Think of CMS configurations where reading or running another user's script usually means gaining privileges to the CMS database.

code_evidence: The hash index is derived only from zend_inline_hash_func(key, key_length) and accel_hash->max_num_entries, with no per-process or per-user namespace component.
Lookup matches solely on hash_value, key_length and memcmp of the key, then returns the cached entry without any permission or ownership check on the underlying script file.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an access decision (returning cached executable bytecode) without verifying the requesting process may access that file, which is a permissions/access-control weakness matching CWE-264. It is not merely a hash-collision issue because memcmp confirms the exact key; the flaw is the absent authorization check.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The cache key is the script filename alone, so a shared OpCache SHM inherited from a common parent allows a child process running under a different EUID to retrieve bytecode compiled for another user's script. Trigger: a hosted user requests a filename already cached by another user; the lookup returns the entry and the opcode executes, defeating file permissions. Cause is the missing permission/ownership validation in the cache lookup; consequence is cross-user script disclosure/execution.

Check HelloRetryRequest cipher consistency earlier.

CVE-2023-23759

description: There is a vulnerability in the fizz library prior to v2023.01.30.00 where a CHECK failure can be triggered remotely. This behavior requires the client supported cipher advertisement changing between the original ClientHello and the second ClientHello, crashing the process (impact is limited to denial of service).

code_evidence: Line 47 derives a cipher from the second ClientHello, and line 48 immediately passes it to verifyCookieState before any consistency check against the previously negotiated cipher.
The HelloRetryRequest path at lines 222-224 stores the first cipher into newState.cipher(), establishing the expected value for the retransmitted ClientHello.
The cipher-mismatch check at lines 106-110 exists but occurs only after setupSchedulerAndContext, so a changed cipher advertisement can reach downstream code before the guard.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit and description state that a remotely triggerable CHECK failure crashes the process, matching CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) where attacker-controlled input reaches an assert-like statement. This is a denial-of-service availability issue, distinct from a memory-corruption weakness.

evidence_lines.code:
auto cipher = negotiateCipher(chlo, state.context()->getSupportedCiphers());
verifyCookieState(cookieState, *version, cipher);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the cipher consistency check is positioned after cipher-dependent processing rather than before it, so a client that alters its supported cipher list between the original and second ClientHello can drive downstream code with an inconsistent cipher. The trigger is the reachable assertion/CHECK failure described in the commit, causing process termination; the supported consequence is denial of service.

commit_msg: Add out-of-bounds check in getCode. Fixes #78
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['                          unsigned short raw[], int nRaw) {', '    if (nRaw != 0) return false;', '      hufDecode(&freq.at(0), &hdec.at(0), ptr, nBits, iM, nRaw, raw);'], 'added_lines': ['                          std::vector<unsigned short> *raw) {', '    if (raw->size() != 0) return false;', '      hufDecode(&freq.at(0), &hdec.at(0), ptr, nBits, iM, raw->size(),', '                raw->data());']}
description: tinyexr 0.9.5 has a heap-based buffer over-read in tinyexr::DecodePixelData in tinyexr.h, related to OpenEXR code.

code_evidence: The guard only checks that the declared bit count fits within the remaining compressed bytes (nBits <= 8 * remaining); it does not verify that the decoded symbol count fits within the destination buffer capacity nRaw.
hufDecode is then invoked with nRaw as the output length while writing into the caller-supplied raw array; the destination size is trusted rather than bounded by the actual decoded output.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe operation is unbounded access relative to the destination buffer size, matching CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read) where data is read past the end of the intended buffer; the patch's added out-of-bounds check in getCode targets this same read-overflow. It is not merely an integer issue, since the missing constraint is a buffer-size bound.

evidence_lines.code: hufDecode(&freq.at(0), &hdec.at(0), ptr, nBits, iM, nRaw, raw);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the decode step uses nRaw as the output limit without confirming the decoded symbol stream stays within the raw buffer, and the preceding check constrains only the input bit count. Trigger: a crafted compressed stream whose nBits passes the input-length check but whose decoded symbols exceed nRaw causes hufDecode to write/read past the raw array, yielding an out-of-bounds access.

commit_msg:
Default initialize fixed point Eigen types.

In certain cases, tensors are filled with default values of the type. But, for these fixed point types, these values were uninitialized. Thus, we would have uninitialized memory access bugs, some of which were caught by MSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 344101137
Change-Id: I14555fda74dca3b5f1582da9008901937e3f14e2
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['QInt8() {}'], 'added_lines': ['QInt8() : value(0) {}']}
description: In affected versions of TensorFlow under certain cases a saved model can trigger use of uninitialized values during code execution. This is caused by having tensor buffers be filled with the default value of the type but forgetting to default initialize the quantized floating point types in Eigen. This is fixed in versions 1.15.5, 2.0.4, 2.1.3, 2.2.2, 2.3.2, and 2.4.0.

code_evidence: The single line defines the user-provided default constructor QInt8() {} with an empty body, leaving the member 'value' (the quantized storage) uninitialized when a QInt8 is default-constructed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-908 covers use of a resource that has not been initialized; here the QInt8 value is a resource left uninitialized by the empty constructor and later consumed. This is distinct from CWE-457 (uninitialized stack variable) since the defect is a missing constructor initializer for a type's member, not a local variable.

evidence_lines.code: QInt8() {}

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the default constructor performs no initialization of the underlying value member. Trigger: code that default-constructs QInt8 objects, e.g., filling tensor buffers with the type's default value, then reads them. Supported consequence: reads of uninitialized memory, yielding indeterminate values (caught by MSAN) and potentially leaking stale data or causing unexpected behavior.

commit_msg:
vgacon: remove software scrollback support

Yunhai Zhang recently fixed a VGA software scrollback bug in commit
ebfdfeeae8c0 ("vgacon: Fix for missing check in scrollback handling"),
but that then made people look more closely at some of this code, and
there were more problems on the vgacon side, but also the fbcon software
scrollback.

We don't really have anybody who maintains this code - probably because
nobody actually _uses_ it any more.  Sure, people still use both VGA and
the framebuffer consoles, but they are no longer the main user
interfaces to the kernel, and haven't been for decades, so these kinds
of extra features end up bitrotting and not really being used.

So rather than try to maintain a likely unused set of code, I'll just
aggressively remove it, and see if anybody even notices.  Maybe there
are people who haven't jumped on the whole GUI badnwagon yet, and think
it's just a fad.  And maybe those people use the scrollback code.

If that turns out to be the case, we can resurrect this again, once
we've found the sucker^Wmaintainer for it who actually uses it.

Tested-by: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Cc: 张云海 <zhangyunhai@nsfocus.com>

Acked-by: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>

Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Lines 10-12 copy to/from c->vc_origin and c->vc_screenbuf bounded by vga_vram_size, showing the console buffer is the data being manipulated in this switch path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the defect is a read that exceeds the intended buffer bounds in the scrollback handling reached from this function. It is not a write overflow (CWE-787) since the supported consequence is reading memory beyond the buffer rather than writing past it.

commit_msg:
opj_mj2_extract: Check provided output prefix for length

This uses snprintf() with correct buffer length instead of sprintf(), which
prevents a buffer overflow when providing a long output prefix. Furthermore
the program exits with an error when the provided output prefix is too long.

Fixes #1088.

description: An issue was discovered in mj2/opj_mj2_extract.c in OpenJPEG 2.3.0. The output prefix was not checked for length, which could overflow a buffer, when providing a prefix with 50 or more characters on the command line.

code_evidence: Line 12 declares a fixed 50-byte stack buffer outfilename.
Line 49 uses sprintf to write argv[2] plus a suffix "_%05d.j2k" (11+ characters) into outfilename with no bound on the length of argv[2], the user-supplied output prefix.
Line 50 then opens the resulting path; the overflow occurs at line 49 before use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the intended boundary of a fixed-size memory buffer (outfilename), which is exactly CWE-119's out-of-bounds write. It is not merely a format-string issue since the format is constant; the defect is the missing length restriction on the destination buffer.

evidence_lines.code: char outfilename[50];
sprintf(outfilename, "%s_%05d.j2k", argv[2], snum);
outfile = fopen(outfilename, "wb");

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded sprintf copies the command-line output prefix into the 50-byte stack buffer. Trigger: invoking the tool with a prefix of roughly 40+ characters so the formatted string exceeds 50 bytes; the write overruns outfilename into adjacent stack memory. Supported consequence: stack buffer overflow, potentially corrupting adjacent locals/control data and crashing or enabling code execution.

commit_msg:
Fix handling of unclosed interpolant in url

Fixes #2661
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      if (!pp) return 0;']}
description: An issue was discovered in LibSass through 3.5.4. An out-of-bounds read of a memory region was found in the function Sass::Prelexer::skip_over_scopes which could be leveraged by an attacker to disclose information or manipulated to read from unmapped memory causing a denial of service.

code_evidence: The loop advances pp via sequence<interpolant, real_uri_value>(pp); if that parse fails it returns a null pointer. The loop condition checks pp before peeking, but after the loop exits pp may be null and is assigned to position without a check. position is then passed to parse_interpolated_chunk(Token(p, position)), so a failed interpolation parse leads to a null end pointer being used as a buffer bound.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the missing null check on pp lets a null end pointer become a buffer boundary, causing reads past the intended input region. It is not merely a null dereference: the value is used as an offset/limit in token construction, producing out-of-bounds memory reads.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the loop can terminate with pp == 0 when sequence<> fails on an unclosed interpolant, and that null is stored in position and used to build a Token. Trigger: malformed URL input containing a hash_lbrace interpolation that does not parse. Consequence: the token's end pointer is null, so downstream parsing computes a length/range from it and reads outside the intended buffer, matching the reported out-of-bounds read in skip_over_scopes.

commit_msg:
avformat/asfdec_o: Check size_bmp more fully

Fixes: integer overflow and out of array access
Fixes: asfo-crash-46080c4341572a7137a162331af77f6ded45cbd7

Found-by: Paul Ch <paulcher@icloud.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (size_bmp > BMP_HEADER_SIZE) {'], 'added_lines': ['    if (size_bmp > BMP_HEADER_SIZE &&', '        size_bmp < INT_MAX - AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE) {']}
description: FFmpeg before commit 2b46ebdbff1d8dec7a3d8ea280a612b91a582869 contains a Buffer Overflow vulnerability in asf_o format demuxer that can result in heap-buffer-overflow that may result in remote code execution. This attack appears to be exploitable via specially crafted ASF file that has to be provided as input to FFmpeg. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in 2b46ebdbff1d8dec7a3d8ea280a612b91a582869 and later.

code_evidence: Line 10 sets size_bmp to FFMAX(size_asf, size_bmp) from attacker-controlled ASF/BMP header fields. The guard at line 11 only checks size_bmp > BMP_HEADER_SIZE, so a large size_bmp passes. Line 13 computes extradata_size = size_bmp - BMP_HEADER_SIZE, and line 14 allocates that size plus AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE; if the addition overflows, a small buffer is allocated. Lines 19-20 memset padding at extradata + extradata_size, and lines 21-22 avio_read writes extradata_size bytes, both beyond the undersized allocation.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the function performs read/write operations outside the intended buffer boundary, here a heap allocation undersized due to unchecked size_bmp. The direct consequence is an out-of-bounds memory write/read, matching the buffer-bounds class rather than a mere resource issue.

Trigger: a crafted ASF file whose header yields a very large size_bmp. commit_msg:
ARM: dma-mapping: don't allow DMA mappings to be marked executable

DMA mapping permissions were being derived from pgprot_kernel directly
without using PAGE_KERNEL.  This causes them to be marked with executable
permission, which is not what we want.  Fix this.

Signed-off-by: Russell King <rmk+kernel@arm.linux.org.uk>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpgprot_t prot = __get_dma_pgprot(attrs, pgprot_kernel);'], 'added_lines': ['\tpgprot_t prot = __get_dma_pgprot(attrs, PAGE_KERNEL);']}
description: arch/arm/mm/dma-mapping.c in the Linux kernel before 3.13 on ARM platforms, as used in Android before 2016-08-05 on Nexus 5 and 7 (2013) devices, does not prevent executable DMA mappings, which might allow local users to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka Android internal bug 28803642 and Qualcomm internal bug CR642735.

code_evidence: Line 4 derives the DMA mapping protection from pgprot_kernel directly, which carries executable permission rather than the non-executable PAGE_KERNEL default.
Lines 8-9 pass this prot value into __dma_alloc, so the executable permission is applied to the returned DMA memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function assigns overly permissive executable access rights to DMA memory, a failure to enforce proper permission constraints; this fits CWE-264's scope of permissions and access-control management. It is permission-related rather than a buffer overflow or type confusion.

evidence_lines.code: pgprot_t prot = __get_dma_pgprot(attrs, pgprot_kernel);

return __dma_alloc(dev, size, handle, gfp, prot, true,
__builtin_return_address(0));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the page protection for DMA allocations is built from pgprot_kernel, which includes execute permission, instead of PAGE_KERNEL. Trigger: any coherent DMA allocation through arm_coherent_dma_alloc receives an executable mapping. Supported consequence: attacker-influenced data placed in such DMA buffers can be executed, weakening memory access protections and enabling privilege escalation.

pptp: verify sockaddr_len in pptp_bind() and pptp_connect()

description: The (1) pptp_bind and (2) pptp_connect functions in drivers/net/ppp/pptp.c in the Linux kernel through 4.3.3 do not verify an address length, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory and bypass the KASLR protection mechanism via a crafted application.

commit_msg:
Tiffsep and Tiffsep1 - abort on multi-page input wtithout %d OutputFile

Bug #701821 "Segmentation fault at tiff//libtiff/tif_dirinfo.c:513 in TIFFFindField"

The tiffsep and tiffsep1 only set 'code' to an error when an attempt is
made to write a second output file without using %d in the OutputFile
specification.

This causes problems later when attempting to process the files. The
devices should exit without trying to further process the pages under
these conditions and this commit returns immediately on error.

The other devices like this already return immediately on error, it
looks like the code here was copied between  devices without realising
that the tiffsep and tiffsep1 devices didn't exit when the error
condition was set.

description: A null pointer dereference vulnerability in devices/gdevtsep.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted postscript file. This is fixed in v9.51.

Lines 30-51: the block is entered only when pdev->file != NULL, parsed.iodev is the default device, and fmt is non-NULL. Inside, line 39-40 walks fmt backwards looking for 'l' or '%' with no lower bound; this is the pointer that was never validated because the multi-page/no-%d error did not abort.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The commit fixes a NULL pointer dereference: continuing after the error condition causes later code to operate on a NULL/invalid pointer (the TIFF field lookup in tif_dirinfo.c). The added goto done aborts before that dereference, matching CWE-476. It is not merely a resource leak or logic error because the supported consequence is a NULL dereference crash.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the missing abort after setting gs_error_ioerror at line 28 lets control flow proceed into code that assumes a valid, well-formed output filename format. When fmt is NULL due to a multi-page output without %d, the fmt-dependent block is skipped, but the error state is left set and later page processing proceeds on a device whose output state is inconsistent, leading to a NULL dereference in downstream TIFF handling. Trigger: crafted PostScript producing multiple pages without %d in OutputFile. Consequence: crash/DoS (NULL pointer dereference).

commit_msg:
Fix Segfault in Concat V2 shape function.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 412120654
Change-Id: I3ff915faea694f9ad8b00024e9af2de9909011be
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  const int min_rank = concat_dim < 0 ? -concat_dim : concat_dim + 1;'], 'added_lines': ['  const int64 min_rank = concat_dim < 0 ? -concat_dim : concat_dim + 1;']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. The implementation of shape inference for `ConcatV2` can be used to trigger a denial of service attack via a segfault caused by a type confusion. The `axis` argument is translated into `concat_dim` in the `ConcatShapeHelper` helper function. Then, a value for `min_rank` is computed based on `concat_dim`. This is then used to validate that the `values` tensor has at least the required rank. However, `WithRankAtLeast` receives the lower bound as a 64-bits value and then compares it against the maximum 32-bits integer value that could be represented. Due to the fact that `min_rank` is a 32-bits value and the value of `axis`, the `rank` argument is a negative value, so the error check is bypassed. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: concat_dim is declared int64_t and assigned from either a DT_INT32 or DT_INT64 tensor, but min_rank is declared as 32-bit int and computed as -concat_dim or concat_dim + 1.
The truncated min_rank is passed to WithRankAtLeast, which receives the lower bound as a 64-bit value, so the rank check is evaluated against a corrupted bound.
concat_dim, not the truncated value, is then used in c->Dim(input, concat_dim) and Subshape, so the validated rank and the used axis disagree.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The same axis value is interpreted as a 64-bit integer for indexing and as a truncated 32-bit integer for validation, so a resource is initialized/checked with one type and used with an incompatible type, matching CWE-843; the consequence is a crash rather than a mere bounds error.

evidence_lines.code: TF_RETURN_IF_ERROR(c->WithRankAtLeast(input, min_rank, &input));
DimensionHandle output_middle = c->Dim(input, concat_dim);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is narrowing a 64-bit axis-derived value into a 32-bit min_rank, so the rank validation at line 41 uses a value inconsistent with the 64-bit concat_dim later used to index the shape. A large or negative axis triggers bypass of the rank check, and the subsequent Dim/Subshape access on an under-ranked input causes a segfault (DoS).

commit_msg: Fix potential out-of-buffer read while parsing corrupt file, closes #38
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (huffcdic->index_count != huffcdic->index_read) {', '        debug_print("CDIC: wrong read index count: %zu, total: %zu\\n", huffcdic->index_read, huffcdic->index_count);', '        return MOBI_DATA_CORRUPT;', '    }']}
description: libmobi is vulnerable to Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset

code_evidence: The loop iterates while i < huff_rec_count - 1, calling mobi_parse_cdic(huffcdic, curr, i++) for each CDIC record and advancing curr = curr->next. A NULL curr is checked at the top, but the number of available CDIC records is never reconciled with huff_rec_count; after the loop the function returns MOBI_SUCCESS unconditionally. The added guard (index_count != index_read) rejects mismatched counts, indicating parsing can stop before all expected indices are filled.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the missing count/chain consistency check allows operations on the symbols buffer beyond its intended populated boundary, matching out-of-bounds memory access. The commit explicitly fixes a potential out-of-buffer read; the concrete out-of-range pointer offset is a lower-level instance of the same buffer-bounds weakness.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser trusts huff_rec_count from the MOBI header but does not enforce that the CDIC record chain supplies exactly huff_rec_count-1 records. Trigger: a corrupt file where the chain ends early or record counts disagree. Consequence: mobi_parse_cdic may leave huffcdic->symbols entries unpopulated or index beyond intended bounds, leading to out-of-buffer reads when decoded later.

description: Modules/_pickle.c in Python before 3.7.1 has an integer overflow via a large LONG_BINPUT value that is mishandled during a "resize to twice the size" attempt. This issue might cause memory exhaustion, but is only relevant if the pickle format is used for serializing tens or hundreds of gigabytes of data. This issue is fixed in: v3.4.10, v3.4.10rc1; v3.5.10, v3.5.10rc1, v3.5.7, v3.5.7rc1, v3.5.8, v3.5.8rc1, v3.5.8rc2, v3.5.9; v3.6.10, v3.6.10rc1, v3.6.11, v3.6.11rc1, v3.6.12, v3.6.7, v3.6.7rc1, v3.6.7rc2, v3.6.8, v3.6.8rc1, v3.6.9, v3.6.9rc1; v3.7.1, v3.7.1rc1, v3.7.1rc2, v3.7.2, v3.7.2rc1, v3.7.3, v3.7.3rc1, v3.7.4, v3.7.4rc1, v3.7.4rc2, v3.7.5, v3.7.5rc1, v3.7.6, v3.7.6rc1, v3.7.7, v3.7.7rc1, v3.7.8, v3.7.8rc1, v3.7.9.

code_evidence: The function takes a signed Py_ssize_t idx and validates it with `idx < 0 || idx >= self->memo_size` before indexing `self->memo[idx]`. The signedness of idx means callers that compute the index from an untrusted LONG_BINPUT value can pass a wrapped/negative value; the function then only rejects it because of the explicit `idx < 0` guard, not because the index arithmetic itself is safe.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the weakness is signed integer overflow/wraparound in the memo index calculation, which the patch addresses by changing the parameter to size_t and dropping the now-unneeded negative check. It is not merely CWE-125: the invalid index is produced by integer overflow, and the bounds check is the mitigation, not the flaw itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the memo index is represented and computed as a signed Py_ssize_t, so index calculations derived from attacker-controlled pickle LONG_BINPUT values can overflow/wrap before reaching this accessor. Trigger: a pickle containing a huge memo index. This accessor's bound check happens to catch negative results, but the underlying signed index computation is the overflow site the commit fixes; supported consequence is out-of-bounds memo access if the guard is absent or bypassed.

commit_msg:
svc: check for allocation overflow in crypto calls

Without checking for overflow there is a risk of allocating a buffer
with size smaller than anticipated and as a consequence of that it might
lead to a heap based overflow with attacker controlled data written
outside the boundaries of the buffer.

Fixes: OP-TEE-2018-0010: "Integer overflow in crypto system calls (x2)"

Signed-off-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Tested-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org> (QEMU v7, v8)
Reviewed-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Riscure <inforequest@riscure.com>
Reported-by: Alyssa Milburn <a.a.milburn@vu.nl>
Acked-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tparams = malloc(sizeof(TEE_Attribute) * param_count);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t alloc_size = 0;', '', '\tif (MUL_OVERFLOW(sizeof(TEE_Attribute), param_count, &alloc_size))', '\t\treturn TEE_ERROR_OVERFLOW;', '', '\tparams = malloc(alloc_size);']}
description: Linaro/OP-TEE OP-TEE 3.3.0 and earlier is affected by: Buffer Overflow. The impact is: Execution of code in TEE core (kernel) context. The component is: optee_os. The fixed version is: 3.4.0 and later.

code_evidence: Line 21 computes the allocation size as sizeof(TEE_Attribute) * param_count using an attacker-influenced param_count without any overflow check. Lines 22-23 only test malloc's return value, and line 24 then calls copy_in_attrs with the same param_count, so the count used for sizing and the count used for copying are identical.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an unchecked integer multiplication used as an allocation size, which wraps and leads to an undersized buffer; this matches CWE-190. The downstream heap overflow is the consequence, not the root cause, so a buffer-overflow label would describe the effect rather than the overflow in the size calculation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the multiplication for malloc can wrap for a large param_count, yielding a small buffer. Trigger: a caller supplies an oversized param_count through the crypto system call. copy_in_attrs then writes param_count attribute entries into the undersized heap buffer, producing a heap overflow with attacker-influenced data.

commit_msg: Fix vulnerability in debug.getinfo
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    api_check(L, tvisfunc(func));'], 'added_lines': ['    if (!tvisfunc(func))', '\t  return 0;']}
description: In LuaJIT through 2.0.5, as used in Moonjit before 2.1.2 and other products, debug.getinfo has a type confusion issue that leads to arbitrary memory write or read operations, because certain cases involving valid stack levels and > options are mishandled. NOTE: The LuaJIT project owner states that the debug libary is unsafe by definition and that this is not a vulnerability. When LuaJIT was originally developed, the expectation was that the entire debug library had no security guarantees and thus it made no sense to assign CVEs. However, not all users of later LuaJIT derivatives share this perspective

code_evidence: The '>' branch takes the top stack slot as a TValue pointer and, before the fix, only asserts tvisfunc(func); the release build's api_check does not enforce the type, so funcV(func) reinterprets whatever value is on top as a GCfunc and accesses fn->c fields later (lines 48-56, 74, 78).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code accesses a TValue resource using an incompatible GCfunc type after a non-enforcing check, matching CWE-843. This is type confusion rather than a simple bounds issue because the same slot is reinterpreted as a different object type.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function value at L->top-1 is assumed to be a function but only checked with a debug-only api_check, so a non-function value is type-confused into a GCfunc. Trigger: calling debug.getinfo with '>'-style options while the top slot holds a non-function value. Consequence: arbitrary memory read/write via the misinterpreted GCfunc fields.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions due to incomplete validation in MKL implementation of requantization, an attacker can trigger undefined behavior via binding a reference to a null pointer or can access data outside the bounds of heap allocated arrays. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl/mkl_requantization_range_per_channel_op.cc) does not validate the dimensions of the `input` tensor. A similar issue occurs in `MklRequantizePerChannelOp`. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl/mkl_requantize_per_channel_op.cc) does not perform full validation for all the input arguments. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 9e62869465573cb2d9b5053f1fa02a81fce21d69 and in the Github commit 203214568f5bc237603dbab6e1fd389f1572f5c9. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: input_requested_min is read via flat<float>()(0) without checking that the tensor is a scalar; a zero-element tensor makes index 0 an out-of-bounds access.
input_requested_max is similarly dereferenced at index 0 with no NumElements()==1 validation.

Only input_min_vec.dim_size(0) and input_max_vec.dim_size(0) are compared to depth; NumElements() of input_max_vec is never checked, so a multi-dimensional or mismatched input_max_vec can pass validation while the loop indexes it.
The loop iterates i < depth and reads input_min_vec_data[i] and input_max_vec_data[i]; if input_max_vec has fewer than depth elements, this reads outside the heap buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The root cause is missing validation of input tensor shapes and element counts before indexing, matching CWE-20's improper input validation: required size/scalar properties are not checked, enabling unsafe downstream access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The kernel derives depth from input_min_vec but does not validate that input_requested_min/input_requested_max are scalars or that input_max_vec has at least depth elements. A crafted model with empty scalar tensors or a short input_max_vec triggers out-of-bounds reads (and a null/zero-size flat access), causing undefined behavior or heap memory disclosure.
