commit_msg:
ServiceManager: Restore basic uid check

Prevent apps from registering services without relying on selinux checks.

Bug: 29431260

Change-Id: I38c6e8bc7f7cba1cbd3568e8fed1ae7ac2054a9b
(cherry picked from commit 2b74d2c1d2a2c1bb6e9c420f7e9b339ba2a95179)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    if (uid >= AID_APP) {', "        return 0; /* Don't allow apps to register services */", '    }', '']}
description: cmds/servicemanager/service_manager.c in ServiceManager in Android 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, 6.x before 2016-10-01, and 7.0 before 2016-10-01 does not properly restrict service registration, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 29431260.

code_evidence: svc_can_register receives the caller's uid and name, but its only authorization decision is check_mac_perms_from_lookup on the "add" permission; there is no check on the numeric uid. Any caller that passes the MAC lookup can reach the return at line 4 and be granted registration.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an access-control decision for service registration without a uid-based restriction, matching CWE-264's permissions/privileges category. This is a missing authorization constraint rather than a memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the registration path delegates all authorization to the MAC permission lookup and never constrains the caller's uid, so an application uid is treated like a system caller. Trigger: a crafted app invokes service registration and satisfies the MAC lookup. Consequence: the app can register services it should not control, enabling privilege gain.

commit_msg:
Bug 790849 - (CVE-2017-17789) CVE-2017-17789 Heap buffer overflow...

... in PSP importer.
Check if declared block length is valid (i.e. within the actual file)
before going further.
Consider the file as broken otherwise and fail loading it.

(cherry picked from commit 28e95fbeb5720e6005a088fa811f5bf3c1af48b8)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      if (block_start + block_total_len > st.st_size)', '        {', '          g_set_error (error, G_FILE_ERROR, G_FILE_ERROR_FAILED,', '                       _("Could not open \'%s\' for reading: %s"),', '                       gimp_filename_to_utf8 (filename),', '                       _("invalid block size"));', '          goto error;', '        }', '']}
description: In GIMP 2.8.22, there is a heap-based buffer overflow in read_channel_data in plug-ins/common/file-psp.c.

code_evidence: The loop reads each block via read_block_header, which supplies block_total_len, then records block_start = ftell(f) [58-62].

After handling the block, the code only checks block_start + block_total_len >= st.st_size to break [139-140]; otherwise it seeks to block_start + block_total_len [141]. There is no check that the declared block_total_len stays within the actual file before the block handlers consume it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing bound check lets file-controlled length drive a write beyond an allocated buffer, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely an out-of-bounds read because the affected channel-data path writes into a heap buffer sized from the same unchecked length.

evidence_lines.code:
while (ftell (f) != st.st_size
&& (id = read_block_header (f, &block_init_len,
&block_total_len)) != -1)
block_start = ftell (f);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the declared block length (block_total_len) from the file is trusted and passed to block readers (e.g., read_channel_data) without verifying it lies within the file. Trigger: a crafted PSP file declares an oversized block length; the reader allocates/uses it and writes past the buffer. Supported consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds write, leading to memory corruption or code execution.

commit_msg:
Bug #484 CVE-2018-17582 Check for corrupt PCAP files

* Check for packets that are larger than 262144 bytes
* Check for capture lengths that are greater than packet length

Example of a corrupt PCAP file ...

sudo src/tcpreplay -i ens33 --unique-ip -t --loop 4 get_next_paket_01
safe_pcap_next ERROR: Invalid packet length in send_packets.c:get_next_packet() line 1054: 8388670 is greater than maximum 262144
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['            pktdata = (u_char *)pcap_next(pcap, pkthdr);', '        pktdata = (u_char *)pcap_next(pcap, pkthdr);'], 'added_lines': ['            pktdata = safe_pcap_next(pcap, pkthdr);', '        pktdata = safe_pcap_next(pcap, pkthdr);']}
description: Tcpreplay v4.3.0 beta1 contains a heap-based buffer over-read. The get_next_packet() function in the send_packets.c file uses the memcpy() function unsafely to copy sequences from the source buffer pktdata to the destination (*prev_packet)->pktdata. This will result in a Denial of Service (DoS) and potentially Information Exposure when the application attempts to process a file.

code_evidence: At line 21 pktdata comes from pcap_next(pcap, pkthdr), and pkthdr->len at line 32 supplies the copy length for safe_malloc(pktlen) and memcpy((*prev_packet)->pktdata, pktdata, pktlen) at lines 33-34, with no check that len <= caplen or a maximum bound.
Line 40 also assigns pktdata directly from pcap_next without validating the returned packet's lengths.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe memcpy at line 34 reads beyond the intended source buffer (pktdata) because the length is unvalidated, matching CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not merely an integer overflow: the defect is reading past the buffer end.

evidence_lines.code: pktdata = (u_char *)pcap_next(pcap, pkthdr);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function trusts the PCAP header's len field and copies that many bytes from pktdata, which only actually holds caplen bytes, so a corrupt file with len > caplen makes memcpy read past the source buffer. Trigger: processing a crafted/corrupt PCAP record where the capture length is smaller than the declared packet length; the consequence is an out-of-bounds heap read causing a crash/DoS and possible information exposure.

commit_msg: Added extra EOF check and some minor refactoring.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  SkipRGBMipmaps(image, dds_info, 4);', '', '  return MagickTrue;'], 'added_lines': ['  return(SkipRGBMipmaps(image,dds_info,4,exception));']}
description: coders/dds.c in ImageMagick allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted DDS file.

code_evidence: Loop bounds use dds_info->height and dds_info->width from the parsed DDS header without any check that they are consistent with the actual blob size.
Per-pixel reads (ReadBlobShort/ReadBlobByte) consume bytes for every width*height pixel; no count of remaining input or EOF check guards these reads before values are written to q.
q is advanced per pixel and SyncAuthenticPixels is called, but SkipRGBMipmaps and return MagickTrue ignore whether the input was exhausted.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function processes attacker-supplied DDS metadata and pixel data without validating required properties (sufficient size/consistency with actual data), matching CWE-20's improper input validation. The supported consequence is DoS from malformed input, not a separate memory-safety class.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: width/height and the pixel data are trusted from the crafted DDS header without validating that the blob contains enough bytes. Trigger: a crafted DDS file declaring dimensions larger than its data. The read loop then consumes beyond available input, producing a crash/DoS as described; the added SkipRGBMipmaps return is not what establishes this.

commit_msg:
perf expr: Fix missing check for return value of hashmap__new()

The hashmap__new() function may return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) when malloc()
fails, add IS_ERR() checking for ctx->ids.

Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Ian Rogers <irogers@google.com>
Cc: Jiri Olsa <jolsa@redhat.com>
Cc: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Cc: Namhyung Kim <namhyung@kernel.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Link: http://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20211212062504.25841-1-linmq006@gmail.com
[ s/kfree()/free()/ and add missing linux/err.h include ]
Signed-off-by: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tif (IS_ERR(ctx->ids)) {', '\t\tfree(ctx);', '\t\treturn NULL;', '\t}']}
description: In the Linux kernel before 5.16, tools/perf/util/expr.c lacks a check for the hashmap__new return value.

code_evidence: Line 7 assigns the result of hashmap__new() directly to ctx->ids without any error check. Lines 8-9 then initialize ctx->runtime and return ctx as if initialization succeeded, propagating an ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) value stored in ctx->ids to all callers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-252 directly matches: the function fails to check the return value of hashmap__new() and proceeds as though initialization succeeded, allowing an unexpected error state to propagate.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: hashmap__new() may return an ERR_PTR on allocation failure, but the return value is stored unchecked. Trigger: memory allocation failure inside hashmap__new(). Consequence: ctx is returned with ctx->ids holding an error pointer, so later hashmap operations dereference an invalid pointer, causing a crash or unexpected state.

commit_msg:
Since commit 9e2369c06c8a18 ("xen: add helpers to allocate unpopulated
memory") foreign mappings are using guest physical addresses allocated
via ZONE_DEVICE functionality.

This will result in problems for the case of no balloon memory hotplug
being configured, as the p2m list will only cover the initial memory
size of the domain. Any ZONE_DEVICE allocated address will be outside
the p2m range and thus a mapping can't be established with that memory
address.

Fix that by extending the p2m size for that case. At the same time add
a check for a to be created mapping to be within the p2m limits in
order to detect errors early.

While changing a comment, remove some 32-bit leftovers.

This is XSA-369.

Fixes: 9e2369c06c8a18 ("xen: add helpers to allocate unpopulated memory")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.9
Reported-by: Marek Marczykowski-Górecki <marmarek@invisiblethingslab.com>
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Jan Beulich <jbeulich@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (unlikely(pfn >= xen_p2m_size)) {', '\t\tBUG_ON(mfn != INVALID_P2M_ENTRY);', '\t\treturn true;', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t/* Only invalid entries allowed above the highest p2m covered frame. */', '\tif (unlikely(pfn >= xen_p2m_size))', '\t\treturn mfn == INVALID_P2M_ENTRY;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel 5.9.x through 5.11.3, as used with Xen. In some less-common configurations, an x86 PV guest OS user can crash a Dom0 or driver domain via a large amount of I/O activity. The issue relates to misuse of guest physical addresses when a configuration has CONFIG_XEN_UNPOPULATED_ALLOC but not CONFIG_XEN_BALLOON_MEMORY_HOTPLUG.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function is a p2m mapping helper that validates pfn against xen_p2m_size; it performs no buffer-size calculation or allocation, so it does not directly support CWE-131.

description: The exif_process_IFD_in_MAKERNOTE function in ext/exif/exif.c in PHP before 5.5.38, 5.6.x before 5.6.24, and 7.x before 7.0.9 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds array access and memory corruption), obtain sensitive information from process memory, or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted JPEG image.

code_evidence: dir_start is computed as value_ptr + maker_note->offset without checking that offset is within value_len; NumDirEntries is then read from dir_start and, in MN_OFFSET_GUESS, php_ifd_get32u reads dir_start+10, both potentially past the buffer end.
The maker_note selection loop only matches make/model/id_string; it does not validate the chosen maker_note->offset against value_len before the pointer arithmetic and reads.

Trigger: a crafted JPEG whose MakerNote selects an entry with an offset near or beyond value_len. Peek for \n in LineBasedFrameDecoder.

Summary:
Previously this could underflow if there was not a following \n.

CVE-2019-3563

Reviewed By: siyengar

Differential Revision: D14935715

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    } else if (terminatorType_ != TerminatorType::NEWLINE &&', "               b == '\\r' && !c.isAtEnd() && c.read<char>() == '\\n') {"], 'added_lines': ['    } else if (', "        terminatorType_ != TerminatorType::NEWLINE && b == '\\r' &&", "        !c.isAtEnd() && *c.peekBytes().data() == '\\n') {"]}
description: Wangle's LineBasedFrameDecoder contains logic for identifying newlines which incorrectly advances a buffer, leading to a potential underflow. This affects versions of Wangle prior to v2019.04.22.00

code_evidence: Line 4 reads a byte b from cursor c. Lines 7-8 check for '\r' and then call c.read<char>() to test for a following '\n', advancing the cursor past a byte even when it is not consumed as part of a matched terminator.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The CWE-787 target reflects a buffer-position accounting flaw that can lead to out-of-bounds memory access; the incorrect cursor advance on line 8 is the root cause enabling the underflow. A pure logic error label would understate that the consequence is memory-boundary violation.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The end-of-line scan advances the cursor via c.read<char>() while probing for a CRLF terminator; when the probed byte is not '\n', the cursor has moved past data that the framing logic still needs. This mis-tracking of buffer position can drive the cursor beyond valid bounds during subsequent parsing, causing an out-of-bounds access rather than a direct in-loop write.

commit_msg:
ipv6: Prevent overrun when parsing v6 header options

The KASAN warning repoted below was discovered with a syzkaller
program.  The reproducer is basically:
  int s = socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_RAW, NEXTHDR_HOP);
  send(s, &one_byte_of_data, 1, MSG_MORE);
  send(s, &more_than_mtu_bytes_data, 2000, 0);

The socket() call sets the nexthdr field of the v6 header to
NEXTHDR_HOP, the first send call primes the payload with a non zero
byte of data, and the second send call triggers the fragmentation path.

The fragmentation code tries to parse the header options in order
to figure out where to insert the fragment option.  Since nexthdr points
to an invalid option, the calculation of the size of the network header
can made to be much larger than the linear section of the skb and data
is read outside of it.

This fix makes ip6_find_1stfrag return an error if it detects
running out-of-bounds.

description: The IPv6 fragmentation implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.11.1 does not consider that the nexthdr field may be associated with an invalid option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and BUG) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted socket and send system calls.

code_evidence: hlen is declared unsigned int [10] and receives ip6_find_1stfragopt(skb, &prevhdr) [15]; nexthdr is then read from *prevhdr [16]. The only size check uses hlen (mtu < hlen + sizeof(...)) [31] and subtraction mtu -= hlen + sizeof(...) [33], so a crafted nexthdr that makes the parser return an oversized hlen is treated as a valid header length.

The derived hlen drives kmemdup(skb_network_header(skb), hlen, ...) [65], __skb_pull(skb, hlen) [74], memcpy(..., tmp_hdr, hlen) [78], left = skb->len - hlen [142], ptr = hlen [143], skb_copy_from_linear_data(..., hlen) [170], and the copy at [177], all reading hlen bytes from a linear region that may be smaller.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory beyond the intended skb buffer using an unvalidated length (hlen) in kmemdup/memcpy/__skb_pull and the slow-path copy, which directly matches CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. It is not merely an integer overflow, since the length is used as-is to index/read past the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of ip6_find_1stfragopt is used as a trusted unsigned header length without validating that it fits the skb linear data; the fix adds an hlen < 0 error check. Trigger: a raw IPv6 socket with nexthdr NEXTHDR_HOP and a payload whose option encoding makes the parser compute a hlen larger than the linear section, then fragmentation runs. Consequence: out-of-bounds reads of skb memory (KASAN slab-out-of-bounds, BUG/crash).

commit_msg: Removed a potential buffer overflow crash in GmfOpenMesh and debugged the test_libmeshb_block_pipeline.f that crashed
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      while(fscanf(msh->hdl, "%s", str) != EOF)'], 'added_lines': ['      while(fscanf(msh->hdl, "%100s", str) != EOF)']}
description: A buffer overflow in the GmfOpenMesh() function of libMeshb v7.61 allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted MESH file.

code_evidence: Line 5 declares a fixed stack buffer str[GmfStrSiz]. Line 8 uses fscanf with an unbounded "%s" conversion into str, so the number of characters read is limited only by the input token length, not by GmfStrSiz. The loop on line 9 continues over arbitrary tokens from the file.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-120 fits because the code copies file input into a fixed-size buffer without checking the input size, producing a classic buffer overflow. It is a write-past-buffer copy rather than an out-of-bounds read, which would instead be CWE-125.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A crafted MESH file containing a token longer than GmfStrSiz causes fscanf to write past the end of the stack buffer str. The unbounded copy is the root cause; the trigger is an overlong whitespace-delimited token, and the supported consequence is stack memory corruption leading to a crash (DoS) and potentially code execution.

description: GPAC v2.1-DEV-rev478-g696e6f868-master was discovered to contain a heap use-after-free via the Q_IsTypeOn function at /gpac/src/bifs/unquantize.c.

code_evidence: The loop at line 18 runs while codec->LastError>=0; on error paths at 21/23 the function returns immediately, bypassing the QP cleanup at line 66.

When a QuantizationParameter node is decoded, gf_bifs_dec_qp_set (33) is called and qp_on is set; the early return at 34 skips gf_bifs_dec_qp_remove (66), leaving the codec's QP state referencing the node.
The early return at 50/53 likewise exits before the cleanup at 66 and before gf_bifs_dec_qp14_set_length at 67.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect is stale-reference reuse: control flow leaves the decoder with a dangling QP reference that is later accessed, matching CWE-416 (use after free). It is not merely an error-handling omission; the consequence is a use-after-free read of freed memory.

evidence_lines.code:
return codec->LastError;
if (e) return e;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: error returns inside the loop skip the single cleanup block that removes the active QP (gf_bifs_dec_qp_remove) and finalizes QP14 length. Trigger: a decoding error after a QuantizationParameter was set (qp_on=1) causes return at 21/23/34/50/53. The codec retains a QP pointer/state to a node that is subsequently freed, and later Q_IsTypeOn/decoder operations dereference the stale QP, yielding a heap use-after-free.

description: Uncontrolled Recursion in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to 2.1.0-DEV.

code_evidence: SFS_ObjectMethodCall calls SFS_Expression at line 4, then SFS_Identifier at line 6 and SFS_Params at line 8 without any recursion-depth or error check after SFS_Expression. The only guard, line 3, checks a pre-existing LastError before descending; nothing bounds or aborts the nested parse once SFS_Expression re-enters parsing. The patch adds exactly such a post-call LastError check after line 4, confirming the missing constraint sits between the recursive descent and subsequent parsing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-674 fits: recursion depth is not controlled and there is no guard terminating the descent, matching uncontrolled recursion with resource-consumption impact. A missing error check alone would be a different weakness; here it is the absent recursion bound that is decisive.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the parser descends into SFS_Expression (and SFS_Params) with no depth limit and no post-descent error check, so a crafted nested script expression keeps re-entering SFS_ObjectMethodCall. Trigger: deeply nested object/method-call syntax in input. Consequence: unbounded recursion exhausts the call stack, causing a crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
This is the candidate patch of CVE-2023-47233 :
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-47233

In brcm80211 driver,it starts with the following invoking chain
to start init a timeout worker:

->brcmf_usb_probe
  ->brcmf_usb_probe_cb
    ->brcmf_attach
      ->brcmf_bus_started
        ->brcmf_cfg80211_attach
          ->wl_init_priv
            ->brcmf_init_escan
              ->INIT_WORK(&cfg->escan_timeout_work,
		  brcmf_cfg80211_escan_timeout_worker);

If we disconnect the USB by hotplug, it will call
brcmf_usb_disconnect to make cleanup. The invoking chain is :

brcmf_usb_disconnect
  ->brcmf_usb_disconnect_cb
    ->brcmf_detach
      ->brcmf_cfg80211_detach
        ->kfree(cfg);

While the timeout woker may still be running. This will cause
a use-after-free bug on cfg in brcmf_cfg80211_escan_timeout_worker.

Fix it by deleting the timer and canceling the worker in
brcmf_cfg80211_detach.

Fixes: e756af5b30b0 ("brcmfmac: add e-scan support.")
Signed-off-by: Zheng Wang <zyytlz.wz@163.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
[arend.vanspriel@broadcom.com: keep timer delete as is and cancel work just before free]
Signed-off-by: Arend van Spriel <arend.vanspriel@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@kernel.org>
Link: https://msgid.link/20240107072504.392713-1-arend.vanspriel@broadcom.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (timer_pending(&cfg->escan_timeout))', '\t\tdel_timer_sync(&cfg->escan_timeout);'], 'added_lines': ['\ttimer_delete_sync(&cfg->escan_timeout);']}
description: The brcm80211 component in the Linux kernel through 6.5.10 has a brcmf_cfg80211_detach use-after-free in the device unplugging (disconnect the USB by hotplug) code. For physically proximate attackers with local access, this "could be exploited in a real world scenario." This is related to brcmf_cfg80211_escan_timeout_worker in drivers/net/wireless/broadcom/brcm80211/brcmfmac/cfg80211.c.

code_evidence: Lines 12–13 read cfg->scan_request and clear it, showing this function operates on the cfg scan state that the disconnect path later frees.

Lines 14–15 only synchronize the escan_timeout timer if timer_pending() is true; they do not cancel the escan_timeout_work worker, so the timeout worker can still run and dereference cfg after brcmf_cfg80211_detach frees it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the worker executes after cfg has been freed and dereferences the stale pointer. This is not merely a race on a live object; the object lifetime ends before the worker's access, which is the defining use-after-free condition.

evidence_lines.code:
scan_request = cfg->scan_request;
cfg->scan_request = NULL;

if (timer_pending(&cfg->escan_timeout))
del_timer_sync(&cfg->escan_timeout);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: scan teardown in this path synchronizes only the escan_timeout timer, not the queued escan_timeout_work that references cfg. Trigger: USB hotplug disconnect frees cfg via brcmf_cfg80211_detach while the timeout worker is pending or running. Consequence: the worker uses freed cfg memory (use-after-free), giving read/modify of freed memory and possible crash or code execution.

description: A buffer overflow vulnerability in jetp3852_print_page() in devices/gdev3852.c of Artifex Software GhostScript v9.50 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a crafted PDF file. This is fixed in v9.51.

code_evidence: A fixed-size stack buffer `data[DATA_SIZE]` is declared; `line_size` from `gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line` is unbounded and used to copy scan lines into `data`.
`memset(end_data, 0, 7)` and the loop writing `odp[LINE_SIZE*2]`/reading `dp[7]` extend past `data` when `line_size` approaches or exceeds DATA_SIZE, corrupting the stack.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Writes past the end of the fixed stack buffer `data` are an out-of-bounds write, matching CWE-787. The related CWE-121 (stack-based buffer overflow) is a more specific child, but the target is the base out-of-bounds write, which fits directly.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: no check that the device-derived `line_size` fits `DATA_SIZE` before writing into the stack array `data`. Trigger: a crafted PDF with wide page or high resolution yields a large `line_size`, so `gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines` and the subsequent spread loop write/read past `data`. Consequence: stack corruption leading to crash/DoS, as stated in the commit.

calculation can easily overflow if too high width or height are given
inside the stream. Nonetheless we would just assume that enough memory
was allocated, try to fill it and overwrite as much memory as wanted.

with full-black and not any random (or not so random) data.

https://scarybeastsecurity.blogspot.gr/2016/11/0day-poc-risky-design-decisions-in.html

Ideally we should just remove this plugin in favour of the one in

description: Integer overflow in the vmnc decoder in the gstreamer allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via large width and height values, which triggers a buffer overflow.

code_evidence: Rectangle width and height are read from the untrusted packet stream as 16-bit values via RFB_GET_UINT16.
The only range check compares r.x + r.width and r.y + r.height against the format dimensions; the additions themselves can wrap, and the check applies only when r.type != TYPE_WMVi.
The validated rectangle struct is passed to the selected handler, which uses width/height for size and offset computations.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the unsafe operation is integer arithmetic on stream-controlled dimensions whose result is assumed large but can wrap, leading to an undersized allocation and buffer overflow. The missing upper bound on width/height is the missing constraint; the memory overwrite is the downstream consequence, not the root weakness.

evidence_lines.code: read = handler (dec, &r, data + offset + 12, len - offset - 12, decode);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: attacker-controlled width/height are used in size arithmetic (e.g., width*height*bpp for allocation and subsequent fill) without a bound on their magnitude. The r.x+r.width check can wrap and is skipped for TYPE_WMVi, so oversized values reach the handler. Trigger: a crafted packet with very large width/height. Consequence: the size calculation wraps to a small value, the buffer is under-allocated, and the fill overwrites memory, causing crash or memory corruption.

description: FreeType before 2.6.1 has a buffer over-read in skip_comment in psaux/psobjs.c because ps_parser_skip_PS_token is mishandled in an FT_New_Memory_Face operation.

code_evidence: For a '>' token, cur++ advances the cursor, then dereferences *cur after only checking cur >= limit; when cur == limit this reads one byte past the buffer.
At Exit, the self-delimiting check dereferences *cur in the error message when cur < limit, and the cursor is stored without clamping to limit, so an out-of-range cursor propagates to later parsing.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads memory past the intended buffer end (the '>' branch and Exit dereference *cur when cur may equal or exceed limit), which is exactly CWE-125; the fix clamps cur to limit to prevent the over-read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: skip_string/skip_procedure/skip_literal_string can return cur beyond limit; the '>' branch and Exit diagnostics then dereference *cur without a cur < limit guard, and the unclamped cursor is written back to parser->cursor, causing an out-of-bounds read.

avformat/pva: Check for EOF before retrying in read_part_of_packet()

Fixes: Infinite loop
Fixes: pva-4b1835dbc2027bf3c567005dcc78e85199240d06

Found-by: Paul Ch <paulcher@icloud.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

description: FFmpeg before commit 9807d3976be0e92e4ece3b4b1701be894cd7c2e1 contains a CWE-835: Infinite loop vulnerability in pva format demuxer that can result in a Vulnerability that allows attackers to consume excessive amount of resources like CPU and RAM. This attack appear to be exploitable via specially crafted PVA file has to be provided as input. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in 9807d3976be0e92e4ece3b4b1701be894cd7c2e1 and later.

code_evidence: When the PES signal or header length is invalid, the code logs a warning, skips length - 9 bytes, and if read_packet is set, jumps via goto recover back to line 8, re-reading the packet header from the current position. On EOF, avio_rb* reads return zeros/EOF values rather than advancing meaningfully, so the same invalid condition recurs and the recover loop repeats indefinitely.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The goto recover construct forms an unbounded retry loop whose exit condition (a valid header) is unreachable once the input reaches EOF, matching CWE-835's unreachable-exit infinite loop. The added EOF check confirms the missing termination condition; this is not merely a resource leak but a non-terminating iteration.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recover path retries without checking for stream EOF, so a crafted PVA file that ends after an invalid PES header causes the goto recover loop to repeat forever. Trigger: attacker-supplied truncated PVA file with invalid pes_signal or zero pes_header_data_length. Consequence: unbounded CPU consumption (denial of service).

Precompute what is needed to call the access function and do not check the
area's num_accesses again as the pointer may not be valid anymore. Use a
counter instead.

Fixes: 51fe6141f0f6 ("iommufd: Data structure to provide IOVA to PFN mapping")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1-v2-9a03761d445d+54-iommufd_syz2_jgg@nvidia.com
Reviewed-by: Kevin Tian <kevin.tian@intel.com>
Reported-by: syzbot+1ad12d16afca0e7d2dde@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/r/0000000000001d40fc05fe385332@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\tiommufd_access_notify_unmap(iopt, area_first,', '\t\t\t\t\t\t    iopt_area_length(area));', '\t\t\tif (WARN_ON(READ_ONCE(area->num_accesses)))'], 'added_lines': ['\tunsigned int tries = 0;', '\t\tif (area_first != start)', '\t\t\ttries = 0;', '', '\t\t\tsize_t length = iopt_area_length(area);', '', '', '\t\t\tiommufd_access_notify_unmap(iopt, area_first, length);', '\t\t\t/* Something is not responding to unmap requests. */', '\t\t\ttries++;', '\t\t\tif (WARN_ON(tries > 100))']}
description: The Linux kernel 6.3 has a use-after-free in iopt_unmap_iova_range in drivers/iommu/iommufd/io_pagetable.c.

code_evidence: After releasing iova_rwsem and domains_rwsem (lines 25-26), the code calls iommufd_access_notify_unmap using area_first and iopt_area_length(area) (lines 27-28), then re-reads area->num_accesses via READ_ONCE(area) (line 29). The area pointer is only protected by the locks that were just dropped, so a concurrent unmap in another thread can free the area while this thread is notifying, making the later area->num_accesses read a use-after-free.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the code reads memory through a pointer (area->num_accesses) after the underlying object may have been freed by a concurrent unmap. The fix replaces the stale pointer read with a local counter (tries), confirming the weakness was reuse of freed memory rather than a locking or bounds error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function dereferences the iopt_area pointer after dropping iova_rwsem, relying on a num_accesses check that can no longer safely observe the freed object. Trigger: concurrent unmap frees the area between the notify call and the READ_ONCE. Consequence: slab-use-after-free read, as confirmed by the KASAN report in iopt_unmap_iova_range.

commit_msg:
dm: Reset virtio device before release

With virtio polling mode enabled, a timer is running in the virtio
backend service. And the timer will also be triggered if its frondend
driver didn't do the device reset in shutdown. A freed virtio device
will be accessed in the polling timer handler.

Do the virtio reset() callback specifically to clear the polling timer
before the free.

Tracked-On: #6147
Signed-off-by: Shuo A Liu <shuo.a.liu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Yonghua Huang <yonghua.huang@intel.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tvirtio_i2c_reset(vi2c);']}
description: The polling timer handler in ACRN before 2.5 has a use-after-free for a freed virtio device, related to devicemodel/hw/pci/virtio/*.c.

code_evidence: virtio_i2c_deinit stops requests and removes the native adapter, destroys both mutexes, then immediately frees vi2c at line 12 and clears dev->arg. The diff adds virtio_i2c_reset(vi2c) before free, indicating the reset callback clears the backend polling timer; without it, the timer handler retains a reference to vi2c after deinitialization.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the polling timer handler dereferences device memory after the deinit function has freed it; the missing reset call is the constraint that would prevent the dangling reference. This is a use-after-free of the device object, not merely a double free or memory leak.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the deinit path tears down the virtio device without first stopping the polling timer that references it. Trigger: a frontend driver that skips device reset during shutdown leaves the polling timer active; the handler then accesses the freed vi2c after free(vi2c). Consequence: use-after-free of the virtio device, allowing reads/writes of freed memory, crash, or potential code execution.

commit_msg:
Validate dimensions of input tensor in `FractionalAvgPoolGrad`

PiperOrigin-RevId: 388286227
Change-Id: Ieb7566155e92acc8993a2212c76deacadc0edc8a
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, in_batch != 0,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("Batch dimension of input must not be 0"));', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, in_rows != 0,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("Rows dimension of input must not be 0"));', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, in_cols != 0,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("Columns dimension of input must not be 0"));', '    OP_REQUIRES(', '        context, in_depth != 0,', '        errors::InvalidArgument("Depth dimension of input must not be 0"));']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the implementation for `tf.raw_ops.FractionalAvgPoolGrad` can be tricked into accessing data outside of bounds of heap allocated buffers. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/f24faa153ad31a4b51578f8181d3aaab77a1ddeb/tensorflow/core/kernels/fractional_avg_pool_op.cc#L205) does not validate that the input tensor is non-empty. Thus, code constructs an empty `EigenDoubleMatrixMap` and then accesses this buffer with indices that are outside of the empty area. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 0f931751fb20f565c4e94aa6df58d54a003cdb30. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Lines 34-37 read the four input shape dimensions without checking that any is nonzero.
Lines 48-50 build an EigenDoubleMatrixMap over the temporary buffer sized in_depth by in_cols*in_rows*in_batch; a zero dimension yields an empty map.
Lines 70-72 compute in_index from in_rows and in_cols, and lines 76-78 write through coeffRef(d, in_index) into that buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes through the Eigen matrix map into a buffer whose size was derived from unvalidated dimensions, allowing writes past the allocated heap region. This is an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); the missing dimension validation is the root cause, and the memory write beyond bounds is the direct consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The shape values from input(0) are trusted without a nonzero check, so a zero batch/rows/cols/depth produces a zero-sized temporary buffer and an empty matrix map. The loop then indexes and writes via coeffRef into that empty buffer, causing a heap out-of-bounds write and possible crash or corruption.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tc_strcpy(theBuffer, key->value.key.string);', '\t\t\t\telse if ((kind == XS_STRING_KIND) || (kind == XS_STRING_X_KIND)) {', "\t\t\t\t\ttheBuffer[0] = '[';", '\t\t\t\t\tc_strcpy(theBuffer + 1, key->value.string);', '\t\t\t\t\tc_strcat(theBuffer, "]");', '\t\t\t\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\t\t\t\t\tc_snprintf(theBuffer, theSize, "%s", key->value.key.string);', '\t\t\t\telse if ((kind == XS_STRING_KIND) || (kind == XS_STRING_X_KIND))', '\t\t\t\t\tc_snprintf(theBuffer, theSize, "[%s]", key->value.string);']}
description: OpenSource Moddable v10.5.0 was discovered to contain a heap buffer overflow in the fxIDToString function at /moddable/xs/sources/xsSymbol.c.

code_evidence: For XS_KEY_KIND/XS_KEY_X_KIND keys, c_strcpy copies the key string into theBuffer without consulting theSize, so a key string longer than the caller-provided buffer writes past its end.

For XS_STRING_KIND/XS_STRING_X_KIND keys, the code writes '[' at index 0, c_strcpy's the string starting at offset 1, then c_strcat appends ']' — again with no bound check against theSize, overflowing when the bracketed string exceeds the buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes attacker-influenced key strings beyond the allocated buffer boundary, matching CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write). It is not merely CWE-120 (unbounded copy) because the concrete defect is writing past the intended buffer's end.

evidence_lines.code:
if ((kind == XS_KEY_KIND) || (kind == XS_KEY_X_KIND))
c_strcpy(theBuffer, key->value.key.string);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: unbounded c_strcpy/c_strcat into theBuffer while theSize is ignored. Trigger: a key whose string (or bracketed string) is longer than the destination buffer. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds write, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling code execution or crash.

commit_msg: Lowered max map_length to prevent an overflow (#271).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    if (map_length >= 32)'], 'added_lines': ['    if (map_length >= 22)']}
description: The ReadPCXImage function in coders/pcx.c in ImageMagick 7.0.4.9 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (attempted large memory allocation and application crash) via a crafted file. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-8862 and CVE-2016-8866.

code_evidence: map_length is read from the file as an unsigned char and only rejected when >= 32; it is then used as a shift count (one << map_length), so values like 31 produce a huge map_length that drives later allocations/indexing.
AcquireQuantumMemory allocates number_colormaps*3*map_length, then the loop reads 3*map_length entries per colormap; the size derives directly from the unchecked/loosely-bounded map_length.
mask=(map_length-1) and indexing colormap[x*map_length+(*p & mask)] compute offsets using map_length, so an oversized map_length yields out-of-bounds reads of the colormap buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads colormap memory at offsets derived from map_length without ensuring they stay within the allocated buffer, which is an out-of-bounds memory read/write within a buffer, matching CWE-119. The fix lowers the threshold to 22, confirming the bound on map_length was the intended constraint.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the file-controlled map_length is only bounded by a too-large threshold (>=32) before being shifted and used to size the colormap allocation and compute index offsets. A crafted RLE file with a large map_length triggers an undersized relative allocation followed by out-of-bounds colormap reads, causing memory corruption or crash.

tvb_generic_clone_offset_len uses tvb_bytes_exist to check that the
requested tvb data is actually available. It did not expect negative

description: In Wireshark 2.6.0, 2.4.0 to 2.4.6, and 2.2.0 to 2.2.14, the LTP dissector and other dissectors could consume excessive memory. This was addressed in epan/tvbuff.c by rejecting negative lengths.

code_evidence: tvb_bytes_exist accepts a signed gint length from callers (e.g. tvb_generic_clone_offset_len) and passes it directly to check_offset_length_no_exception without any check that length is non-negative. The function only returns FALSE when check_offset_length_no_exception reports an exception; a negative length is not treated as invalid there, so the function can return TRUE for a negative length.

This is distinct from an arithmetic overflow alone: the missing constraint on the input value is the root cause that lets the bad length propagate.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the length parameter is a signed integer that is never validated for negativity before being handed to downstream offset/length arithmetic. Trigger: a dissector or clone routine derives a negative length from packet data and calls tvb_bytes_exist, which approves it. Consequence: the caller proceeds to allocate/consume memory based on the unchecked value, yielding excessive memory consumption (DoS).

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.MaxPool3DGradGrad` is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/596c05a159b6fbb9e39ca10b3f7753b7244fa1e9/tensorflow/core/kernels/pooling_ops_3d.cc#L694-L696) does not check that the initialization of `Pool3dParameters` completes successfully. In turn, this might cause a heap buffer overflow, depending on default initialized values. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Pool3dParameters params is constructed from tensor_in.shape() and context; the constructor uses OP_REQUIRES, so a failed assertion leaves params with invalid data, yet execution continues.
The only guards before launch check dimensionality and that element counts are non-zero; no check verifies tensor_in, tensor_out, and out_grad_backprop share compatible element counts.
params with invalid shape data and mismatched tensors are passed directly to LaunchMaxPooling3dGradGradOp, which indexes buffers using params-derived dimensions.

evidence_lines.code:
Pool3dParameters params{context,  ksize_,       stride_,
padding_, data_format_, tensor_in.shape()};

LaunchMaxPooling3dGradGradOp<Device, T>::launch(
context, params, tensor_in, tensor_out, out_grad_backprop, output);

Trigger: crafted input shapes that fail constructor validation while passing the dims>0 and NumElements>0 checks. The launcher then computes offsets from invalid params and writes past the output buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds write.

and provide the correct length.

description: The IKEv2 parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isakmp.c, several functions.

code_evidence: Inside the while loop, ND_TCHECK(*ext) only validates one byte at the pointer type of *ext, then UNALIGNED_MEMCPY(&e, ext, sizeof(e)) copies a full struct isakmp_gen from ext. commit_msg:
floppy_revalidate() doesn't perform any error handling on lock_fdc()
result. lock_fdc() might actually be interrupted by a signal (it waits for
fdc becoming non-busy interruptibly). In such case, floppy_revalidate()
proceeds as if it had claimed the lock, but it fact it doesn't.

In case of multiple threads trying to open("/dev/fdX"), this leads to
serious corruptions all over the place, because all of a sudden there is
no critical section protection (that'd otherwise be guaranteed by locked
fd) whatsoever.

While at this, fix the fact that the 'interruptible' parameter to
lock_fdc() doesn't make any sense whatsoever, because we always wait
interruptibly anyway.

Most of the lock_fdc() callsites do properly handle error (and propagate
EINTR), but floppy_revalidate() and floppy_check_events() don't. Fix this.

Spotted by 'syzkaller' tool.

Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Tested-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tlock_fdc(drive, false);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tres = lock_fdc(drive);', '\t\tif (res)', '\t\t\treturn res;']}
description: A race condition was found in the Linux kernels implementation of the floppy disk drive controller driver software. The impact of this issue is lessened by the fact that the default permissions on the floppy device (/dev/fd0) are restricted to root. If the permissions on the device have changed the impact changes greatly. In the default configuration root (or equivalent) permissions are required to attack this flaw.

code_evidence: lock_fdc(drive, false) is called without checking its return value; execution continues into the critical section at lines 14-19 regardless of whether the lock was actually acquired. Since lock_fdc waits interruptibly, a signal can abort the wait, leaving the driver's shared state unprotected.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function fails to enforce exclusivity: it enters a shared-resource critical section without holding the lock, allowing an interfering concurrent sequence to modify the same floppy driver state. This is improper synchronization leading to a race, matching CWE-362; the missing return-value check is the concrete cause rather than a mere logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the return value of the interruptible lock_fdc() is discarded, so an interrupted lock acquisition is treated as success. Trigger: concurrent threads open("/dev/fdX") while a signal interrupts one waiter. Consequence: multiple sequences mutate UDRS flags, fake_change and generation without mutual exclusion, causing corruption (integrity loss) and instability.

commit_msg:
sched/fair: Fix low cpu usage with high throttling by removing expiration of cpu-local slices

It has been observed, that highly-threaded, non-cpu-bound applications
running under cpu.cfs_quota_us constraints can hit a high percentage of
periods throttled while simultaneously not consuming the allocated
amount of quota. This use case is typical of user-interactive non-cpu
bound applications, such as those running in kubernetes or mesos when
run on multiple cpu cores.

This has been root caused to cpu-local run queue being allocated per cpu
bandwidth slices, and then not fully using that slice within the period.
At which point the slice and quota expires. This expiration of unused
slice results in applications not being able to utilize the quota for
which they are allocated.

The non-expiration of per-cpu slices was recently fixed by
'commit 512ac999d275 ("sched/fair: Fix bandwidth timer clock drift
condition")'. Prior to that it appears that this had been broken since
at least 'commit 51f2176d74ac ("sched/fair: Fix unlocked reads of some
cfs_b->quota/period")' which was introduced in v3.16-rc1 in 2014. That
added the following conditional which resulted in slices never being
expired.

if (cfs_rq->runtime_expires != cfs_b->runtime_expires) {
	/* extend local deadline, drift is bounded above by 2 ticks */
	cfs_rq->runtime_expires += TICK_NSEC;

Because this was broken for nearly 5 years, and has recently been fixed
and is now being noticed by many users running kubernetes
(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/67577) it is my opinion
that the mechanisms around expiring runtime should be removed
altogether.

This allows quota already allocated to per-cpu run-queues to live longer
than the period boundary. This allows threads on runqueues that do not
use much CPU to continue to use their remaining slice over a longer
period of time than cpu.cfs_period_us. However, this helps prevent the
above condition of hitting throttling while also not fully utilizing
your cpu quota.

This theoretically allows a machine to use slightly more than its
allotted quota in some periods. This overflow would be bounded by the
remaining quota left on each per-cpu runqueueu. This is typically no
more than min_cfs_rq_runtime=1ms per cpu. For CPU bound tasks this will
change nothing, as they should theoretically fully utilize all of their
quota in each period. For user-interactive tasks as described above this
provides a much better user/application experience as their cpu
utilization will more closely match the amount they requested when they
hit throttling. This means that cpu limits no longer strictly apply per
period for non-cpu bound applications, but that they are still accurate
over longer timeframes.

This greatly improves performance of high-thread-count, non-cpu bound
applications with low cfs_quota_us allocation on high-core-count
machines. In the case of an artificial testcase (10ms/100ms of quota on
80 CPU machine), this commit resulted in almost 30x performance
improvement, while still maintaining correct cpu quota restrictions.
That testcase is available at https://github.com/indeedeng/fibtest.

Fixes: 512ac999d275 ("sched/fair: Fix bandwidth timer clock drift condition")
Signed-off-by: Dave Chiluk <chiluk+linux@indeed.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Phil Auld <pauld@redhat.com>

Cc: Ingo Molnar <mingo@redhat.com>

Cc: Jonathan Corbet <corbet@lwn.net>
Cc: Kyle Anderson <kwa@yelp.com>
Cc: Gabriel Munos <gmunoz@netflix.com>
Cc: Peter Oskolkov <posk@posk.io>
Cc: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Cc: Brendan Gregg <bgregg@netflix.com>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1563900266-19734-2-git-send-email-chiluk+linux@indeed.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tu64 runtime, runtime_expires;', '\truntime_expires = cfs_b->runtime_expires;', '', '\t\truntime = distribute_cfs_runtime(cfs_b, runtime,', '\t\t\t\t\t\t runtime_expires);'], 'added_lines': ['\tu64 runtime;', '\t\truntime = distribute_cfs_runtime(cfs_b, runtime);']}
description: kernel/sched/fair.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.9, when cpu.cfs_quota_us is used (e.g., with Kubernetes), allows attackers to cause a denial of service against non-cpu-bound applications by generating a workload that triggers unwanted slice expiration, aka CID-de53fd7aedb1. (In other words, although this slice expiration would typically be seen with benign workloads, it is possible that an attacker could calculate how many stray requests are required to force an entire Kubernetes cluster into a low-performance state caused by slice expiration, and ensure that a DDoS attack sent that number of stray requests. An attack does not affect the stability of the kernel; it only causes mismanagement of application execution.)

code_evidence: The function captures a snapshot of cfs_b->runtime_expires into a local variable (line 17) and passes it, along with the distributed runtime, into distribute_cfs_runtime (lines 22-23). The local snapshot is the per-period expiration deadline used to bound how long runtime slices remain valid; tying distribution to this snapshot is the mechanism that lets unused per-CPU slices expire at the period boundary.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The code fails to maintain the limited CPU-bandwidth resource across period boundaries: it enforces an expiration that discards allocated-but-unused quota, so the resource cannot be fully used and the workload is throttled. That is improper control of a limited resource's allocation/maintenance, fitting CWE-400; the consequence is availability degradation rather than memory corruption.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: per-CPU runtime slices are granted an expiration deadline equal to cfs_b->runtime_expires, so any slice not consumed within the period is reclaimed rather than carried forward. Trigger: a non-CPU-bound, highly-threaded workload under cpu.cfs_quota_us that cannot consume its per-CPU slice before the deadline. Consequence: the runqueue is throttled while quota remains unused, degrading availability of the constrained application (supported DoS/resource-mismanagement impact).

description: GPAC 0.7.1 has a buffer overflow issue in gf_import_message() in media_import.c.

joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes past the end of the intended buffer (szMsg), matching CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write. It is not merely a format-string issue (CWE-134), since the format is variadic and the defect is the missing output length constraint.

char szMsg[1024];
vsprintf(szMsg, format, args);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: an unbounded formatting function targets a fixed-size stack buffer. Trigger: a call whose formatted message exceeds 1024 bytes. Consequence: out-of-bounds stack write, corrupting adjacent memory and potentially enabling code execution or a crash.

commit_msg:
The current CIPSO and CALIPSO refcounting scheme for the DOI
definitions is a bit flawed in that we:

1. Don't correctly match gets/puts in netlbl_cipsov4_list().
2. Decrement the refcount on each attempt to remove the DOI from the
   DOI list, only removing it from the list once the refcount drops
   to zero.

This patch fixes these problems by adding the missing "puts" to
netlbl_cipsov4_list() and introduces a more conventional, i.e.
not-buggy, refcounting mechanism to the DOI definitions.  Upon the
addition of a DOI to the DOI list, it is initialized with a refcount
of one, removing a DOI from the list removes it from the list and
drops the refcount by one; "gets" and "puts" behave as expected with
respect to refcounts, increasing and decreasing the DOI's refcount by
one.

description: The Linux kernel before 5.11.14 has a use-after-free in cipso_v4_genopt in net/ipv4/cipso_ipv4.c because the CIPSO and CALIPSO refcounting for the DOI definitions is mishandled, aka CID-ad5d07f4a9cd. This leads to writing an arbitrary value.

code_evidence: rcu_read_lock() is taken and doi_def is obtained via cipso_v4_doi_getdef(doi), which takes a reference; on success the normal path at line 120 only does rcu_read_unlock() without releasing the DOI reference.
The list_retry and list_failure_lock error paths also unlock RCU and free/retry without dropping the DOI reference obtained at line 30.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-416 fits because the mishandled refcount allows the DOI definition memory to be freed while still reachable, and later use of the dangling doi_def pointer constitutes a use-after-free. This is a reference-counting lifetime bug rather than a simple memory leak, since the freed object is subsequently accessed.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function acquires a reference to the DOI definition via cipso_v4_doi_getdef() but never balances it with cipso_v4_doi_putdef() on the success or error paths. This leaks a reference, so when the DOI is later removed from the list and its refcount is decremented, the object is not freed at the expected time or is freed while still referenced, leading to a use-after-free when cipso_v4_genopt subsequently dereferences the DOI definition.

description: A remote code execution vulnerability in FLACExtractor.cpp in libstagefright in Mediaserver could enable an attacker using a specially crafted file to cause memory corruption during media file and data processing. This issue is rated as Critical due to the possibility of remote code execution within the context of the Mediaserver process. Product: Android. Versions: 4.4.4, 5.0.2, 5.1.1, 6.0, 6.0.1, 7.0, 7.1.1, 7.1.2. Android ID: A-34970788.

code_evidence: The function signature takes src as an unbounded pointer-to-pointer (const int *const *src), and line 5 dereferences src[c][i] inside a loop bounded only by nChannels and nSamples, with no check that nChannels is within the allocated channel-array size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the code performs a buffer index operation (src[c][i]) without restricting c to the buffer's intended boundary, allowing reads outside the channel-pointer array. The patch adds a fixed [kMaxChannels] bound, confirming the missing bound is the weakness.

evidence_lines.code:

*dst++ = src[c][i];

commit_msg:
rsvg: Add rsvg_acquire_node()

This function does proper recursion checks when looking up resources
from URLs and thereby helps avoiding infinite loops when cyclic
references span multiple types of elements.

description: librsvg before 2.40.12 allows context-dependent attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop, stack consumption, and application crash) via cyclic references in an SVG document.

code_evidence: The free function releases drawsub_stack and ptrs but performs no validation of recursive resource references before teardown.
It unconditionally frees handle after releasing members, with no guard against a cyclic reference graph that caused unbounded recursion before this point.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-20 fits because the weakness is failure to validate that referenced resources do not form cycles before processing them, allowing unsafe input to reach recursion. This is improper input validation of reference consistency rather than a memory-corruption flaw.

evidence_lines.code:
g_slist_free (handle->drawsub_stack);
g_slist_free (handle->ptrs);
g_free (handle);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is the absence of recursion/cycle validation when resources are resolved through URLs; cyclic SVG references drive repeated traversal, causing infinite loop and stack consumption that crashes the application. Fixed OOB read in ntlm_av_pair_get

commit_msg:
f2fs: fix potential panic during fstrim

As Ju Hyung Park reported:

"When 'fstrim' is called for manual trim, a BUG() can be triggered
randomly with this patch.

I'm seeing this issue on both x86 Desktop and arm64 Android phone.

On x86 Desktop, this was caused during Ubuntu boot-up. I have a
cronjob installed which calls 'fstrim -v /' during boot. On arm64
Android, this was caused during GC looping with 1ms gc_min_sleep_time
& gc_max_sleep_time."

Root cause of this issue is that f2fs_wait_discard_bios can only be
used by f2fs_put_super, because during put_super there must be no
other referrers, so it can ignore discard entry's reference count
when removing the entry, otherwise in other caller we will hit bug_on
in __remove_discard_cmd as there may be other issuer added reference
count in discard entry.

Thread A				Thread B
					- issue_discard_thread
- f2fs_ioc_fitrim
 - f2fs_trim_fs
  - f2fs_wait_discard_bios
   - __issue_discard_cmd
    - __submit_discard_cmd
					 - __wait_discard_cmd
					  - dc->ref++
					  - __wait_one_discard_bio
   - __wait_discard_cmd
    - __remove_discard_cmd
     - f2fs_bug_on(sbi, dc->ref)

Fixes: 969d1b180d987c2be02de890d0fff0f66a0e80de
Reported-by: Ju Hyung Park <qkrwngud825@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Chao Yu <yuchao0@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Jaegeuk Kim <jaegeuk@kernel.org>

description: The f2fs implementation in the Linux kernel before 4.14 mishandles reference counts associated with f2fs_wait_discard_bios calls, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (BUG), as demonstrated by fstrim.

commit_msg:
Bug 689699: Avoid buffer overrun.

When cleaning a pdf file, various lists (of pdf_xref_len length) are
defined early on.

If we trigger a repair during the clean, this can cause pdf_xref_len
to increase causing an overrun.

Fix this by watching for changes in the length, and checking accesses
to the list for validity.

This also appears to fix bugs 698700-698703.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\topts->use_list = fz_malloc_array(ctx, xref_len + 3, sizeof(int));', '\topts->ofs_list = fz_malloc_array(ctx, xref_len + 3, sizeof(int64_t));', '\topts->gen_list = fz_calloc(ctx, xref_len + 3, sizeof(int));', '\topts->renumber_map = fz_malloc_array(ctx, xref_len + 3, sizeof(int));', '\topts->rev_renumber_map = fz_malloc_array(ctx, xref_len + 3, sizeof(int));', '\tfor (num = 0; num < xref_len; num++)', '\t{', '\t\topts->use_list[num] = 0;', '\t\topts->ofs_list[num] = 0;', '\t\topts->renumber_map[num] = num;', '\t\topts->rev_renumber_map[num] = num;', '\t}'], 'added_lines': ['\topts->list_len = 0;', '\topts->use_list = NULL;', '\topts->ofs_list = NULL;', '\topts->gen_list = NULL;', '\topts->renumber_map = NULL;', '\topts->rev_renumber_map = NULL;', '\texpand_lists(ctx, opts, xref_len + 3);']}
description: pdf/pdf-write.c in Artifex MuPDF before 1.12.0 mishandles certain length changes when a repair operation occurs during a clean operation, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted PDF document.

code_evidence: Line 4 reads xref_len once; lines 17-21 allocate five parallel arrays sized xref_len+3 based on that snapshot.
Lines 24-30 then iterate num < xref_len and write use_list, ofs_list, renumber_map and rev_renumber_map using the same snapshot length, with no re-check of pdf_xref_len.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function establishes fixed-size heap buffers and then performs indexed writes into them under an assumption of a stable length, directly matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds buffer operation. The fix confirms this by replacing fixed allocation with expand_lists and a tracked list_len, guarding accesses against length changes.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The arrays are sized and indexed from a single xref_len value captured at entry. If a repair during the clean operation grows the document's xref length, later accesses in this write-state machinery use indices beyond the originally allocated buffers, causing an out-of-bounds read/write and crash. The cause is the missing length-change/validity check; the supported consequence is memory corruption/denial of service.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    AP4_Atom(AP4_ATOM_TYPE_STCO, size, version, flags)'], 'added_lines': ['    AP4_Atom(AP4_ATOM_TYPE_STCO, size, version, flags),', '    m_EntryCount(0)', '    if (size < AP4_FULL_ATOM_HEADER_SIZE+4) {', '        return;', '    }']}
description: An issue was discovered in Bento4 1.5.1-627. The AP4_StcoAtom class in Core/Ap4StcoAtom.cpp has an attempted excessive memory allocation when called from AP4_AtomFactory::CreateAtomFromStream in Core/Ap4AtomFactory.cpp, as demonstrated by mp42hls.

code_evidence: m_EntryCount is read directly from the stream with no check that size is large enough to contain the 4-byte count plus entries; the clamp at line 8 computes (size-AP4_FULL_ATOM_HEADER_SIZE-4)/4 using unsigned arithmetic, so a size smaller than the header+4 underflows to a huge value and the comparison fails to constrain m_EntryCount.
m_Entries and buffer are then allocated with m_EntryCount and m_EntryCount*4 based on this attacker-controlled, effectively unbounded count.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates arrays sized by an unvalidated field from attacker-controlled input, matching CWE-770's missing restriction on resource allocation. It is not a simple integer overflow because the allocation size derives directly from the unchecked count; the fix adds a size floor and initializes the count.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the entry count taken from the untrusted stco atom is used to size heap allocations without validating the declared atom size against the header minimum, and the unsigned size subtraction underflows. Trigger: a crafted MP4 atom with a small size field but a large entry count. Consequence: attempted excessive memory allocation, leading to memory-exhaustion denial of service.

commit_msg:
If sctp_destroy_sock is called without sock_net(sk)->sctp.addr_wq_lock
held and sp->do_auto_asconf is true, then an element is removed
from the auto_asconf_splist without any proper locking.

This can happen in the following functions:
1. In sctp_accept, if sctp_sock_migrate fails.
2. In inet_create or inet6_create, if there is a bpf program
   attached to BPF_CGROUP_INET_SOCK_CREATE which denies
   creation of the sctp socket.

The bug is fixed by acquiring addr_wq_lock in sctp_destroy_sock
instead of sctp_close.

This addresses CVE-2021-23133.

Reported-by: Or Cohen <orcohen@paloaltonetworks.com>
Reviewed-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Fixes: 610236587600 ("bpf: Add new cgroup attach type to enable sock modifications")
Signed-off-by: Or Cohen <orcohen@paloaltonetworks.com>
Acked-by: Marcelo Ricardo Leitner <marcelo.leitner@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\t\tspin_lock_bh(&sock_net(sk)->sctp.addr_wq_lock);', '\t\tspin_unlock_bh(&sock_net(sk)->sctp.addr_wq_lock);']}
description: A race condition in Linux kernel SCTP sockets (net/sctp/socket.c) before 5.12-rc8 can lead to kernel privilege escalation from the context of a network service or an unprivileged process. If sctp_destroy_sock is called without sock_net(sk)->sctp.addr_wq_lock then an element is removed from the auto_asconf_splist list without any proper locking. This can be exploited by an attacker with network service privileges to escalate to root or from the context of an unprivileged user directly if a BPF_CGROUP_INET_SOCK_CREATE is attached which denies creation of some SCTP socket.

code_evidence: In sctp_destroy_sock, when sp->do_auto_asconf is true the code clears the flag and calls list_del(&sp->auto_asconf_list) on the shared auto_asconf_splist without holding sock_net(sk)->sctp.addr_wq_lock, so the list mutation is not serialized against other users of the same list.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function mutates a shared list without exclusive access, allowing an interfering concurrent sequence to modify the same resource; this is exactly improper synchronization in a concurrent sequence (CWE-362), rather than a memory-safety bug in the list API itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the removal of the socket's node from the shared auto_asconf_splist is performed without the addr_wq_lock that other code paths use. Trigger: sctp_destroy_sock runs with do_auto_asconf set, e.g. via sctp_accept failure or a bpf cgroup hook denying socket creation, concurrently with another list operation. Consequence: concurrent list modification corrupts the list, enabling a race with security impact (privilege escalation).

commit_msg:
As part of CVE-2013-4288, the D-Bus clients were allowed (and
encouraged) to submit the UID of the subject of authorization checks
to avoid races against UID changes (notably using executables
set-UID to root).

However, that also allowed any client to submit an arbitrary UID, and
that could be used to bypass "can only ask about / affect the same UID"
checks in CheckAuthorization / RegisterAuthenticationAgent /
UnregisterAuthenticationAgent.  This allowed an attacker:

- With CheckAuthorization, to cause the registered authentication
  agent in victim's session to pop up a dialog, or to determine whether
  the victim currently has a temporary authorization to perform an
  operation.

  (In principle, the attacker can also determine whether JavaScript
  rules allow the victim process to perform an operation; however,
  usually rules base their decisions on information determined from
  the supplied UID, so the attacker usually won't learn anything new.)

- With RegisterAuthenticationAgent, to prevent the victim's
  authentication agent to work (for a specific victim process),
  or to learn about which operations requiring authorization
  the victim is attempting.

To fix this, expose internal _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() /
obsolete polkit_unix_process_get_owner() as a private
polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__() (being more explicit about the
dangers on relying on it), and use it in
polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() to return
a boolean indicating whether the subject UID may be caller-chosen.

Then, in the permission checks that require the subject to be
equal to the caller, fail on caller-chosen UIDs (and continue
through the pre-existing code paths which allow root, or root-designated
server processes, to ask about arbitrary subjects.)

Signed-off-by: Miloslav Trmač <mitr@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  guint32 uid;', '      uid = polkit_unix_process_get_uid (POLKIT_UNIX_PROCESS (subject));', '      if ((gint) uid == -1)', '      ret = polkit_unix_user_new (uid);'], 'added_lines': ['                                                     gboolean                     *result_matches,', '  gboolean matches;', '  matches = FALSE;', '      gint subject_uid, current_uid;', '      GError *local_error;', '', '      subject_uid = polkit_unix_process_get_uid (POLKIT_UNIX_PROCESS (subject));', '      if (subject_uid == -1)', '      local_error = NULL;', '      current_uid = polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__ (POLKIT_UNIX_PROCESS (subject), &local_error);', '      if (local_error != NULL)', '\t{', '\t  g_propagate_error (error, local_error);', '\t  goto out;', '\t}', '      ret = polkit_unix_user_new (subject_uid);', '      matches = (subject_uid == current_uid);', '      matches = TRUE;', '      uid_t uid;', '      matches = TRUE;', '  if (result_matches != NULL)', '    {', '      *result_matches = matches;', '    }']}
description: A flaw was found in polkit before version 0.116. The implementation of the polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization function in polkitd allows to test for authentication and trigger authentication of unrelated processes owned by other users. This may result in a local DoS and information disclosure.

code_evidence: For a Unix-process subject, the function derives the identity solely from the client-supplied subject via polkit_unix_process_get_uid and immediately builds a PolkitIdentity with polkit_unix_user_new(uid). No check verifies that this UID corresponds to the caller's actual process owner or that the caller is privileged; the function returns the caller-chosen identity as authoritative.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-862 fits because the function returns an authorization-relevant identity without any check that the caller may act for that subject, i.e., a missing authorization check. It is not merely an input-validation issue: the defect is the absence of an ownership/privilege check on the subject before it is used for authorization decisions.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the function treats the UID embedded in a client-supplied PolkitSubject as trusted and returns it without verifying it matches the real process owner or caller. Trigger: an attacker submits a Unix-process subject naming another user's UID. Consequence: downstream authorization checks operate on an attacker-chosen identity, enabling information disclosure and DoS against other users' sessions.

commit_msg:
TROVE-2017-005: Fix assertion failure in connection_edge_process_relay_cell

On an hidden service rendezvous circuit, a BEGIN_DIR could be sent
(maliciously) which would trigger a tor_assert() because
connection_edge_process_relay_cell() thought that the circuit is an
or_circuit_t but is an origin circuit in reality.

Fixes #22494

Reported-by: Roger Dingledine <arma@torproject.org>
Signed-off-by: David Goulet <dgoulet@torproject.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      if (rh.command == RELAY_COMMAND_BEGIN_DIR) {'], 'added_lines': ['      if (rh.command == RELAY_COMMAND_BEGIN_DIR &&', '          circ->purpose != CIRCUIT_PURPOSE_S_REND_JOINED) {']}
description: The hidden-service feature in Tor before 0.3.0.8 allows a denial of service (assertion failure and daemon exit) in the connection_edge_process_relay_cell function via a BEGIN_DIR cell on a rendezvous circuit.

code_evidence: BEGIN_DIR is handled alongside BEGIN; when layer_hint is set and purpose is not S_REND_JOINED, the cell is dropped, but on a rendezvous circuit (purpose S_REND_JOINED) execution continues past this guard.
The second guard only rejects BEGIN when layer_hint != cpath->prev; a malicious BEGIN_DIR from the final hop passes through.
With no conn attached, the BEGIN_DIR branch assigns circ->dirreq_id and then dereferences TO_OR_CIRCUIT(circ)->p_chan, assuming circ is an or_circuit_t.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe TO_OR_CIRCUIT macro performs a tor_assert on the circuit type; attacker-controlled cell input on a rendezvous circuit reaches it, causing a reachable assertion and process exit, matching CWE-617. This is not merely a type-confusion memory error because the supported consequence is the assertion-triggered crash.

Trigger: an attacker sends a BEGIN_DIR cell with stream_id 0 on an S_REND_JOINED circuit, bypassing the purpose/layer checks. Consequence: the TO_OR_CIRCUIT assertion fails, aborting the daemon (DoS).

Fixes: 1519/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-5286680976162816

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/targets/ffmpeg

description: libavcodec/scpr.c in FFmpeg 3.3 before 3.3.1 does not properly validate height and width data, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted file.

code_evidence: The second loop scans c from x*16 up to 255, incrementing c on each iteration; if the accumulated frequency never exceeds value, the loop terminates with c == 256.

Line 30 then writes pixel->freq[c] = cnt_c + step, indexing the 256-element freq array at index 256, which is out of bounds. Line 31 similarly writes pixel->lookup[x] where x can reach 16, out of bounds for the 16-element lookup array.

pixel->lookup[x] = cnt_x + step;

Trigger: a crafted range-coded value that causes both loops to run to completion (x==16, c==256). commit_msg:
Better handling of truncated data when reading strings

Summary:
Currently we read string size and blindly pre-allocate it. This allows malicious attacker to send a few bytes message and cause server to allocate huge amount of memory (>1GB).

This diff changes the logic to check if we have enough data in the buffer before allocating the string.

This is a second part of a fix for CVE-2019-3553.

Reviewed By: vitaut

Differential Revision: D14393393

fbshipit-source-id: e2046d2f5b087d3abc9a9d2c6c107cf088673057
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (!in_.canAdvance(size)) {', '      protocol::TProtocolException::throwTruncatedData();', '    }']}
description: C++ Facebook Thrift servers would not error upon receiving messages declaring containers of sizes larger than the payload. As a result, malicious clients could send short messages which would result in a large memory allocation, potentially leading to denial of service. This issue affects Facebook Thrift prior to v2020.02.03.00.

code_evidence: When the incoming buffer length is smaller than the declared string size, the function reserves `size` bytes before any data is confirmed available, letting an attacker-supplied size drive a large upfront allocation.
The loop then consumes data via `peekBytes`; if no data remains it throws, but this happens only after the reservation, so the allocation is already made based on the unvalidated size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function allocates memory sized by an attacker-controlled value without a bound tied to actual available data, matching CWE-770's resource allocation without limits. This is the allocation cause, distinct from the later truncation check that only fires after reserving.

evidence_lines.code:
if (static_cast<int32_t>(in_.length()) < size) {
str.reserve(size);   }

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the declared string size is used to reserve memory without verifying the buffer can supply that many bytes. Trigger: a malicious client sends a short message declaring a very large string size. Consequence: an oversized memory allocation occurs, enabling memory-exhaustion denial of service.
