description:
TimescaleDB, an open-source time-series SQL database, has a privilege escalation vulnerability in versions 2.8.0 through 2.9.2. During installation, TimescaleDB creates a telemetry job that is runs as the installation user. The queries run as part of the telemetry data collection were not run with a locked down `search_path`, allowing malicious users to create functions that would be executed by the telemetry job, leading to privilege escalation. In order to be able to take advantage of this vulnerability, a user would need to be able to create objects in a database and then get a superuser to install TimescaleDB into their database. When TimescaleDB is installed as trusted extension, non-superusers can install the extension without help from a superuser.

Version 2.9.3 fixes this issue. As a mitigation, the `search_path` of the user running the telemetry job can be locked down to not include schemas writable by other users. The vulnerability is not exploitable on instances in Timescale Cloud and Managed Service for TimescaleDB due to additional security provisions in place on those platforms.

code_evidence: appendStringInfo builds a SQL statement that calls the unqualified max() aggregate while interpolating the hypertable's schema and table names via quote_identifier; the aggregate name is not schema-qualified.
The constructed command is executed through SPI_execute, which resolves unqualified function names against the caller's search_path.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unqualified aggregate lets an attacker-supplied function run under the privileged telemetry job's context, i.e. improper privilege management allowing an unintended sphere of control. This is the privilege-escalation root cause; CWE-269 fits as the target rather than a mere impact label.

evidence_lines.code:
appendStringInfo(command,
"SELECT max(%s) FROM %s.%s",
quote_identifier(NameStr(dim->fd.column_name)),
quote_identifier(NameStr(ht->fd.schema_name)),
quote_identifier(NameStr(ht->fd.table_name)));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the telemetry query invokes max() without a schema-qualified name, so resolution depends on the current search_path. Trigger: a user who can create objects in a schema on the search_path defines a malicious max() function, which the telemetry job (running as the installation/superuser) then executes; consequence is privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Fix leak with ASN.1 combine.

When parsing a combined structure pass a flag to the decode routine
so on error a pointer to the parent structure is not zeroed as
this will leak any additional components in the parent.

This can leak memory in any application parsing PKCS#7 or CMS structures.

CVE-2015-3195.

Thanks to Adam Langley (Google/BoringSSL) for discovering this bug using
libFuzzer.

PR#4131

Reviewed-by: Richard Levitte <levitte@openssl.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    ASN1_item_ex_free(pval, it);'], 'added_lines': ['    int combine = aclass & ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE;', '    aclass &= ~ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE;', '    if (combine == 0)', '        ASN1_item_ex_free(pval, it);']}
description: The ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE implementation in crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c in OpenSSL before 0.9.8zh, 1.0.0 before 1.0.0t, 1.0.1 before 1.0.1q, and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2e mishandles errors caused by malformed X509_ATTRIBUTE data, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory by triggering a decoding failure in a PKCS#7 or CMS application.

commit_msg:
HID: elo: fix memory leak in elo_probe

When hid_parse() in elo_probe() fails, it forgets to call usb_put_dev to
decrease the refcount.

Fix this by adding usb_put_dev() in the error handling code of elo_probe().

Fixes: fbf42729d0e9 ("HID: elo: update the reference count of the usb device structure")
Reported-by: syzkaller <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Signed-off-by: Dongliang Mu <mudongliangabcd@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['\tusb_put_dev(udev);']}
description: In drivers/hid/hid-elo.c in the Linux kernel before 5.16.11, a memory leak exists for a certain hid_parse error condition.

code_evidence: Line 13 acquires a reference on the USB device via usb_get_dev(udev) and stores it in priv->usbdev. Lines 15-18 detect hid_parse failure and jump to err_free; the err_free block at lines 30-32 frees only priv and returns, never calling usb_put_dev on the acquired reference.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because an acquired resource reference is not released on an error path, so the referenced memory remains unavailable for reuse. This is a missing release of a held reference rather than a use-after-free, since no pointer is later dereferenced after release.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the error path for a failed hid_parse releases the allocated priv but not the USB device reference taken by usb_get_dev. Trigger: hid_parse returns nonzero, routing execution to err_free. Consequence: the usb_device refcount is never decremented, leaking the device structure on each such failure.

commit_msg:
Jan Kara's analysis of the syzbot report (edited):

  The reproducer opens a directory on FUSE filesystem, it then attaches
  dnotify mark to the open directory.  After that a fuse_do_getattr() call
  finds that attributes returned by the server are inconsistent, and calls
  make_bad_inode() which, among other things does:

          inode->i_mode = S_IFREG;

  This then confuses dnotify which doesn't tear down its structures
  properly and eventually crashes.

Avoid calling make_bad_inode() on a live inode: switch to a private flag on
the fuse inode.  Also add the test to ops which the bad_inode_ops would
have caught.

This bug goes back to the initial merge of fuse in 2.6.14...

Reported-by: syzbot+f427adf9324b92652ccc@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (fuse_is_bad(inode))', '\t\treturn -EIO;']}
description: An issue was discovered in the FUSE filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 5.10.6, aka CID-5d069dbe8aaf. fuse_do_getattr() calls make_bad_inode() in inappropriate situations, causing a system crash. NOTE: the original fix for this vulnerability was incomplete, and its incompleteness is tracked as CVE-2021-28950.

code_evidence: The function proceeds directly to generic_file_open and fuse_do_open without checking whether the inode has been marked bad; the patch adds a fuse_is_bad(inode) guard returning -EIO before line 11.
On success, fuse_finish_open at line 26 installs state (e.g., dnotify/lease-related structures) on the inode without verifying its validity.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-459 fits because the weakness is failure to clean up/handle invalidated inode state: the open path lacks the fuse_is_bad check, allowing structures to be established against a bad inode without proper release, matching incomplete cleanup rather than a memory-safety flaw.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: fuse_open_common does not reject an inode that fuse_do_getattr() previously invalidated via make_bad_inode(), so open continues on a live but inconsistent inode. Trigger: opening a directory whose server returns inconsistent attributes. Consequence: supporting dnotify structures are set up but not torn down properly, leading to a crash.

commit_msg:
netfilter: x_tables: check for size overflow

Ben Hawkes says:
 integer overflow in xt_alloc_table_info, which on 32-bit systems can
 lead to small structure allocation and a copy_from_user based heap
 corruption.

Reported-by: Ben Hawkes <hawkes@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\tif (sz < sizeof(*info))', '\t\treturn NULL;']}
description: Integer overflow in the xt_alloc_table_info function in net/netfilter/x_tables.c in the Linux kernel through 4.5.2 on 32-bit platforms allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (heap memory corruption) via an IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt call.

code_evidence: sz is computed as sizeof(*info) + size with size an unsigned int; on 32-bit systems the addition can wrap, yielding a small sz.
The only bound check compares the page count derived from size against totalram_pages; it does not validate sz, so a wrapped small sz proceeds to kmalloc/vmalloc.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function performs an unchecked numeric addition whose overflow produces an undersized allocation, matching numeric error/overflow weaknesses (CWE-189). The consequence is heap corruption rather than merely a logic error.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the allocation size sz = sizeof(*info) + size is computed without overflow checking, so a large attacker-supplied size wraps to a small value on 32-bit platforms. Trigger: a local user passes an oversized table size via IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE. The small allocation is then filled with the caller's larger data, causing heap corruption.

commit_msg:
tools/xenstore: fix checking node permissions

Today chk_domain_generation() is being used to check whether a node
permission entry is still valid or whether it is referring to a domain
no longer existing. This is done by comparing the node's and the
domain's generation count.

In case no struct domain is existing for a checked domain, but the
domain itself is valid, chk_domain_generation() assumes it is being
called due to the first node created for a new domain and it will
return success.

This might be wrong in case the checked permission is related to an
old domain, which has just been replaced with a new domain using the
same domid.

Fix that by letting chk_domain_generation() fail in case a struct
domain isn't found. In order to cover the case of the first node for
a new domain try to allocate the needed struct domain explicitly when
processing the related SET_PERMS command. In case a referenced domain
isn't existing, flag the related permission to be ignored right away.

This is XSA-417 / CVE-2022-42320.

Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (ret < 0)', '\t\treturn errno;', '\t\tif (ret < 0)', '\t\t\treturn errno;'], 'added_lines': []}
description: Xenstore: Guests can get access to Xenstore nodes of deleted domains Access rights of Xenstore nodes are per domid. When a domain is gone, there might be Xenstore nodes left with access rights containing the domid of the removed domain. This is normally no problem, as those access right entries will be corrected when such a node is written later. There is a small time window when a new domain is created, where the access rights of a past domain with the same domid as the new one will be regarded to be still valid, leading to the new domain being able to get access to a node which was meant to be accessible by the removed domain. For this to happen another domain needs to write the node before the newly created domain is being introduced to Xenstore by dom0.

joint-evidence.rejection_reason: The function handles permission-entry validation and stale domid access rights, not failure to clean up temporary or supporting resources; the removed errno checks relate to generation validation, not incomplete cleanup.

commit_msg:
gvariant: Don’t allow child elements to overlap with each other

If different elements of a variable sized array can overlap with each
other then we can cause a `GVariant` to normalise to a much larger type.

This commit changes the behaviour of `GVariant` with non-normal form data. If
an invalid frame offset is found all subsequent elements are given their
default value.

When retrieving an element at index `n` we scan the frame offsets up to index
`n` and if they are not in order we return an element with the default value
for that type.  This guarantees that elements don't overlap with each
other.  We remember the offset we've scanned up to so we don't need to
repeat this work on subsequent accesses.  We skip these checks for trusted
data.

Unfortunately this makes random access of untrusted data O(n) — at least
on first access.  It doesn't affect the algorithmic complexity of accessing
elements in order, such as when using the `GVariantIter` interface.  Also:
the cost of validation will be amortised as the `GVariant` instance is
continued to be used.

I've implemented this with 4 different functions, 1 for each element size,
rather than looping calling `gvs_read_unaligned_le` in the hope that the
compiler will find it easy to optimise and should produce fairly tight
code.

Fixes: #2121
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  value.ordered_offsets_up_to = 0;']}
description: A flaw was found in GLib. GVariant deserialization is vulnerable to an exponential blowup issue where a crafted GVariant can cause excessive processing, leading to denial of service.

code_evidence: The function validates a serialised maybe value from untrusted data: it checks size==0, requires a trailing NUL byte (lines 4-7), then unwraps the element type and decrements size before recursing into g_variant_serialised_is_normal (lines 8-11). The patch adds resetting ordered_offsets_up_to=0 at line 10, so the recursion re-validates frame offsets rather than trusting stale ordering state. Without this reset, overlapping child elements in non-normal form data could pass the normality check.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function is part of deserializing untrusted GVariant data and its validation of the resulting structure was insufficient, matching CWE-502. The fix adds a constraint (resetting offset-ordering state) during deserialization rather than a generic memory-safety flaw, so CWE-502 fits the root cause and DoS consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the recursive deserialization validation reused ordering state (ordered_offsets_up_to) across nested element types, so overlapping variable-sized array elements were not re-checked. Trigger: crafted untrusted GVariant bytes with out-of-order frame offsets. Consequence: the data normalises to a much larger type, causing exponential resource consumption and denial of service.

description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. The implementation of `tf.raw_ops.MaxPoolGradWithArgmax` can cause reads outside of bounds of heap allocated data if attacker supplies specially crafted inputs. The implementation(https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/31bd5026304677faa8a0b77602c6154171b9aec1/tensorflow/core/kernels/image/draw_bounding_box_op.cc#L116-L130) assumes that the last element of `boxes` input is 4, as required by [the op](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/DrawBoundingBoxesV2). Since this is not checked attackers passing values less than 4 can write outside of bounds of heap allocated objects and cause memory corruption. If the last dimension in `boxes` is less than 4, accesses similar to `tboxes(b, bb, 3)` will access data outside of bounds. Further during code execution there are also writes to these indices. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.5.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.4.2, TensorFlow 2.3.3, TensorFlow 2.2.3 and TensorFlow 2.1.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Input tensor `boxes` is only checked for rank 3 (line 8); the size of its last dimension is never constrained before `boxes.tensor<T, 3>()` is bound at line 53.
The box coordinate reads `tboxes(b, bb, 0..3)` at lines 57, 60, 64, 67 assume the last dimension has at least four elements.
The clamped box bounds are then used to index `canvas(b, row, col, c)` and write color values at lines 120-121, 127-128, 134-135 and 141-142.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing dimension check lets attacker-controlled indices write past the end of the allocated output buffer, which is precisely an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). A related out-of-bounds read also occurs, but the write into `canvas` is the direct memory-corruption consequence of the unchecked box width.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the kernel accepts a `boxes` tensor whose third dimension is less than 4 without validating it, while downstream coordinate reads and canvas writes assume four components per box. Trigger: an attacker supplies a `boxes` input with last dimension < 4, causing `tboxes(b, bb, 3)` to read past the tensor and the derived indices to drive out-of-bounds writes into the heap-allocated canvas. Supported consequence: heap memory corruption, including potential crash or code execution.

This commit enforces strict invariant on ASS_Outline
to contain point coordinates into predetermined range.

Fixes https://github.com/libass/libass/issues/431.

commit_msg:
journalctl: verify sealed log epochs are continuous

Currently empty epochs are not sealed. This allows an attacker to truncate
a sealed log and continue it without any problems showing when verifying the
log.

This partially addresses CVE-2023-31438. One way to extend this change to
address CVE-2023-31438 completely, would be to verify that there is exactly
one seal per epoch (and not sealing when the epoch has not ended yet).

the change also adds a journal-file flag: HEADER_COMPATIBLE_SEALED_CONTINUOUS
this flag indicates that a journal file is sealed continuously and decides whether
any missing crypto epochs should trigger a warning or an error.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['                if (epoch < goal) {', '                        r = journal_file_append_tag(f);', '                        if (r < 0)', '                                return r;', '                }']}
description: An issue was discovered in systemd 253. An attacker can truncate a sealed log file and then resume log sealing such that checking the integrity shows no error, despite modifications. NOTE: the vendor reportedly sent "a reply denying that any of the finding was a security vulnerability."

code_evidence: The loop advances the FSPRG state with FSPRG_Evolve and reads the resulting epoch, but the only acceptance test is epoch == goal; there is no check that each intermediate epoch was actually sealed. A truncated and resealed log can therefore present a later goal epoch without the intervening epochs, and the function returns 0 at line 17 as if the chain were continuous.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-354 fits because the integrity verification of the sealed log (the FSPRG epoch chain) is incomplete: intermediate integrity check values are not validated. This is distinct from a mere off-by-one, since the missing constraint is validation of the check values themselves.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the seal-chain continuity check compares only the final epoch, not the intermediate sealed epochs. Trigger: an attacker truncates a sealed journal and resumes sealing at a later epoch. Consequence: journal_file_fsprg_evolve succeeds and integrity verification reports no error despite the removed epochs.

commit_msg:
Create a context more than once causes memory leak issue.
Juest return if the context exists.

Signed-off-by: Li Qiang <liq3ea@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['      return;', '', '   dctx = dec_ctx[handle];', '   if (dctx)']}
description: Memory leak in the vrend_renderer_context_create_internal function in vrend_decode.c in virglrenderer before 0.6.0 allows local guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host memory consumption) by repeatedly creating a decode context.

code_evidence: Only the handle bound is checked; no check whether dec_ctx[handle] already holds an allocated context, so repeated calls proceed to allocate again.
A fresh struct vrend_decode_ctx is malloc'd and the code returns only on allocation failure, not on an existing context.
The newly allocated dctx (with its grctx and ds) is stored into dec_ctx[handle], overwriting the previous pointer without freeing it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function leaks an allocated resource by overwriting the only reference to the previous context, matching CWE-399 resource-management errors (specifically the memory-leak pattern). The issue is resource mismanagement, not an out-of-bounds write from the handle check.

if (handle >= VREND_MAX_CTX)
return;

dctx->ds = &dctx->ids;
dec_ctx[handle] = dctx;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the create function lacks an idempotency/existence check for dec_ctx[handle] and unconditionally overwrites the slot with a new malloc'd context. Trigger: a local guest repeatedly invokes context creation with the same handle. Consequence: each prior vrend_decode_ctx (and its grctx) becomes unreachable, consuming host memory until denial of service.

commit_msg:
If the device node of dvb_frontend is open() and the device is
disconnected, many kinds of UAFs may occur when calling close()
on the device node.

The root cause of this is that wake_up() for dvbdev->wait_queue
is implemented in the dvb_frontend_release() function, but
wait_event() is not implemented in the dvb_frontend_stop() function.

So, implement wait_event() function in dvb_frontend_stop() and
add 'remove_mutex' which prevents race condition for 'fe->exit'.

[mchehab: fix a couple of checkpatch warnings and some mistakes at the error handling logic]

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-media/20221117045925.14297-2-imv4bel@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@kernel.org>

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 6.0.9. drivers/media/dvb-core/dvb_frontend.c has a race condition that can cause a use-after-free when a device is disconnected.

code_evidence: After dvb_generic_release, the function checks dvbdev->users == -1 and wakes fepriv->wait_queue; the exit state and wait_queue signaling happen without any lock protecting fe->exit against concurrent teardown.
The fe->exit check at line 25 followed by wake_up and ts_bus_ctrl(fe, 0) at lines 26-28 reads fe/fe->exit unsynchronized, so a concurrent disconnect path can free fe between the check and use.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unsafe check-then-use of shared fe state across concurrent close() and disconnect sequences is a classic TOCTOU race with improper synchronization, matching CWE-362; the UAF is the resulting consequence, not a separate missing-bound weakness.

if (dvbdev->users == -1) {
wake_up(&fepriv->wait_queue);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: dvb_frontend_release reads fe->exit and dereferences fe->ops without synchronization, while the disconnect/stop path does not wait for this release sequence. Trigger: a userspace close() races with device disconnection. Consequence: use-after-free of the dvb_frontend state, leading to memory corruption or crash.

commit_msg:
Fixed bug: barriers cannot be active during sweep

Barriers cannot be active during sweep, even in generational mode.
(Although gen. mode is not incremental, it can hit a barrier when
deleting a thread and closing its upvalues.)  The colors of objects are
being changed during sweep and, therefore, cannot be trusted.

commit_msg:
Add missing validation to `maxpooling_op.cc`

PiperOrigin-RevId: 387932441
Change-Id: I43a0b24e6a12cc965611144ba035accd384594b9
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['  if (tensor_in.NumElements() == 0 || output->NumElements() == 0) return;']}
description: TensorFlow is an end-to-end open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions an attacker can trigger a denial of service via a segmentation fault in `tf.raw_ops.MaxPoolGrad` caused by missing validation. The [implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/460e000de3a83278fb00b61a16d161b1964f15f4/tensorflow/core/kernels/maxpooling_op.cc) misses some validation for the `orig_input` and `orig_output` tensors. The fixes for CVE-2021-29579 were incomplete. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit 136b51f10903e044308cf77117c0ed9871350475. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.6.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.5.1, TensorFlow 2.4.3, and TensorFlow 2.3.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Eigen maps are constructed directly from tensor_in and output using dimensions taken from params (params.depth, params.tensor_in_cols/rows/batch, params.out_width/out_height) without checking that the tensors actually contain the required number of elements.

The shard lambda then offsets out_mat.data() and out_arg_max_mat.data() by start*output_image_size and writes via coeffRef/setConstant, so a zero-sized or mismatched tensor yields out-of-bounds accesses.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-1284 fits because the code accepts size/length quantities from params and tensor shapes without validating that they satisfy required properties (non-zero, matching element counts) before using them to index and write memory; the missing check is the root cause of the out-of-bounds access.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The function trusts the quantity parameters (depth, rows/cols, batch, output dimensions) to describe the input and output tensor sizes, but never validates that tensor_in.NumElements() and output->NumElements() are consistent and non-zero. When orig_input or orig_output is empty, the Eigen maps and shard offsets address memory beyond the allocated buffers, triggering the segmentation fault (DoS).

commit_msg:
Fix #69975: PHP segfaults when accessing nvarchar(max) defined columns

The SQL Server Native Client 11.0 and maybe other ODBC drivers report
NVARCHAR(MAX) columns as SQL_WVARCHAR with size 0. This causes too small a
buffer to be emalloc'd, likely causing a segfault in the following. As we don't
know the real size of the column data, we treat such colums as
SQL_WLONGVARCHAR.

The related bug #67437 suggests that some drivers report a size of ~4GB. It is
not certain that this is really the case (there might be some integer overflow
involved, and anyway, there has been no feedback), so we do not cater for this
now. However, it would not be hard to treat all sizes above a certain threshold
in a similar way, i.e. as SQL_WLONGVARCHAR.

(cherry picked from commit 16db4d1462bf3eacb93c0cd940f799160a284b24)
(cherry picked from commit 344ff5dd4c538eaebea075f7705321f8b86d0b47)
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '\t\t\t\t/* Workaround for drivers that report NVARCHAR(MAX) columns as SQL_WVARCHAR with size 0 (bug #69975) */', '\t\t\t\tif (result->values[i].coltype == SQL_WVARCHAR && displaysize == 0) {', '\t\t\t\t\tresult->values[i].coltype = SQL_WLONGVARCHAR;', '\t\t\t\t\tresult->values[i].value = NULL;', '\t\t\t\t\tbreak;', '\t\t\t\t}']}
description: The odbc_bindcols function in ext/odbc/php_odbc.c in PHP before 5.6.12 mishandles driver behavior for SQL_WVARCHAR columns, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) in opportunistic circumstances by leveraging use of the odbc_fetch_array function to access a certain type of Microsoft SQL Server table.

code_evidence: Lines 46-47 fetch the column's display/octet size from the driver into displaysize without checking that the reported size is meaningful. Lines 49-53 only fall back to SQL_COLUMN_DISPLAY_SIZE when the octet-length call fails; a successful but zero size is accepted as-is.

Lines 58-61 use displaysize directly as the allocation size (displaysize + 1); a zero or undersized value yields a too-small buffer that is then passed as the column buffer to SQLBindCol on lines 62-63.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function accepts external metadata (driver-reported size) and fails to validate that it is a usable positive value before using it for allocation, matching CWE-20's improper validation of input metadata. This is not merely a type-confusion or encoding issue; the unchecked input property (size) directly drives unsafe processing.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The driver-reported column size (metadata) is trusted without validation. A driver that reports SQL_WVARCHAR with displaysize 0 yields a minimal emalloc, and the subsequent SQLBindCol writes the actual column data into that undersized buffer, causing a crash/segfault. Root cause is the missing size check; the consequence is a denial-of-service crash when fetching such a column.

commit_msg:
Since the tee subsystem does not keep a strong reference to its idle
shared memory buffers, it races with other threads that try to destroy a
shared memory through a close of its dma-buf fd or by unmapping the
memory.

In tee_shm_get_from_id() when a lookup in teedev->idr has been
successful, it is possible that the tee_shm is in the dma-buf teardown
path, but that path is blocked by the teedev mutex. Since we don't have
an API to tell if the tee_shm is in the dma-buf teardown path or not we
must find another way of detecting this condition.

Fix this by doing the reference counting directly on the tee_shm using a
new refcount_t refcount field. dma-buf is replaced by using
anon_inode_getfd() instead, this separates the life-cycle of the
underlying file from the tee_shm. tee_shm_put() is updated to hold the
mutex when decreasing the refcount to 0 and then remove the tee_shm from
teedev->idr before releasing the mutex. This means that the tee_shm can
never be found unless it has a refcount larger than 0.

Fixes: 967c9cca2cc5 ("tee: generic TEE subsystem")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Reviewed-by: Lars Persson <larper@axis.com>
Reviewed-by: Sumit Garg <sumit.garg@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Patrik Lantz <patrik.lantz@axis.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tif (flags & TEE_SHM_DMA_BUF) {', '\t\tDEFINE_DMA_BUF_EXPORT_INFO(exp_info);', '', '\t\texp_info.ops = &tee_shm_dma_buf_ops;', '\t\texp_info.size = shm->size;', '\t\texp_info.flags = O_RDWR;', '\t\texp_info.priv = shm;', '', '\t\tshm->dmabuf = dma_buf_export(&exp_info);', '\t\tif (IS_ERR(shm->dmabuf)) {', '\t\t\tret = ERR_CAST(shm->dmabuf);', '\t\t\tteedev->desc->ops->shm_unregister(ctx, shm);', '\t\t\tgoto err;', '\t\t}', '\t}', ''], 'added_lines': ['\trefcount_set(&shm->refcount, 1);']}
description: A use-after-free exists in drivers/tee/tee_shm.c in the TEE subsystem in the Linux kernel through 5.15.11. This occurs because of a race condition in tee_shm_get_from_id during an attempt to free a shared memory object.

code_evidence: shm is allocated with kzalloc and its fields (flags, ctx, id) are initialized, but no lifetime reference is established before the object is published into teedev->idr.
The idr_alloc inserts shm into the shared teedev->idr under mutex, exposing the object to concurrent lookup via tee_shm_get_from_id; the mutex only protects the insertion, not subsequent lifetime.
The dma-buf export is tied to shm and on export failure shm_unregister is called and control goes to err, which frees shm; a concurrent lookup can still obtain a pointer to this shared object.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function exposes a shared object through a mutex-protected idr while its destruction is serialized on a different path, so concurrent lookup and teardown can interleave without exclusivity. This is a classic concurrent access with improper synchronization (CWE-362); the use-after-free is the downstream consequence, not the race itself.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the shared tee_shm is published in teedev->idr without an owning reference that keeps it alive, so its lifetime is coupled to the dma-buf/file teardown path. Trigger: one thread performs tee_shm_get_from_id lookup while another closes the dma-buf fd or unmaps, causing teardown and freeing of the same shm. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the shared memory object, leading to instability or memory corruption.

[CAUSE]
Commit a27a94c2b0c7 ("btrfs: Make btrfs_find_device_by_devspec return
btrfs_device directly") moves the "missing" device path check into
btrfs_rm_device().

But btrfs_rm_device() itself can have case where it only receives
@devid, with NULL as @device_path.

In that case, calling strcmp() on NULL will trigger the NULL pointer
dereference.

Before that commit, we handle the "missing" case inside
btrfs_find_device_by_devspec(), which will not check @device_path at all
if @devid is provided, thus no way to trigger the bug.

This flaw allows a local attacker to crash the system or leak kernel internal information. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

If the lookup returns -ENOENT, the error branch evaluates PTR_ERR(device) == -ENOENT && strcmp(device_path, "missing") == 0, invoking strcmp on the NULL device_path before any NULL check.

description: A heap-based buffer over-read was discovered in canUnpack in p_mach.cpp in UPX 3.95 via a crafted Mach-O file.

code_evidence: headway is taken directly from mhdri.sizeofcmds (line 12); the buffer rawmseg is allocated with that attacker-controlled size and filled via readx (lines 17-18).

The loop walks ncmds commands, advancing ptr by ptr->cmdsize (line 28) without validating that the command fits within the allocated rawmseg or headway; segptr is then dereferenced (line 29-30) before any bounds check.
The only size check (lines 49-54) subtracts cmdsize after the segment fields have already been read, so it cannot prevent the out-of-bounds access.

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: A crafted Mach-O header supplies sizeofcmds/ncmds and command cmdsize values that are not constrained against the allocated buffer. The loop dereferences ptr as Mach_segment_command and reads segname/filesize/fileoff before any bound check, so a malformed cmdsize or ncmds causes reads past rawmseg. The added patch validates cmdsize and segment file offsets to prevent this.

commit_msg:
Fixing security fixes in boosted trees ops

PiperOrigin-RevId: 405669548
Change-Id: Iae224d240d1779bcc02405c2fff99785644fbd0d
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    DCHECK_LE(num_sparse_entries, batch_size * feature_dims);'], 'added_lines': ['    OP_REQUIRES(context, num_sparse_entries <= batch_size * feature_dims,', '                errors::InvalidArgument(', '                    "feature_indices dim0 should be <= gradients dim0 * "', '                    "feature_shape[1]. features_indices dim0: ",', '                    num_sparse_entries, " gradients dim0: ", batch_size,', '                    ", feature_shape[1]: ", feature_dims));']}
description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. In affected versions the code for boosted trees in TensorFlow is still missing validation. As a result, attackers can trigger denial of service (via dereferencing `nullptr`s or via `CHECK`-failures) as well as abuse undefined behavior (binding references to `nullptr`s). An attacker can also read and write from heap buffers, depending on the API that gets used and the arguments that are passed to the call. Given that the boosted trees implementation in TensorFlow is unmaintained, it is recommend to no longer use these APIs. We will deprecate TensorFlow's boosted trees APIs in subsequent releases. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.7.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.6.1, TensorFlow 2.5.2, and TensorFlow 2.4.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: num_sparse_entries, batch_size and feature_dims are taken from the input tensors; the only bound on num_sparse_entries is a DCHECK_LE that is compiled out in release builds.
The loop iterates i < num_sparse_entries and reads feature_indices(i,0), feature_indices(i,1) and feature_values(i) without any runtime validation, then uses instance to index node_ids(instance).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The missing runtime bound lets attacker-controlled indices drive dereferences of pointers derived from tensors (node_ids, feature_indices) that are not validated, consistent with CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference as part of the described crash/DoS impact. The patch replaces the DCHECK with OP_REQUIRES, confirming the missing validation is the root cause.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the relationship num_sparse_entries <= batch_size * feature_dims is enforced only by a DCHECK, which is removed in opt builds. A caller can supply feature_indices with more rows than the gradients allow, so the loop reads out-of-range entries and indexes node_ids(instance) beyond its buffer, yielding invalid or null-backed memory access. Consequence: heap out-of-bounds read/write and crash/DoS.

commit_msg:
CVE-2017-12897/ISO CLNS: Use ND_TTEST() for the bounds checks in isoclns_print().

This fixes a buffer over-read discovered by Kamil Frankowicz.

Don't pass the remaining caplen - that's too hard to get right, and we
were getting it wrong in at least one case; just use ND_TTEST().

Add a test using the capture file supplied by the reporter(s).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\tisoclns_print(ndo, p + 1, length - 1, caplen - 1);'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tisoclns_print(ndo, p + 1, length - 1);']}
description: The ISO CLNS parser in tcpdump before 4.9.2 has a buffer over-read in print-isoclns.c:isoclns_print().

code_evidence: For ETHERTYPE_ISO, the code checks length==0 || caplen==0 then calls isoclns_print(ndo, p+1, length-1, caplen-1). It advances p by one and derives caplen-1, but the callee's bounds checks rely on caplen; passing a decremented caplen that is not consistently tied to the advanced pointer can let the ISO CLNS parser read past the captured buffer. The commit replaces this call to drop the caplen argument and use ND_TTEST().
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-125 fits because the unsafe operation is reading packet data past the end of the intended capture buffer due to incorrect remaining-length accounting. This is an out-of-bounds read, not a write; the consequence is memory read beyond bounds.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the caller passes a manually decremented caplen (caplen-1) alongside p+1 into isoclns_print, so the parser's remaining-capture accounting can be wrong and it reads beyond the captured data. Trigger: a packet with ETHERTYPE_ISO whose ISO CLNS content causes the parser to consume up to the stale caplen. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of packet buffer memory, potentially crash or info disclosure.

commit_msg:
analysisd: fix heap overflow in rootkit decoder.

The `RK_File` function of the rootcheck decoder needs to ensure it
doesn't index outside of `MAX_AGENTS` when trying to find/open
a rootcheck file for a given agent.

Prev. to this change the value of `i` could exceed `MAX_AGENTS`
resulting in a heap buffer overflow accessing `rk_agent_ips[i]` or
`rk_agent_fps[i]`.

The fix is adapted from similar logic in the syscheck decoder, added as
a response to a matching vulnerability in that decoder patched in 2012.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['    while (rk_agent_ips[i] != NULL) {'], 'added_lines': ['    while (i < MAX_AGENTS && rk_agent_ips[i] != NULL) {', '    }', '', "    /* If here, our agent wasn't found */", '    if (i == MAX_AGENTS) {', '        merror("%s: Unable to open rootcheck file. Increase MAX_AGENTS.", ARGV0);', '        return (NULL);']}
description: In OSSEC-HIDS 2.7 through 3.5.0, the server component responsible for log analysis (ossec-analysisd) is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer overflow in the rootcheck decoder component via an authenticated client.

code_evidence: The loop iterates while rk_agent_ips[i] is non-NULL and increments i without any bound check against MAX_AGENTS, so i can grow past the fixed-size rk_agent_ips/rk_agent_fps arrays when no match is found.
After the loop, rk_agent_ips[i] is written with strdup(agent) and rk_agent_fps[i] is written with fopen at the same unbounded index, writing past the end of the heap arrays.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the function performs writes (strdup, fopen assignment) to fixed-size agent arrays at an index that can be >= MAX_AGENTS. The missing bounds check is the root cause; the out-of-bounds write is the directly supported consequence, not merely an out-of-bounds read.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the linear scan of rk_agent_ips lacks an index bound, so an agent string that never matches (or a full table) drives i beyond MAX_AGENTS. Trigger: an authenticated client supplies an agent name reaching RK_File. Consequence: the writes at rk_agent_ips[i] and rk_agent_fps[i] exceed the heap buffer bounds, causing heap corruption and possible crash or code execution.

commit_msg:
decompile: fix null pointer dereference in newVar3

getString (indirectly called by getName) is passed a variable of non
standard type 10 (= "PUSH_VARIABLE"), which seems to return the
string contained in passed variable, without quotes. If contained
string is NULL, a NULL pointer is returned, which later causes NULL
pointer dereference.

In this patch we address this issue such that if the variable contains
an invalid string, we act just like in the PUSH_STRING case. Otherwise
a copy of the string is returned.

Fixes: #118 (CVE-2018-7866).
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\t\treturn act->p.String;'], 'added_lines': ['\t\tif (!act->p.String)', '\t\t{', '\t\t        SWF_warn("WARNING: Call to getString with PUSH_VARIABLE defining NULL string.\\n");', '\t\t        break;', '\t\t}', '\t\tt=malloc(strlen(act->p.String)+1); /* NULL character */', '\t\tstrcpy(t,act->p.String);', '\t\treturn t;']}
description: A NULL pointer dereference was discovered in newVar3 in util/decompile.c in libming 0.4.8. The vulnerability causes a segmentation fault and application crash, which leads to denial of service.

code_evidence: In the PUSH_VARIABLE case, getString returns act->p.String directly without checking whether it is NULL; the caller (e.g., getName) then uses the returned pointer, dereferencing NULL.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: Returning an unchecked NULL pointer that is later dereferenced is exactly CWE-476; the consequence is a crash rather than memory corruption or use-after-free.

evidence_lines.code:
case PUSH_VARIABLE: 
return act->p.String;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the PUSH_VARIABLE branch returns act->p.String with no NULL check, unlike the PUSH_STRING branch which guards it. Trigger: a crafted SWF yields a variable whose contained string is NULL; the returned NULL propagates to the caller and is dereferenced, causing a segmentation fault and DoS.

commit_msg:
svc: check for allocation overflow in syscall_cryp_obj_populate

Without checking for overflow there is a risk of allocating a buffer
with size smaller than anticipated and as a consequence of that it might
lead to a heap based overflow with attacker controlled data written
outside the boundaries of the buffer.

Fixes: OP-TEE-2018-0009: "Integer overflow in crypto system calls"

Signed-off-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org>
Tested-by: Joakim Bech <joakim.bech@linaro.org> (QEMU v7, v8)
Reviewed-by: Jens Wiklander <jens.wiklander@linaro.org>
Reported-by: Riscure <inforequest@riscure.com>
Reported-by: Alyssa Milburn <a.a.milburn@vu.nl>
Acked-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@linaro.org>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tattrs = malloc(sizeof(TEE_Attribute) * attr_count);'], 'added_lines': ['\tsize_t alloc_size = 0;', '', '\tif (MUL_OVERFLOW(sizeof(TEE_Attribute), attr_count, &alloc_size))', '\t\treturn TEE_ERROR_OVERFLOW;', '', '\tattrs = malloc(alloc_size);', '']}
description: Linaro/OP-TEE OP-TEE 3.3.0 and earlier is affected by: Buffer Overflow. The impact is: Code execution in context of TEE core (kernel). The component is: optee_os. The fixed version is: 3.4.0 and later.

code_evidence: The allocation size is computed as sizeof(TEE_Attribute) * attr_count at line 24, where attr_count is an unsigned long supplied by the caller, and the product is passed directly to malloc without any overflow check. The only validation is that malloc did not return NULL (line 25-26).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-190 fits because the size calculation sizeof(TEE_Attribute) * attr_count can wrap, and the wrapped result is used as an allocation size before a copy of attacker-controlled data. This is an integer overflow used to size memory, not a simple missing bounds check (CWE-787), which is only the downstream consequence.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the multiplication for the buffer size is performed without an overflow guard, so a large attr_count can wrap the product to a small value. Trigger: a caller passes a large attr_count; the small buffer is allocated, then copy_in_attrs (line 27-28) writes attr_count attributes into it, causing a heap-based out-of-bounds write with attacker-controlled data. Consequence: memory corruption potentially leading to code execution in the TEE core.

commit_msg:
win: fix unsavory rwlock fallback implementation

Before this patch an uv_mutex_t (backed by a critical section) could be
released by a tread different from the thread that acquired it, which is
not allowed. This is fixed by using a semaphore instead.

Note that the affected code paths were used on Windows XP and Windows
Server 2003 only.

Fixes: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/515
PR-URL: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/pull/516
Reviewed-By: Ben Noordhuis <info@bnoordhuis.nl>
Reviewed-By: Saúl Ibarra Corretgé <saghul@gmail.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  err = uv_mutex_trylock(&rwlock->fallback_.read_mutex_);', '  if (err)', '    goto out;', '  if (rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_ == 0)', '    err = uv_mutex_trylock(&rwlock->fallback_.write_mutex_);', '  if (err == 0)', '    rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_++;', '', '  uv_mutex_unlock(&rwlock->fallback_.read_mutex_);', '', 'out:'], 'added_lines': ['  if (!TryEnterCriticalSection(&rwlock->fallback_.read_lock_.cs))', '    return UV_EAGAIN;', '  if (rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_ == 0) {', '    DWORD r = WaitForSingleObject(rwlock->fallback_.write_lock_.sem, 0);', '    if (r == WAIT_OBJECT_0)', '      rwlock->fallback_.num_readers_++;', '    else if (r == WAIT_TIMEOUT)', '      err = UV_EAGAIN;', '    else if (r == WAIT_FAILED)', '      err = uv_translate_sys_error(GetLastError());', '    else', '      err = UV_EIO;', '  }', '  LeaveCriticalSection(&rwlock->fallback_.read_lock_.cs);']}
description: The uv_rwlock_t fallback implementation for Windows XP and Server 2003 in libuv before 1.7.4 does not properly prevent threads from releasing the locks of other threads, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (deadlock) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging a race condition.

code_evidence: Acquires read_mutex_ with uv_mutex_trylock and, on failure, jumps to out without touching read_mutex_.
When num_readers_ is 0, tries write_mutex_; if that succeeds num_readers_ is incremented, so a reader holds the write lock until it later unlocks.

Releases read_mutex_ unconditionally after inspecting num_readers_ and possibly acquiring write_mutex_. The mutex is a critical-section-backed uv_mutex_t, which may be released by a thread other than the one that acquired it.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: This is a concurrent shared-resource sequence whose exclusivity/atomicity is violated because a lock can be released by a non-owning thread, allowing an interfering thread to race on the rwlock state; that matches CWE-362 rather than a mere improper input validation issue.

evidence_lines.code: uv_mutex_unlock(&rwlock->fallback_.read_mutex_);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: The fallback rwlock guards its reader/writer state with a uv_mutex_t backed by a critical section, but the mutex is unlocked on a path where ownership is not guaranteed to be thread-local. Under concurrent tryrdlock/unlock sequences, another thread can release the lock, leaving the shared num_readers_/write_mutex_ state inconsistent and producing a deadlock (DoS).

description: All versions of Quagga, 0.93 through 1.1.0, are vulnerable to an unbounded memory allocation in the telnet 'vty' CLI, leading to a Denial-of-Service of Quagga daemons, or even the entire host. When Quagga daemons are configured with their telnet CLI enabled, anyone who can connect to the TCP ports can trigger this vulnerability, prior to authentication. Most distributions restrict the Quagga telnet interface to local access only by default. The Quagga telnet interface 'vty' input buffer grows automatically, without bound, so long as a newline is not entered. This allows an attacker to cause the Quagga daemon to allocate unbounded memory by sending very long strings without a newline. Eventually the daemon is terminated by the system, or the system itself runs out of memory. This is fixed in Quagga 1.1.1 and Free Range Routing (FRR) Protocol Suite 2017-01-10.

code_evidence: vty_ensure (vty, vty->length + 1) is called to grow the buffer, then vty->buf[vty->cp++] = c writes at index cp. The only bound check afterwards is cp > length, which increments length but does not prevent the write. If cp already equals or exceeds the allocated/valid length, the store to vty->buf[cp] occurs outside the buffer's intended boundary.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function writes one byte through vty->buf[vty->cp++] without an effective upper-bound constraint on cp, directly matching CWE-119's out-of-bounds write within a memory buffer. The unbounded-allocation DoS described in the advisory is a separate consequence; the code-level defect here is the missing bound on the buffer index.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the write to vty->buf[vty->cp++] happens before confirming cp is within the valid buffer region; the post-write cp > length check only adjusts length and cannot undo the out-of-bounds store. Trigger: a caller path where cp reaches or exceeds length (e.g. repeated overwrite insertion at the end). Supported consequence: out-of-bounds write into adjacent memory, corrupting program data (CWE-119 impact).

Fix/improve buffer overflow in MSG_ReadBits/MSG_WriteBits

Prevent reading past end of message in MSG_ReadBits. If read past
end of msg->data buffer (16348 bytes) the engine could SEGFAULT.
Make MSG_WriteBits use an exact buffer overflow check instead of
possibly failing with a few bytes left.

description: Buffer overflow in ioquake3 before 2017-08-02 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted packet.

code_evidence: Huff_offsetTransmit receives only fout and *offset, with no buffer length or maxoffset bound. It calls send(huff->loc[ch], NULL, fout), which writes the Huffman code bits into fout starting at bloc without any capacity check, then stores the advanced position back into *offset.

The patch adds maxoffset to enforce the bound, confirming the missing constraint is the buffer limit rather than an unrelated weakness.

Trigger: a crafted or long packet causes many Huffman transmissions, exhausting the fixed message buffer. Consequence: out-of-bounds writes, memory corruption, and possibly a crash (SEGFAULT).

commit_msg:
Fix for CVE-2018-16790 -- Verify bounds before binary length read.

As reported here: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/CDRIVER-2819,
a heap overread occurs due a failure to correctly verify data
bounds.

In the original check, len - o returns the data left including the
sizeof(l) we just read. Instead, the comparison should check
against the data left NOT including the binary int32, i.e. just
subtype (byte*) instead of int32 subtype (byte*).

Added in test for corrupted BSON example.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['      if (l >= (len - o)) {'], 'added_lines': ['      if (l >= (len - o - 4)) {']}
description: _bson_iter_next_internal in bson-iter.c in libbson 1.12.0, as used in MongoDB mongo-c-driver and other products, has a heap-based buffer over-read via a crafted bson buffer.

code_evidence: Bounds check `if (o >= (len - 4))` guards only the 4-byte length read at line 84, then the length `l` is validated with `if (l >= (len - o))` at line 86. The remaining data after `o` includes the 4-byte length just read, so this comparison overestimates available payload by 4 bytes.

Next, `subtype = *(iter->raw + iter->d2)` is read at line 90, and for the deprecated subtype, `memcpy (&binary_len, (iter->raw + iter->d3), sizeof (binary_len))` reads 4 bytes at line 97. `iter->d3 = o + 5`, so this read spans `o+5..o+8`; a crafted buffer where `l` passes the faulty check but leaves fewer than 4 bytes past the subtype causes the memcpy to read past `iter->raw + iter->len`.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function reads past the intended buffer boundary (the memcpy of binary_len at line 97) because of an incorrect bounds constraint, which is exactly CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read. It is not CWE-787 (write) or CWE-190 (integer overflow): the flaw is a missing/subtracted length term in a read bound check, not an arithmetic wrap or a write past the buffer.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the binary length check `l >= (len - o)` fails to subtract the 4-byte int32 length already consumed, so it permits `l` values larger than the actual remaining data. Trigger: a crafted BSON binary element with the deprecated subtype whose declared length passes the faulty check but whose buffer ends before the 4-byte inner binary_len. Consequence: heap-based out-of-bounds read via memcpy, leaking adjacent heap memory or crashing.

Prevent memory leak in decoding PNG images.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 409300653
Change-Id: I6182124c545989cef80cefd439b659095920763b
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['', '    // If we reach this point, then there is data in `decode` which must be', '    // freed by the time we end execution in this function. We cannot call', '    // `png::CommonFreeDecode()` before an `OP_REQUIRES` because if', '    // `OP_REQUIRES` constraint is satisfied then the data would be freed', "    // prematurely. Instead, let's use a `Cleanup` object.", '    auto cleanup = gtl::MakeCleanup([&decode]() {', '      std::cerr << "Cleanup called...\\n";', '      png::CommonFreeDecode(&decode);', '    });']}
description: Tensorflow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. When decoding PNG images TensorFlow can produce a memory leak if the image is invalid. After calling `png::CommonInitDecode(..., &decode)`, the `decode` value contains allocated buffers which can only be freed by calling `png::CommonFreeDecode(&decode)`. However, several error case in the function implementation invoke the `OP_REQUIRES` macro which immediately terminates the execution of the function, without allowing for the memory free to occur. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3, as these are also affected and still in supported range.

code_evidence: Line 3 declares a stack png::DecodeContext; lines 4-6 call png::CommonInitDecode, which on success allocates internal buffers in decode.

Lines 11-17 detect oversized dimensions and call OP_REQUIRES(context, false, ...), which returns from the function before any png::CommonFreeDecode(&decode) is invoked, abandoning the buffers allocated by CommonInitDecode.
Lines 41-47 similarly call OP_REQUIRES on a failed CommonFinishDecode, another early-exit path that skips freeing decode's buffers.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-401 fits because allocated memory is not released after its effective lifetime on error paths, matching the 'error conditions' cause. The added cleanup object confirms the missing release; this is a leak (CWE-401), not a use-after-free, since memory is never freed.

evidence_lines.code:
if (data_type_ == DataType::DT_UINT8) {
OP_REQUIRES(
context,
png::CommonFinishDecode(
reinterpret_cast<png_bytep>(output->flat<uint8>().data()),
decode.channels * width * sizeof(uint8), &decode),
errors::InvalidArgument("Invalid PNG data, size ", input.size()));

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: decode's buffers allocated by CommonInitDecode are freed only on the normal path, while OP_REQUIRES error paths (invalid dimensions at lines 11-17, failed finish at 41-47) return early without calling png::CommonFreeDecode. Trigger: malformed PNG input satisfying those error conditions. Consequence: each failed decode leaks allocated memory, enabling memory exhaustion/DoS.

description: A HTTP response header injection vulnerability in Swoole v4.5.2 allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via supplying a crafted URL.

code_evidence: When a value v is provided, the else branch at lines 22-24 passes the externally supplied header value directly to add_assoc_stringl_ex without validating vlen bytes for CR, LF or NUL; the key is formatted but the value bytes are stored verbatim. The diff adds a loop rejecting '\n','\r','\0' before this same add_assoc_stringl_ex call, confirming the pre-fix function accepted unvalidated special elements into the header record.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-74 fits because externally influenced data is placed into an output structure (the HTTP header record) without neutralizing special elements ('\r','\n') that alter how a downstream HTTP component parses it. This is the injection class; the CRLF-specific child would be more precise, but the target is CWE-74.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the header value is concatenated into the response header set without neutralizing CR/LF (and NUL) bytes. Trigger: attacker-controlled input reaches v/vlen, e.g. via a crafted URL. Consequence: injected line breaks split or add headers, enabling response header injection/CRLF injection into the downstream HTTP response parser.

description: Nagios Core before 4.3.3 creates a nagios.lock PID file after dropping privileges to a non-root account, which might allow local users to kill arbitrary processes by leveraging access to this non-root account for nagios.lock modification before a root script executes a "kill `cat /pathname/nagios.lock`" command.

code_evidence: The privilege drop (drop_privileges) is performed at line 258, after the main config is read, but before daemon_init() at line 272.
daemon_init() is invoked at line 272 only after privileges have been dropped; it creates the PID/lock file (lock_file) while running as the non-root nagios user.
On exit, line 415 unlinks lock_file, but the lock file was written without root ownership/initialization ordering.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-665 fits because the lock-file resource is initialized (created/owned) in an improper order/state relative to privilege dropping, leaving it in an unexpected state (attacker-writable) when later used. evidence_lines.code:
if(daemon_mode == TRUE)
unlink(lock_file);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the daemonization/lock-file initialization step is ordered after drop_privileges, so nagios.lock is created and owned by the unprivileged account rather than root. Supported consequence: killing of arbitrary processes.

description: Use After Free in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.2.

code_evidence: On the empty-tree path, tree->root is assigned the result of _node_new and only checked for NULL; there is no ownership or lifetime tracking of the node or of the head/parent sentinels used later.

The traversal initializes a stack RRBNode head via memset and sets parent = &head while g and p start NULL; _set_link(parent, q, 1) is invoked before any node exists, so link manipulation depends on sentinel state rather than a validated node.

The out_exit label unconditionally dereferences tree->root->red and tree->root->parent; if insertion fails on the q == NULL branch (line 21-22) the function returns early, but if the root node was freed or replaced elsewhere, these writes target stale memory.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The defect matches CWE-416: the code reuses a pointer to a node after it may have been freed, and performs writes (red/parent) through that stale reference. It is not merely a NULL-dereference (CWE-476) because the failure mode is operating on memory no longer owned by the tree, which the target CWE describes.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause is that the function writes tree->root->red and tree->root->parent at out_exit without verifying tree->root still refers to a live node, and rotations/_set_link mutate parent links that may point to the stack sentinel or a freed node. Trigger: an insertion path where the root or a rotated node is freed/replaced and the stale pointer is later dereferenced at lines 58-59, yielding a write-after-free that can corrupt memory or crash.

commit_msg:
With write operation on psi files replacing old trigger with a new one,
the lifetime of its waitqueue is totally arbitrary. Overwriting an
existing trigger causes its waitqueue to be freed and pending poll()
will stumble on trigger->event_wait which was destroyed.
Fix this by disallowing to redefine an existing psi trigger. If a write
operation is used on a file descriptor with an already existing psi
trigger, the operation will fail with EBUSY error.
Also bypass a check for psi_disabled in the psi_trigger_destroy as the
flag can be flipped after the trigger is created, leading to a memory
leak.

Fixes: 0e94682b73bf ("psi: introduce psi monitor")
Reported-by: syzbot+cdb5dd11c97cc532efad@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Suggested-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Analyzed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Suren Baghdasaryan <surenb@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Eric Biggers <ebiggers@google.com>
Acked-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220111232309.1786347-1-surenb@google.com
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tpsi_trigger_replace(&ctx->psi.trigger, new);', ''], 'added_lines': ['\t/* Allow only one trigger per file descriptor */', '\tif (ctx->psi.trigger) {', '\t\tcgroup_put(cgrp);', '\t\treturn -EBUSY;', '\t}', '', '\tsmp_store_release(&ctx->psi.trigger, new);']}
description: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's implementation of Pressure Stall Information. While the feature is disabled by default, it could allow an attacker to crash the system or have other memory-corruption side effects.

code_evidence: Line 13 selects the psi_group; line 14 creates a new trigger, and line 19 unconditionally calls psi_trigger_replace on ctx->psi.trigger, overwriting whatever trigger was previously stored for this open file. The function never checks whether ctx->psi.trigger is already non-NULL before replacing it, so a second write on the same file descriptor frees the existing trigger's waitqueue while prior poll() waiters may still reference trigger->event_wait.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The old trigger object and its embedded waitqueue are freed by the replacement while outstanding poll() references remain, and those references are subsequently used. That is use-after-free of the trigger/waitqueue memory, matching CWE-416 rather than a mere leak or double free.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the write path allows redefining an existing psi trigger, and psi_trigger_replace frees the old trigger and its waitqueue. Trigger: a second write to a file descriptor that already has a trigger; pending poll() callers that captured trigger->event_wait then dereference freed memory, producing use-after-free (crash or memory corruption).

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 5.0.4. The 9p filesystem did not protect i_size_write() properly, which causes an i_size_read() infinite loop and denial of service on SMP systems.

code_evidence: After v9fs_init_inode succeeds, the new inode is populated by v9fs_stat2inode_dotl(st, inode), which writes inode->i_size via i_size_write(). This call is made without holding inode->i_lock, even though the inode is newly locked and concurrently reachable through iget5_locked.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function's unprotected i_size_write() enables i_size_read() to loop indefinitely because the seqcount exit condition is never reached, matching CWE-835's infinite loop with unreachable exit condition affecting availability. This is a concurrency-induced loop, not merely a race data corruption issue.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: i_size_write() is performed without the inode->i_lock protection required for the seqcount used by i_size_read(). Trigger: concurrent v9fs_vfs_getattr/v9fs_vfs_getattr_dotl calls run generic_fillattr(), whose i_size_read() spins in read_seqcount_begin() while the seqcount is left inconsistent on 32-bit SMP. Supported consequence: infinite loop and soft-lockup CPU consumption (DoS).

commit_msg:
As part of CVE-2013-4288, the D-Bus clients were allowed (and
encouraged) to submit the UID of the subject of authorization checks
to avoid races against UID changes (notably using executables
set-UID to root).

However, that also allowed any client to submit an arbitrary UID, and
that could be used to bypass "can only ask about / affect the same UID"
checks in CheckAuthorization / RegisterAuthenticationAgent /
UnregisterAuthenticationAgent.  This allowed an attacker:

- With CheckAuthorization, to cause the registered authentication
  agent in victim's session to pop up a dialog, or to determine whether
  the victim currently has a temporary authorization to perform an
  operation.

  (In principle, the attacker can also determine whether JavaScript
  rules allow the victim process to perform an operation; however,
  usually rules base their decisions on information determined from
  the supplied UID, so the attacker usually won't learn anything new.)

- With RegisterAuthenticationAgent, to prevent the victim's
  authentication agent to work (for a specific victim process),
  or to learn about which operations requiring authorization
  the victim is attempting.

To fix this, expose internal _polkit_unix_process_get_owner() /
obsolete polkit_unix_process_get_owner() as a private
polkit_unix_process_get_racy_uid__() (being more explicit about the
dangers on relying on it), and use it in
polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject() to return
a boolean indicating whether the subject UID may be caller-chosen.

Then, in the permission checks that require the subject to be
equal to the caller, fail on caller-chosen UIDs (and continue
through the pre-existing code paths which allow root, or root-designated
server processes, to ask about arbitrary subjects.)

Signed-off-by: Miloslav Trmač <mitr@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  user_of_caller = polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject (priv->session_monitor, caller, NULL);', '  user_of_subject = polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject (priv->session_monitor, subject, NULL);', '  if (!polkit_identity_equal (user_of_caller, user_of_subject))'], 'added_lines': ['  gboolean user_of_subject_matches;', '  user_of_caller = polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject (priv->session_monitor, caller, NULL, NULL);', '  user_of_subject = polkit_backend_session_monitor_get_user_for_subject (priv->session_monitor, subject, &user_of_subject_matches, NULL);', '  if (!user_of_subject_matches', '      || !polkit_identity_equal (user_of_caller, user_of_subject))']}
description: A flaw was found in polkit before version 0.116. The implementation of the polkit_backend_interactive_authority_check_authorization function in polkitd allows to test for authentication and trigger authentication of unrelated processes owned by other users. This may result in a local DoS and information disclosure.

code_evidence: The function resolves the caller's identity at line 61 and the subject's identity at line 70, then only checks identity equality at line 79. When the subject is a unix-process, its UID is caller-supplied (racy UID), so an attacker can pass a subject whose UID equals the caller's UID and satisfy the equality check without owning that process.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-862 fits because the function fails to enforce an ownership constraint (subject must genuinely belong to the caller) before performing the privileged registration action; the equality check is not a sufficient authorization gate for caller-chosen UIDs.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ownership/authorization check relies solely on polkit_identity_equal between caller and subject, while the subject's reported UID may be attacker-chosen. Trigger: a local caller supplies a unix-process subject with a spoofed UID matching its own. Consequence: the caller registers an authentication agent for a process it does not own, enabling DoS against the victim's agent and disclosure of the victim's authorization requests.

commit_msg: Added received buffer size checks.
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    }', '', "    // Check that frame size isn't bigger than a JoinAccept with CFList size", '    if( encJoinAcceptSize > LORAMAC_JOIN_ACCEPT_FRAME_MAX_SIZE )', '    {', '        return SECURE_ELEMENT_ERROR_BUF_SIZE;']}

The crypto call passes encJoinAccept + 1 and encJoinAcceptSize - 1 as the source length, letting the routine process up to 254 bytes into decJoinAccept + 1; decJoinAccept has no validated capacity here.
The same unchecked size reaches the second crypto call, so both decryption paths can write beyond the destination buffer.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The unchecked input size is used directly in a buffer copy/decrypt operation that writes into decJoinAccept, matching CWE-120's pattern of copying input without verifying it fits the output. It is not merely an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) because the operation writes into the destination buffer.

lr1110_crypto_process_join_accept(
&LR1110, ( lr1110_crypto_status_t* ) &status, convert_key_id_from_se_to_lr1110( encKeyID ),
convert_key_id_from_se_to_lr1110( NWK_KEY ), ( lr1110_crypto_lorawan_version_t ) 0, micHeader10,

commit_msg:
hw/net: Fix a heap overflow in xlnx.xps-ethernetlite

The .receive callback of xlnx.xps-ethernetlite doesn't check the length
of data before calling memcpy. As a result, the NetClientState object in
heap will be overflowed. All versions of qemu with xlnx.xps-ethernetlite
will be affected.

Reported-by: chaojianhu <chaojianhu@hotmail.com>
Signed-off-by: chaojianhu <chaojianhu@hotmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': [], 'added_lines': ['    if (size > (R_MAX - R_RX_BUF0 - rxbase) * 4) {', '        D(qemu_log("ethlite packet is too big, size=%x\\n", size));', '        return -1;', '    }']}
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the .receive callback of xlnx.xps-ethernetlite in QEMU (aka Quick Emulator) allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the QEMU host via a large ethlite packet.

code_evidence: Line 4 derives rxbase from the guest-controlled s->rxbuf, and line 12 copies the incoming packet of length size into s->regs at offset rxbase + R_RX_BUF0 without any bounds check on size or rxbase.
Lines 5-6 show that packets not addressed to the NIC are returned early, but a matching packet (or a broadcast with the 0x80 bit set) reaches the memcpy with its full attacker-controlled size.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-787 fits because the memcpy at line 12 writes attacker-controlled data beyond the intended s->regs buffer, an out-of-bounds write. The missing length validation is the cause; heap corruption is the consequence, not a separate weakness such as CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read).

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned int rxbase = s->rxbuf * (0x800 / 4);
memcpy(&s->regs[rxbase + R_RX_BUF0], buf, size);

if (!(buf[0] & 0x80) && memcmp(&s->conf.macaddr.a[0], buf, 6))
return size;

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the receive callback trusts the packet size and rxbase when computing the destination offset into the fixed-size s->regs array, with no check that size fits within the remaining buffer. Trigger: a large ethlite packet (with matching/broadcast address) passes the early filter and reaches line 12. Consequence: memcpy writes past the end of s->regs, corrupting adjacent heap memory and potentially enabling host code execution or a crash.

code_evidence: augmentation_data_len is parsed from the ELF via READ_ULEB into an unsigned long (line 10), and its width is passed out through p_aug_len (line 4).
After parsing, line 65 compares augmentation_data_len against (size_t)(end - start); a length that exceeds the remaining buffer must be rejected here.
If the check passes, line 71 advances start by augmentation_data_len, and line 80 computes qend = q + augmentation_data_len; the inner loop later uses q at line 86 (size_of_encoded_value(*q)).
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The weakness is an integer truncation/wraparound in the size comparison that defeats a bounds check on attacker-controlled length data, matching CWE-190. It is not merely a plain out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), because the overflow in the length comparison is what permits the subsequent over-read.

evidence_lines.code:
unsigned long *p_aug_len, unsigned char **p_aug)
unsigned long augmentation_data_len = 0;

qend = q + augmentation_data_len;
q += 1 + size_of_encoded_value (*q);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the ULEB-derived augmentation_data_len is a 64-bit unsigned long compared against a size_t cast of (end - start); on a 32-bit size_t build the cast truncates the remaining length, so a huge value can pass the bounds check. Trigger: a crafted ELF whose CIE 'z' augmentation length is large. Consequence: start += augmentation_data_len moves past the buffer and qend wraps, so later dereferences such as size_of_encoded_value(*q) read out of bounds, crashing the tool.
