description: omx/OMXNodeInstance.cpp in libstagefright in mediaserver in Android 4.x before 4.4.4, 5.0.x before 5.0.2, 5.1.x before 5.1.1, and 6.x before 2016-08-01 does not validate the buffer port, which allows attackers to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka internal bug 28816827.

code_evidence: findBufferHeader is called with only the codec buffer handle from msg.u.extended_buffer_data.buffer, without specifying kPortIndexOutput, so the lookup is not restricted to the output port.
The returned buffer is dereferenced unconditionally: buffer->pAppPrivate is read and cast to BufferMeta, then buffer_meta->CopyFromOMX(buffer) is invoked.
The same unchecked buffer is passed to bufferSource->codecBufferFilled(buffer) and its fields (nTimeStamp, nOffset, nFilledLen, nAllocLen) are used in bounds arithmetic.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-119 fits because the unchecked buffer resolution leads to reads and writes through a pointer not constrained to the intended buffer region. The missing port validation and NULL check are the enabling weakness; the out-of-bounds memory operation is the direct consequence.

evidence_lines.code:
OMX_BUFFERHEADERTYPE *buffer =
findBufferHeader(msg.u.extended_buffer_data.buffer);

BufferMeta *buffer_meta =
static_cast<BufferMeta *>(buffer->pAppPrivate);

buffer_meta->CopyFromOMX(buffer);
bufferSource->codecBufferFilled(buffer);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the FILL_BUFFER_DONE path resolves a codec buffer without validating that it belongs to the output port, and no NULL check guards the result. A crafted application can supply a buffer handle that resolves to an unexpected or absent header; the subsequent pointer dereference and CopyFromOMX operate on memory outside the intended buffer, enabling out-of-bounds access and privilege escalation.

commit_msg:
Curl_auth_create_plain_message: fix too-large-input-check

CVE-2018-16839
Reported-by: Harry Sintonen
Bug: https://curl.haxx.se/docs/CVE-2018-16839.html
diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['  if((ulen > SIZE_T_MAX/2) || (plen > (SIZE_T_MAX/2 - 2)))'], 'added_lines': ['  if((ulen > SIZE_T_MAX/4) || (plen > (SIZE_T_MAX/2 - 2)))']}
description: Curl versions 7.33.0 through 7.61.1 are vulnerable to a buffer overrun in the SASL authentication code that may lead to denial of service.

code_evidence: Line 14 computes plen = strlen(passwdp); line 17 computes plainlen = 2 * ulen + plen + 2, a size_t arithmetic expression whose overflow is guarded only by the line 15 check that fails to bound ulen to SIZE_T_MAX/4 (the fix changes /2 to /4).

Line 18 allocates plainlen bytes; lines 21, 23 and 25 then memcpy ulen, ulen and plen bytes into that buffer at offsets 0, ulen+1 and 2*ulen+2, so an undersized allocation from the arithmetic overflow leads to out-of-bounds writes.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The guard against size_t overflow is insufficient, so the computed length no longer matches the data written, and memcpy operations write past the malloc'd buffer's intended boundary, which is the boundary-restriction weakness described by CWE-119. The root arithmetic-overflow error enables the out-of-bounds write that CWE-119 captures.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the pre-allocation overflow check at line 15 permits ulen values up to SIZE_T_MAX/2, but plainlen at line 17 doubles ulen plus plen and adds 2, so with large userp the size_t sum wraps to a small value. Trigger: a long SASL username passed to this function. Consequence: malloc at line 18 allocates a buffer smaller than the writes at lines 21-25 require, producing a heap buffer overrun (CWE-119) that can crash or corrupt memory.

cpu_hotplug_lock.rw_sem lock depends on the &sb->s_type->i_mutex_key lock.

sched_features, this way cpu_hotplug_lock.rw_sem no longer depends on
&sb->s_type->i_mutex_key.

diff_line_info: {'deleted_lines': ['\tstatic_key_disable(&sched_feat_keys[i]);'], 'added_lines': ['\tstatic_key_disable_cpuslocked(&sched_feat_keys[i]);']}
description: Race condition in the audit_log_single_execve_arg function in kernel/auditsc.c in the Linux kernel through 4.7 allows local users to bypass intended character-set restrictions or disrupt system-call auditing by changing a certain string, aka a "double fetch" vulnerability.

code_evidence: sched_feat_disable() calls static_key_disable() on the shared sched_feat_keys[i] without holding cpu_hotplug_lock, whereas the write path sched_feat_write() acquires that lock via cpus_read_lock() before modifying the key; the function therefore mutates the static key without the lock that serializes concurrent key updates.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: CWE-362 fits because the shared static key is accessed without the synchronization that other concurrent key-update sequences require, violating exclusivity. This is a synchronization/lock-order defect, not the double-fetch race described in the unrelated description.

evidence_lines.code: static_key_disable(&sched_feat_keys[i]);

joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: the static key is disabled without cpu_hotplug_lock, so it can be modified concurrently with a key update that requires that lock, creating a lock-order inversion against the debugfs inode mutex. Trigger: writing to sched_features while cpufreq initialization holds cpu_hotplug_lock and takes the same inode mutex. Supported consequence: circular locking dependency and potential deadlock/hang (availability impact).

commit_msg:
Patch series "Fix several device private page reference counting issues",
v2

This series aims to fix a number of page reference counting issues in
drivers dealing with device private ZONE_DEVICE pages.  These result in
use-after-free type bugs, either from accessing a struct page which no
longer exists because it has been removed or accessing fields within the
struct page which are no longer valid because the page has been freed.

During normal usage it is unlikely these will cause any problems.  However
without these fixes it is possible to crash the kernel from userspace. 
These crashes can be triggered either by unloading the kernel module or
unbinding the device from the driver prior to a userspace task exiting. 
In modules such as Nouveau it is also possible to trigger some of these
issues by explicitly closing the device file-descriptor prior to the task
exiting and then accessing device private memory.

This involves some minor changes to both PowerPC and AMD GPU code. 
Unfortunately I lack hardware to test either of those so any help there
would be appreciated.  The changes mimic what is done in for both Nouveau
and hmm-tests though so I doubt they will cause problems.


This patch (of 8):

When the CPU tries to access a device private page the migrate_to_ram()
callback associated with the pgmap for the page is called.  However no
reference is taken on the faulting page.  Therefore a concurrent migration
of the device private page can free the page and possibly the underlying
pgmap.  This results in a race which can crash the kernel due to the
migrate_to_ram() function pointer becoming invalid.  It also means drivers
can't reliably read the zone_device_data field because the page may have
been freed with memunmap_pages().

Close the race by getting a reference on the page while holding the ptl to
ensure it has not been freed.  Unfortunately the elevated reference count
will cause the migration required to handle the fault to fail.  To avoid
this failure pass the faulting page into the migrate_vma functions so that
if an elevated reference count is found it can be checked to see if it's
expected or not.

description: A vulnerability was found in Linux Kernel. It has been classified as problematic. Affected is an unknown function of the file mm/memory.c of the component Driver Handler. The manipulation leads to use after free. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-211020.

code_evidence: The loop iterates the prange's address range, finds each VMA, and calls svm_migrate_vma_to_ram() for [addr,next); the return value r is only checked for <0 or accumulated into upages. No reference is taken on the faulting page before this migration call, so the page/pgmap associated with the fault can be concurrently freed.
joint-evidence.cwe_rationale: The function drives migration of a page whose lifetime is not protected by a reference, matching CWE-416's use of memory after it has been freed. This is not merely a missing NULL check; the weakness is the absent lifetime constraint on the page/pgmap during use.
joint-evidence.vulnerability_mechanism: Root cause: migrate_to_ram() path migrates device-private pages without first pinning the faulting page. Trigger: a concurrent migration or driver unbind/memunmap_pages() frees the page and possibly pgmap while svm_migrate_vma_to_ram() is using it. Supported consequence: use-after-free of the struct page and pgmap, leading to kernel crash or invalid access to page fields.
